findings.evidence: Code treats BadZipFile as the corrupt-workbook path. openpyxl can also reject unsupported extensions with InvalidFileException, invalid XML with ValueError, or packages without a workbook part with I/O errors.
findings.impact: The student learns one corruption symptom as if it were the corruption category.
findings.fix: Classify a deliberately bounded set of openpyxl/ZIP parsing failures and leave unexpected exceptions fatal; record exception type and stage.
findings.attack: Some corrupt/invalid workbook inputs can escape the classifier and crash the whole batch, contradicting the promised isolation behavior.
findings.defense: BadZipFile is a useful first minimal example because XLSX is a ZIP container.

findings.title: A beginner cannot bridge from a three-line fake opener to the promised resilient file-processing harness without unstated design work.
findings.evidence: Prose promises per-file timeout, maximum size, ok/corrupt/locked counters, summary JSON, quarantine move and quarantine hash. Code implements none of timeout/size/quarantine/hash/JSON and prints only ok_count.
findings.impact: A beginner cannot bridge from a three-line fake opener to the promised resilient file-processing harness without unstated design work.
findings.fix: Implement size precheck, bounded processing strategy, all counters, quarantine move/copy policy, full SHA-256 and JSON summary in the theory example or explicitly defer each item.
findings.attack: The operational controls exist only as prose, so the learner cannot reproduce the stated robust batch behavior.
findings.defense: The code intentionally focuses on classification while prose previews the full project.

findings.title: The conceptual warning is stronger than the executable demonstration, leaving a predictable formula-cache misconception.
findings.evidence: The opening implies the displayed number is calculated when Excel opens the file. Later prose correctly says data_only reads a stored cache, but the demo never shows the key failure: a newly written formula can reopen with data_only=True as None/stale because openpyxl does not calculate it; workbook calculation mode is not introduced.
findings.impact: The conceptual warning is stronger than the executable demonstration, leaving a predictable formula-cache misconception.
findings.fix: Demonstrate formula-view versus data_only view after save, explain possible None/stale cache, and mention Excel calculation mode/recalculation as an external dependency.
findings.attack: The novice may infer that opening/reopening is equivalent to calculation.
findings.defense: T1-B explicitly warns that openpyxl has no Excel calculation engine and that caches are uncontrolled.

findings.title: Two different contracts—machine lookup and human presentation order—are collapsed into one rule.
findings.evidence: Figure says reading by name survives tab reordering; paragraph says order and names are part of the contract without defining why order must be stable.
findings.impact: Two different contracts—machine lookup and human presentation order—are collapsed into one rule.
findings.fix: State that code resolves sheets by name; validate order only if the VP template explicitly defines a visual-order requirement.
findings.attack: The learner may reintroduce positional brittleness even after being told to avoid it.
findings.defense: Visual tab order can itself be a presentation requirement even when programmatic lookup uses names.

findings.title: Normalizes weak/truncated identifiers in an audit manifest.
findings.evidence: input_sha1_8 keeps only eight hexadecimal characters (32 bits) of SHA-1.
findings.impact: Normalizes weak/truncated identifiers in an audit manifest.
findings.fix: Use full SHA-256 for artifact identity; if a short display id is useful, store it separately from the authoritative digest.
findings.attack: Collision probability becomes material across many artifacts and the name implies stronger identity than the field provides.
findings.defense: The field is not used for cryptographic security and the course fixture is tiny.

findings.title: The novice cannot infer whether an allowlist failure is a real domain rule or arbitrary fixture choice.
findings.evidence: A Peru-positioned reporting factory repeatedly mixes Lima, Madrid, Bogota, Barcelona and 'Lima-Madrid' without defining a multinational market dimension or coherent region domain.
findings.impact: The novice cannot infer whether an allowlist failure is a real domain rule or arbitrary fixture choice.
findings.fix: Use coherent Peru regions/cities throughout, or explicitly rename the field market and define a multinational allowlist.
findings.attack: Domain-validation examples become self-contradictory: whether a city is valid depends on an unstated geography model.
findings.defense: The data are synthetic and international examples can demonstrate generality.
findings.location: T1-A.p3; T2-B.code; T3-A.p3; T3-B.p3; T3-B.code; T4-A.p3

findings.title: Learner may overwrite a previously valid report with a half-written file.
findings.evidence: The factory saves directly to the final output path. A process/filesystem failure during save can leave a partial output even though the master remains safe.
findings.impact: Learner may overwrite a previously valid report with a half-written file.
findings.fix: Save to a temporary sibling file, reopen/validate it, then replace the destination atomically when the platform/filesystem supports it.
findings.attack: A lesson named robust reporting factory should not equate master safety with output durability.
findings.defense: Atomic replacement is a more advanced filesystem concern and the synthetic lab uses a temporary directory.

findings.title: Unnecessary lexical switching increases extraneous cognitive load and weakens self-sufficiency.
findings.evidence: factory, master, workbook, sheet, header, named range, schema, endpoint, KPI, headless, fills, borders, path, diff, layout, merge, pivot, fail-closed, allowlist, batch, lock, summary, digest and hash appear at high density; several are not introduced Spanish-first.
findings.impact: Unnecessary lexical switching increases extraneous cognitive load and weakens self-sufficiency.
findings.fix: Keep literal API identifiers but introduce concepts Spanish-first: libro/hoja/encabezado, plantilla maestra, procesamiento por lotes, lista permitida, manifiesto de corrida, huella SHA-256, cierre ante fallo.
findings.attack: The ZERO_TECH reader must decode vocabulary while simultaneously learning file integrity, Excel internals and auditability.
findings.defense: Many are real library/API terms and some are explained parenthetically.
findings.location: jobRelevance; learningOutcomes; T1-A; T1-B; T2-A; T2-B; T3-A; T3-B; T4-A; T4-B

findings.title: A novice gets abstraction without explanatory payoff.
findings.evidence: The lesson calls an Excel workbook a 'grafo de hojas + celdas + encabezados' without defining nodes, edges or what prediction the graph model enables.
findings.impact: A novice gets abstraction without explanatory payoff.
findings.fix: Replace with a concrete hierarchy: workbook contains sheets; sheets contain cells/ranges; tables and named ranges provide stable addressable regions.
findings.attack: The metaphor imports a later technical concept while adding no operational guidance and may suggest relationships that Excel does not represent as a graph here.
findings.defense: It is informal language meant to convey nested structure rather than graph theory.

findings.title: A polished report can launder an upstream false-green metric into an apparently audited executive artifact.
findings.evidence: Opening and T3-B require DOCX/PDF to share totals and n with S18-S20, but the campaign ledger marks S18-S20 REPAIR_REQUIRED and specifically rejects S20 reconciliation/provenance flags as trusted.
findings.impact: A polished report can launder an upstream false-green metric into an apparently audited executive artifact.
findings.fix: Require one validated upstream payload identity and re-run the critical reconciliation at the S21 boundary before rendering any document.

findings.title: The central CP-N2-B integration claim is never demonstrated; all local examples can pass while cross-artifact drift remains possible.
findings.evidence: The gate says one run generates dashboard, workbook, DOCX/PDF with reconciled numbers, but the eight theory snippets are isolated fixtures with separately hardcoded values and no orchestrating run.
findings.impact: The central CP-N2-B integration claim is never demonstrated; all local examples can pass while cross-artifact drift remains possible.
findings.fix: Add one closure harness that loads the validated payload once, renders all artifacts, reopens them, reconciles canonical records, hashes outputs and leaves pending_review.

findings.title: The learner sees presentation separation but not the provenance contract the outcome actually requires.
findings.evidence: T1-A promises a versioned context with run_id/metrics/limits reused across artifacts; s21_th_1 passes three ad-hoc keyword arguments and contains no run_id, version or reusable context object.
findings.impact: The learner sees presentation separation but not the provenance contract the outcome actually requires.
findings.fix: Build and validate a context object with schema_version, run_id, payload_id, canonical metric records and limits, then reuse it in at least two renderers.

findings.title: A missing n/source/limit can disappear silently from an executive document instead of failing closed.
findings.evidence: T1-A tells a serious factory to configure StrictUndefined, but both theory Jinja environments use the default Undefined behavior. Current Jinja renders a missing variable as an empty string by default.
findings.impact: A missing n/source/limit can disappear silently from an executive document instead of failing closed.
findings.fix: Use Environment(undefined=StrictUndefined, ...) in the canonical factory environment and demonstrate a missing required key raising before publication.

findings.title: Missingness and redaction have different semantics, audit implications and denominator treatment; one glyph makes them indistinguishable to…
findings.evidence: Opening says the same em dash represents both a missing value and a value that exists but must not be shown.
findings.impact: Missingness and redaction have different semantics, audit implications and denominator treatment; one glyph makes them indistinguishable to the reader.
findings.fix: Keep status metadata and visibly distinguish '— (sin dato)' from 'REDACTADO' or another explicit policy-approved marker.

findings.title: The canonical example does not implement one of the subtopic's main safety rules.
findings.evidence: T1-B promises None -> —, but s21_th_2 always executes '%.2f'|format(r.median). In the current runtime median=None raises TypeError: must be real number, not NoneType.
findings.impact: The canonical example does not implement one of the subtopic's main safety rules.
findings.fix: Branch before formatting or centralize format_metric(value, status, precision) so None returns an explicit missing token and numeric values follow the canonical display policy.

findings.title: A document with bold Normal paragraphs can satisfy the published theory check while failing the semantic outline contract.
findings.evidence: Learning outcome and prose require extraction of real Heading styles, yet s21_th_3 only checks text substrings and PK signature. It never inspects p.style.name or heading order after reopening.
findings.impact: A document with bold Normal paragraphs can satisfy the published theory check while failing the semantic outline contract.
findings.fix: After reopening, assert the expected Title/Heading levels and logical order, and test table headers/alt properties where the report contains those elements.

findings.title: The visual QA gate can be green on an unreadable page.
findings.evidence: T2-B says PNG render proves visual legibility; code only checks png.exists() and size > 0. A white-on-white text PDF reproduced both extractable n=40 and a non-empty PNG while the text was visually invisible.
findings.impact: The visual QA gate can be green on an unreadable page.
findings.fix: Call rendering a surface for review, not proof. Record actual human/visual-harness review of clipping, contrast, font rendering, pagination and figure/table placement.

findings.title: The learner never practices the abstention branch that is the core distinction of the subtopic.
findings.evidence: T2-B prose promises an image-only PDF negative case and needs_ocr, but s21_th_4 generates only a digital text PDF and never computes or prints needs_ocr.
findings.impact: The learner never practices the abstention branch that is the core distinction of the subtopic.
findings.fix: Create a synthetic image-only PDF fixture, show extract_text empty/insufficient, set needs_ocr=true and prohibit downstream factual extraction until OCR is explicitly performed and reviewed.

findings.title: A searchable PDF can still be inaccessible to assistive technology.
findings.evidence: S21 claims accessible reporting, but the ReportLab canvas example only draws text and tests extraction/render. It does not establish tagged headings, reading order, document language, table structure or image alternatives for the PDF.
findings.impact: A searchable PDF can still be inaccessible to assistive technology.
findings.fix: Either generate/test a tagged accessible PDF path or explicitly state that the simple ReportLab canvas PDF is a visual/digital artifact whose accessibility is not established; require PDF accessibility checks before the CP-N2-B gate.

findings.title: An eloquent but untraceable finding can pass the example because the promised acceptance rules are not executable.
findings.evidence: T3-A describes pack_report validation requiring n, unit and H->evidence and says decision=None, but s21_th_5 is only a hardcoded dict with no validator and no decision field.
findings.impact: An eloquent but untraceable finding can pass the example because the promised acceptance rules are not executable.
findings.fix: Implement validate_report(report) that checks required sections, canonical metric references, n/unit, evidence IDs, limits and explicit decision=None/pending-human-decision state.

findings.title: The central closure control can never detect an Excel/DOCX/dashboard disagreement.
findings.evidence: T3-B claims checksum/parity across PNG, XLSX and DOCX and shared run_id, but s21_th_6 opens none of those artifacts. It asserts only that the character string '40' appears in a caption and prints an in-memory metrics dict.
findings.impact: The central closure control can never detect an Excel/DOCX/dashboard disagreement.
findings.fix: Extract canonical records from each generated artifact and compare key, metric, numeric value, denominator, filter/universe, display precision and run_id; fail closed on any mismatch.

findings.title: Different underlying channel values can be hidden by display rounding, exactly the discrepancy S21 claims to prevent.
findings.evidence: s21_th_7 rounds [28.04, 28.0, 28] to one decimal, obtains [28.0, 28.0, 28.0], and declares consistente=True.
findings.impact: Different underlying channel values can be hidden by display rounding, exactly the discrepancy S21 claims to prevent.
findings.fix: First compare canonical numeric values/metric IDs before formatting; separately test that equal canonical values produce the same display string under the declared presentation profile.

findings.title: The report boundary reintroduces the numerical representation defect the early curriculum told the learner to avoid.
findings.evidence: T4-A normalizes monetary values with round(float(v), precision), while S02 explicitly established Decimal for soles and warned against converting money back to float.
findings.impact: The report boundary reintroduces the numerical representation defect the early curriculum told the learner to avoid.
findings.fix: Carry Decimal or integer cents into the publication context; use explicit quantization/formatting policy without round(float(...)) for PEN.

findings.title: The learner can copy an alt string that fails the exact accessibility rule being taught.
findings.evidence: T4-A says alt text must mention n and unit, but its example is 'Barras mediana por región, n por barra en tooltip': it contains neither an actual n nor PEN and delegates information to a tooltip unavailable in a static document.
findings.impact: The learner can copy an alt string that fails the exact accessibility rule being taught.
findings.fix: Use a concrete equivalent such as 'Ticket mediano por región en la muestra web: Lima 28.0 PEN (n=40), ...' or point to an adjacent accessible table containing all values.

findings.title: A document can satisfy length/heading-presence heuristics while remaining inaccessible.
findings.evidence: T4-A reduces the minimum to has_h1 plus at least one alt longer than 10 characters; theory code implements neither. It omits logical heading order, actual alt attachment, simple table/header semantics and document accessibility inspection.
findings.impact: A document can satisfy length/heading-presence heuristics while remaining inaccessible.
findings.fix: Define observable DOCX/PDF accessibility checks aligned to the artifact: logical heading hierarchy, actual alternative text on visuals, simple header-marked tables, language/reading order where supported, and a documented accessibility review.

findings.title: The manifest can assert a healthy package without observing any package file.
findings.evidence: s21_th_8 hardcodes {'dashboard':'ok','xlsx':'ok','doc':'ok'}, hashes the literal bytes b'synthetic', and computes no artifact hash despite prose requiring hashes of artifacts and visual checklist evidence.
findings.impact: The manifest can assert a healthy package without observing any package file.
findings.fix: Derive status from executed checks and compute SHA-256 for the validated input payload, template/source artifacts and each actual output file.

findings.title: The package can appear complete without a persisted reviewable state transition or evidence of human inspection.
findings.evidence: T4-B specifies ready(checklist)=all(dashboard,xlsx,doc), a pending_review manifest on disk and human actor/timestamp workflow; s21_th_8 has no checklist function, no visual review fields and only prints JSON to stdout.
findings.impact: The package can appear complete without a persisted reviewable state transition or evidence of human inspection.
findings.fix: Persist manifest.json atomically with checklist results, artifact identities and pending_review; only a later human review action may add reviewer/timestamp and transition to approved/rejected.

findings.title: A shared source reduces drift but renderers, formatting, stale artifacts, manual edits and code defects can still produce disagreement.
findings.evidence: Opening says one source makes disagreement 'imposible en vez de improbable'.
findings.impact: A shared source reduces drift but renderers, formatting, stale artifacts, manual edits and code defects can still produce disagreement.
findings.fix: Say a single canonical payload plus post-render reconciliation makes disagreement detectable and blocks publication.

findings.title: Learners may equate HTML escaping with universal sanitization or document safety.
findings.evidence: Opening frames escaping as if direct field insertion generically breaks 'the document', while Jinja autoescape is specifically an HTML/XML escaping policy and the course also creates DOCX via python-docx and plain text/Markdown.
findings.impact: Learners may equate HTML escaping with universal sanitization or document safety.
findings.fix: Teach sink-specific encoding: HTML autoescape for HTML, library-managed OOXML text for python-docx, and explicit plain-text/Markdown character policy; never call one escape mechanism universal sanitization.

findings.title: The learner cannot tell whether the canonical payload stores full-precision values, rounded publication values or display strings.
findings.evidence: T1-A says KPIs arrive already rounded from Python, while T1-B explicitly formats 28.456 to 28.46 in Jinja and T4-A allows one decimal in summaries versus two in detail.
findings.impact: The learner cannot tell whether the canonical payload stores full-precision values, rounded publication values or display strings.
findings.fix: Define three layers: canonical numeric value, publication/quantization rule if business-required, and channel display precision. Formatting may change the string but must not be used to prove source-value equality.

findings.title: A fresh learner environment can fail for a dependency-name collision despite installing the documented pymupdf package.
findings.evidence: PDF examples import fitz. Current PyMuPDF documentation recommends import pymupdf; the legacy fitz name can collide with an unrelated PyPI package named fitz.
findings.impact: A fresh learner environment can fail for a dependency-name collision despite installing the documented pymupdf package.
findings.fix: Use import pymupdf and pymupdf.open(...); if fitz is mentioned, label it as legacy compatibility only.

findings.title: The course lowers Spanish redaction quality for a workaround not demonstrated to be necessary in the supported stack.
findings.evidence: Opening callout says ReportLab/Helvetica demos intentionally write 'sintetico' ASCII. In the current runtime, ReportLab default Helvetica and pypdf round-trip 'sintético' correctly.
findings.impact: The course lowers Spanish redaction quality for a workaround not demonstrated to be necessary in the supported stack.
findings.fix: Write correct es-PE text with accents; if a font limitation is ever real, teach font embedding/Unicode support explicitly instead of normalizing Spanish to ASCII.

findings.title: Population/coverage language becomes incoherent and weakens the course's Peru-grounded business scenario.
findings.evidence: CASO-LIM-021 repeatedly compares Lima and Madrid as region peers without defining a multinational universe, continuing the geography ambiguity already flagged in S19-S20.
findings.impact: Population/coverage language becomes incoherent and weakens the course's Peru-grounded business scenario.
findings.fix: Use a coherent Peru fixture (for example Lima/Arequipa/Trujillo) or explicitly rename the dimension to market/city and define the multinational universe.

findings.title: Unnecessary lexical switching increases extraneous cognitive load in a course whose stated language is Peruvian Spanish.
findings.evidence: Dense use of context, factory, provenance, missing, caption, bundle, outline, a11y, pending_review and other English terms appears faster than stable Spanish-first definitions.
findings.impact: Unnecessary lexical switching increases extraneous cognitive load in a course whose stated language is Peruvian Spanish.
findings.fix: Introduce Spanish concept first and preserve API/status literals only where they are actual code contracts, e.g. contexto, factoría/generador de reportes, trazabilidad/procedencia, dato faltante, pie de figura, paquete, esquema, accesibilidad.

findings.title: UNTRUSTED_S21_PACKAGE_ASSUMED_RECONCILED
findings.evidence: S22 repeatedly says the S21 report package is already reconciled and uses its run data as input.
findings.impact: S21 remains REPAIR_REQUIRED; its parity/provenance/pending_review evidence is not creditable. S22 can therefore package or route an unverified report.

findings.title: ROUTABLE_EXAMPLE_PE_USED_AS_LAB_EMAIL_DOMAIN
findings.evidence: The lab allowlists and addresses use @example.pe and explicitly say it is not an impossible-to-route domain.
findings.impact: RFC/IANA reserve .test/.example/.invalid and example.com/net/org, not example.pe. A future provider adapter could accidentally address a real domain, contradicting the no-real-email gate.

findings.title: BCC_PRIVACY_MODEL_INCOMPLETE_FOR_EXTERNAL_RECIPIENTS
findings.evidence: The section treats moving externals to BCC as a privacy protection for the recipient list.
findings.impact: BCC hides BCC addresses from other recipients, but BCC recipients normally still receive visible To/Cc headers. Individual sends are required when an external must not learn internal recipient addresses.

findings.title: SANITIZER_ALLOWED_HOSTS_PARAMETER_BYPASSED_BY_HARDCODED_SUFFIX
findings.evidence: sanitize_html accepts allowed_hosts but also always permits host.endswith('.example.pe').
findings.impact: Passing allowed_hosts={'corp.pe'} still permits sub.example.pe. The security parameter does not actually define the policy.

findings.title: DRAFT_ONLY_LEAST_PRIVILEGE_CHECK_ACCEPTS_SEND
findings.evidence: least_privilege_ok treats mail.send as part of the allowed capability set and only excludes mail.full.
findings.impact: A granted ['mail.draft','mail.send'] evaluates True even though the callout says deny mail.send for a draft-only lab.

findings.title: SCOPE_POLICY_IS_HARDCODED_NOT_OBSERVED
findings.evidence: Prose says requested∩allowed and granted scopes are audited, but the example hardcodes requested_scopes/granted_scopes and never validates a provider response or fail-closes on missing/unexpected grants.
findings.impact: Learners can print least_privilege_ok without demonstrating that authorization actually matches policy.

findings.title: DRAFT_EXPIRY_NOT_INTEGRATED_WITH_APPROVAL_STATE
findings.evidence: T2-B says expired drafts cannot be promoted without regeneration/reapproval; T4 approval state machine never checks draft expiry or draft usability.
findings.impact: An approval can remain 'approved' after the underlying draft expires or changes.

findings.title: DEDUPE_OVERWRITES_FIRST_RECIPIENT_ROLE
findings.evidence: T3-B promises dedupe preserving first appearance, but OrderedDict assignment replaces the value for a duplicate email.
findings.impact: A later duplicate can change a first BCC entry into To/CC and increase disclosure while preserving the original position.

findings.title: EXTERNAL_RECIPIENT_POLICY_HARDCODED_TO_OTHER_TEST
findings.evidence: T3-B says every external domain is forced to BCC, but code only checks email.endswith('@other.test').
findings.impact: Any other external domain remains visible, so the policy does not generalize beyond the fixture.

findings.title: APPROVER_ROLE_NOT_AUTHORIZED
findings.evidence: approval_sm.py accepts any actor string for approve.
findings.impact: The same analyst who submitted can call approve and reach approved. 'Human approval' is not equivalent to an authorized independent reviewer.

findings.title: APPROVAL_AUDIT_MISSING_TIMESTAMP_AND_COMMENTS
findings.evidence: The transition log stores from/to/action/actor only.
findings.impact: S21 carry-forward and S22 prose require actor, timestamp and review comments/notes; these are necessary to reconstruct who approved what and when.

findings.title: APPROVAL_NOT_BOUND_TO_EXACT_DRAFT_CONTENT
findings.evidence: Approval transitions contain no draft_id, message hash, recipient set, subject, attachment hashes or body version.
findings.impact: A message can be edited after approval without invalidating the approval record. Human review must bind to the exact bytes/payload reviewed.

findings.title: EVERY_RECIPIENT_CONFIRMATION_GATE_NOT_IMPLEMENTED
findings.evidence: Tagline says every recipient requires confirmation, but the state machine approves one draft state with no per-recipient confirmation evidence.
findings.impact: A multi-recipient draft can be approved without showing that each To/Cc/Bcc address was reviewed.

findings.title: IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_OMITS_MESSAGE_PAYLOAD_FIELDS
findings.evidence: Key is sha256(run_id|to|body_ver)[:16].
findings.impact: Subject, body content hash, Cc/Bcc, attachments, sender and recipient-set version are absent; changed content can reuse an old draft if body_ver is not manually bumped.

findings.title: TRUNCATED_NONATOMIC_KEY_CANNOT_GUARANTEE_IDEMPOTENCY
findings.evidence: Outcome says 'Garantizar idempotencia' using sha256[:16] and a normal dict check-then-insert.
findings.impact: Sixteen hex characters are a 64-bit prefix and there is no collision check or atomic uniqueness. Concurrent workers can also race through the membership check.

findings.title: IDEMPOTENCY_AUDIT_LOG_LACKS_ACTOR_TIMESTAMP_AND_STATE
findings.evidence: T4-B says audit log records create/submit/approve/retry_hit with actor and timestamps in production; example only logs create/retry_hit with key/draft_id.
findings.impact: The final idempotency example does not satisfy its own audit-log outcome or connect to the approval log.

findings.title: NO_INTEGRATED_PERSISTED_DRAFT_APPROVAL_WORKFLOW
findings.evidence: Theory examples separately demonstrate MIME, sanitizer, scopes, draft store, recipients, list hygiene, approval and key.
findings.impact: No executable flow consumes a validated S21 manifest, creates a persisted .eml/sandbox draft, binds verified recipients, submits it, records approval, checks expiry/idempotency and persists one audit trail. The section gate is therefore not demonstrated end-to-end.

findings.title: EMAIL_IRREVERSIBILITY_OVERCLAIM
findings.evidence: Opening says an email 'no se puede deshacer'.
findings.impact: Recall/retraction mechanisms exist in limited systems; the transferable rule is that delivery cannot be reliably revoked once a recipient/provider has received the message.

findings.title: ATTACHMENT_DESCRIBED_AS_CONTROLLED_DISCLOSURE_SURFACE
findings.evidence: T3-B suggests sensitive detail can live in a 'controlled attachment' instead of the body.
findings.impact: An email attachment is copied to the recipient and can be forwarded; it is not equivalent to an access-controlled portal. Disclosure minimization must cover attachments too.

findings.title: MIME_HEADER_COUNT_FALSE_GREEN
findings.evidence: T1-A says counting Content-Type headers validates that the multipart tree is correctly nested.
findings.impact: The number of Content-Type headers does not prove multipart/alternative placement, attachment disposition, or part semantics; different trees can have the same count.

findings.title: PLAIN_TEXT_PRESENTED_AS_PROTOCOL_MANDATORY
findings.evidence: Figure/callout say the plain-text part is 'not optional' and many clients/filters require it.
findings.impact: multipart/alternative text+HTML is strong compatibility practice, but an HTML-only MIME message is not categorically invalid. Teach it as a robustness/accessibility requirement of the course, not a universal protocol law.

findings.title: RELATIVE_LINK_POLICY_CONTRADICTS_IMPLEMENTATION
findings.evidence: T1-B says relative routes are allowed, but sanitize_html only permits URLs matching ^https?://.
findings.impact: A documented allowed class is always blocked, making the contract and code disagree.

findings.title: FILE_DRAFT_ADAPTER_IS_MEMORY_ONLY_AND_MISSING_IDS_CRASH
findings.evidence: FileDraftAdapter stores drafts only in a dict and is_usable directly indexes self.store[draft_id].
findings.impact: The name suggests file persistence that does not exist, and an unknown ID raises KeyError instead of an explicit not-found/unusable result.

findings.title: RECIPIENT_FORMAT_CHECK_ACCEPTS_WHITESPACE_AND_CONTROL_SHAPES
findings.evidence: verify uses ^[^@]+@[^@]+\.[^@]+$ as a 'bad_format' gate.
findings.impact: It accepts strings such as 'a b@example.pe' and even newline-containing local parts. A basic gate should at least reject whitespace/control characters or use a standard parser.

findings.title: DECLARED_CANDIDATE_RECIPIENT_STATE_NEVER_EXISTS
findings.evidence: Prose defines unresolved → candidate → verified|rejected.
findings.impact: The implementation jumps directly from directory lookup to verified/rejected; candidate is not represented or audited.

findings.title: LIST_SIZE_AND_OPTOUT_CONTRACT_NOT_IMPLEMENTED
findings.evidence: T3-B says the lab models a list-size cap and synthetic opt-out flag.
findings.impact: Neither appears in the canonical theory code, so two announced privacy controls are prose-only.

findings.title: SPANGLISH_AND_WIDOW_TERM_DENSITY
findings.evidence: Learner-facing prose rapidly stacks draft, sandbox, fail-closed, scope, key, store, workflow, allowlist, BCC, HITL and audit log.
findings.impact: Several are glossed, but density remains high for ZERO_TECH and Spanish-first guidance can be more consistent.

findings.title: GENERIC_LINK_TEXT_WEAKENS_EMAIL_ACCESSIBILITY
findings.evidence: Sanitizer emits enlace for every permitted review URL.
findings.impact: Generic repeated link text gives little destination/purpose context to screen-reader and skim users; the reviewed action should have meaningful link text such as 'Revisar borrador del run …'.

findings.title: Browser automation can operationalize a stale or unverified payload.
findings.evidence: Opening/reference treat the S21 report and S22 human-approved draft as established inputs.
findings.impact: Browser automation can operationalize a stale or unverified payload.
findings.fix: Require a validated persisted S21/S22 handoff object and recheck its hashes/state before any downstream browser action.
findings.attack: S21/S22 remain REPAIR_REQUIRED; those artifacts and approval bindings are not creditable.
findings.defense: The curriculum needs continuity across sections.

findings.title: Learner is taught an unsafe ordering of evidence acquisition and human approval.
findings.evidence: Reference says S22 already left an approved email draft, then S23 obtains the report from the practice site.
findings.impact: Learner is taught an unsafe ordering of evidence acquisition and human approval.
findings.fix: State whether S23 is an independent new run; otherwise fetch/verify first, regenerate the draft, then require fresh approval.
findings.attack: If S23 obtains new report data after approval, the S22 draft approval is stale unless the new report is explicitly unrelated.
findings.defense: S23 may be intended as a separate adapter exercise.

findings.title: A learner can pass the theory without demonstrating Playwright behavior at all.
findings.evidence: The only real Playwright block is explicitly a non-executed sketch; graded/theory examples primarily use dict models.
findings.impact: A learner can pass the theory without demonstrating Playwright behavior at all.
findings.fix: Include one minimal controlled local web fixture and execute the end-to-end Playwright contract in theory/lab evidence.
findings.attack: The roadmap gate promises a robot against a controlled test site with real trace/download evidence.
findings.defense: Dict models improve portability and conceptual isolation.

findings.title: Canonical example can return a path to a file that no longer exists.
findings.evidence: playwright_sketch.py calls download.path(), closes browser, then returns that path.
findings.impact: Canonical example can return a path to a file that no longer exists.
findings.fix: Persist with download.save_as() before closing the context and return the persisted path.
findings.attack: Playwright deletes context-owned temporary downloads when the context closes; remote connections may not support path().
findings.defense: The sketch only illustrates API shape.

findings.title: The real Playwright path fails the section's own definition of success.
findings.evidence: The real sketch never checks download.failure(), suggested filename, size, expected hash or saved bytes.
findings.impact: The real Playwright path fails the section's own definition of success.
findings.fix: save_as, inspect failure/filename, compute full SHA-256, parse/validate expected content and record provenance.
findings.attack: The gate says download verificado, not merely download observed.
findings.defense: T2-A later discusses hashes conceptually.

findings.title: The model teaches a silent wrong-click failure mode Playwright is designed to reject.
findings.evidence: Custom get_by_role returns hits[0] when multiple role/name matches exist.
findings.impact: The model teaches a silent wrong-click failure mode Playwright is designed to reject.
findings.fix: Require len(hits)==1 and add zero-match and multi-match negative fixtures.
findings.attack: Playwright locator actions require a unique target; ambiguity should fail rather than select the first node.
findings.defense: The fixture contains one matching button in the happy path.

findings.title: Learner sees a success-only waiting example while the text claims robust failure evidence.
findings.evidence: T1-B says timeout should attach trace, but its code has no timeout evidence path and no negative fixture.
findings.impact: Learner sees a success-only waiting example while the text claims robust failure evidence.
findings.fix: Add a timeout fixture that produces a real trace/evidence record consumed by T3-A.
findings.attack: The diagnostic behavior is asserted rather than demonstrated.
findings.defense: Tracing is covered later in T3-A.

findings.title: The example can never catch the central failure: exporting the wrong report.
findings.evidence: T2-A upload stores bytes under plantilla.xlsx; download reads those exact same bytes back under the same name.
findings.impact: The example can never catch the central failure: exporting the wrong report.
findings.fix: Separate upload input from generated output bytes and compare the persisted output against an independently defined expected contract.
findings.attack: This models an echo, not a portal-generated export, and never compares the digest against an independent expected value.
findings.defense: It demonstrates byte hashing mechanics.

findings.title: Learners can transfer the pattern to real portals and accidentally leak session credentials.
findings.evidence: storage_state reuse is taught without warning that the state itself may contain impersonation-capable cookies/headers.
findings.impact: Learners can transfer the pattern to real portals and accidentally leak session credentials.
findings.fix: Teach storage_state as a secret-bearing artifact: gitignore, least-privilege test account, expiry, restricted retention and no logging.
findings.attack: Playwright explicitly warns not to commit auth state and recommends a gitignored auth directory.
findings.defense: The lab uses demo credentials.

findings.title: Another analyst cannot reproduce the failure despite the lesson claiming they can.
findings.evidence: on_failure returns traces/{step}.zip and shots/{step}.png strings but creates neither artifact.
findings.impact: Another analyst cannot reproduce the failure despite the lesson claiming they can.
findings.fix: Generate trace and screenshot in the controlled Playwright run, then assert existence/nonzero size and attach hashes.
findings.attack: The callout/gate require openable trace evidence; a path string is not a trace.
findings.defense: The lab models package keys.

findings.title: Operational transfer can turn diagnostic evidence into a data-leak artifact.
findings.evidence: Theory says never PII in screenshots/logs, but tracing can capture DOM snapshots and network activity and no redaction/retention mechanism is shown.
findings.impact: Operational transfer can turn diagnostic evidence into a data-leak artifact.
findings.fix: Use synthetic/test accounts, define trace retention/access, block or redact sensitive fields/routes, and forbid production PII in training fixtures.
findings.attack: A trace may expose more sensitive material than a screenshot; a prose prohibition does not sanitize it.
findings.defense: The lab is synthetic.

findings.title: Imports a Selenium/ElementHandle recovery model into a locator-first Playwright lesson.
findings.evidence: Recovery teaches err=='stale' and reobtaining a locator after re-render as a classic failure mode.
findings.impact: Imports a Selenium/ElementHandle recovery model into a locator-first Playwright lesson.
findings.fix: Teach locator re-resolution as the default; reserve explicit recovery for page/business-state invalidation, not ordinary DOM replacement.
findings.attack: Playwright Locators already resolve an up-to-date element on each action; ElementHandle use is discouraged and is the stale-object mental model.
findings.defense: Renavigation can still be necessary when business state is invalid.

findings.title: Success can be reported even when the supplied operation was never invoked.
findings.evidence: run_with_retry(fn, errors, ...) never calls fn; it consumes a pre-scripted error list.
findings.impact: Success can be reported even when the supplied operation was never invoked.
findings.fix: Call the operation per attempt via a deterministic fake that raises typed errors, then record attempts and postconditions.
findings.attack: The function name and prose claim action retry/recovery, but no action is executed.
findings.defense: The list is a deterministic teaching fixture.

findings.title: The executable policy contradicts the strongest safety insight in the paragraph.
findings.evidence: should_retry marks all timeout/network/429 kinds retryable without knowing the operation or whether a side effect already occurred.
findings.impact: The executable policy contradicts the strongest safety insight in the paragraph.
findings.fix: Classify retryability by error plus operation semantics; check server-side postcondition/idempotency key before repeating and honor provider backoff.
findings.attack: A timeout after a successful server-side action can duplicate an export/submit; 429 should obey Retry-After/backoff where applicable.
findings.defense: The prose later acknowledges idempotence windows and business keys.

findings.title: Learner cannot test the crash window the section explicitly identifies.
findings.evidence: Learning outcome and prose require checkpoint reanudación; the theory code implements no checkpoint or persisted last_ok_step.
findings.impact: Learner cannot test the crash window the section explicitly identifies.
findings.fix: Add a persisted checkpoint fixture with a crash-after-effect-before-checkpoint negative test and an idempotent server-side key.
findings.attack: A central T3 competency exists only as prose.
findings.defense: The paragraph explains the conceptual hazard unusually well.

findings.title: The robot can choose the wrong integration while claiming API-first correctness.
findings.evidence: choose_integration selects API/export/RPA from booleans only and does not emit the reason/runbook evidence promised in prose.
findings.impact: The robot can choose the wrong integration while claiming API-first correctness.
findings.fix: Evaluate equivalence, authorization, freshness, provider policy and auditability, then persist method+reason+evidence.
findings.attack: Availability alone does not prove the API/export is authorized, fresh, equivalent to the required report or contractually allowed.
findings.defense: The hierarchy is a useful default bias away from brittle UI automation.

findings.title: Handoff is a label, not an actionable continuation packet.
findings.evidence: T4-B prose requires minimal url/step/screenshot payload; handle_blockers returns only action/reason/queue.
findings.impact: Handoff is a label, not an actionable continuation packet.
findings.fix: Return run_id, safe URL, step, screenshot/trace references, last verified checkpoint and allowed next actions.
findings.attack: The human cannot resume from the promised context.
findings.defense: The code demonstrates blocker priority correctly: ToS before CAPTCHA.

findings.title: A later reviewer cannot prove which approved payload drove which browser run/download.
findings.evidence: Theory examples emit isolated dicts/prints without one persisted audit chain linking S21 payload, S22 draft/approval and S23 browser action.
findings.impact: A later reviewer cannot prove which approved payload drove which browser run/download.
findings.fix: Carry run_id and immutable hashes through every event and write an append-only browser-action manifest.
findings.attack: The campaign handoff explicitly requires a persisted lineage; browser automation is the highest-risk place to break it.
findings.defense: Individual subtopics intentionally isolate concepts.

findings.title: Conflates test resilience with accessibility conformance.
findings.evidence: Theory/callout use the equation 'accesibilidad = estabilidad'.
findings.impact: Conflates test resilience with accessibility conformance.
findings.fix: Say user-facing locators often improve resilience and provide accessibility feedback, but do not replace accessibility testing.
findings.attack: Role locators often improve resilience but do not prove accessibility; accessible names can also change.
findings.defense: The mnemonic encourages user-facing selectors.

findings.title: Learner may reject a better explicit test contract because it appears lower in a rigid ranking.
findings.evidence: A universal role→label→testid→text→CSS order is prescribed.
findings.impact: Learner may reject a better explicit test contract because it appears lower in a rigid ranking.
findings.fix: Teach two goals: user-visible semantics when behavior matters; explicit test ID when stable product contract is the goal; CSS/XPath last.
findings.attack: Playwright recommends user-facing attributes and explicit contracts; test IDs may be the most resilient even though they are not user-facing.
findings.defense: A default heuristic reduces novice choice overload.

findings.title: The simplified model becomes technically incorrect at the boundary learners are meant to reason about.
findings.evidence: wait_until uses while waited <= timeout and advances before exit; 500ms timeout reaches fake clock 600ms on never-ready path.
findings.impact: The simplified model becomes technically incorrect at the boundary learners are meant to reason about.
findings.fix: Use deadline-based polling and explicitly distinguish custom business readiness from built-in actionability and web-first assertions.
findings.attack: The simulation misrepresents timeout boundaries and models only one predicate, not Playwright actionability/auto-retrying assertions.
findings.defense: It is intended as a simplified polling analogy.

findings.title: Teaches a display identifier as though it were the integrity value.
findings.evidence: Theory truncates SHA-256 to 12 hex characters for a verification artifact.
findings.impact: Teaches a display identifier as though it were the integrity value.
findings.fix: Store full SHA-256; optionally display a short prefix separately.
findings.attack: A display prefix can be convenient, but a verification/provenance identity should retain the full digest.
findings.defense: The fixture is synthetic and small.

findings.title: A novice can leave without seeing what a Playwright Page Object actually encapsulates.
findings.evidence: The Page Object example wraps a dict auth state but contains no Playwright Page or locator to centralize.
findings.impact: A novice can leave without seeing what a Playwright Page Object actually encapsulates.
findings.fix: Add a minimal real PO wrapping Page and locators while retaining the dict model as a conceptual precursor.
findings.attack: It does not demonstrate the maintenance benefit described in the paragraph.
findings.defense: The lab intentionally models behavior without Chromium.

findings.title: Learner receives conflicting instructions about diagnostic packaging.
findings.evidence: Prose says filter console logs by ERR; code stores console[-3:] unfiltered.
findings.impact: Learner receives conflicting instructions about diagnostic packaging.
findings.fix: Implement structured severity filtering while preserving a bounded context window around the error.
findings.attack: The claimed signal-to-noise policy is not implemented.
findings.defense: The sample list is only three messages.

findings.title: Turns a preference into a universal architectural mandate.
findings.evidence: Callout says every RPA flow should have a ticket to replace it with API when an API exists.
findings.impact: Turns a preference into a universal architectural mandate.
findings.fix: Create a replacement ticket only when an API/export path is demonstrably equivalent and allowed.
findings.attack: An API may exist but not expose equivalent or authorized functionality.
findings.defense: It pushes teams toward lower-fragility integrations.

findings.title: Extraneous cognitive load obscures the actual control logic.
findings.evidence: Dense unexplained or weakly glossed terms include locator, testid, layout, readiness, step, storage_state, Page Object, trace, on-call, flake, runner, stale, checkpoint, runbook, fallback, ToS and handoff.
findings.impact: Extraneous cognitive load obscures the actual control logic.
findings.fix: Introduce Spanish concept first with the API term in parentheses, then use a consistent vocabulary.
findings.attack: ZERO_TECH learners must infer many operational concepts from English jargon rather than content.
findings.defense: API identifiers such as get_by_role and storage_state must remain literal.

findings.title: The only diagram in the theory increases split attention instead of dual-coding the current subtopic.
findings.evidence: The only theory figure sits under T1-B Auto-waiting y assertions, but its caption centers CAPTCHA/handoff and its alt describes login→form→export→verify with a post-export side-effect boundary.
findings.impact: The only diagram in the theory increases split attention instead of dual-coding the current subtopic.
findings.fix: Move the current recovery diagram to T3-B/T4-B and give T1-B a small actionability/assertion timeline: locator→actionability checks→action→web-first postcondition→timeout evidence.
findings.attack: The visual teaches T3/T4 recovery/idempotence/blocker concepts at the point where the learner is supposed to consolidate actionability and assertions.
findings.defense: The figure does contain a general workflow and can preview later risk boundaries.

findings.title: OCR can begin from a stale, missing, duplicated or wrong source document.
findings.evidence: Reference says the input is 'Una descarga verificada del adaptador web de S23'.
findings.impact: OCR can begin from a stale, missing, duplicated or wrong source document.
findings.fix: Require a persisted source file with full SHA-256, size/type/content validation, browser_run_id and uniqueness/currentness evidence before S24 intake.
findings.attack: S23's real sketch returns a temporary download path after context close and its verification/hash contract remains unearned.
findings.defense: Curricular continuity needs a source artifact from S23.

findings.title: Learner can satisfy the apparent OCR gate without demonstrating OCR acquisition, page rendering or engine output at all.
findings.evidence: Canonical theory operates on metadata dicts and pre-supplied OCR tokens; no theory block sends a synthetic image/PDF through an OCR engine.
findings.impact: Learner can satisfy the apparent OCR gate without demonstrating OCR acquisition, page rendering or engine output at all.
findings.fix: Retain fake unit tests but add at least one tiny synthetic image/PDF fixture executed through a real/local OCR adapter or controlled deterministic OCR fixture that starts from pixels.
findings.attack: Roadmap gate says extract fields from synthetic documents, not merely parse observations invented before the function is called.
findings.defense: Fake adapters are appropriate for deterministic unit tests and are honestly labeled.

findings.title: Downstream gates can treat a 96-PPI source as if it met the 200 threshold.
findings.evidence: preprocess_meta sets out['dpi']=max(source_dpi,200), so a 96-dpi source becomes dpi=200 without any raster operation.
findings.impact: Downstream gates can treat a 96-PPI source as if it met the 200 threshold.
findings.fix: Keep source_ppi immutable; record target_ppi/resample_planned separately. Never use a synthetic 'dpi' overwrite as evidence that capture quality improved.
findings.attack: The prose correctly says upscaling does not recover detail; changing the metadata field creates an even stronger false claim because no pixels changed at all.
findings.defense: Comments call this a planned metadata decision rather than OpenCV processing.

findings.title: Audit flags can say the image was transformed when nothing happened to it.
findings.evidence: deskew_applied=True, skew_deg=0.0, crop_box and contrast are emitted although no raster is deskewed/cropped/contrasted.
findings.impact: Audit flags can say the image was transformed when nothing happened to it.
findings.fix: Rename to *_required/*_planned in metadata-only exercises; only write *_applied after a real transform and bind it to a processed-image hash.
findings.attack: Names such as '*_applied' assert completed transformations, not plans.
findings.defense: Comments disclose the simulation.

findings.title: A real adaptation of the example can delete edge evidence while reporting a successful preprocess.
findings.evidence: Every image gets a fixed 2% crop while the callout requires that crop not cut a seal/total.
findings.impact: A real adaptation of the example can delete edge evidence while reporting a successful preprocess.
findings.fix: Make crop candidate-driven, verify content/bounds against the source, preserve pre/post previews or transform metadata, and fail to manual crop when uncertain.
findings.attack: No content-preservation check proves the 2% border is safe for a particular page.
findings.defense: The fixture is synthetic and the crop is explicitly didactic.

findings.title: The executable contract does not implement the quality gate it teaches.
findings.evidence: fix_orientation returns max score unconditionally; the <0.5 manual_orient rule appears only in prose/callout, and ties are not handled.
findings.impact: The executable contract does not implement the quality gate it teaches.
findings.fix: Return status auto/manual; require minimum score plus ambiguity margin; ties/near-ties -> manual_orient.
findings.attack: Runtime returns (0,0.4) for a low-confidence case and silently chooses the first orientation on an equal-score tie.
findings.defense: The function returns the score so a caller could decide.

findings.title: Without an explicit adapter boundary, low-confidence real OCR can be autoaccepted by two orders of magnitude.
findings.evidence: Course contract and threshold use confidence 0-1; opening callout allows TesseractAdapter when installed.
findings.impact: Without an explicit adapter boundary, low-confidence real OCR can be autoaccepted by two orders of magnitude.
findings.fix: Define adapter_confidence_01 = clamp(raw_conf/100) for Tesseract and test 55 -> 0.55; log engine/raw scale/normalized value.
findings.attack: Tesseract ResultIterator::Confidence is documented on 0-100. A raw 55 would pass conf>=0.85 unless explicitly divided by 100.
findings.defense: A well-written adapter could normalize the engine value.

findings.title: The central evidence rectangle can point to the wrong region.
findings.evidence: The course promises bbox lets a reviewer highlight the value on the original, while preprocessing includes crop, deskew and rotation.
findings.impact: The central evidence rectangle can point to the wrong region.
findings.fix: Persist page index, coordinate space, processed dimensions, source/processed hashes and transform matrix; review against the exact rendition that produced the bbox or invert the transform.
findings.attack: Those transforms change coordinates. bbox on the processed page cannot be overlaid on the original without transform lineage or the exact processed rendition.
findings.defense: T4-B later mentions page dimensions and a revisable rendition conceptually.

findings.title: A reviewer cannot reproduce which bytes/config produced a field.
findings.evidence: Canonical field output names source_doc_id/schema_version but code never binds fields to full source hash, processed page hash, engine/version, language/config or preprocessing version.
findings.impact: A reviewer cannot reproduce which bytes/config produced a field.
findings.fix: Emit source_sha256, page, processed_sha256, preprocess_config/version, OCR engine/model/version/lang, schema_version and field bbox/confidence with each run.
findings.attack: The job relevance promises auditable evidence and reproducibility.
findings.defense: The section is contract-first and some metadata is described in prose.

findings.title: Ambiguous OCR evidence can be silently collapsed into one authoritative-looking field.
findings.evidence: kv_from_lines returns only {key:value}; it drops bbox/confidence and duplicate keys overwrite silently.
findings.impact: Ambiguous OCR evidence can be silently collapsed into one authoritative-looking field.
findings.fix: Return a list/candidates per key with value, conf, bbox, page/source; duplicate competing values -> ambiguity reason/review.
findings.attack: The adjacent paragraph/callout says evidence is value+bbox+conf; runtime duplicate RUC keeps only the last value.
findings.defense: The code is a minimal string parsing exercise.

findings.title: S24 regresses the curriculum's own monetary contract at the document-intake boundary.
findings.evidence: Schema declares total float; line sums and 0.01 reconciliation use binary floats.
findings.impact: S24 regresses the curriculum's own monetary contract at the document-intake boundary.
findings.fix: Normalize monetary strings directly into Decimal from string (or integer cents), quantize explicitly and reconcile using the same type.
findings.attack: S02 established Decimal/integer-cent semantics for PEN, and Python Decimal docs specifically recommend exact decimal arithmetic for accounting invariants.
findings.defense: The lab values shown happen to be exactly simple enough to print cleanly.

findings.title: A syntactically plausible but wrong monetary value can autoenter cross-field validation.
findings.evidence: Prose says EN-thousands '1,150.00' must be rejected/out-of-policy, but norm_total treats any comma+dot as PE and returns 1.15.
findings.impact: A syntactically plausible but wrong monetary value can autoenter cross-field validation.
findings.fix: Validate an explicit regex/grammar before conversion; reject unsupported mixed separators/scientific notation instead of guessing.
findings.attack: Runtime confirms the exact prohibited format is silently transformed into the wrong amount; scientific notation '1e3' is also accepted despite not being documented.
findings.defense: The fixture examples are limited to PE notation.

findings.title: Unexpected OCR corruption can be converted into an invented identity-like identifier.
findings.evidence: norm_ruc rejects only [A-Za-z] then removes every remaining non-digit with \D.
findings.impact: Unexpected OCR corruption can be converted into an invented identity-like identifier.
findings.fix: Allowlist only documented benign separators; any other Unicode letter/symbol/control character -> None/review. Preserve raw value alongside normalized.
findings.attack: Runtime shows Ñ, emoji and unsupported separators can be silently deleted, producing a plausible 11-digit RUC despite the prose 'una letra -> None'.
findings.defense: Common ASCII OCR confusions are caught.

findings.title: Changing the schema does not change the validator; the advertised versioned contract is decorative.
findings.evidence: SCHEMA is {'ruc':'str11','total':'float','fecha':'date'} but is never used to drive validation and does not encode requiredness despite prose saying schema defines required fields.
findings.impact: Changing the schema does not change the validator; the advertised versioned contract is decorative.
findings.fix: Represent required/type/normalizer/rules in one schema object and have extraction/validation consume that exact version.
findings.attack: schema_version is manually printed while behavior is hardcoded elsewhere.
findings.defense: Pure normalization functions make concepts easy to learn.

findings.title: A common OCR omission can crash processing instead of entering human review.
findings.evidence: validate accesses doc['total']; a missing total raises KeyError.
findings.impact: A common OCR omission can crash processing instead of entering human review.
findings.fix: Validate presence/types before arithmetic; missing total -> total_missing reason and needs_review; never perform subtraction on absent/invalid values.
findings.attack: Theory says missing/low-quality docs accumulate reasons and one bad doc must not stop the batch.
findings.defense: The happy-path fixture always includes total.

findings.title: The field-by-field abstention policy is not actually field-by-field.
findings.evidence: T2 identifies RUC and total as critical, but validate checks only conf_ruc and ignores total/fecha confidence and fecha validity.
findings.impact: The field-by-field abstention policy is not actually field-by-field.
findings.fix: Drive confidence/required checks from schema for every critical field and distinguish missing confidence from low confidence.
findings.attack: A low-confidence total can auto-pass if the arithmetic happens to match the same OCR-derived lines.
findings.defense: RUC is used as the focused didactic example.

findings.title: The reviewer cannot perform the evidence check the narrative describes.
findings.evidence: validate returns ('needs_review', reasons) but no queue item contains source, page, bbox, raw/normalized values or review state.
findings.impact: The reviewer cannot perform the evidence check the narrative describes.
findings.fix: Create a persisted/synthetic queue record with run/doc/page/field/raw/value/conf/bbox/reasons/status and reviewer decision fields.
findings.attack: Roadmap T3 and job relevance explicitly promise a human review queue as the product.
findings.defense: A status tuple can illustrate routing logic.

findings.title: Accuracy can be inflated by jointly missing fields and the evaluation crashes on an empty slice.
findings.evidence: field_acc uses raw equality pred==true and divides by len(rows).
findings.impact: Accuracy can be inflated by jointly missing fields and the evaluation crashes on an empty slice.
findings.fix: Define eligible labeled denominator, extraction/missing rates and conditional exact-match separately; return NA/not_evaluable for n=0.
findings.attack: None==None is counted correct; an empty golden raises ZeroDivisionError. Missing ground truth/prediction need explicit scoring policy.
findings.defense: Current fixture contains complete labels.

findings.title: Dashboard can report 0.7 when end-to-end intake auto coverage is 0.35 for the same 7 auto,3 review,5 reject,5 fail population.
findings.evidence: coverage_auto = auto/(auto+review), while T4-B introduces reject and OCR-failure/fallback outcomes.
findings.impact: Dashboard can report 0.7 when end-to-end intake auto coverage is 0.35 for the same 7 auto,3 review,5 reject,5 fail population.
findings.fix: Name denominators explicitly: admitted_selective_coverage and end_to_end_auto_rate; report reject/fail/rescan separately.
findings.attack: Rejects/ocr_fail disappear from the denominator, making end-to-end automation coverage look better than intake reality.
findings.defense: The formula may mean coverage among admitted/extracted documents only.

findings.title: The central abstention trade-off is described but not measured.
findings.evidence: field accuracy is computed on a 2-doc golden while coverage_auto uses unrelated hardcoded 7/3 counts.
findings.impact: The central abstention trade-off is described but not measured.
findings.fix: On one golden set, apply threshold t, compute coverage(t), error/accuracy on autoaccepted critical fields, review rate and threshold curves/slices.
findings.attack: You cannot judge whether a confidence threshold improves safe automation when accuracy and coverage are not computed from the same predictions/threshold.
findings.defense: The paragraph says they are different metrics and the tiny numbers are pedagogical.

findings.title: Malformed intake metadata can stop the worker before the advertised fallback/review routing.
findings.evidence: gate_file directly indexes meta['mime'] and meta['n_bytes'].
findings.impact: Malformed intake metadata can stop the worker before the advertised fallback/review routing.
findings.fix: Validate metadata schema first; absent/invalid fields -> reject/review with explicit reason and continue batch.
findings.attack: Missing/malformed metadata raises KeyError rather than a controlled reject/review reason.
findings.defense: Fixtures always provide both fields.

findings.title: The learner never demonstrates the terminal state that is supposed to prevent retry loops on corrupt documents.
findings.evidence: Learning outcome and T4-B prose promise ocr_fail -> human_rescan, but hostile_gate.py has no OCR failure path or rescan record.
findings.impact: The learner never demonstrates the terminal state that is supposed to prevent retry loops on corrupt documents.
findings.fix: Add an OCR result/error router with bounded retry for transient engine faults and human_rescan for deterministic/corrupt input, preserving reason/evidence.
findings.attack: The fallback is a major T4 ownership item, not a footnote.
findings.defense: gate_file runs before OCR, so failure may occur later.

findings.title: A privacy instruction can destroy the evidence required for HITL/audit.
findings.evidence: T4-B paragraph says bbox needs a controlled revisable rendition; callout says 'Borra imágenes crudas cuando el expediente solo necesita campos + bbox'.
findings.impact: A privacy instruction can destroy the evidence required for HITL/audit.
findings.fix: Define retention classes explicitly: keep the exact review rendition under access control until decision/retention expiry; delete redundant raw copies only after evidence lineage remains usable.
findings.attack: If that raw/processed image is the only review rendition, deleting it makes bbox evidence unusable.
findings.defense: The paragraph itself asks for a controlled review copy and expiry.

findings.title: Learner can generalize OCR as the default path for every PDF.
findings.evidence: Theory begins from a scanned-image model and provides no native-text bypass for digitally-born PDFs.
findings.impact: Learner can generalize OCR as the default path for every PDF.
findings.fix: Add a routing gate: native digital text -> text extraction; raster/image or unusable text layer -> OCR; preserve the chosen mode in provenance.
findings.attack: S21 already distinguishes digital PDFs from image/OCR cases; OCRing a native text PDF needlessly discards stronger information.
findings.defense: The opening explicitly talks about an 'factura escaneada' and S24 is the OCR-focused section.

findings.title: Quality gates become arbitrary rather than evidence-based.
findings.evidence: Prose recommends capture at >=300 PPI effective, while code/callout make >=200 the passing lab floor.
findings.impact: Quality gates become arbitrary rather than evidence-based.
findings.fix: State explicitly: 200 is a didactic warning floor only; 300 is the preferred capture target; calibrate by font size/corpus and actual OCR evaluation.
findings.attack: The learner is given two different minima with no rationale for when 200 is sufficient.
findings.defense: Tesseract documentation says ~300 is generally beneficial, not a universal hard failure threshold; a 200 lab floor can be a deliberate simplification.

findings.title: Outcome wording exceeds demonstrated competence.
findings.evidence: Learning outcome says correct noise before OCR; denoise_binary merely flips synthetic 1 flags to 0 and never modifies image data.
findings.impact: Outcome wording exceeds demonstrated competence.
findings.fix: Either narrow the outcome to choosing/logging a denoise policy or add one real image-processing example and compare before/after OCR quality.
findings.attack: The student does not learn or demonstrate a denoise operation.
findings.defense: The function explicitly says it is a contract simulation.

findings.title: The limitation is stated but the simple algorithm is presented as 'orden de lectura'.
findings.evidence: T2-A sorts tokens by (y0,x0) while warning not to concatenate columns blindly.
findings.impact: The limitation is stated but the simple algorithm is presented as 'orden de lectura'.
findings.fix: Name it single-column-only; add a two-column counterexample that must abstain or route to a layout-aware adapter.
findings.attack: Global y/x sorting is exactly the kind of heuristic that can interleave multi-column content.
findings.defense: Advanced multi-column layout is declared out of scope.

findings.title: Learner may mistake a convenient cutoff for a calibrated probability of correctness.
findings.evidence: Token confidences are treated as field confidences with one universal 0.85 threshold.
findings.impact: Learner may mistake a convenient cutoff for a calibrated probability of correctness.
findings.fix: Define token->field aggregation and evaluate threshold curves on the same golden set; keep 0.85 visibly didactic.
findings.attack: Fields may span multiple tokens and confidence meaning differs by engine/entity level; threshold quality should be evaluated per field/corpus.
findings.defense: 0.85 is explicitly labeled a didactic lab threshold.

findings.title: Learner sees a throughput guarantee not demonstrated at this layer.
findings.evidence: Theory says one needs_review document should not stop the nightly batch, but no theory code iterates documents or isolates per-document failures.
findings.impact: Learner sees a throughput guarantee not demonstrated at this layer.
findings.fix: Add a tiny three-document fixture: ok/review/parser-error; prove all records yield terminal intake states without losing later documents.
findings.attack: The code even has KeyError paths that could terminate a batch.
findings.defense: Batch orchestration may be deferred to S26.

findings.title: A novice may confuse formula demonstration with evidence sufficient to set an SLO.
findings.evidence: A 2-document golden is discussed next to per-field SLOs without uncertainty/sample counts beyond n implicit in code.
findings.impact: A novice may confuse formula demonstration with evidence sufficient to set an SLO.
findings.fix: Separate 'toy calculation' from 'gate dataset'; always report n and uncertainty/error slices before promoting an SLO claim.
findings.attack: Two examples cannot support a reliability commitment.
findings.defense: It is explicitly a tiny synthetic teaching set, not a production benchmark.

findings.title: The heading/outcome can still be read as stronger protection than the executable code provides.
findings.evidence: Heading says hostile files, but implemented gate is only caller-provided MIME + compressed byte size; prose acknowledges this as layer 1.
findings.impact: The heading/outcome can still be read as stronger protection than the executable code provides.
findings.fix: Call it 'layer-1 admission screen'; add at least a magic-signature negative fixture and resource/page/time budget concept, with deeper parsing explicitly deferred.
findings.attack: Small malicious PDFs/images or spoofed MIME can still reach vulnerable parsers; file size alone does not bound page/content-stream/decompression work.
findings.defense: The section explicitly says signatures/isolated parsing/sandbox are production layer 2, so it does not fully claim security.

findings.title: The S24->S25 handoff lacks a simple trust-boundary label.
findings.evidence: Extracted OCR text is normalized as data but never marked untrusted before the next S25 LLM/prompting section.
findings.impact: The S24->S25 handoff lacks a simple trust-boundary label.
findings.fix: Mark source/OCR text as untrusted_document_content and require downstream prompt/template separation; leave detailed prompt-injection defenses to S25.
findings.attack: Hostile documents can contain instructions/markup that should remain data, not control text for downstream models.
findings.defense: Prompt injection is explicitly owned by S25.

findings.title: Language switching adds extraneous cognitive load to an already high-load document pipeline.
findings.evidence: Dense terms include intake, bbox, confidence, schema, cross-field, golden, coverage_auto, HITL, fallback, deskew, crop, layout, adapter and runbook.
findings.impact: Language switching adds extraneous cognitive load to an already high-load document pipeline.
findings.fix: Introduce Spanish first plus literal term once: admisión (intake), caja delimitadora (bbox), confianza, esquema, validación entre campos, conjunto de referencia (golden), cobertura automática, revisión humana, alternativa/fallback.
findings.attack: Many are introduced in English before a stable Spanish mental model, despite ZERO_TECH entry assumptions.
findings.defense: Literal API/data-contract names must remain recognizable to practitioners.

findings.title: A model can amplify an upstream false-green field into a persuasive narrative/classification.
findings.evidence: Opening treats S24 extracted fields as available inputs for model judgment.
findings.impact: A model can amplify an upstream false-green field into a persuasive narrative/classification.
findings.fix: Require a validated S24 handoff record with source hash, raw+normalized values, confidence scale/version and review state; otherwise route human.
findings.attack: S24 remains REPAIR_REQUIRED: provenance, bbox lineage, monetary semantics, confidence normalization and review completion are not creditable.
findings.defense: Curriculum continuity requires consuming prior artifacts.

findings.title: A learner can satisfy theory without demonstrating endpoint invocation, serialization, HTTP errors, provider auth or actual model output nor…
findings.evidence: All executable theory inference is a keyword mock or deterministic dict builder; real transformers/HTTP calls are comments/reference only.
findings.impact: A learner can satisfy theory without demonstrating endpoint invocation, serialization, HTTP errors, provider auth or actual model output normalization.
findings.fix: Keep mocks, but add one controlled real/local transformers adapter or approved HTTP test double that exercises the same contract end-to-end.
findings.attack: Roadmap/title promise Hugging Face pipelines/endpoints and a classifier/extractor plus narrative generator.
findings.defense: Mocks make the lesson reproducible without downloading weights or requiring network access.

findings.title: The most important nouns in the gate are simulated away, so model-specific failure modes never appear.
findings.evidence: hf_mock is a keyword rule classifier and prompt_struct.build_output is a normal Python dict constructor; there is no specialized extractor and no model-generated narrative.
findings.impact: The most important nouns in the gate are simulated away, so model-specific failure modes never appear.
findings.fix: Demonstrate at least one actual specialized model output and one model-generated structured narrative on synthetic data, both behind deterministic contract tests.
findings.attack: Tagline/gate claim specialized classifier/extractor and narrative generator.
findings.defense: The lesson intentionally focuses on contracts rather than weights.

findings.title: Architecture can be locked in before evidence shows it adds value.
findings.evidence: choose_stack selects rules/specialized/LLM from task flags before any quality, latency, privacy, cost or baseline measurement.
findings.impact: Architecture can be locked in before evidence shows it adds value.
findings.fix: Use the tree only to generate candidates; final choice must compare candidates on the same fixed eval set plus operational/governance constraints.
findings.attack: The section's own promotion contract requires eval vs baseline, yet stack selection is rule-of-thumb only.
findings.defense: T4 evaluates later.

findings.title: A governance check can be skipped while deployment still returns a positive choice.
findings.evidence: deploy_choice only checks has_pii_live and a two-license allowlist; intended/not_for is explicitly delegated to the caller.
findings.impact: A governance check can be skipped while deployment still returns a positive choice.
findings.fix: Create one fail-closed deployment policy that combines intended/out-of-scope use, license/legal review, data class, provider approval, residency/retention and network/auth controls.
findings.attack: The same prohibited-use card can return cloud_or_local; policy safety depends on another caller remembering an unstated composition order.
findings.defense: The comment says the caller applies blocked_use separately.

findings.title: Golden results and cached outputs cannot be bound to exact model artifacts/configuration.
findings.evidence: Prose promises model/card version metadata; executable adapters emit only model='demo-cls' or model='demo' and no revision/card hash/config.
findings.impact: Golden results and cached outputs cannot be bound to exact model artifacts/configuration.
findings.fix: Persist model repository/id + immutable revision/hash, task/config, tokenizer/prompt/schema versions and card source hash.
findings.attack: A mutable model id cannot reproduce a past classification or cache entry.
findings.defense: Synthetic fixture ids are stable within one code sample.

findings.title: The primary inference path can consume document directives before the promised security gate is demonstrated.
findings.evidence: T2-A says injection indications go human_review, but classifier adapter accepts arbitrary texts without a trust marker or injection/risk route.
findings.impact: The primary inference path can consume document directives before the promised security gate is demonstrated.
findings.fix: Carry trust/source metadata through every adapter and centralize the policy route before any model/tool-capable path.
findings.attack: S24 OCR is explicitly untrusted_document_content from the carry-forward contract.
findings.defense: Detailed injection controls appear in T4-B.

findings.title: A model/config update can reuse stale output as if current.
findings.evidence: cache key is sha256(model|text)[:12].
findings.impact: A model/config update can reuse stale output as if current.
findings.fix: Hash the complete canonical inference identity with full SHA-256; use a short prefix only for display.
findings.attack: It omits immutable model revision, task/config, prompt/schema/tokenizer version and policy; truncation also weakens collision margin.
findings.defense: For a tiny synthetic pure classifier, model+text often determines output.

findings.title: One endpoint/model can permanently disable all inference in-process and there is no recovery probe or observable alert.
findings.evidence: One global failures counter opens after 3 and never transitions half-open/closed; no timer, endpoint key or alert is implemented.
findings.impact: One endpoint/model can permanently disable all inference in-process and there is no recovery probe or observable alert.
findings.fix: Scope breaker by dependency, add closed/open/half_open state with cooldown/recovery probe and emit an alert/event when state changes.
findings.attack: Runtime probe shows even a later healthy-looking call returns circuit=open forever.
findings.defense: The heading explicitly says circuit breaker simple.

findings.title: Downstream code can mistake a routing hint for handled work.
