findings.evidence: Open circuit returns {'fallback':'rules_or_human'} but executes neither a rule nor a human-review enqueue.
findings.impact: Downstream code can mistake a routing hint for handled work.
findings.fix: Return a typed routing decision consumed by an actual deterministic fallback or persisted review item; never present it as completed inference.
findings.attack: A label is not a fallback path.
findings.defense: The example is intended to teach routing semantics.

findings.title: An output can satisfy the displayed prompt while violating the section's authoritative narrative contract and tagline evidence requirement.
findings.evidence: Reference contract requires hallazgo,n,mediana,evidence_ids,model; T3-A outputs hallazgo,n,mediana,limite.
findings.impact: An output can satisfy the displayed prompt while violating the section's authoritative narrative contract and tagline evidence requirement.
findings.fix: Use one versioned narrative schema everywhere; include evidence_ids/model and optional limitations as an additional validated field.
findings.attack: The canonical prompting example omits both evidence linkage and model identity.
findings.defense: limite demonstrates a useful limitation field.

findings.title: The canonical example normalizes exactly the unsupported factual addition the section says to reject.
findings.evidence: PROMPT context contains 'mediana Lima=28 n=40' but generated example says 'Mediana Lima 28 PEN'.
findings.impact: The canonical example normalizes exactly the unsupported factual addition the section says to reject.
findings.fix: Include unit=PEN in the trusted context/evidence or remove PEN from hallazgo; add a grounding validator against supplied fields.
findings.attack: PEN is absent from the supplied context, directly violating 'no inventes'.
findings.defense: Earlier reporting sections often use PEN.

findings.title: The AI layer reintroduces floating-point monetary semantics into evidence/reporting.
findings.evidence: Narrative fixture uses mediana=28.0 and hallazgo='28 PEN'.
findings.impact: The AI layer reintroduces floating-point monetary semantics into evidence/reporting.
findings.fix: Pass canonical monetary values as Decimal/string minor-unit representations and format for display separately.
findings.attack: S02 established Decimal/integer-cent semantics for money; S24 monetary float was explicitly not creditable.
findings.defense: This is display-only synthetic data.

findings.title: Type-invalid, out-of-domain or unexpected-property output can be called schema-valid.
findings.evidence: schema_ok and T3-A validation require key presence only; runtime accepts {'h':123,'n':'one'}.
findings.impact: Type-invalid, out-of-domain or unexpected-property output can be called schema-valid.
findings.fix: Keep the key-presence exercise as first layer, then validate types, enums/ranges, required evidence ids and additional-properties policy with a real schema validator or equivalent code.
findings.attack: The gate says JSON validado and the contracts specify typed semantic fields.
findings.defense: The prose explicitly calls this a minimum gate rather than full JSON Schema.

findings.title: A fluent but fabricated value/reference can pass schema validation and golden plumbing.
findings.evidence: No code verifies hallazgo/n/mediana against trusted S24/S21 values or checks that evidence_ids exist.
findings.impact: A fluent but fabricated value/reference can pass schema validation and golden plumbing.
findings.fix: Validate every evidence id against the run's evidence registry and compare derived numeric claims to canonical values/units before human review.
findings.attack: S25 repeatedly promises no output without evidence, but structural JSON alone does not prove grounding.
findings.defense: T4 prose says evidence_ids should exist in the OCR fixture.

findings.title: The learner can mistake name allowlisting for least privilege/action authorization.
findings.evidence: Tool policy checks only step['name']; arguments, resource scope, side-effect class and original user intent are absent, and allowed tools are logged ok=True without execution.
findings.impact: The learner can mistake name allowlisting for least privilege/action authorization.
findings.fix: Validate tool name + typed args + resource/tenant + side-effect policy + approval requirement, execute through a sandboxed adapter, then validate result.
findings.attack: Allowlisted function names can still perform unsafe actions with malicious arguments.
findings.defense: The lab focuses on the first allowlist concept.

findings.title: Successful tool status is fabricated and the highest-risk boundary—validating tool output before narration—is absent.
findings.evidence: Prose promises plan→tool→validar→narrar; code implements think/tool/deny only and hardcodes ok=True.
findings.impact: Successful tool status is fabricated and the highest-risk boundary—validating tool output before narration—is absent.
findings.fix: Model explicit plan, authorization, execution, result validation and narrative stages with typed statuses/evidence.
findings.attack: No validation or narration checkpoint exists.
findings.defense: It demonstrates stop-on-denial.

findings.title: Field accuracy can be inflated by absence rather than correct prediction.
findings.evidence: field_match_rate uses pred.get(k)==gold.get(k) across union keys.
findings.impact: Field accuracy can be inflated by absence rather than correct prediction.
findings.fix: Compare key presence separately from value equality; a missing key must be a miss unless the schema explicitly defines omission as the gold representation.
findings.attack: Runtime: field_match_rate({}, {'x':None}) == 1.0, so a missing prediction is counted correct when gold is null.
findings.defense: Using union avoids KeyError for missing keys.

findings.title: There is no executable evidence that the AI improves over a simpler alternative or that prompt iterations use the same test set.
findings.evidence: T4-A code evaluates only model predictions; no baseline rows, model revision, fixed eval-set id or promotion rule are present.
findings.impact: There is no executable evidence that the AI improves over a simpler alternative or that prompt iterations use the same test set.
findings.fix: Evaluate candidate and baseline on the identical versioned golden set, persist metrics/cost/latency/safety, and define a fail-closed promotion rule.
findings.attack: Tagline/callout explicitly say no acceptance without eval vs baseline, and the figure says cases must not change between rounds.
findings.defense: The prose names rules/model anterior as baseline.

findings.title: S25 can claim outputs are reviewed without evidence a human ever saw them.
findings.evidence: human_review/HITL appears as strings/booleans; no persisted review item, reviewer, timestamp, decision or corrected output exists.
findings.impact: S25 can claim outputs are reviewed without evidence a human ever saw them.
findings.fix: At minimum emit a review record schema and require an explicit reviewed decision before downstream report/email use.
findings.attack: A routing label does not demonstrate human review.
findings.defense: S26 later orchestrates HITL more fully.

findings.title: The executable example demonstrates detection without enforcement and can normalize 'flagged but still sent' behavior.
findings.evidence: injection_signal(doc) is True for the canonical malicious document, but build_request(doc) is still called and contains the same untrusted document.
findings.impact: The executable example demonstrates detection without enforcement and can normalize 'flagged but still sent' behavior.
findings.fix: Make policy routing explicit: signal may raise review/deny, while defense-in-depth still treats undetected content as untrusted and constrains outputs/actions.
findings.attack: The section rule says injection indications derive to human_review.
findings.defense: The text correctly says regex is telemetry, not the real control.

findings.title: Learner can confuse metadata with enforcement.
findings.evidence: build_request sets requires_human_approval=True but no controller consumes it; system/untrusted_document are custom dict fields rather than a demonstrated provider role/action boundary.
findings.impact: Learner can confuse metadata with enforcement.
findings.fix: Separate generation from action execution and enforce approval in the action gateway using a persisted reviewer decision bound to exact output/action.
findings.attack: A boolean declaration does not block an external action.
findings.defense: The request object is a policy contract rather than a send action.

findings.title: Learner can treat sample count as scientific selection criterion instead of a toy lab heuristic.
findings.evidence: choose_stack hardcodes specialized_model when n_train >= 500.
findings.impact: Learner can treat sample count as scientific selection criterion instead of a toy lab heuristic.
findings.fix: Label 500 explicitly as a fixture value and make measured validation vs baseline the actual selection gate.
findings.attack: No universal 500-example threshold determines whether a specialized model is appropriate; task difficulty, class balance, label quality, baseline and model family matter.
findings.defense: A simple threshold reduces novice decision complexity.

findings.title: Learner may expect machine-readable fields that many real cards do not provide.
findings.evidence: Prose/code treat card['not_for'] as though it were a universal structured model-card field.
findings.impact: Learner may expect machine-readable fields that many real cards do not provide.
findings.fix: State that not_for is the course's normalized governance field extracted from Out-of-Scope Use/limitations, and preserve source evidence.
findings.attack: Hugging Face model cards are Markdown+metadata; out-of-scope/misuse information is documented content and not guaranteed as a normalized not_for key.
findings.defense: The lab can normalize documentation into a local governance record.

findings.title: An endpoint with malformed score/unknown label can pass downstream until later logic breaks.
findings.evidence: Classifier contract checks are described as keys/types, but hf_mock simply returns dicts; no validator enforces label enum, score numeric/range, cardinality or model revision.
findings.impact: An endpoint with malformed score/unknown label can pass downstream until later logic breaks.
findings.fix: Implement an explicit adapter validator for list cardinality, types, label domain, finite score range and immutable model metadata.
findings.attack: Same shape does not guarantee semantically compatible adapters.
findings.defense: The mock illustrates the base label/score shape documented by HF.

findings.title: Learner does not practice batch sizing, provider response cardinality, timeout configuration or client-specific timeout exceptions.
findings.evidence: Outcome promises batching and timeout operation; code loops a list in a mock and simulates timeout with fail=True rather than configuring a client/request timeout or batch policy.
findings.impact: Learner does not practice batch sizing, provider response cardinality, timeout configuration or client-specific timeout exceptions.
findings.fix: Add controlled batch and HTTP-client test-double cases for partial/malformed batch responses and configured timeout exceptions.
findings.attack: Operational behavior is asserted but not exercised.
findings.defense: Network-independent simulation is deliberate.

findings.title: Learner may treat an arbitrary character formula as a cloud cost estimate.
findings.evidence: cost=COST_PER_1K*len(text)/1000 while prose says tokens or requests; no currency/provider/pricing version is recorded.
findings.impact: Learner may treat an arbitrary character formula as a cloud cost estimate.
findings.fix: Declare the unit explicitly; for token pricing use the actual tokenizer/usage response, and version provider/model/currency/pricing date.
findings.attack: Characters are not tokens and per-request pricing is a different unit.
findings.defense: It is a toy estimate.

findings.title: Roadmap promises a concrete model-specific capability that learners never see, while source silently changes scope.
findings.evidence: Roadmap T3 explicitly names GLM-5.2 thinking/tools/checkpoints; canonical S25 deliberately removes product-specific treatment and never mentions GLM-5.2.
findings.impact: Roadmap promises a concrete model-specific capability that learners never see, while source silently changes scope.
findings.fix: Either revise roadmap to generic provider-neutral reasoning/tools or add a clearly optional GLM-5.2 mapping that remains subordinate to generic safety contracts.
findings.attack: GLM-5.2 is current, so the omission is not justified by obsolescence.
findings.defense: Generic patterns transfer better across providers.

findings.title: Learner may build observability around unavailable/sensitive reasoning text instead of externally verifiable actions.
findings.evidence: run_checkpointed logs {'think': note} as an auditable checkpoint.
findings.impact: Learner may build observability around unavailable/sensitive reasoning text instead of externally verifiable actions.
findings.fix: Rename to plan/rationale summary and never require or persist hidden chain-of-thought.
findings.attack: Hidden chain-of-thought is not a portable API contract and logging private reasoning is unnecessary; auditable systems should log plans, decisions, tool intents/results and policy reasons.
findings.defense: The fixture uses an explicit synthetic note, not an actual provider chain-of-thought.

findings.title: A filtered/no-eligible slice crashes instead of reporting not_evaluable and n=0.
findings.evidence: eval_rows divides by len(rows) with no empty-set contract.
findings.impact: A filtered/no-eligible slice crashes instead of reporting not_evaluable and n=0.
findings.fix: Return a typed not_evaluable result with n, denominators and exclusion reasons.
findings.attack: eval_rows([]) raises ZeroDivisionError.
findings.defense: The shown fixture is nonempty.

findings.title: Future adapters can regress to an autonomous sensitive label without failing the shown tests.
findings.evidence: T4-B says route policy auto_fraud_label=False, but no theory code actually carries or asserts that field.
findings.impact: Future adapters can regress to an autonomous sensitive label without failing the shown tests.
findings.fix: Make prohibited downstream decisions an explicit contract/test and verify no adapter maps model score to fraud adjudication.
findings.attack: A stated policy has no executable regression guard.
findings.defense: Other prose repeatedly says score is not fraud.

findings.title: High code-switching load competes with already difficult model-risk concepts.
findings.evidence: Dense terms include stack, fine-tuned, label set, golden, baseline, adapter, batch, cache, fallback, circuit breaker, schema rate, prompt injection, tools/checkpoints/HITL.
findings.impact: High code-switching load competes with already difficult model-risk concepts.
findings.fix: Introduce Spanish concept first, keep API literals in code, and repeat one stable term thereafter.
findings.attack: Many are introduced in clusters rather than Spanish-first causal explanations.
findings.defense: Several terms receive parenthetical translations.

findings.title: The scarce diagram creates split attention instead of dual-coding the current endpoint contract.
findings.evidence: S25-eval-loop sits under T2-A Pipelines/endpoints, but caption/alt describe prompt→output→evaluate→adjust and fixed evaluation cases.
findings.impact: The scarce diagram creates split attention instead of dual-coding the current endpoint contract.
findings.fix: Move eval-loop to T4-A; give T2-A a diagram raw HF/HTTP response→adapter normalization→contract validation→typed result/human_review.
findings.attack: The figure visually teaches T3/T4 prompt evaluation while learner is studying adapter normalization.
findings.defense: Evaluation continuity is relevant to any adapter.

findings.title: The capstone can promote a run whose source, approval, OCR or AI evidence was never trustworthy.
findings.evidence: Opening/reference and E2E treat prior ingest/report/OCR/AI pieces as working inputs although S21-S25 remain REPAIR_REQUIRED.
findings.impact: The capstone can promote a run whose source, approval, OCR or AI evidence was never trustworthy.
findings.fix: Require a versioned handoff manifest and revalidate every upstream artifact/hash/review state before the DAG can mark a node ready.
findings.attack: Orchestration can launder false-green labels from earlier sections into a final success artifact.
findings.defense: An integrator must compose prior modules.

findings.title: The graph conflates pre-draft business review with final draft approval and loses the safety contract inherited from S22.
findings.evidence: Canonical path is report → approve → draft_email; S22 requires approval bound to exact draft/message/recipients.
findings.impact: The graph conflates pre-draft business review with final draft approval and loses the safety contract inherited from S22.
findings.fix: Model distinct gates: analysis/report/recipient approvals → create draft → final draft/recipient approval bound to draft hash; never treat the first gate as final email approval.
findings.attack: A human cannot approve the exact email draft before that draft exists.
findings.defense: The S26 approve node may intend approval of analysis/report/recipient rather than the final email.

findings.title: Learner receives an unsafe default retry heuristic before idempotency is actually established.
findings.evidence: Opening says an exhausted timeout usually heals itself and deserves retry.
findings.impact: Learner receives an unsafe default retry heuristic before idempotency is actually established.
findings.fix: Classify timeout as outcome-unknown; retry only after idempotency/postcondition verification or for explicitly side-effect-free operations.
findings.attack: A timeout can occur after a side effect committed; blind retry can duplicate exports/drafts/writes.
findings.defense: The paragraph later says steps should be idempotent.

findings.title: The learner can mistake incomplete scheduling for successful DAG validation.
findings.evidence: topo() returns order without checking len(order)==len(nodes).
findings.impact: The learner can mistake incomplete scheduling for successful DAG validation.
findings.fix: After Kahn traversal, raise a typed CycleError unless every node was emitted; add full-cycle and partial-cycle negative fixtures.
findings.attack: A cyclic component is silently omitted; a partially cyclic graph returns a plausible partial order.
findings.defense: A fully cyclic graph returns an empty list and therefore might not start.

findings.title: Outcome 'tasks/flows/DAG con estados' is not demonstrated by theory code.
findings.evidence: Theory promises pending/running/success/failed/skipped, global flow state, timestamp and run_id per node; code only returns node names.
findings.impact: Outcome 'tasks/flows/DAG con estados' is not demonstrated by theory code.
findings.fix: Add a node-state record with allowed transitions, timestamps, run_id, dependency outcome and explicit skipped semantics.
findings.attack: No state transition, timestamp, skip rule, dependency failure or global flow status is executable.
findings.defense: The example focuses narrowly on topological order.

findings.title: run_id cannot reliably join evidence across versions/reprocessing.
findings.evidence: Prose calls run_id, trigger, git_sha and data_cutoff immutable; build_run_meta omits git_sha, hardcodes trigger/manual and returns a mutable dict.
findings.impact: run_id cannot reliably join evidence across versions/reprocessing.
findings.fix: Include git_sha/config/schema/source hashes/trigger/data_cutoff and freeze or hash the canonical run manifest; create a new run on any change.
findings.attack: The object cannot prove code version or immutable start snapshot and can be modified after creation.
findings.defense: It is a didactic metadata sketch.

findings.title: Learner can confuse declaring a limit with enforcing one.
findings.evidence: api_rpm and max_parallel_tasks are dictionary values; prose says api_rpm>60 blocks schedule, but no preflight/limiter exists.
findings.impact: Learner can confuse declaring a limit with enforcing one.
findings.fix: Implement validation plus an actual semaphore/token-bucket/adaptor limit and a negative fixture proving >60 cannot enable the schedule.
findings.attack: build_run_meta('r',100) succeeds and nothing enforces rate/concurrency.
findings.defense: The section may intend configuration before a later runner.

findings.title: A correct warning is not evidence that the gate was met.
findings.evidence: T2-A acknowledges its set dies with the process; the integrated E2E never uses the promised JSON/persistent checkpoint.
findings.impact: A correct warning is not evidence that the gate was met.
findings.fix: Persist checkpoints atomically outside process, kill/restart the runner, and prove already-completed work is not repeated.
findings.attack: The section's failure-recovery promise is not demonstrated across process restart.
findings.defense: The paragraph correctly explains the limitation.

findings.title: The executable behavior contradicts the resiliency mechanism being taught.
findings.evidence: backoff_sleep_ms computes delays, but process_with_dlq never sleeps/uses them and has no jitter.
findings.impact: The executable behavior contradicts the resiliency mechanism being taught.
findings.fix: Inject a sleeper, use capped exponential backoff plus jitter, persist attempt timing and test with deterministic seeded jitter.
findings.attack: The retry loop is immediate despite claiming retry with backoff; synchronized retries can amplify load.
findings.defense: The numeric formula is taught separately.

findings.title: The central decision boundary of retry policy is absent.
findings.evidence: process_with_dlq receives flaky_ids rather than typed provider/data/configuration failures.
findings.impact: The central decision boundary of retry policy is absent.
findings.fix: Classify errors explicitly and route transient/provider errors to bounded retry, permanent data/config errors to review/DLQ without retry.
findings.attack: No code demonstrates 'retry transient, do not retry invalid schema'.
findings.defense: flaky_ids simplifies deterministic labs.

findings.title: Duplicate keys are not idempotency when payload changes silently replace prior state.
findings.evidence: write_report and write_draft assign directly into store[run_id].
findings.impact: Duplicate keys are not idempotency when payload changes silently replace prior state.
findings.fix: Use an atomic create-once record with payload hash/status; same key+same payload returns stored result, same key+different payload fails.
findings.attack: A second call with the same key overwrites the first body; runtime check v1→v2 leaves v2.
findings.defense: A dictionary prevents duplicate keys.

findings.title: The abstraction will not safely generalize to the concurrent/entity-level system it claims to teach.
findings.evidence: Code keys report/draft only by run_id while prose names (run_id, entity_id).
findings.impact: The abstraction will not safely generalize to the concurrent/entity-level system it claims to teach.
findings.fix: Canonical key must include operation + run + entity/artifact + immutable payload/config/schema hash, persisted atomically.
findings.attack: Different entities or artifact versions inside one run collide and payload/config version is not checked.
findings.defense: The lab creates one report per run.

findings.title: Learning outcome 'garantizar concurrencia' is unsupported.
findings.evidence: Prose describes locked flag/lease TTL; theory code contains no lock or concurrent execution.
findings.impact: Learning outcome 'garantizar concurrencia' is unsupported.
findings.fix: Demonstrate atomic acquire/lease/expiry and simultaneous-worker negative test; avoid check-then-set races.
findings.attack: Nothing prevents two workers from passing a check and writing simultaneously.
findings.defense: Concurrency implementation is deferred conceptually to production.

findings.title: The compensation destroys evidence needed for audit/review.
findings.evidence: rollback replaces {'body':body,'status':'active'} with {'status':'superseded'}.
findings.impact: The compensation destroys evidence needed for audit/review.
findings.fix: Preserve immutable artifact/version/body/hash and append a superseded status/event rather than replacing the record.
findings.attack: The original report body disappears although prose explicitly says not to delete it from defense history.
findings.defense: The record key remains.

findings.title: Operational cleanup is confused with audit deletion.
findings.evidence: rollback pop() deletes the draft entirely.
findings.impact: Operational cleanup is confused with audit deletion.
findings.fix: Delete provider-side mutable draft if needed but retain an immutable hashed snapshot/status=canceled in the audit store.
findings.attack: A compensated draft vanishes, preventing reconstruction of what was generated and why it was withdrawn.
findings.defense: Removing an unsent draft can be a valid compensation.

findings.title: The core human gate can fail open under non-happy statuses.
findings.evidence: all_clear is true whenever no item has status='pending'.
findings.impact: The core human gate can fail open under non-happy statuses.
findings.fix: Require exact approved state for the exact required artifact/version in all three queues; every other terminal/intermediate state blocks.
findings.attack: A rejected/error/needs_revision artifact yields pending=0 and can open the gate.
findings.defense: Current fixture contains only pending items.

findings.title: Human review is used as a blanket substitute for machine-contract validation.
findings.evidence: ai_assist is treated as a pipeline node whose output feeds report; S25 audit found ungrounded/schema-invalid outputs and no baseline promotion gate.
findings.impact: Human review is used as a blanket substitute for machine-contract validation.
findings.fix: Before report state can be ready, validate S25 output against immutable model/config/schema/evidence lineage and fail closed on invalid/ungrounded output.
findings.attack: S26 does not revalidate model revision, typed schema, evidence ids or candidate-vs-baseline status before consuming it.
findings.defense: S26 says AI only proposes and human review follows.

findings.title: The audit contract is materially incomplete.
findings.evidence: Prose requires {action,actor,ts,reason?}; act() omits ts.
findings.impact: The audit contract is materially incomplete.
findings.fix: Generate timezone-aware immutable timestamp plus run_id/artifact_version and persist it append-only.
findings.attack: Decision ordering and timing cannot be reconstructed reliably.
findings.defense: List order preserves local call order.

findings.title: Runbook routing cannot rely on reasons being present.
findings.evidence: Callout says reject without reason is rejected at API; act(...,'reject',reason=None) succeeds.
findings.impact: Runbook routing cannot rely on reasons being present.
findings.fix: Validate allowed actions and require nonblank reason/reason_code for reject/edit where policy requires it.
findings.attack: The code contradicts the stated mandatory rejection reason.
findings.defense: No reject call appears in the happy-path example.

findings.title: Approval can refer ambiguously to pre- or post-edit content.
findings.evidence: Prose says edit versions 1→2 without deleting history; act() stores only an action record and no content/version/hash.
findings.impact: Approval can refer ambiguously to pre- or post-edit content.
findings.fix: Store immutable artifact versions; edit creates v+1 with parent hash, and approval names the exact version/hash.
findings.attack: There is no edited artifact version to review or bind approval to.
findings.defense: The audit event records that an edit happened.

findings.title: 'Human approval' is merely a label, not an authorized, attributable control.
findings.evidence: act() accepts arbitrary action/actor and artifact id; no role authorization or artifact hash/version binding exists.
findings.impact: 'Human approval' is merely a label, not an authorized, attributable control.
findings.fix: Resolve authorized reviewer roles, enforce separation where required and bind decision to exact run/artifact/version/recipient set.
findings.attack: Any synthetic actor can approve any id and the same actor could create/edit/approve without policy checks.
findings.defense: Actors are synthetic because the lab avoids PII.

findings.title: A learner can emit green E2E while nothing ran.
findings.evidence: e2e_vp assigns 'success' to every step without executing any step.
findings.impact: A learner can emit green E2E while nothing ran.
findings.fix: Run actual section adapters/stubs with assertions, collect their returned artifact hashes/states and derive success from observed results only.
findings.attack: It manufactures exactly the evidence the promotion gate is supposed to prove.
findings.defense: It can be read as the shape of an evidence package.

findings.title: The strongest gate in the section is self-certified.
findings.evidence: n2_regression is hardcoded to 'pass'; CP-N2-A/B/C and CF-2 are not executed or referenced by artifact.
findings.impact: The strongest gate in the section is self-certified.
findings.fix: Load signed/tested regression result manifests with test counts/commit/source hashes and refuse promotion if any required suite is missing or failed.
findings.attack: Promotion evidence is a literal string, despite text saying real, not planned.
findings.defense: The snippet demonstrates package fields.

findings.title: Security/control compliance is represented by literals instead of checks.
findings.evidence: fraud_labels=0 is assigned; secrets-outside-repo and least scopes are prose only.
findings.impact: Security/control compliance is represented by literals instead of checks.
findings.fix: Derive fraud-label count from emitted artifacts, scan fixtures/logs for forbidden data/secrets and validate effective provider/tool permissions where relevant.
findings.attack: No scan/query proves absence of forbidden labels/secrets or scope violations.
findings.defense: The lab uses synthetic data and no real providers.

findings.title: Learner is taught to populate KPI fields rather than measure/derive them.
findings.evidence: cost_tokens=1200 and value_minutes_saved_est=45 are hardcoded; no model price, RPA duration, budget or manual baseline measurement is used.
findings.impact: Learner is taught to populate KPI fields rather than measure/derive them.
findings.fix: Calculate tokens from observed calls with model/version pricing snapshot; measure RPA/manual baseline on declared fixtures and label uncertainty/sample size.
findings.attack: The tagline/job relevance promise bounded cost and value evidence, but the package contains invented numbers.
findings.defense: The paragraph labels minutes saved as an estimate, not financial promise.

findings.title: Section closes with only a manufactured happy path despite claiming recovery evidence.
findings.evidence: Paragraph says any failed step makes E2E false; e2e_vp has no failure input/path and always returns success.
findings.impact: Section closes with only a manufactured happy path despite claiming recovery evidence.
findings.fix: Add injected failures before/after side effects, process restart, retry exhaustion, human reject and verify final E2E/promotion is false or recovered with evidence.
findings.attack: The gate never demonstrates recovery, blocking or fail-closed behavior under failure.
findings.defense: Failure handling is discussed in T2.

findings.title: The integrator loses the provenance needed to defend the final outcome.
findings.evidence: No integrated record links S21 report/S22 approvals/S23 download/S24 OCR/S25 model output to S26 review/draft by hashes and versions.
findings.impact: The integrator loses the provenance needed to defend the final outcome.
findings.fix: Persist one lineage graph/manifest carrying immutable artifact hashes, schema/model revisions, reviewer decisions and parent-child edges through every node.
findings.attack: run_id alone cannot prove which exact artifact/model/reviewer decision produced the final draft.
findings.defense: The narrative repeatedly names a common VP pipeline.

findings.title: The generic helper is less deterministic than the surrounding reproducibility claims.
findings.evidence: topo() seeds deque from a set of zero-indegree nodes.
findings.impact: The generic helper is less deterministic than the surrounding reproducibility claims.
findings.fix: Use a stable ordered node registry or heap/sorted tie-break and state that multiple valid topological orders may exist.
findings.attack: With multiple roots, order can vary with hash iteration rather than a documented tie-break, weakening reproducibility.
findings.defense: The canonical seven-step chain has one root.

findings.title: Outcome 'configurar schedules' is overclaimed as operational capability.
findings.evidence: Cron and timezone are printed strings; disable_schedule/drain are prose only.
findings.impact: Outcome 'configurar schedules' is overclaimed as operational capability.
findings.fix: Label the string as schedule specification and add a small state machine or real approved scheduler adapter demonstrating enable/disable/drain.
findings.attack: No scheduler state, timezone binding, enable/disable action or drain behavior is demonstrated.
findings.defense: A conceptual cron example is legitimate at this level.

findings.title: DLQ can still become the silent graveyard the text warns against.
findings.evidence: DLQ item stores id/reason/owner only; prose/callout promise owner and SLA and the section discusses operation.
findings.impact: DLQ can still become the silent graveyard the text warns against.
findings.fix: Define a DLQ record contract with lineage, attempts, timestamps, owner, SLA, status and controlled redrive/reject workflow.
findings.attack: No SLA, run_id, payload hash, first/last failure, retry history, retention, alert or redrive path is modeled.
findings.defense: A minimal list is sufficient to introduce the concept.

findings.title: Learner cannot reliably trace prose to output.
findings.evidence: Paragraph says analysis=1, report=1, recipient=0; code/output use recipient=1.
findings.impact: Learner cannot reliably trace prose to output.
findings.fix: Use one fixture consistently and include the zero-recipient case if that is the intended teaching point.
findings.attack: The explanatory case and executable case are different while presented as the same case.
findings.defense: Both correctly result in blocked/all_clear False.

findings.title: The learner can mistake usage convention for storage invariant.
findings.evidence: audit is a normal mutable in-memory Python list.
findings.impact: The learner can mistake usage convention for storage invariant.
findings.fix: Teach append-only as an invariant backed by persistent event records/hashes or clearly label the list as a non-enforcing simulation.
findings.attack: Entries can be edited/deleted and disappear on process exit; append-only is asserted rather than enforced.
findings.defense: The example itself only calls append.

findings.title: Alert behavior cannot be reproduced from the stated SLO.
findings.evidence: Prose says success_rate≥0.95 diario; code names success_rate_7d.
findings.impact: Alert behavior cannot be reproduced from the stated SLO.
findings.fix: Choose one window and encode numerator, denominator, window and evaluation cadence consistently.
findings.attack: Daily and rolling-seven-day objectives are different operational contracts.
findings.defense: Both use the same illustrative threshold.

findings.title: Learner sees alert arithmetic rather than a defendable service objective.
findings.evidence: success_rate_7d and p95_duration_min have no event population/eligibility definition or error-budget/reaction policy.
findings.impact: Learner sees alert arithmetic rather than a defendable service objective.
findings.fix: Define eligible runs, success predicate, window, measurement point, target, error budget and response before calculating alerts.
findings.attack: A numeric target without SLI semantics can be gamed by skipped/rejected runs or changing denominators.
findings.defense: The section calls the SLO synthetic.

findings.title: The learner gets an unsafe universal incident sequence.
findings.evidence: Runbook orders disable_schedule → drain → page oncall and defines drain as emptying workers before notification.
findings.impact: The learner gets an unsafe universal incident sequence.
findings.fix: Detect/page immediately according to severity, quiesce new work, drain/cancel with timeout and explicit side-effect policy, then diagnose/recover.
findings.attack: A drain can stall; delaying notification until after completion can hide a P0 and mixes mitigation with escalation.
findings.defense: For a small synthetic batch the sequence may finish quickly.

findings.title: Known false-green states can be treated as trusted test fixtures and laundered into N3.
findings.evidence: S27 declares Nivel 2 as prerequisite and opens as if the S26 pipeline and its prior contracts can simply be assumed.
findings.impact: Known false-green states can be treated as trusted test fixtures and laundered into N3.
findings.fix: State that Level-2 artifacts are untrusted until regression manifests pass; make known S26 defects first-class regression targets.
findings.attack: S26 is REPAIR_REQUIRED and its promotion evidence includes hardcoded success/pass values.
findings.defense: A new level needs a narrative bridge from earlier work.

findings.title: Fixtures copied into later integration tests can target a routable namespace while being described as safe synthetic.
findings.evidence: Opening/callouts/code repeatedly use @example.pe and call those contacts safe synthetic data.
findings.impact: Fixtures copied into later integration tests can target a routable namespace while being described as safe synthetic.
findings.fix: Use ana@equipo.test, example.com, or another reserved documentation/test domain consistently.
findings.attack: IANA reserves .test/.example/.invalid and example.com/net/org, not example.pe.
findings.defense: The theory examples do not send mail.

findings.title: Learner can complete theory without learning pytest's actual collection, parametrization, fixtures, failure reporting or lifecycle.
findings.evidence: Core theory repeatedly substitutes plain Python for pytest: simulated fixture helper, custom assert_raises, manual table loops, manual branch counters; no canonical theory output shows a real pytest collection/failure/pass cycle.
findings.impact: Learner can complete theory without learning pytest's actual collection, parametrization, fixtures, failure reporting or lifecycle.
findings.fix: Require pytest in the local venv and execute at least one real test module per T2/T3/T4 contract, keeping simulations only as explanatory precursors.
findings.attack: The section is explicitly 'Estrategia de pruebas con pytest' and the roadmap says pytest becomes systematic from S27.
findings.defense: Plain-Python analogies keep browser/runtime examples portable.

findings.title: The section teaching reliable oracles includes a property that provides effectively zero fault-detection power.
findings.evidence: T1-B offers 'longitud >= 0 tras normalizar' as an invariant oracle.
findings.impact: The section teaching reliable oracles includes a property that provides effectively zero fault-detection power.
findings.fix: Replace with nontrivial invariants such as idempotence, no leading/trailing whitespace, single internal whitespace policy, and explicit empty-input behavior.
findings.attack: For any returned string, length>=0 is tautologically true and cannot detect meaningful normalization regressions.
findings.defense: The paragraph also gives useful fixed-value and idempotence oracle examples.

findings.title: The canonical executable can display a failed contract while the test runner stays green.
findings.evidence: T2-A's table uses all(...) and prints param_ok; rows are called 'conceptual node ids' but are not pytest invocations and no assert consumes param_ok.
findings.impact: The canonical executable can display a failed contract while the test runner stays green.
findings.fix: Execute the real @pytest.mark.parametrize test with ids and remove the print-only pseudo-parametrization.
findings.attack: An audit run constructed from the same pattern returned pytest exit code 0/'2 passed' while param_ok=False for a deliberately wrong table row.
findings.defense: The comments show a correct @pytest.mark.parametrize form for local use.

findings.title: The named production behavior can change independently without the advertised test existing.
findings.evidence: Learning outcome promises deterministic tests for normalize_name and exact_match; canonical code defines no exact_match function and only compares two normalize_name calls inline.
findings.impact: The named production behavior can change independently without the advertised test existing.
findings.fix: Define/import exact_match and test its public behavior, including positive, negative, missing and Unicode cases.
findings.attack: Testing an expression is not a regression contract for a public exact_match implementation/API.
findings.defense: The equality expression models the intended exact-match semantics.

findings.title: Learner may understand copying data but not how fixture request, scope, teardown or factory lifecycle actually works.
findings.evidence: T2-B says fixtures inject dependencies without globals, but executable theory uses a normal fixture_contacts function backed by global _base_contacts; no @pytest.fixture or factory fixture actually runs.
findings.impact: Learner may understand copying data but not how fixture request, scope, teardown or factory lifecycle actually works.
findings.fix: Run real function-scope and session/package fixture tests, including a factory and an intentionally contaminated wide-scope negative fixture.
findings.attack: The lesson's fixture-specific lifecycle/isolation behavior is never demonstrated by pytest.
findings.defense: Comments contain a syntactically correct pytest.fixture example and deepcopy illustrates isolation.

findings.title: The example violates the resource-lifecycle contract it just taught.
findings.evidence: T3-A explains that NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False) must be cleaned in finally or replaced by tmp_path, but the canonical code never unlinks the created path.
findings.impact: The example violates the resource-lifecycle contract it just taught.
findings.fix: Use tmp_path in real pytest or unlink the named temporary file in finally.
findings.attack: Runtime validation confirmed the file still existed after the demo.
findings.defense: TemporaryDirectory is cleaned correctly in the previous example.

findings.title: The section explicitly names a high-risk negative class without providing the regression contract, and invalid scores can reach threshold lo…
findings.evidence: T3-B says negative cases include score out of range, but parse_score only rejects blank strings and classify_pair accepts arbitrary floats.
findings.impact: The section explicitly names a high-risk negative class without providing the regression contract, and invalid scores can reach threshold logic.
findings.fix: Validate finite score and allowed range before classification; parameterize blank, malformed, NaN, infinity, negative and >1 inputs.
findings.attack: Runtime checks show nan, inf, -0.1 and 1.5 are accepted; NaN silently becomes non_match.
findings.defense: parse_score is introduced only to demonstrate exception testing, not as a complete business validator.

findings.title: Learner can believe edge coverage exists because the prose enumerates it even though the suite does not.
findings.evidence: T3-B promises None, empty, wrong type, broken encoding and score-out-of-range coverage, but canonical executable tests only four require_email cases.
findings.impact: Learner can believe edge coverage exists because the prose enumerates it even though the suite does not.
findings.fix: Add parameterized negative tables for each public function, especially score finite/range, Unicode/encoding boundary and None/wrong type.
findings.attack: Several named failure classes have no executable contract in the section where they are introduced.
findings.defense: The paragraph says design a table and examples are illustrative rather than exhaustive.

findings.title: The anti-pattern is identical to the print-only contract the section warns against.
findings.evidence: negative_messages.py accumulates booleans and only prints neg_ok; it never asserts all(results).
findings.impact: The anti-pattern is identical to the print-only contract the section warns against.
findings.fix: Convert rows to pytest.parametrize and assert the expected exception/value per invocation.
findings.attack: A wrong row can produce neg_ok False without failing the process/test runner.
findings.defense: The canonical fixed rows currently evaluate True.

findings.title: Learner can report 'branch coverage' without measuring code branches at all.
findings.evidence: T4-A calls the topic branch coverage but executable code manually increments auto/review/non counters; it never enables Coverage.py branch measurement or consumes a report.
findings.impact: Learner can report 'branch coverage' without measuring code branches at all.
findings.fix: Use coverage.py/pytest-cov with branch measurement, then separately track business-risk scenario coverage.
findings.attack: Coverage.py defines branch coverage as observed source-to-destination execution opportunities; output categories are not equivalent.
findings.defense: The manual counters visualize business branch coverage without adding a dependency.

findings.title: The metric stays green while a high-risk threshold contract changes.
findings.evidence: T4-A uses [0.95,0.7,0.2,0.9] and reports 3/3 outcomes; it omits the 0.6 boundary, just-below/above boundaries and invalid/nonfinite scores.
findings.impact: The metric stays green while a high-risk threshold contract changes.
findings.fix: Parameterize each boundary at/just below/just above and invalid values; assert exact labels independently of branch-count metrics.
findings.attack: A mutation from score>=0.9 to score>0.9 changed the 0.9 result but the manual counter still reported 3/3.
findings.defense: 0.9 at least includes one exact boundary case.

findings.title: A direct output comparison is labeled as evidence that the suite protects the contract, which it does not demonstrate.
findings.evidence: mutation_useful.py sets mutation_killed = normalize_name_mutated(raw) != oracle; it never runs the test suite against the mutant.
findings.impact: A direct output comparison is labeled as evidence that the suite protects the contract, which it does not demonstrate.
findings.fix: Inject/swap the implementation under test and show an actual pytest failure; optionally use mutmut later.
findings.attack: Mutation testing defines a killed mutant by a test failing when mutated production code runs.
findings.defense: The section explicitly says conceptual/manual mutation is acceptable initially.

findings.title: Learner never sees the evidence sequence that distinguishes a regression test from a post-hoc green test.
findings.evidence: Opening/gate repeatedly require bug_repro -> failing regression -> fix -> passing regression, but no canonical theory example shows a known bug failing before the repair and passing afterward.
findings.impact: Learner never sees the evidence sequence that distinguishes a regression test from a post-hoc green test.
findings.fix: Include one real red-green bug reproduction with captured pytest failure output, repair, rerun and permanent regression test.
findings.attack: The defining section behavior is asserted, not demonstrated.
findings.defense: Mutation example is intended to show a failure-sensitive contract conceptually.

findings.title: The course's own risk-first rule is not applied at the level transition, and N2 defects can remain green while N3 starts.
findings.evidence: S27 teaches risk-first testing but ignores the known high-severity S26 failures carried into the continuation ledger and spends theory on toy normalize/email examples instead.
findings.impact: The course's own risk-first rule is not applied at the level transition, and N2 defects can remain green while N3 starts.
findings.fix: Add a small inherited-regression pack for Level-2 gates before CP-N3-A tests; then proceed to normalize/matching.
findings.attack: The campaign already knows concrete partial-cycle, HITL-gate, idempotency, persistence and hardcoded-E2E defects—exactly the highest-value regression targets.
findings.defense: Roadmap defines S27 as start CP-N3-A focused on normalización/matching rather than retrofitting S26.

findings.title: Learner may think every valid new test must historically fail before it has evidentiary value.
findings.evidence: Opening says a test that never failed has not proved that it knows how to detect anything.
findings.impact: Learner may think every valid new test must historically fail before it has evidentiary value.
findings.fix: Scope the rule to bug regression and explain mutation/fault injection as one way to validate sensitivity for other tests.
findings.attack: That is defensible for a regression reproducer but overbroad for newly specified behavior or straightforward invariant tests.
findings.defense: The sentence strongly encourages red-green discipline and mutation sensitivity.

findings.title: The learner's advance organizer understates a major closing competence.
findings.evidence: Reference says T4 closes with branch coverage but omits the roadmap's second T4 half: conceptual mutation, useful failures and maintenance.
findings.impact: The learner's advance organizer understates a major closing competence.
findings.fix: Name both branch/risk coverage and mutation/failure/maintenance in the T4 reference sentence.
findings.attack: The reference block is supposed to define section order/scope.
findings.defense: The omitted material appears later in theory.

findings.title: A heuristic becomes doctrine and can discourage integration/E2E tests that cover unique failure surfaces.
findings.evidence: Theory says risk changes time allocation 'not the form of the pyramid' and prescribes the pyramid as fixed.
findings.impact: A heuristic becomes doctrine and can discourage integration/E2E tests that cover unique failure surfaces.
findings.fix: Present the pyramid as a default cost/confidence heuristic; add tests at the lowest layer that can prove the behavior, moving upward where lower layers cannot.
findings.attack: Best-practice material describes the pyramid as a rule of thumb and explicitly notes its simplifications; high-level tests are appropriate when they provide confidence unavailable below.
findings.defense: Many small tests and fewer high-level tests is a useful default heuristic.

findings.title: Learners may optimize test counts to an invented formula rather than reason about failure modes and confidence.
findings.evidence: Risk score impact×likelihood is mapped to exact quotas: >=15 means >=5 tests; 8–14 means 2–3; <8 means smoke+negative.
findings.impact: Learners may optimize test counts to an invented formula rather than reason about failure modes and confidence.
findings.fix: Keep qualitative risk ranking; derive concrete cases from failure modes/branches and record rationale instead of fixed quotas.
findings.attack: No calibration, evidence or project-specific rationale supports those numeric cutoffs or counts.
findings.defense: The paragraph calls the score a practical, non-scientific prioritization device.

findings.title: Language switching competes with the testing concepts being learned.
findings.evidence: Theory densely mixes clerical queue, merge, drift, smoke, retro, flake, node id, factory, scope, raw, mock, CI and contract without always introducing Spanish-first meanings.
findings.impact: Language switching competes with the testing concepts being learned.
findings.fix: Introduce Spanish-first meanings once (cola de revisión manual, prueba mínima/smoke, identificador de caso/node id, etc.) and then retain API literals.
findings.attack: The reader model is competent but not the author; several terms carry process meaning beyond literal translation.
findings.defense: S27 begins the advanced integration phase and some terms were seen earlier.

findings.title: Learners can over-mock and remove the boundary they intended to test.
findings.evidence: T1-B lists 'red o disco no mockeados' as examples of fragile/flaky oracles.
findings.impact: Learners can over-mock and remove the boundary they intended to test.
findings.fix: Distinguish uncontrolled external dependencies from controlled local temp filesystem/integration boundaries.
findings.attack: Real filesystem behavior through tmp_path can be deterministic and is often exactly what an integration test should exercise; mocking disk is not intrinsically safer.
findings.defense: Uncontrolled external I/O can make tests environment-dependent.

findings.title: Learner can create a Test* class that pytest silently refuses to collect and not understand why.
findings.evidence: T2-A says pytest discovers Test* classes but omits the no-__init__ condition and configurability of discovery patterns.
findings.impact: Learner can create a Test* class that pytest silently refuses to collect and not understand why.
findings.fix: State the default conditions precisely and note that configuration can change patterns.
findings.attack: Current pytest docs explicitly require Test-prefixed classes without __init__ under default discovery.
findings.defense: The lesson focuses mainly on function tests and default conventions.

findings.title: Reference is technically incomplete and turns a safety heuristic into an absolute API rule.
findings.evidence: Theory lists function/class/module/session scopes and says session should only be used for expensive read-only resources.
findings.impact: Reference is technically incomplete and turns a safety heuristic into an absolute API rule.
findings.fix: Include package scope and phrase read-only as a default risk-reduction rule rather than a prohibition.
findings.attack: Current pytest also supports package scope; wider scopes can safely manage mutable resources when lifecycle/reset semantics are explicit.
findings.defense: Read-only is a conservative novice-safe heuristic.

findings.title: Learner can blame -x for order coupling it does not create.
findings.evidence: T2-B says 'si ves un fallo que solo aparece con -x...' and later correctly says -x neither reorders tests nor causes new failures.
findings.impact: Learner can blame -x for order coupling it does not create.
findings.fix: Say -x only truncates observation after the first failure; use explicit random-order runs/seeds to diagnose order dependence.
findings.attack: The same paragraph presents an impossible diagnostic cue under normal pytest semantics.
findings.defense: It is trying to distinguish first-failure visibility from order randomization.

findings.title: Learner may blur numerical tolerance with the business definition of a threshold boundary.
findings.evidence: Theory broadly says matching probabilities should use isclose rather than equality and places this next to threshold decisions.
findings.impact: Learner may blur numerical tolerance with the business definition of a threshold boundary.
findings.fix: Separate value-approximation tests from threshold classification tests and show both patterns.
findings.attack: Approximate equality is appropriate for computed numeric expectations, but threshold branch semantics themselves require exact boundary tests (at, just below, just above).
findings.defense: The code uses explicit tolerances and does not directly apply isclose inside classify_pair.

findings.title: Learners may count cases rather than enumerate contract partitions and risks.
findings.evidence: Theory mandates at least one happy and three negative cases per public function.
findings.impact: Learners may count cases rather than enumerate contract partitions and risks.
findings.fix: Require coverage of identified input partitions/failure modes, with a small minimum only as a scaffold if explicitly labeled heuristic.
findings.attack: The number of meaningful negative cases depends on the contract/failure modes; three can be insufficient or wasteful.
findings.defense: A minimum helps novices remember to test failures.

findings.title: Overclaim weakens epistemic discipline in a section about evidence.
findings.evidence: Coverage callout says if review branch is never tested, the review queue 'se romperá en producción'.
findings.impact: Overclaim weakens epistemic discipline in a section about evidence.
findings.fix: Use 'puede romperse sin que CI lo detecte' and keep the causal claim bounded.
findings.attack: Untested code is higher risk but failure is not logically guaranteed.
findings.defense: The warning is intended to motivate risk-based testing.

findings.title: Learner may confuse behavioral contract tests with consumer/provider interface contract testing.
findings.evidence: Job relevance lists unit/contract/integration as layers while the section uses 'contrato' mainly to mean behavioral promise and the roadmap pyramid is unit/integration/E2E.
findings.impact: Learner may confuse behavioral contract tests with consumer/provider interface contract testing.
findings.fix: Define 'contrato de comportamiento' for this section and reserve 'contract test' for interface/provider-consumer testing when introduced.
findings.attack: 'Contract test' is also a distinct testing category in common practice, so the term changes meaning without clarification.
findings.defense: In Spanish prose 'contrato ejecutable' is a useful metaphor for assertions.

findings.title: The only AAA diagram can encode the wrong temporal model of when expected truth is established.
findings.evidence: S27-aaa-oracle alt says the oracle 'enters' after Act and also omits accents in 'despues/oraculo'.
findings.impact: The only AAA diagram can encode the wrong temporal model of when expected truth is established.
findings.fix: Show expected/oracle defined in Arrange, Act producing actual, and Assert comparing actual to expected; fix Spanish accents in alt text.
findings.attack: Expected behavior should be chosen independently before observing the Act result; placing the oracle after Act risks encouraging derivation from current output, the exact anti-pattern the section warns against.
findings.defense: Visually, Assert occurs after Act and consumes the oracle there.

findings.title: KNOWN_S26_REGRESSIONS_IGNORED_AT_LEVEL3_ENTRY
findings.evidence: S27 carry-forward requires a minimal inherited regression pack for cycle/HITL/idempotency/restart/compensation/E2E; S28 theory starts new ER properties without those tests.
findings.impact: The course teaches risk-first testing while ignoring the highest-known regression risks at the level boundary.
findings.attack: A new suite can go green while the known S26 critical controls remain broken.
findings.defense: S28 is scoped to QA of CP-N3-A rather than retrofitting all Level-2 defects.

findings.title: NON_RESERVED_EXAMPLE_PE_REINTRODUCED
findings.evidence: Fixtures and FakeHTTP use @example.pe / https://example.pe/er.
findings.impact: A supposedly synthetic namespace can become routable when tests later cross real HTTP/email boundaries.
findings.attack: IANA reserves example.com/example.org and special-use test domains, not example.pe.
findings.defense: No canonical snippet performs a real request to that URL today.

findings.title: SYSTEMATIC_PYTEST_PROMISE_STILL_REPLACED_BY_PRINTS
findings.evidence: Theory snippets compute idempotent_ok/symmetric/meta/dirty/drift/contract/encoding/stable and print them; they are not collected pytest assertions.
findings.impact: A broken contract can print False and the process can still exit successfully.
findings.attack: Roadmap says from S27 pytest is systematic and S28 gate is an executable suite.
findings.defense: I Do later contains some test_* functions and the theory code is illustrative.

findings.title: T1A_INVARIANT_FAILURE_DOES_NOT_FAIL_THE_SUITE
findings.evidence: invariants_gen.py accumulates bad cases and prints idempotent_ok instead of asserting len(bad)==0.
findings.impact: A discovered counterexample can leave the script exit code green.
findings.attack: This defeats the section's executable-contract gate.
findings.defense: The boolean makes the result visible to a reader.

findings.title: EMPTY_EMPTY_NAMES_SCORE_AS_PERFECT_MATCH
findings.evidence: sim_token returns 1.0 when both token sets are empty and the canonical pairs include ('','').
findings.impact: Missing data becomes strong positive identity evidence.
findings.attack: Two unknown names should not create perfect evidence unless the contract explicitly defines a special non-evidentiary sentinel.
findings.defense: Mathematically some Jaccard conventions define empty-empty similarity as 1.

findings.title: METAMORPHIC_TEST_TESTS_DUPLICATED_INLINE_EXPRESSION_NOT_PRODUCTION_NORMALIZER
findings.evidence: meta_ok repeats join/split/casefold expressions on both sides instead of calling the normalize API used by the ER pipeline.
findings.impact: Production normalize can be broken while this property remains green.
findings.attack: Properties must target the actual public behavior under test.
findings.defense: The expression demonstrates the mathematical relation in minimal code.

findings.title: SCHEMA_VALIDATOR_DOES_NOT_ENFORCE_ITS_DECLARED_TYPES_AND_DOMAINS
findings.evidence: validate_record accepts id='   ', email='@', score=True and accepts numeric strings through float coercion.
findings.impact: Rows can satisfy the regression contract while violating the stated schema.
findings.attack: A schema contract should distinguish type validation from intentional coercion and reject whitespace-only identifiers/degenerate addresses.
findings.defense: The validator is explicitly didactic and minimal.

findings.title: BATCH_QUALITY_CLAIMS_ARE_NOT_TESTABLE_BY_ROW_VALIDATOR
findings.evidence: Prose names unique ids, pair cardinality and UTF-8 legibility; validate_record only sees one decoded dict.
findings.impact: Core quality invariants can never fail in the demonstrated contract.
findings.attack: Uniqueness/cardinality require batch context and encoding requires byte/decode boundary evidence.
findings.defense: Later integration code covers pair count and Unicode normalization partially.

findings.title: FAIL_CLOSED_BATCH_STOP_EXISTS_ONLY_IN_PROSE
findings.evidence: Theory says a broken batch stops with report; code only builds report and prints dirty_n.
findings.impact: The learner sees detection but not enforcement.
findings.attack: A regression gate must raise/fail or return an explicit blocking result consumed by the caller.
findings.defense: The snippet focuses on the validator rather than orchestration.

findings.title: GOLDEN_IS_NOT_A_VERSIONED_PERSISTED_ARTIFACT
findings.evidence: golden_drift.py constructs two in-memory dicts and compares them.
findings.impact: The section does not demonstrate the file/version/change-review properties that define a golden snapshot.
findings.attack: No JSON/CSV file is loaded, hashed, committed or diffed.
findings.defense: In-memory dicts isolate the drift/reconcile concept from file I/O.

findings.title: GOLDEN_APPROVAL_IS_AN_UNAUTHENTICATED_BOOLEAN_AND_RECONCILE_DOES_NOT_RECONCILE
findings.evidence: reconcile(old,new,approved=True) returns 'updated' but records no reviewer/timestamp/note/hash and persists nothing.
findings.impact: A caller can self-approve a regression and no auditable golden changes.
findings.attack: This contradicts the paragraph requiring human review plus change note.
findings.defense: approved is a didactic placeholder for a later workflow.

findings.title: 503_RETRY_AND_TIMEOUT_CLAIM_NOT_EXECUTED
findings.evidence: T3-A says the pattern demonstrates retries on 503; FakeHTTP only returns a dict containing status and no service/retry function is called.
findings.impact: A learner may mistake controllable fake response data for tested retry behavior.
findings.attack: Inject a sequence of 503/200 or timeout exception and assert attempts/backoff/result.
findings.defense: The subtopic's primary construct is doubles, not retry policy itself.

findings.title: TEXT_NORMALIZATION_CONTRACT_CONTRADICTS_ITS_OWN_NFC_NFD_REQUIREMENT
findings.evidence: T3-B normalize uses casefold+split only; T4-A says NFC/NFD must be unified with unicodedata.normalize.
findings.impact: Visually equivalent names can fail match in one canonical layer and pass in another.
findings.attack: Runtime check: 'José' NFC and its NFD form remain unequal after casefold+split.
findings.defense: T4-A introduces the additional normalization specifically at integration time.

findings.title: INTEGRATION_DEMO_HAS_NO_ASSERTIONS_OR_PYTEST_GATE
findings.evidence: integration_sqlite.py returns n/pairs/encoding_ok and prints them.
findings.impact: A wrong row count or pair result can still produce exit code 0.
findings.attack: The integration block should be a real test with exact assertions and cleanup fixture.
findings.defense: The query itself is real SQLite integration rather than a fake DB.

findings.title: TAGLINE_PROMISE_TIMEOUT_ORDER_AND_RESUMPTION_UNEARNED
findings.evidence: Public/source tagline promises encoding, cardinality, order, timeout and resumption; theory executes only basic Unicode normalization and a pair query plus deterministic sorting.
findings.impact: Learner can complete theory without ever proving timeout or checkpoint resumption.
findings.attack: Add explicit failure-injection tests for timeout and persistent checkpoint restart.
findings.defense: Some of these dimensions may be exercised in later I Do/practice content outside LESSONS_ONLY scope.

findings.title: NO_REAL_E2E_INGEST_TO_PAIRS_TO_REVIEW
findings.evidence: T4-A defines E2E as ingest→pairs→review, but canonical theory only creates a SQLite table and query.
findings.impact: The distinction between integration and E2E is described but not demonstrated.
findings.attack: Run a synthetic record through validation, persistence, candidate generation and review artifact creation.
findings.defense: Roadmap increment emphasizes a suite, and a minimal integration example need not also be full E2E.

findings.title: FLAKY_BAD_IS_EFFECTIVELY_A_TAUTOLOGY_NOT_A_FLAKE
findings.evidence: random.random()>0.0 almost always true and datetime.now().microsecond>=0 is always true.
findings.impact: The canonical anti-pattern almost never exhibits the intermittent failure it claims to model.
findings.attack: Use an actually intermittent predicate or better, an order/time-dependent deterministic reproducer.
findings.defense: It visually contains two uncontrolled dependencies and is labeled anti-pattern.

findings.title: PROPERTY_FIGURE_FALSELY_NESTS_EXAMPLE_TESTS_INSIDE_PROPERTY_TESTS
findings.evidence: Figure alt describes property-based as a containing region around example-based tests.
findings.impact: Learner may infer property tests subsume example tests instead of complementing them.
findings.attack: Current Hypothesis docs explicitly say property-based testing is a powerful addition and not always a replacement.
findings.defense: The figure likely intends to convey broader input exploration, not formal set inclusion.

findings.title: PROPERTY_QUANTIFIER_OMITS_INPUT_DOMAIN
findings.evidence: Opening says a property must hold siempre / sin importar la entrada.
findings.impact: Learner may apply invariants to invalid inputs outside the declared strategy/preconditions.
findings.attack: Properties quantify over a defined domain/strategy, not arbitrary Python values.
findings.defense: Subsequent text mentions strategies and generated input spaces.

findings.title: HYPOTHESIS_REPRODUCTION_MISSTATED_AS_EXACT_SEED
findings.evidence: Opening claims that on a counterexample the tool returns the exact seed to reproduce it.
findings.impact: Creates the wrong failure-reproduction model for Hypothesis.
findings.attack: Hypothesis primarily reports falsifying examples, uses its example database and can emit reproduce_failure; seed is not normally the sole artifact.
findings.defense: Hypothesis does expose seed controls and can print seeds in some situations.

findings.title: HUNDREDS_OF_INPUTS_FALSE_PRECISION
findings.evidence: Opening says the machine generates hundreds of inputs.
findings.impact: Turns configurable test effort into a pseudo-guaranteed quantity.
findings.attack: Current Hypothesis default max_examples is 100 and actual execution can differ due to phases/filtering/settings.
findings.defense: The word is illustrative rather than a formal guarantee.

findings.title: GLOBAL_FIXED_RANDOM_SEED_BOTH_NARROWS_EXPLORATION_AND_MUTATES_SHARED_STATE
findings.evidence: random.seed(42) is called at module level and stable() reseeds the module RNG.
findings.impact: Tests repeatedly explore the same small sample and can couple other tests through global RNG state.
findings.attack: Use random.Random(seed) for isolation and property tooling/example database for broader exploration.
findings.defense: Fixed seeds provide deterministic CI and reproducibility for a beginner lab.

findings.title: RANDOM_WITHOUT_SEED_EQ_FLAKE_OVERGENERALIZATION
findings.evidence: Callout says Random sin seed en CI es flake.
findings.impact: Conflates nondeterministic input generation with intermittent test failure.
findings.attack: A randomized test can remain correct if failures are reproducible/captured; a flake is intermittent pass/fail without code change.
findings.defense: Uncontrolled randomness is a common cause of flaky behavior.

findings.title: DIRECTED_EDIT_DISTANCE_EXAMPLE_MISLEADS
findings.evidence: Callout contrasts test_jaccard_is_symmetric with test_edit_distance_directed.
findings.impact: Learner may believe standard edit/Levenshtein distance is inherently directed.
findings.attack: Standard Levenshtein with symmetric costs is symmetric; direction requires a deliberately asymmetric cost/algorithm contract.
findings.defense: The text says algunas distancias dirigidas rather than all edit distances.

findings.title: CASEFOLD_ONLY_CASING_ABSOLUTE_IS_TECHNICALLY_FALSE
findings.evidence: Text says casefold normaliza mayúsculas y minúsculas, y solo eso.
findings.impact: Creates an inaccurate Unicode model.
findings.attack: Python documents casefold as more aggressive than lower, e.g. ß→ss; the correct limit is that it is not Unicode normalization.
findings.defense: The intended warning—casefold does not normalize NFC/NFD—is correct.

findings.title: RAW_GOLDEN_EQUALITY_CONFUSES_ORDER_NOISE_WITH_SEMANTIC_DRIFT
findings.evidence: golden != current compares list order directly while prose identifies ordering as possible noise.
findings.impact: Harmless ordering changes can block CI or be misclassified as matcher drift.
findings.attack: Canonicalize unordered pair sets and controlled numeric tolerances before semantic diff.
findings.defense: The supplied minimal fixture preserves order so the immediate example is deterministic.

findings.title: DRIFT_TERM_OVERLOADED_WITH_SNAPSHOT_DIFFERENCE
findings.evidence: Any golden diff is called drift.
findings.impact: Prepares confusion with later data/model drift where the measured phenomenon is distribution/performance change over time.
findings.attack: Use golden_diff/snapshot_diff here and reserve drift or qualify it explicitly.
findings.defense: The paragraph defines its local meaning before use.

findings.title: FAKE_HTTP_CAN_DRIFT_FROM_REAL_CLIENT_CONTRACT
findings.evidence: FakeHTTP invents get_json(url) and arbitrary response shape without interface/spec checking.
findings.impact: Production client signature/shape can change while fake-based tests remain green.
findings.attack: Use a Protocol/interface, contract test, or autospec for mocks where appropriate.
findings.defense: A hand-written fake can intentionally implement a stable application-owned adapter interface.

findings.title: MOCKS_DEFINED_BUT_NO_ACTUAL_MOCK_INTERACTION_TEST_IS_SHOWN
findings.evidence: T3-A defines Mock/Fake/Stub, but canonical executable demonstrates only hand-written fakes/dicts.
findings.impact: The learner cannot practice when interaction assertions are useful or risky.
findings.attack: Show one autospecced interaction boundary and contrast it with fake state-based testing.
findings.defense: Learning outcome emphasizes controlled doubles broadly, not unittest.mock specifically.

findings.title: GLOBAL_PATCHING_DISMISSED_TOO_BROADLY
findings.evidence: Callout says no parches globales salvo legado.
findings.impact: Learner may avoid safe scoped environment/module patches even when dependency injection is impractical.
findings.attack: pytest monkeypatch is a supported fixture that restores changes automatically after the test.
findings.defense: Dependency injection is generally the more explicit design for application-owned dependencies.

findings.title: FAKE_NETWORK_OR_DISK_HEURISTIC_TOO_BROAD
findings.evidence: T3-B says if code talks to network or disk, fake the boundary.
findings.impact: Learner may mock away the filesystem/database integration behavior the test is supposed to verify.
findings.attack: Choose doubles based on test scope; tmp_path/SQLite/Testcontainers should remain real when that boundary is the construct.
findings.defense: The surrounding paragraph is explicitly warning against over-mocking and later demonstrates real SQLite.

findings.title: FLAKE_RATE_GATE_HAS_NO_MEASUREMENT_CONTRACT
findings.evidence: Prose says job fails if flake_rate>0 but defines no repeated-run population, window, denominator or quarantine treatment.
findings.impact: A metric can be reported or gamed without a reproducible definition.
findings.attack: Define attempts/runs/test set/window and distinguish first-run failure from retry recovery.
findings.defense: Zero flakes is an aspirational gate and details could live in CI tooling.

findings.title: STABLE_HELPER_RESEEDS_GLOBAL_RNG_AND_CAN_COUPLE_TESTS
findings.evidence: stable(seed) calls random.seed(seed) on the module generator every invocation.
findings.impact: Tests executed after it may observe a reset random sequence.
findings.attack: Use rng=random.Random(seed) local to the helper/fixture.
findings.defense: The example is single-process and intentionally demonstrates deterministic output.

findings.title: CONTRACT_TEST_TERMINOLOGY_REMAINS_AMBIGUOUS
findings.evidence: Outcome says contract tests of borders while prose mostly means behavioral input/output tests; provider-consumer compatibility is not distinguished.
findings.impact: Learner can carry an overloaded meaning into service/API testing.
findings.attack: Name behavioral contracts/spec tests separately from interface/provider-consumer contract tests.
findings.defense: The local section context consistently uses contract as executable behavior, so readers can infer the intended sense.

findings.title: IDEMPOTENCE_CONFLATED_WITH_DETERMINISM
findings.evidence: T1-B says that if f(f(x)) != f(x), matching becomes no determinista entre corridas.
findings.impact: Learner may conflate two different guarantees: determinism means same input gives same output; idempotence means reapplying the transformation does not change the result.
findings.attack: A function such as f(x)=x+1 is deterministic and not idempotent. The S28 risk is repeated transformation/drift across stages, not randomness.
findings.defense: The paragraph is trying to explain an operational symptom of repeated normalization rather than formally define determinism.

findings.title: PREREQUISITE_REGRESSION_DEBT_LAUNDERED
findings.evidence: S29 begins a truth-store layer without preserving the known critical S26 regression pack required by S28 continuation.
findings.impact: Risk-first testing learned in S27 is abandoned at the exact point where persistence would fossilize defects.
findings.attack: A relational store can make bad upstream success/approval labels look more authoritative simply by persisting them.
findings.defense: S29's nominal prerequisites are S12 and S28, not every prior implementation detail.

findings.title: PYTEST_GATE_STILL_ABSENT
findings.evidence: All eight canonical theory code blocks use prints/manual booleans; none is a collected pytest test despite S27-S28 carry-forward requiring executable repository/transaction/migration tests.
findings.impact: The section cannot claim tested constraints/repository behavior from its canonical theory evidence.
findings.attack: Wrong SQL can still exit 0 if a learner only observes printed output.
findings.defense: The mini-labs are explanatory snippets, not explicitly named tests.

findings.title: CANDIDATE_MEMBERSHIP_AND_RESOLVED_MEMBERSHIP_CONFLATED
findings.evidence: Reference says a source record may link to multiple candidate entities through entity_source_links while resolution remains open.
findings.impact: S30 may consume ambiguous memberships as resolved truth.
findings.attack: Candidate hypotheses and resolved source→entity membership are different domain states; putting both into an undifferentiated membership table obscures whether a link is proposed, accepted, rejected, or superseded.
findings.defense: An N-N link table is structurally flexible and can later receive status/temporal columns.

findings.title: ROADMAP_TRUTH_STORE_MODEL_NOT_MATERIALIZED
findings.evidence: Theory promises source_records, entity_source_links, entities, candidate_pairs, decisions and evidence, but canonical executable model never creates the complete graph.
findings.impact: No canonical integration proves referential integrity or history across the actual store graph.
findings.attack: The authoritative gate requires all five artifact families to remain reconstructable.
findings.defense: Each mini-lab isolates one concept to reduce cognitive load.

findings.title: PAIR_UNIQUENESS_PROMISED_BUT_MISSING
findings.evidence: T1-A prose requires CHECK(entity_a<entity_b) plus UNIQUE(entity_a,entity_b), but keys_constraints.py omits UNIQUE.
findings.impact: The same canonical candidate can exist more than once and receive divergent decisions.
findings.attack: Runtime accepted a second (e1,e2) row with another id.
findings.defense: Mirror pairs are blocked by A<B and primary-key ids are unique.

findings.title: SQLITE_DYNAMIC_TYPING_BREAKS_SCORE_TYPE_CONTRACT
findings.evidence: score REAL + CHECK range accepts Python True as 1.0 and text '0.5' as 0.5 under SQLite affinity.
findings.impact: A truth store can normalize wrong input types into plausible scores without recording the coercion.
findings.attack: S28 required explicit type/coercion policy; S29 silently treats coercion as valid.
findings.defense: SQLite affinity and numeric coercion are legitimate engine behavior and the range remains protected.

findings.title: APPEND_ONLY_IS_NOT_ENFORCED
