findings.evidence: decisions has no trigger/authorization layer preventing UPDATE or DELETE; runtime update and delete both succeed.
findings.impact: The core audit-history guarantee can be bypassed accidentally or by future repository methods.
findings.attack: Calling a table append-only while ordinary write paths can rewrite/delete it is a policy claim, not a database invariant.
findings.defense: Application repository code could enforce append-only even if SQLite itself does not.

findings.title: PROVENANCE_REFERENCES_ARE_UNVERIFIED_STRINGS
findings.evidence: temporality demo stores evidence_ref TEXT with no evidence table/FK and no FK from decisions.pair_id to candidate_pairs.
findings.impact: A decision can claim evidence that cannot be resolved or reproduced.
findings.attack: Runtime allows evidence refs/pairs that do not exist.
findings.defense: The block is scoped to event history rather than full schema integration.

findings.title: DECLARED_RUN_SOURCE_PROVENANCE_NOT_STORED
findings.evidence: Prose names source_system, source_record_id, ingested_at, transform_version and run_id, but temporality_prov.py stores none except a free-form evidence_ref.
findings.impact: The learner cannot reconstruct which source bytes/transformation produced the decision.
findings.attack: Printing 'provenance ev_02' does not prove lineage.
findings.defense: The fields are described conceptually and could live in other tables.

findings.title: ANY_DECISION_FALSELY_MEANS_NOT_PENDING
findings.evidence: Pending queue uses NOT EXISTS(any decisions row), while the same section inserts label='review' as a decision state.
findings.impact: Queue semantics can silently hide unresolved cases.
findings.attack: A pair routed to review disappears from the review queue merely because the routing decision exists.
findings.defense: The authors may intend decisions to mean completed human decisions and 'review' as a pedagogical placeholder.

findings.title: RANK_BEFORE_ANTIJOIN_DROPS_VALID_PENDING_CASES
findings.evidence: CTE assigns ROW_NUMBER to all pairs, applies rn<=3, then removes decided rows.
findings.impact: Top-N review capacity can be underfilled and cases starved.
findings.attack: If top three are decided, lower-scoring pending pairs are never considered; runtime returned [] although p4,p5 were pending.
findings.defense: The three-row toy fixture does not expose the failure.

findings.title: PLAN_DEMO_DOES_NOT_INSPECT_SCAN_VS_SEARCH
findings.evidence: card_null_plan.py prints only len(plan), despite prose/outcome requiring reasoning about SCAN vs SEARCH/index use.
findings.impact: The T2-B observable outcome is not demonstrated where taught.
findings.attack: A one-row plan can be a SCAN or SEARCH; row count of plan does not answer the question.
findings.defense: T4-A later demonstrates index-related plan text.

findings.title: DECISION_EVIDENCE_RELATIONSHIP_CONTRADICTS_MODEL
findings.evidence: T1-A says evidence is child of decision (FK decisions.id); ACID demo creates evidence(pair_id) with no decision_id or FK.
findings.impact: Later decisions for the same pair can become indistinguishable from evidence intended for earlier versions.
findings.attack: Atomic insertion does not prove evidence belongs to the exact decision version.
findings.defense: pair_id can group both rows in the toy lab.

findings.title: UPSERT_KEY_DOES_NOT_MATCH_REINGEST_CONTRACT
findings.evidence: Prose says same source_system/external_id drives reingest; upsert demo conflicts only on entities.id and stores neither source_system nor external_id.
findings.impact: Learner may conflate source-record identity with resolved-entity identity.
findings.attack: The example cannot prove idempotency for the natural source identity it names.
findings.defense: Stable entity id can serve as a simplified key in the isolated example.

findings.title: STALE_REPLAY_OVERWRITES_NEWER_ENTITY_STATE
findings.evidence: DO UPDATE always copies excluded name/updated with no freshness predicate.
findings.impact: Recovery/retry can regress canonical entity state.
findings.attack: Runtime showed updated=2/'Newest' overwritten by replay updated=1/'Stale'. SQLite supports a WHERE predicate on DO UPDATE for this purpose.
findings.defense: The toy example assumes arrivals are ordered.

findings.title: ENTITY_UPSERT_CONFLICTS_WITH_ROADMAP_HISTORY_GATE
findings.evidence: Roadmap gate says source records, entities, candidate pairs, decisions and evidence remain preserved without overwriting history; T3-B overwrites entity attributes in place.
findings.impact: The truth store cannot reconstruct which canonical entity attributes were visible when a decision was made.
findings.attack: Only decision history is protected; entity state history is destroyed.
findings.defense: Roadmap can be read as preserving decision/evidence history while allowing mutable canonical attributes.

findings.title: INTEGRITYERROR_IS_MISCLASSIFIED_AS_RETRYABLE
findings.evidence: T3-B recommends retry if IntegrityError occurs from conflict.
findings.impact: Retries can loop or hide malformed data instead of resolving concurrency safely.
findings.attack: IntegrityError covers UNIQUE/FK/CHECK/NOT NULL; many are deterministic data/invariant failures, and duplicate pair conflicts need idempotent resolution rather than blind retry.
findings.defense: The sentence specifically mentions pair conflict under concurrent workers.

findings.title: RESTART_AND_IDEMPOTENCY_ARE_CLAIMED_NOT_TESTED
findings.evidence: Prose says crash jobs return to pending and reapply idempotently, but all demos use :memory: and no reopen/checkpoint path exists.
findings.impact: S28's unfinished restart requirement remains unverified at the persistence layer where it belongs.
findings.attack: An in-memory DB vanishes on process restart.
findings.defense: True multi-connection contention is explicitly deferred to S38.

findings.title: NO_DROP_WITHOUT_BACKUP_IS_ONLY_A_SLOGAN
findings.evidence: T4-A states no_drop_without_backup but canonical code neither creates/verifies a backup nor blocks DROP.
findings.impact: Destructive migration safety is asserted without evidence.
findings.attack: The safety gate has no executable enforcement or test.
findings.defense: It is framed as policy for lab/production rather than SQLite feature.

findings.title: REPOSITORY_SCHEMA_DROPS_CORE_CONSTRAINTS
findings.evidence: repo_pool_tests.py pairs table has only id PK; no FK, score CHECK, A<B or pair UNIQUE.
findings.impact: The abstraction layer silently weakens the truth-store invariants taught earlier.
findings.attack: Runtime accepts same-entity, reversed and score=9 pairs.
findings.defense: The block's focus is repository shape and pending anti-join.

findings.title: REPOSITORY_IS_NOT_TESTED
findings.evidence: T4-B says 'Prueba el repository' and callout says assert, but canonical code only prints pending/pattern/test_db.
findings.impact: The final theory block ends without satisfying its own testability outcome.
findings.attack: There is no pytest constraint or pending test to block regression.
findings.defense: The You Do may ask the learner to add tests later.

findings.title: IN_MEMORY_REPOSITORY_CANNOT_PROVE_PERSISTENCE_OR_REOPEN
findings.evidence: All repository/storage demos use sqlite :memory: on a single connection.
findings.impact: Critical persistence semantics are never exercised despite being carry-forward requirements.
findings.attack: Restart, migration state, durability and connection initialization (including foreign_keys) disappear when connection closes.
findings.defense: SQLite :memory: is explicitly presented as local test substitute, not production proof.

findings.title: DECISION_LABEL_DOMAIN_IS_UNCONSTRAINED
findings.evidence: decisions.label is TEXT NOT NULL with no CHECK/reference table for allowed states.
findings.impact: State-machine correctness is not protected at the persistence boundary.
findings.attack: Typos such as 'mach' or ambiguous 'review' enter the truth store and directly affect queue semantics.
findings.defense: Allowed labels may be enforced in application code later.

findings.title: SOURCE_LINK_DELETE_DESTROYS_HISTORY
findings.evidence: Reference says undoing a source/entity link should remove a row from entity_source_links.
findings.impact: Entity provenance can no longer reconstruct previous linkage decisions.
findings.attack: DELETE erases exactly the membership history the roadmap requires preserving unless the link itself is versioned/evented.
findings.defense: The paragraph may mean remove current membership rather than delete audit history.

findings.title: FOREIGN_KEY_CAUSALITY_OVERCLAIM
findings.evidence: Reference says that 'with a FK, each change of opinion would erase the previous one.'
findings.impact: Learner may attribute temporal-model defects to the wrong relational mechanism.
findings.attack: A foreign key does not imply overwrite; history loss comes from storing only current membership in one mutable row rather than from FK semantics.
findings.defense: The sentence is contrasting a direct FK column with a link table in simplified language.

findings.title: TEMPORAL_ORDER_IS_UNDERSPECIFIED
findings.evidence: Both sample decisions receive the identical timestamp and history is ordered by surrogate id.
findings.impact: The phrase 'what the reviewer saw Tuesday' is stronger than the schema can establish.
findings.attack: Insertion order is not the same contract as event/valid time; delayed events or imports can reorder history.
findings.defense: For this lab the rows are inserted synchronously and id ordering is deterministic.

findings.title: ROW_NUMBER_TIES_HAVE_NO_STABLE_TIEBREAKER
findings.evidence: ROW_NUMBER windows order only by score DESC.
findings.impact: Queue order can change across plans/data and make tests/audits unstable.
findings.attack: Equal-score peers have no declared business ordering; S28 required deterministic ordering contracts.
findings.defense: Toy fixture scores are unique.

findings.title: QUERY_PLAN_FIGURE_TEACHES_WRONG_READING_RULE
findings.evidence: Figure caption says 'El plan es un árbol y se lee de abajo hacia arriba.'
findings.impact: Learner may misread actual EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN nesting.
findings.attack: SQLite documentation says entry order indicates nesting: first scan is outer loop, last inner; a universal bottom-up reading rule is misleading.
findings.defense: Trees are often visually inspected from leaves toward root when reasoning about data flow.

findings.title: PYTHON_NONE_SQL_NULL_WORDING_IS_MISLEADING
findings.evidence: Paragraph says 'NULL en SQL no es Python None.'
findings.impact: Learner may avoid or misunderstand correct parameter binding with None.
findings.attack: Python sqlite3 maps None↔NULL directly; the important difference is SQL three-valued comparison semantics, not representation mapping.
findings.defense: The intended warning is semantic, not adapter-level.

findings.title: SCHEMA_MIGRATIONS_ROW_IS_NOT_EXECUTABLE_MIGRATION_HISTORY
findings.evidence: Mini-lab creates final schema/index and inserts (1,'init_pairs') manually.
findings.impact: A learner can mark a migration applied without proving the schema transition occurred.
findings.attack: No migration artifact, dependency/order check, idempotent runner, upgrade/downgrade, applied_at or checksum exists.
findings.defense: The section only introduces migration versioning, not Alembic tooling.

findings.title: EXPLAIN_OUTPUT_STRING_MATCH_IS_BRITTLE
findings.evidence: indexes_migrate.py declares uses_index if plan contains idx name, USING INDEX, or generic INDEX.
findings.impact: Learner sees a brittle text heuristic presented as a migration/index gate.
findings.attack: SQLite explicitly warns EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN output format can change and applications should not depend on it.
findings.defense: The prose itself notes plan text may vary and this is a teaching assertion, not production parser.

findings.title: REPOSITORY_API_IS_OVERCLAIMED
findings.evidence: Prose names get_entity, insert_decision, pending; PairRepo implements only add_pair and pending.
findings.impact: Learner cannot see where transaction/provenance invariants belong in the repository abstraction.
findings.attack: The example does not demonstrate decision transaction/history methods or entity retrieval boundaries.
findings.defense: Not every method needs to appear in one minimal repository example.

findings.title: THIRD_NORMAL_FORM_IS_OVERCLAIMED
findings.evidence: T1-A equates a few anti-duplication choices with 'Normaliza a 3NF'.
findings.impact: Learner may think 'do not copy canonical_name' is a sufficient definition of 3NF.
findings.attack: 3NF is a dependency-based property of the complete relation design; the section neither states functional dependencies nor proves the whole model satisfies it.
findings.defense: The phrase is used as a practical design heuristic rather than a normalization proof.

findings.title: REDACTION_WIDOW_TERMS_AND_LANGUAGE_MIX
findings.evidence: High density of append-only, provenance, fan-out, blocking, CTE, window, anti-join, pending, upsert, pooling, acquire and repository appears with uneven Spanish anchoring.
findings.impact: Cognitive load is spent decoding vocabulary instead of relational invariants.
findings.attack: The learner is at Level 3 but the section still introduces multiple new systems terms per paragraph without a stable Spanish-first glossary.
findings.defense: Many are unavoidable API/industry terms and several are glossed locally.

findings.title: S29-F06 duplicate canonical candidate pair accepted despite prose promising UNIQUE
S29-F08 decisions are mutable/deletable despite append-only truth-store claim
S29-F09/F10/F18 evidence/provenance references are not enforced or linked to exact decision versions
S29-F12/F13 review queue semantics hide review states and rank before filtering pending cases
S29-F20 stale replay overwrites newer entity state
S29-F21 entity upsert contradicts roadmap requirement to preserve entity history
S29-F22 IntegrityError is treated as retryable conflict without classifying permanent invariant failures
S29-F27 repository abstraction drops the constraints taught earlier
S29-F30 persistence/reopen behavior is never tested
S29-F32 deleting source/entity links would erase membership history
PREREQUISITE_TRUTH_STORE_NOT_CREDITABLE
findings.evidence: S30 says S29's pair/decision store feeds the engine, but S29 audit confirmed duplicate canonical pairs, mutable decisions, unconstrained labels and free-form evidence refs.
findings.impact: A probabilistic engine can learn/evaluate against non-reconstructable truth and then export clusters as if evidence were stable.
findings.fix: Validate canonical pair uniqueness, immutable/versioned labels, source/entity version and evidence provenance at the S29→S30 boundary.
findings.attack: Training/evaluating from those rows can duplicate examples, mutate historical labels or detach evidence after the fact.
findings.defense: S30 uses synthetic examples and does not explicitly claim production data ingestion.

findings.title: TESTABLE_ENGINE_WITHOUT_PYTEST_GATES
findings.evidence: The section calls the engine testable and invokes S27/S28 suite, but theory blocks end in print outputs rather than pytest assertions/failure gates.
findings.impact: The section's defining gate remains observational rather than executable in the canonical lesson.
findings.fix: Turn comparator, blocking, threshold, cluster and evaluation contracts into collected pytest tests.
findings.attack: A behavior-changing regression can still exit 0 if printed output is not inspected.
findings.defense: The blocks are demonstrations, not the final You Do suite.
findings.location: tagline/reference promotion + all 8 theory code blocks

findings.title: SCORE_ROLE_CONTRADICTION
findings.evidence: Opening/job text says the score only orders a human queue, while T3-A performs auto_match/non_match and T3-B auto-unions pairs into clusters.
findings.impact: Contradictory automation boundary undermines human-control semantics.
findings.fix: State explicitly that identity scores may drive bounded auto-match/non-match only when calibrated/validated; fraud/risk remains out of scope, and uncertain/insufficient evidence routes to review.
findings.attack: Learner cannot tell whether score is advisory-only or can trigger automatic identity merges/rejections.
findings.defense: The ethical intent is to distinguish identity decisions from fraud/risk conclusions.

findings.title: EMAIL_LOCAL_PART_CASE_COLLAPSE
findings.evidence: exact() casefolds the entire email; RFC 5321 requires preserving/treating mailbox local-part case sensitivity while domain is case-insensitive, even though case-sensitive mailboxes are discouraged.
findings.impact: An exact comparator can manufacture strong identity evidence.
findings.fix: Preserve raw email; normalize domain case; make any provider-specific local-part canonicalization an explicit, tested policy rather than universal casefold.
findings.attack: Two distinct mailbox local-parts can become an exact identity agreement.
findings.defense: Most modern providers behave case-insensitively and pedagogical fixtures are synthetic.
findings.location: T1-A comparators.py / I Do exact email

findings.title: COMPARATORS_LACK_SHARED_UNICODE_NORMALIZATION
findings.evidence: exact/token use casefold+split, edit uses raw strings, blocking separately requires accent folding; NFC vs NFD José scores 0 in exact/token.
findings.impact: Comparator inconsistency corrupts weights and candidate recall.
findings.fix: Define one shared normalization pipeline with explicit field-specific policies and test NFC/NFD before all comparators/blocking.
findings.attack: The same visible identity receives different evidence solely due to Unicode representation/comparator path.
findings.defense: T2 intentionally demonstrates accent-folding as a blocking lesson.

findings.title: EDIT_EMPTY_EMPTY_BECOMES_PERFECT_MATCH
findings.evidence: edit_sim('', '') returns 1.0 while exact/token return missing and prose says two empties are not agreement.
findings.impact: Mathematical similarity is incorrectly promoted to identity evidence in violation of the section's missing contract.
findings.fix: Apply missing precondition before edit/date comparators; return None/ComparisonResult(missing).
findings.attack: A missing name can contribute maximal evidence if routed through edit comparator.
findings.defense: Mathematically edit distance of two empty strings is zero.

findings.title: DATE_COMPARATOR_MISSING_CRASH
findings.evidence: date_sim(None, valid_date) raises TypeError.
findings.impact: The public comparator API is brittle and the missing contract is not centralized/enforced.
findings.fix: Use a wrapper/result type that checks missing before every comparator and carries observed/missing state.
findings.attack: Real missing birth dates are expected by T1-B but date comparator cannot represent them.
findings.defense: T1-A says comparators assume observed inputs.

findings.title: FREQUENCY_WEIGHT_NEVER_REACHES_SCORER
findings.evidence: frequency_weight is demonstrated separately; pair_score uses static weights and never consumes per-value frequency adjustment.
findings.impact: A learned concept has no effect on the actual matching decision.
findings.fix: Carry effective per-field/per-value contribution into the scorer and explanation, or narrow the outcome to conceptual demonstration.
findings.attack: Outcome promises frequent-value downweighting but decision path ignores it.
findings.defense: It is presented as a didactic heuristic rather than full FS term-frequency adjustment.

findings.title: MISSING_BLOCK_KEYS_COLLIDE
findings.evidence: Missing/blank name and city map to the same key '|'.
findings.impact: Missingness can explode candidate cost and contaminate candidate sets.
findings.fix: Fail/route missing blocking attributes or use multiple safe rules with explicit missing-key policy and max-block guard.
findings.attack: Many incomplete records can create the exact monster block T2-B warns against, and may generate low-quality comparisons.
findings.defense: The fixture has complete name/city fields.

findings.title: MISSING_DENOMINATOR_CONTRADICTION
findings.evidence: Prose says missing fields are omitted from numerator and denominator; pair_score iterates all weights and TypeErrors when a similarity is None.
findings.impact: Theory code contradicts the lesson's most important missing-data safeguard.
findings.fix: Build observed keys first and compute numerator/denominator only from finite non-None similarities.
findings.attack: The central missingness policy is not implemented in canonical scorer.
findings.defense: The You Do starter later contains an observed-key variant.

findings.title: ZERO_EVIDENCE_AUTO_NON_MATCH
findings.evidence: No observed fields yields score 0.0, and decide(0.0) returns non_match.
findings.impact: Directly violates missing≠disagreement and can create false negatives without human review.
findings.fix: Represent insufficient evidence separately (None/abstain) and route to review/no-decision, not non_match.
findings.attack: Absence of evidence becomes evidence of different identity.
findings.defense: 0.0 is a convenient numeric fallback.

findings.title: THRESHOLD_CONTRACT_UNVALIDATED
findings.evidence: No validation for finite score or 0<=t_low<t_high<=1; t_high=.5,t_low=.9 makes score .7 auto_match.
findings.impact: A configuration error can auto-merge records under nonsensical thresholds.
findings.fix: Validate score finite/in-range and threshold ordering before decisions.
findings.attack: Misconfiguration can invert/overlap policy regions silently; NaN falls through to review without being rejected.
findings.defense: Defaults are sensible in the toy fixture.

findings.title: THRESHOLDS_AND_WEIGHTS_NOT_ESTIMATED
findings.evidence: Weights and .9/.5 thresholds are hardcoded; no training/selection function consumes the labelled training split or business cost/capacity.
findings.impact: The main decision policy is asserted rather than evaluated.
findings.fix: Separate didactic baseline from an executable threshold-selection exercise on train labels; freeze selection before holdout evaluation.
findings.attack: Roadmap explicitly calls for entrenamiento/estimación and the prose says threshold choice has asymmetric consequences.
findings.defense: The section labels the scorer didactic and permits hand-set weights.

findings.title: PROBABILISTIC_TITLE_WITH_NO_PROBABILISTIC_ESTIMATION
findings.evidence: No prior match probability, m/u estimation or conversion to match probability is executed; current Splink/Fellegi-Sunter materials define trained match weights from m/u and probabilistic scoring.
findings.impact: Section title/roadmap competency is not achieved by canonical theory code even though the disclaimer prevents a worse misconception.
findings.fix: Either implement a minimal genuine FS estimation path or rename/narrow the executable claim to an interpretable heuristic ER baseline that prepares for probabilistic ER.
findings.attack: Weighted average similarity is not itself probabilistic ER.
findings.defense: The prose explicitly says simplified didactic and not calibrated probability.

findings.title: CLERICAL_QUEUE_RECORD_INCOMPLETE
findings.evidence: Prose requires actor/timestamp/actions; code stores only pair, score and explain.
findings.impact: Review cannot be audited or reconciled with S29 truth-store semantics.
findings.fix: Use a review item/decision contract with pair_id/version, source/evidence refs, allowed actions, actor, timestamp and status.
findings.attack: No reviewer identity, decision state, artifact/version, timestamps or evidence provenance exists.
findings.defense: The list is a minimal in-memory illustration.

findings.title: COMMENT_AS_HUMAN_APPROVAL
findings.evidence: The code comments 'clerical: aprueba e3-e4' and directly calls uf.union without validating/storing an approval event.
findings.impact: The learner sees no executable boundary between proposal and approved merge.
findings.fix: Pass an immutable approved decision record from S29 into merge logic and reject uncertain/missing/unapproved states.
findings.attack: A source-code comment substitutes for the human review that gates a destructive cluster merge.
findings.defense: The code is illustrating the effect after approval.

findings.title: UNION_FIND_CANNOT_ENFORCE_NEGATIVE_CONSTRAINTS
findings.evidence: Prose says review contradictions such as A=B, B!=C, A=C; UnionFind stores only positive connectivity and no non_match constraints.
findings.impact: A bridge can merge entities despite an explicit negative clerical label.
findings.fix: Maintain cannot-link/non-match constraints and validate proposed component merge against them before union.
findings.attack: The advertised contradiction check is impossible with the shown data structure alone.
findings.defense: Union-Find is appropriate for transitive positive closure and prose warns about bridges.

findings.title: AUTO_UNIONS_HAVE_NO_SCORE_OR_PROVENANCE
findings.evidence: e1-e2 and e2-e3 are literal 'auto matches' unioned without score, threshold version, comparator contributions, source versions or decision ids.
findings.impact: The graph boundary inherits opaque identity merges.
findings.fix: Every union must consume a validated pair-decision artifact with provenance and decision policy version.
findings.attack: Clusters exported to S31 cannot be reconstructed from evidence.
findings.defense: They are tiny synthetic setup edges.

findings.title: EVALUATION_DISCONNECTED_FROM_ENGINE
findings.evidence: T4-B uses hardcoded y_true/y_pred, hardcoded clusters and pred_pairs unrelated to T2 candidates, T3 scores/thresholds or T4-A test split.
findings.impact: The promotion gate does not actually evaluate the engine it claims to close.
findings.fix: Generate holdout predictions from the frozen S30 pipeline and feed those exact pair ids/labels into pairwise and cluster metrics.
findings.attack: Metrics can remain unchanged while the engine logic is broken.
findings.defense: Toy vectors isolate metric formulas for teaching.

findings.title: PRF_ZIP_TRUNCATION_FALSE_PERFECT_METRICS
findings.evidence: prf([1,0],[1]) returns precision=recall=F1=1.0 because zip silently ignores the unmatched second label.
findings.impact: Evaluation helper can produce a materially false green.
findings.fix: Assert equal nonzero lengths, aligned pair ids and allowed labels before metric calculation.
findings.attack: Missing predictions can disappear from denominators.
findings.defense: Canonical vectors have equal length.

findings.title: COCLUSTER_QUALITY_CAN_HIDE_TRANSITIVE_OVERMERGE
findings.evidence: Function divides over caller-provided pred_pairs instead of enumerating all unordered pairs that the predicted clusters co-locate. A 3-node predicted cluster with gold only e1-e2 scores 1.0 if caller passes only edge e1-e2, but true pair precision across the cluster is 1/3.
findings.impact: Exactly the overmerge failure cluster metrics are meant to expose can be missed.
findings.fix: Derive all co-cluster unordered pairs from predicted clusters or use established cluster metrics; never trust a hand-supplied edge list as the cluster denominator.
findings.attack: Union-Find's transitive closure creates implied pairs not present in the edge list.
findings.defense: The demo explicitly passes the only predicted pair in its tiny scenario and labels metric simplified.

findings.title: ERROR_SLICES_OUTCOME_NOT_IMPLEMENTED
findings.evidence: Code prints only integer error indices; no source/missing_phone/common_last_name/city attributes are joined or aggregated into slices.
findings.impact: The learner cannot diagnose systematic error from canonical evidence.
findings.fix: Carry pair metadata and aggregate FP/FN/support by declared slices on holdout predictions.
findings.attack: Outcome promises actionable error slices but no slice is calculated.
findings.defense: Paragraph calls the indices the seed of a slice.

findings.title: ER_FEATURES_AND_DECISIONS_DROP_S29_PROVENANCE
findings.evidence: Comparison outputs/explain dicts carry similarities only; pair/source/entity version, comparator/model version, label decision id and evidence refs are absent.

findings.attack: Later entity changes or stale replays can retroactively change what a training label appears to mean.
findings.defense: All data are synthetic and focused on algorithmic concepts.

findings.title: UNRESERVED_SYNTHETIC_DOMAIN
findings.evidence: Fixtures repeatedly use @example.pe. IANA reserves example.com/example.org and special-use .test, not example.pe.
findings.impact: Unsafe habit crosses into later integration workflows.
findings.fix: Use @equipo.test or @example.com.
findings.attack: Copied fixtures can accidentally target a registrable/routable namespace.
findings.defense: No email is actually sent in theory.

findings.title: WHITESPACE_IS_NOT_MISSING
findings.evidence: Only None or exact empty string is missing; whitespace-only values are treated as observed disagreement/agreement after casefold.
findings.impact: Pipeline behavior depends on undocumented preprocessing order.
findings.fix: Normalize/strip first or define missing via canonicalized value and test whitespace-only inputs.
findings.attack: Source cleaning commonly yields whitespace placeholders.
findings.defense: Earlier normalization may be intended to trim fields.

findings.title: FREQUENCY_TABLE_DOMAIN_UNVALIDATED
findings.evidence: freq 0 raises ZeroDivisionError; negative count returns negative identity weight.
findings.impact: The heuristic lacks a basic data contract.
findings.fix: Validate finite positive counts/support and define unseen-value policy.
findings.attack: Malformed or stale frequency tables create invalid scores.
findings.defense: The toy dictionary contains only positive counts.

findings.title: INFORMATIVE_MISSINGNESS_ONLY_NARRATED
findings.evidence: Prose says model missingness by source_system; no code accepts source_system or estimates source-specific missing patterns.
findings.impact: Outcome overstates treatment of informative missingness.
findings.fix: Add source-aware missingness diagnostics/policy or explicitly defer modeling and narrow the claim.
findings.attack: MCAR warning has no executable consequence.
findings.defense: The section intentionally stays with a simple observed-field scorer.

findings.title: BLOCK_KEY_NONE_CITY_CRASH
findings.evidence: rec.get('city','')[:3] crashes when city exists with None.
findings.impact: Blocking fails before scorer on valid missing-data states.
findings.fix: Normalize null/blank explicitly and validate field type.
findings.attack: Schema missingness may be represented as null, not absent key.
findings.defense: Synthetic fixture uses strings.

findings.title: CANDIDATE_RECALL_NO_POSITIVE_SUPPORT_CRASH
findings.evidence: len(gold & candidates)/len(gold) raises ZeroDivisionError when a slice contains no gold matches.
findings.impact: Metric code is not robust and can hide unsupported slices.
findings.fix: Return NA/None with support=0 and always report denominator.
findings.attack: Evaluation by slice can legitimately have zero positives.
findings.defense: Main synthetic gold contains one match.

findings.title: BLOCK_COST_FORMULA_NOT_DEDUPED_ACROSS_OR_RULES
findings.evidence: sum C(n_b,2) is exact for disjoint buckets from one partition, but multiple OR blocking rules can produce the same pair more than once before dedup; Splink reports cumulative unique comparisons across rule lists.
findings.impact: Cost estimation does not generalize to the multi-rule strategy taught immediately before it.
findings.fix: State the scope and, for OR rules, compute/deduplicate candidate pair identities or use cumulative comparisons.
findings.attack: Learner may sum per-rule bucket costs and overstate actual unique scored pairs or miss rule-order effects.
findings.defense: The code accepts one list of disjoint block sizes, where the formula is valid.

findings.title: CALIBRATION_TERM_OVERLOADED
findings.evidence: 'Calibración' is used for tuning weights/thresholds while the score is explicitly not probability-calibrated; later curriculum uses calibration in the reliability/Brier sense.
findings.impact: Terminology creates future conceptual debt.
findings.fix: Call this 'ajuste/selección de pesos y umbrales'; reserve probability calibration for reliability calibration.
findings.attack: Learner may conflate threshold tuning with probability calibration.
findings.defense: The paragraph defines its local meaning.

findings.title: LABEL_SPACE_PRINT_NOT_ENFORCEMENT
findings.evidence: The allowed labels are printed as a static list; no API validates incoming label values or blocks fraud/other strings.
findings.impact: A stated safety boundary has no executable gate.
findings.fix: Use enum/check constraint and explicit parser rejecting out-of-domain labels.
findings.attack: S29 already allows arbitrary decision labels.
findings.defense: The ethics boundary is repeated in prose/callout.

findings.title: METRIC_LABEL_DOMAIN_UNVALIDATED
findings.evidence: Only exact integer 0/1 comparisons count; unexpected labels/booleans/None can silently fall outside tp/fp/fn accounting.
findings.impact: Dirty label data can silently shrink effective support.
findings.fix: Validate schema/domain and report support/confusion counts.
findings.attack: S29 decision labels are currently unconstrained strings.
findings.defense: Synthetic vectors are binary integers.

findings.title: EMPTY_SUPPORT_REPORTED_AS_ZERO_PERFORMANCE
findings.evidence: Empty gold or empty predicted pair sets return 0.0 without support metadata.
findings.impact: Small slices become misleading and incomparable.
findings.fix: Return NA/None plus numerator/denominator/support.
findings.attack: No evidence is conflated with measured zero quality/completeness.
findings.defense: Returning 0 avoids division errors in toy code.

findings.title: PREVALENCE_REQUIRED_BUT_NOT_REPORTED
findings.evidence: Prose requires match rate/base rate in the gold; theory code reports only split counts/overlap.
findings.impact: Canonical theory does not demonstrate a metric it says must accompany evaluation.
findings.fix: Report positives/negatives/prevalence for train and holdout alongside P/R/F1.
findings.attack: P/R interpretation loses essential context in imbalanced ER.
findings.defense: The prevalence exercise appears later outside lessons-only theory.

findings.title: Graph nodes/clusters can persist false ER merges as if they were relational truth.
findings.evidence: Roadmap requires S30; authoritative roadmap also says S31 must not start until S30/CP-N3-A is approved, while S30 audit is REPAIR_REQUIRED.
findings.impact: Graph nodes/clusters can persist false ER merges as if they were relational truth.
findings.fix: Declare S30 artifacts untrusted until upstream regression/gate passes; graph fixtures should be independent synthetic truth meanwhile.

findings.title: A bad identity merge becomes a supernode that fabricates downstream paths and centrality.
findings.evidence: Text says S30 resolved identities and canonical ER ids feed graph nodes, but S30 union edges lack required immutable decision/evidence/cannot-link provenance.
findings.impact: A bad identity merge becomes a supernode that fabricates downstream paths and centrality.
findings.fix: Require node lineage back to canonical pair, source/entity versions, decision/evidence ids and model/policy version.

findings.title: Broken provenance/path semantics can still look green in screenshots/output.
findings.evidence: Since S27 roadmap requires systematic pytest, but S31 mostly prints outputs and uses plain asserts; graph invariants do not produce a section-level pytest gate.
findings.impact: Broken provenance/path semantics can still look green in screenshots/output.
findings.fix: Move graph invariants and regression cases into pytest with failing exit status.

findings.title: A node pair can have several edges but a path cannot name which exact observation supports the hop.
findings.evidence: Section requires a multigraph and citable evidence per hop, yet no stable edge_id/key is defined for parallel edges.
findings.impact: A node pair can have several edges but a path cannot name which exact observation supports the hop.
findings.fix: Give each raw/derived edge a stable edge_id and preserve MultiGraph-style edge keys.

findings.title: The course's own minimum provenance contract is not met by its canonical examples.
findings.evidence: Prose defines provenance as source_system+run_id+record_id. T1-A stores only record_id; T1-B stores source+record_id, no run_id and field naming differs.
findings.impact: The course's own minimum provenance contract is not met by its canonical examples.
findings.fix: One edge schema with source_system, run_id, record_id, edge_id and timestamp/version fields where applicable.

findings.title: Derived relationship loses the two observations and derivation that justify it.
findings.evidence: shared_phone/shared_email are declared derived shortcuts, but shared_phone carries a single record_id as if one source row proved a two-entity shared-value relation.
findings.impact: Derived relationship loses the two observations and derivation that justify it.
findings.fix: Derived edge references both source observations plus derivation/version; primary contact-node edges remain authoritative.

findings.title: Learner cannot know whether a direct entity transfer edge is valid and paths erase account ownership hops.
findings.evidence: Reference says transfer is account→account, never person→person; multigraph_prov creates transfer E1→E2 entities.
findings.impact: Learner cannot know whether a direct entity transfer edge is valid and paths erase account ownership hops.
findings.fix: Keep transfer account→account or label any entity-level edge explicitly as a derived projection with provenance.

findings.title: Edges from incompatible years can be combined into a misleading relationship path.
findings.evidence: Text promises path/aggregate filtering by time window; code only stores/sorts timestamps and never filters a window.
findings.impact: Edges from incompatible years can be combined into a misleading relationship path.
findings.fix: Implement window predicate and preserve timezone-aware timestamps; test inclusion/exclusion boundaries.

findings.title: The main table→graph transformation produces unauditable edges.
findings.evidence: Builder emits owns/transfer/has_phone/has_email edges without record_id/source_system/run_id/ts despite reference input contract.
findings.impact: The main table→graph transformation produces unauditable edges.
findings.fix: Every emitted edge inherits exact source row identity and run provenance.

findings.title: An entity id equal to a phone/email/account string silently collapses distinct node types.
findings.evidence: Entity ids, account ids and raw contact values are unioned into one set of strings without kind namespace.
findings.impact: An entity id equal to a phone/email/account string silently collapses distinct node types.
findings.fix: Use typed node keys such as ('entity',id), ('account',id), ('phone',normalized_value_id).

findings.title: PII remains embedded in graph identity, logs, serialized payloads and screenshots even if labels are redacted.
findings.evidence: Raw emails and phones are node IDs; T4 only masks display labels.
findings.impact: PII remains embedded in graph identity, logs, serialized payloads and screenshots even if labels are redacted.
findings.fix: Use pseudonymous contact-value ids; authorized evidence store resolves them separately.

findings.title: A duplicate ingestion row can fabricate a shared-contact signal.
findings.evidence: shared = len(phones) != len(set(phones)) detects duplicate rows, not two distinct entities sharing the same phone.
findings.impact: A duplicate ingestion row can fabricate a shared-contact signal.
findings.fix: Group normalized value→distinct canonical entity ids and require cardinality >=2.

findings.title: Lineage from raw identities to canonical nodes is promised but absent.
findings.evidence: Narrative requires raw_id→canonical_id map to rewrite edges; dedup_agg code never implements the map or rewiring.
findings.impact: Lineage from raw identities to canonical nodes is promised but absent.
findings.fix: Persist resolution-map version and use it explicitly during edge projection.

findings.title: Retries inflate money/frequency and hub/path evidence.
findings.evidence: Aggregation does not deduplicate record_id; replay of tx-1 doubles sum/count and stores tx-1 twice.
findings.impact: Retries inflate money/frequency and hub/path evidence.
findings.fix: Dedup by immutable source-event identity before aggregation; flag conflicting duplicate payloads.

findings.title: A reviewer cannot resolve ambiguous record ids across systems/runs or verify temporal scope.
findings.evidence: Aggregate retains only record_id list, while source/run/time are omitted and min/max ts promised in prose are absent.
findings.impact: A reviewer cannot resolve ambiguous record ids across systems/runs or verify temporal scope.
findings.fix: Keep structured detail refs (source_system,run_id,record_id,ts) and derive summary metadata.

findings.title: Ten parallel transfers become degree 1, directly contradicting the lesson.
findings.evidence: Paragraph correctly defines degree as number of incident edges in multigraph; code stores neighbors in set and degree=len(adj[n]), counting distinct neighbors instead.
findings.impact: Ten parallel transfers become degree 1, directly contradicting the lesson.
findings.fix: Represent edge multiplicity or use MultiGraph degree; separately expose unique-neighbor count.

findings.title: Case isolates disappear from graph-quality/cardinality checks.
findings.evidence: components() iterates adjacency keys created from edges; isolated declared nodes never appear. NetworkX defines a single isolated node as a connected component.
findings.impact: Case isolates disappear from graph-quality/cardinality checks.
findings.fix: Build components over explicit node set plus adjacency.

findings.title: The gate asks 'what supports each step?' but code cannot answer it.
findings.evidence: Paragraph says reproducible path lists nodes and supporting edges/record_ids; bfs_path returns only node list.
findings.impact: The gate asks 'what supports each step?' but code cannot answer it.
findings.fix: Return ordered hops containing edge_id, type, direction, ts, source/run/record refs.

findings.title: Even if later adding edge evidence, the traversal no longer knows which multiedge was used.
findings.evidence: adjacency set collapses all parallel edge distinctions and metadata before BFS.
findings.impact: Even if later adding edge evidence, the traversal no longer knows which multiedge was used.
findings.fix: Traverse edge records/keys, not neighbor-only set, and define deterministic edge-selection rule.

findings.title: A path can stitch edges that never coexisted in the case window.
findings.evidence: BFS ignores timestamps/windows entirely.
findings.impact: A path can stitch edges that never coexisted in the case window.
findings.fix: Filter eligible edges by explicit as-of/window before traversal and include window in returned evidence.

findings.title: The advertised quality gate does not test the graph it claims to validate.
findings.evidence: Text requires self-loop, graph weight, provenance and idempotence tests; code asserts reachability plus all(w>=0 for w in [1,2,0]), an unrelated literal list.
findings.impact: The advertised quality gate does not test the graph it claims to validate.
findings.fix: Create pytest fixtures with actual edge metadata and explicit red tests for each invariant.

findings.title: Most stated invariants are impossible to verify after construction.
findings.evidence: build(edges) accepts only (u,v) and discards type, weight, provenance and time.
findings.impact: Most stated invariants are impossible to verify after construction.
findings.fix: Test the canonical typed edge model rather than a metadata-free shadow graph.

findings.title: A missing evidence object can render as a blank hop instead of blocking the explanation.
findings.evidence: edge_evidence uses store.get(edge_id,{}) and silently returns empty dict for unknown edge.
findings.impact: A missing evidence object can render as a blank hop instead of blocking the explanation.
findings.fix: Raise EvidenceNotFound/return typed error; path publication fails closed when any hop evidence is unavailable.

findings.title: Learner cannot reproduce the advertised reviewer evidence panel.
findings.evidence: Storyboard says each hop shows records, ts and source; the store contains records/source but no ts.
findings.impact: Learner cannot reproduce the advertised reviewer evidence panel.
findings.fix: Store per-record timestamps or detail refs and render exact hop evidence.

findings.title: The section gate's principal user flow exists only in prose.
findings.evidence: Storyboard path is E1→ph:900→E2, but code contains only one direct transfer edge and never constructs ego/path/hop clicks.
findings.impact: The section gate's principal user flow exists only in prose.
findings.fix: Execute the same CASO-LIM-031 path through graph builder, ego extraction, traversal and evidence resolver.

findings.title: The visual teaches a topology that the reference explicitly forbids and erases ownership evidence.
findings.evidence: Figure alt says Ana is directly connected to Luis through a transfer, but canonical schema says transfer is account→account and entity relationship path must preserve owns hops.
findings.impact: The visual teaches a topology that the reference explicitly forbids and erases ownership evidence.
findings.fix: Draw entity→owns→account→transfer→account←owns←entity, or label any direct entity transfer edge as a derived projection with source path.

findings.title: Synthetic examples can accidentally cross a real namespace boundary.
findings.evidence: Uses @example.pe; IANA reserves example.com/example.org and special-use test names, not example.pe.
findings.impact: Synthetic examples can accidentally cross a real namespace boundary.
findings.fix: Use @equipo.test or example.com.

findings.title: Aggregations/rankings can combine semantically different quantities.
findings.evidence: T1-A requires units per etype; T1-B uses generic amount for transfer and shared_email, with no unit.
findings.impact: Aggregations/rankings can combine semantically different quantities.
findings.fix: Use weight+unit consistently and avoid amount on non-monetary edges.

findings.title: Retry/reingestion can duplicate multiedges or aggregates.
findings.evidence: Text says stable ids make construction idempotent; stable node labels alone do not prevent duplicate edge materialization on replay.
findings.impact: Retry/reingestion can duplicate multiedges or aggregates.
findings.fix: Define edge identity/upsert/replay semantics and test build(build_input twice) equivalence.

findings.title: Different units/windows can be merged into one summary.
findings.evidence: Prose says key includes unit/window when applicable; code key is only src,dst,etype.
findings.impact: Different units/windows can be merged into one summary.
findings.fix: Version aggregation policy and include unit/window/direction dimensions explicitly.

findings.title: Learner may think switching libraries automatically solves evidence-path provenance.
findings.evidence: Callout says networkx.shortest_path covers the same contract on MultiGraph; current NetworkX returns a list of nodes for source+target, not edge keys/evidence.
findings.impact: Learner may think switching libraries automatically solves evidence-path provenance.
findings.fix: Say NetworkX covers shortest-node-path traversal; edge-key/evidence resolution remains application logic.

findings.title: Ethical interpretation is narrated but not executable/auditable.
findings.evidence: Prose requires etype/time/node-kind context before prioritization; code has untyped timeless edges and literal not_guilt=True.
findings.impact: Ethical interpretation is narrated but not executable/auditable.
findings.fix: Compute metric on a declared filtered graph and return filter context alongside score.

findings.title: A nonexistent entity can appear as a one-node case subgraph.
findings.evidence: With defaultdict, ego(adj,'MISSING') returns {'MISSING'} instead of applying a declared missing-seed policy.
findings.impact: A nonexistent entity can appear as a one-node case subgraph.
findings.fix: Validate seed membership and raise typed error or return explicit not_found result.

findings.title: Masking can be mistaken for access control.
findings.evidence: Prose says roles see only what they need; code implements display masking only, no role/authorization check.
findings.impact: Masking can be mistaken for access control.
findings.fix: Bound the lab claim to redaction or add an explicit role-policy adapter/test.

findings.title: A declared scalability policy is represented by a string rather than behavior.
findings.evidence: Code prints 'subgraph_only' but implements neither n_nodes render threshold nor summary mode/top hubs/components/etype counts.
findings.impact: A declared scalability policy is represented by a string rather than behavior.
findings.fix: Implement small-vs-summary decision function with illustrative configurable threshold and tests.

findings.title: A wrong ER merge or graph edge becomes a learned feature and can contaminate every downstream baseline.
findings.evidence: Roadmap requires S31; continuation marks S31 REPAIR_REQUIRED with broken edge provenance, temporal traversal and graph invariants.
findings.impact: A wrong ER merge or graph edge becomes a learned feature and can contaminate every downstream baseline.
findings.fix: Gate S31 lineage/invariants before graph features; synthetic fixtures must reproduce the repaired contract.
findings.attack: S32 treats S31 graph outputs as usable feature inputs.
findings.defense: S32 uses a tiny synthetic graph fixture rather than claiming it is production truth.

findings.title: Feature evidence is unauditable and can inherit future or malformed graph state.
findings.evidence: T2-A graph_feats accepts attrs/neighbors/paths only; no edge_id, graph_version, as_of, etype filter, direction, source or record references.
findings.impact: Feature evidence is unauditable and can inherit future or malformed graph state.
findings.fix: Pass a versioned as-of graph view and persist derivation metadata with each relational feature.
findings.attack: The resulting degree/path/shared values cannot be reconstructed from evidence.
findings.defense: The prose says features are only topology observed in t.

findings.title: The section calls promotion failures gates without executable failure semantics.
findings.evidence: All eight theory demos end in prints or literal flags; no pytest gate is shown although the roadmap requires systematic pytest from S27.
findings.impact: The section calls promotion failures gates without executable failure semantics.
findings.fix: Convert each contract to pytest assertions/raises and keep prints only as diagnostics.
findings.attack: A broken feature definition can still exit zero.
findings.defense: The snippets are explanatory mini-demos.

findings.title: The catalog is not an executable schema and train/serve type drift can pass the gate.
findings.evidence: Prose/outcome promise dtype and missing policy; catalog_check validates only key membership.
findings.impact: The catalog is not an executable schema and train/serve type drift can pass the gate.

findings.title: Routing and feature ordering become ambiguous and versioning cannot describe the actual model inputs.
findings.evidence: set(schema[numeric]+categorical+text) hides duplicate membership; note_len is produced but schema registers raw note instead of the derived feature named in prose.

findings.defense: The fixed example has no duplicate keys.

findings.title: The lesson silently erases a missingness signal it later says must be preserved.
findings.evidence: catalog_check returns note_len=0 when note is absent.
findings.impact: The lesson silently erases a missingness signal it later says must be preserved.
findings.fix: Emit note_missing plus note_len only for observed text, or apply the catalog's explicit missing policy.
findings.attack: Missing text and an observed empty string become identical before the missing policy is applied.

findings.title: Pandas/NumPy-derived data can carry NaN into model features while silent_fill still prints False.

findings.impact: Pandas/NumPy-derived data can carry NaN into model features while silent_fill still prints False.
findings.fix: Use a documented missing predicate covering None/NaN for the supported data types.

findings.title: A routine edge case becomes an untyped runtime failure in serve.

findings.impact: A routine edge case becomes an untyped runtime failure in serve.

findings.title: A learner can mistake a hard-coded assertion for proof that train-only state was used.

findings.impact: A learner can mistake a hard-coded assertion for proof that train-only state was used.

findings.attack: The output claims a property that was not computed.

findings.title: The exact false-evidence pattern rejected in S30/S31 reappears as a model feature.

findings.title: Graph features can leak future relationships even if transaction windows elsewhere are half-open.
findings.evidence: graph_feats consumes current neighbors/path tables without feature cutoff or temporal edge filtering.
findings.impact: Graph features can leak future relationships even if transaction windows elsewhere are half-open.

findings.title: The model can interpret absence as ordered numeric evidence.

findings.title: The learner cannot tell whether roadmap 'distance' means geographic/entity distance or path distance and receives no distance contract.

findings.title: Outcome 'conteos y frecuencias' is not demonstrated and cannot be regression-tested.

findings.title: The key question 'would this value exist at t?' is not satisfied by occurrence time alone.

findings.attack: A successfully fitted training batch is indistinguishable from an unfitted transformer.

findings.title: Two runs carrying the same fs-v1 string can implement different vocab/scaling/catalog logic.

findings.title: Versioning is ceremonial rather than an enforceable compatibility boundary.

findings.title: Real data with entities on both sides cannot be split by the taught function; the learner has no method to produce a valid group-aware holdo…

findings.title: The later gate promotes based on an incomplete scanner and can miss obvious response-derived features.

findings.title: The core train≡serve gate is not tested; errors can cancel in aggregate.

findings.title: A learner sees diagnostics rather than an actual blocking gate, repeating the false-green pattern from S27-S31.

findings.title: A later production implementation may deserialize an untrusted or incompatible artifact.

findings.title: Learners may copy an unscaled threshold as a generic monitoring rule.

findings.title: Operators cannot distinguish response/future leakage from train-serving mismatch and choose the correct repair.

findings.title: The conceptual difficulty of leakage is compounded by avoidable terminology decoding.
findings.evidence: Dense code-switching includes feature catalog, dtype, row, keys, fill, z-score, vocab, one-hot, Pipeline, ColumnTransformer, custom transformer, joblib, pickle, group split, tol and CI; several are used before a concrete Spanish-first definition.

findings.title: The S32→S33 contract is not machine-valid and the prerequisite gate is bypassed.

findings.title: Train runs cannot prove which S32 transformation produced their features.

findings.title: The section called 'responsible baselines' does not mechanically reject irresponsible runs.

findings.impact: The section called 'responsible baselines' does not mechanically reject irresponsible runs.

findings.title: The learner can train on an ambiguous policy label and mistake it for ground truth.

findings.title: Prose fail-closed policy is not implemented.
findings.evidence: frame_task only checks substring 'fraud'. It does not enforce needs_review_*, horizon>0, or agreement between target suffix and horizon.
findings.impact: Prose fail-closed policy is not implemented.

findings.attack: Invalid framing passes the canonical helper.

findings.title: Right-censoring can contaminate training/evaluation labels.

findings.defense: All examples are synthetic and tiny.

findings.title: The executable contract is narrower than the prose without fail-closed validation.
findings.evidence: prevalence=sum(y)/len(y) and dummy_and_cost assume non-empty binary numeric labels without checking them.
findings.impact: The executable contract is narrower than the prose without fail-closed validation.
findings.fix: Validate support>0 and label domain exactly {0,1}; report positive support and prevalence.
findings.attack: Empty or multiclass/invalid labels crash or produce meaningless prevalence/cost.
findings.defense: Fixtures use 0/1.

findings.title: The baseline itself is leaked, invalidating the central comparison.
findings.evidence: dummy_and_cost(y) derives majority from the same y on which accuracy/cost are measured.
findings.impact: The baseline itself is leaked, invalidating the central comparison.

findings.defense: The canonical binary int fixture commonly yields 0.

findings.title: The code cannot distinguish a prior heuristic from a post-hoc optimized rule.

findings.fix: Record rule_id/version, threshold source and train-only selection or pre-model domain provenance before holdout evaluation.

findings.title: The declared business objective is not comparable across alternatives.

findings.title: The executable flag contradicts the lesson's own responsible-baseline doctrine.

findings.title: The section's headline gate is never actually executed end to end.

findings.impact: The section's headline gate is never actually executed end to end.

findings.title: The interpretability guardrails are presentation flags rather than validated model metadata.

findings.title: Progressive disclosure is weakened exactly where core supervised-evaluation skills are incomplete.

findings.impact: The ablation is methodologically uncontrolled and exact loss comparison is not attributable solely to tanh.

findings.title: The learner never demonstrates that a tree candidate learned from data or beat the baselines.

findings.impact: The learner never demonstrates that a tree candidate learned from data or beat the baselines.

findings.attack: A supervised tree lesson is reduced to thresholding and voting mechanics.

findings.title: The section's headline gate is advisory text rather than an executable decision.
findings.evidence: No canonical function blocks promotion based on best baseline, cost, split validity, S32 manifest, or CV results. Job relevance mentions dummy; theory later admits rule may be stronger.

findings.fix: Create a promotion function that requires valid upstream manifest/splits and candidate improvement over the best frozen baseline on the predeclared primary objective.
findings.attack: A model can be labeled beats_dummy=True and still lose to the rule, cost objective or invalid split.
findings.defense: The prose repeatedly states such a model should not be promoted.

findings.title: Unnecessary cognitive load and test/validation terminology drift.
findings.evidence: S33-overfit-gap is attached to T1-A unit/target/horizon and its alt says train/test/baseline although overfit is taught later using train-valid.
findings.impact: Unnecessary cognitive load and test/validation terminology drift.
findings.fix: Move the figure to T3-B and use train/valid consistently.
findings.attack: A future concept and inconsistent split name are injected before their explanation.
findings.defense: It previews the section's later problem.

findings.title: Concept-to-library bridge is time-sensitive and presently underspecified.
findings.evidence: Future-facing text teaches sklearn penalty='l2' + C. Current scikit-learn 1.8+ deprecates penalty and current docs express penalty choice via l1_ratio, while C remains inverse strength.
findings.impact: Concept-to-library bridge is time-sensitive and presently underspecified.
findings.fix: Pin the sklearn version for the lesson or teach the current l1_ratio/C API with a version note.
findings.attack: A learner following current API guidance receives stale parameter advice unless the course pins an older sklearn contract.
findings.defense: The snippet does not import sklearn and the L2 concept remains correct.

findings.title: An advanced model gate should distinguish invalid score from valid non-priority prediction.
findings.evidence: sigmoid(-1000) overflows and pred_at with NaN silently returns 0.
findings.impact: An advanced model gate should distinguish invalid score from valid non-priority prediction.
findings.fix: Validate finite z/x and use a numerically stable expit implementation.
findings.attack: Non-finite/big-magnitude inputs turn numerical invalidity into a negative class or exception.
findings.defense: Toy inputs are small and finite.

findings.title: A good complexity-control lesson becomes a false empirical rule.
findings.evidence: Text says a small neural network 'casi nunca gana' a well-made logistic regression on tabular data.
findings.impact: A good complexity-control lesson becomes a false empirical rule.
findings.fix: Say the network must beat a strong logistic baseline on this dataset; do not predict the winner generically.
findings.attack: Nonlinear tabular problems can strongly favor nonlinear models; the claim lacks scope/evidence.
findings.defense: It is intended to discourage unjustified complexity.

findings.title: Avoidable factual error in a nonessential tangent.
findings.evidence: T4-A says Meta's lab 'publicó PyTorch' in 2016. PyTorch Foundation history says development began in 2016 and PyTorch launched in 2017.
findings.impact: Avoidable factual error in a nonessential tangent.
findings.fix: Use 'el desarrollo comenzó en 2016 y el lanzamiento público llegó en 2017'.
findings.attack: Historical date is wrong.
findings.defense: 2016 is genuinely the development-start year.

findings.title: A transient market assertion distracts from S33 and can age rapidly.
findings.evidence: T4-A asserts 2026 PyTorch dominance in research/production and names Meta/OpenAI/Tesla without a learner-visible current source.
findings.impact: A transient market assertion distracts from S33 and can age rapidly.
findings.fix: Remove the ranking claim or cite a dated methodology and label it as a snapshot, not a durable curriculum fact.
findings.attack: Labor/usage share is time-sensitive and source-dependent; official PyTorch material supports broad research/production adoption, not this precise comparative labor-market claim.
findings.defense: PyTorch is undeniably a primary research/production platform and TensorFlow remains widely used.

findings.title: Seed is taught as a stronger guarantee than it is.
findings.evidence: seeded_ints calls global random.seed; prose equates a seed with auditable reproducibility.
findings.impact: Seed is taught as a stronger guarantee than it is.
findings.fix: Use a local RNG and log seed together with data, split, feature-set, code and library versions.
findings.attack: Global reseeding changes unrelated consumers, and reproducibility also depends on data/split/code/library/model versions.
findings.defense: The snippet only demonstrates seeded pseudo-random numbers.

findings.title: Widow term breaks progressive disclosure for the ZERO_TECH learner model.
findings.evidence: tracking example introduces f1 as a metric, while the roadmap teaches F-score in S34 and S33 never defines F1.
findings.impact: Widow term breaks progressive disclosure for the ZERO_TECH learner model.
findings.fix: Either define F1 briefly or keep S33 tracking to metrics already taught and introduce F1 in S34.
findings.attack: A next-section metric appears as if already learned.
findings.defense: F1 is common ML vocabulary and not manipulated here.

findings.title: The experiment summary lacks basic denominator evidence.
findings.evidence: mean_fold([]) divides by zero; fold support/validity is not stored with the mean.
findings.impact: The experiment summary lacks basic denominator evidence.
findings.fix: Reject empty folds and log per-fold support/groups/metric before aggregate mean/std.
findings.attack: Missing folds can crash or a mean can be reported without sample/group support.
findings.defense: Canonical fixture always has three folds.

findings.title: It weakens the core idea that ML must beat the strongest simple alternative, not merely majority.
findings.evidence: S33-baseline-gap visual compares majority/logistic/complex model but omits the simple rule that the section calls the second mandatory baseline.
findings.impact: It weakens the core idea that ML must beat the strongest simple alternative, not merely majority.
findings.fix: Include both dummy and rule baselines or label the chart explicitly as one illustrative baseline only.
findings.attack: The visual model makes 'baseline' look singular when the lesson later requires dual anchors.
findings.defense: A figure can simplify the comparison.

findings.title: Connective tissue is stale after source expansion from the older 28-paragraph version to the current 46-paragraph theory.
findings.evidence: The reference block says T4 closes with experiment logging + group CV and lists the roadmap sequence, but current theory also contains a five-paragraph NN block, a four-paragraph framework survey and a second temporal T4-B block.
findings.impact: Connective tissue is stale after source expansion from the older 28-paragraph version to the current 46-paragraph theory.
findings.fix: Either move extensions out or update the map with explicit optional/extension branches without pretending they are part of the core gate.
findings.attack: The learner-facing map no longer describes the actual section they must navigate.
findings.defense: Some additions are optional/extension material.

findings.title: S33-F09 dummy baseline is fit on the evaluation labels and can turn a proper 0% holdout baseline into 100%
S33-F04/F05/F06 target is not operationally observable/validated/mature despite being called observable
S33-F12/F13/F14 candidate comparison ignores consistent cost/best-baseline/same-holdout evaluation
S33-F15 logistic regression is never fit; L2 is a params label rather than training evidence
S33-F29/F33/F36 required Pipeline/CV does not fit preprocessing+model within folds
S33-F35 pairwise unit can leak an entity across folds because one group id cannot represent two endpoints
S33-F40 yesterday temporal baseline consumes validation-horizon actuals and is incomparable to the fixed-origin seasonal baseline
S33-F43 no executable promotion gate exists
S34 treats S33 scores as trustworthy although S33 remains REPAIR_REQUIRED with baseline leakage, no fitted logistic/CV and no promotion gate.
findings.fix: Reject scores unless a machine-valid S33 run manifest is supplied.
findings.attack: S33 quedó REPAIR_REQUIRED: dummy con leakage, logística no ajustada, CV no ejecutada y promotion gate inexistente.
findings.defense: El concepto de evaluar scores downstream es válido, pero solo si existe un run S33 machine-valid.

findings.title: No S34 metric/calibration API requires run_id, feature-set hash, split manifest, target/horizon or sample IDs.
findings.fix: Introduce PredictionRow/RunManifest lineage before evaluation.
findings.attack: Métricas/calibración pueden aplicarse a un vector sin saber qué modelo, datos o cutoff lo produjo.
findings.defense: Para una mini-demostración manual no hace falta un MLOps completo; para el gate curricular sí hace falta identidad mínima del artefacto.

findings.title: Critical policies are prints/literals such as accuracy_only=False, resample_global=False, accuracy_enough=False and force_label=False, not executable gates.
findings.fix: Turn policy invariants into pytest/assertions over real functions.
findings.attack: Cambiar el código real para violar la política no obliga a fallar el proceso.
findings.defense: Los prints sirven para explicación; no sirven como evidence gate desde S27.

findings.title: confusion_counts and average_precision use zip without cardinality or sample-id alignment; missing rows silently disappear.
findings.fix: Require one gold and one prediction per sample_id and equal validated cardinality.

findings.title: Binary metric helpers accept non-binary/NaN labels or predictions; invalid rows can disappear from TP/FP/FN/TN.
findings.fix: Validate finite binary domain before counting.

findings.title: Hand-rolled AP ranks tied scores individually; AP changes with input order whereas threshold-based AP must be tie-invariant.
findings.fix: Use sklearn average_precision_score or group tied scores by threshold.

findings.title: accuracy_only=False is written rather than derived, so REJECT_ACCURACY_ONLY cannot fire.
findings.fix: Validate the actual report fields.

findings.title: precision@k/recall@k receive only preordered labels, not scores; the helper cannot prove ranking order.
findings.fix: Accept keyed score/label rows and sort inside the metric boundary.

findings.title: k and n_pos are unvalidated; k=0 crashes, negative k yields nonsense, k>N changes denominator, and bad n_pos can make recall>1.
findings.fix: Require 1<=k<=N and derive n_pos from the eligible gold set.

findings.title: No stable rule exists when the top-k cutoff crosses equal scores; input order can change queue precision.
findings.fix: Version a deterministic secondary key or an explicit include-all-ties policy.

findings.title: top-k is measured on three rows while overload uses unrelated load=50/capacity=10, so the capacity evidence is disconnected from the ranked queue.
findings.fix: Derive n_review/load from the same eligible ranked rows and policy.

findings.title: The T1-B figure talks about uncertainty, five guards, invalid_input and accept although none exists in the top-k theory/code.
findings.fix: Replace with a ranking/capacity figure or move a coherent abstention figure to T4-B.

findings.title: apply_rebalance_in_fold does not rebalance anything and fold_plan hardcodes test_untouched=True even for resample_global=True.
findings.fix: Execute train-only weighting/resampling and make global resampling fail.

findings.title: weight_ratio has no support/domain contract; n1=0 divides by zero.
findings.fix: Require positive integer class counts and report support.

findings.title: StratifiedKFold is explained but never executed or checked for per-fold class support.
findings.fix: Build real folds and report class counts in every train/valid fold.

findings.title: Plain StratifiedKFold ignores S33 entity-pair grouping and can reintroduce endpoint leakage while balancing labels.
findings.fix: Use group-aware stratification/custom pair-endpoint grouping when unseen-entity generalization is the estimand.

findings.title: prevalence(pos,n) accepts impossible counts and divides by zero for n=0.
findings.fix: Validate n>0 and 0<=pos<=n.

findings.title: accuracy_enough=False is another literal rather than an executable prevalence-aware report gate.
findings.fix: Require base rate/support plus queue metrics in validate_imbalance_report.

findings.title: brier_mean silently truncates with zip, divides by len(ps), accepts empty/mismatched vectors and probabilities outside [0,1].
findings.fix: Validate sample alignment, binary labels, finite probabilities in [0,1] and non-empty support.

findings.title: All bins are half-open; the final [0.7,1.0) omits p=1.0 even though calibrate_affine clips outputs to exactly 1.0.
findings.fix: Make the final bin right-inclusive while keeping internal bins half-open.

findings.title: A single bin with abs(mean_p-freq)<=0.1 is elevated to calibrated=True with no support; chance agreement can certify a globally uncalibrated model.
findings.fix: Call it bin_aligned and assess multiple bins with support before a model-level calibration verdict.

findings.title: The paragraph says the affine map must not be called Platt while the code docstring calls it a simplified Platt implementation.
findings.fix: Rename it explicitly as an affine didactic calibrator, not Platt scaling.

findings.title: a=0.8,b=0.1 and calibrator_set='holdout_v1' are hard-coded; no fitting or split-disjointness is demonstrated.
findings.fix: Fit on an identified calibration split and persist split/model/calibrator provenance.

findings.title: The calibrator rounds to two decimals before downstream decisions and does not validate finite inputs or monotonic orientation; rounding 0.595 to 0.60 flips a threshold decision.
findings.fix: Keep full precision internally, round only display values and validate finite/monotone calibration parameters.

findings.title: The prose requires Brier/reliability on data not used to fit calibration, but canonical code never performs that evaluation or a final test.
findings.fix: Add calibration-fit and independent calibration-eval/final-test stages.

findings.title: choose_thr tunes directly on labeled rows without threshold-validation/final-test provenance; same-set reporting would be selection-biased.
findings.fix: Tune threshold on a named validation/CV artifact and evaluate the frozen policy once on untouched final test.

findings.title: choose_thr does not validate vector lengths, binary labels, finite scores, nonnegative costs, capacity or no-feasible-policy cases; capacity=0 returns None/inf.
findings.fix: Fail closed on invalid inputs and explicit no-feasible policy.

findings.title: The optimizer always rejects n_review==0, which can force a dominated policy when no review is legitimately cheapest.
findings.fix: Include threshold>max(score) as no-review or declare/validate min_reviews>0 as a business constraint.

findings.title: thr-v1 is a literal not bound to model, calibrator, cost matrix, capacity, prevalence or tuning snapshot.
findings.fix: Persist an immutable ThresholdManifest with hashes and policy parameters.

findings.title: T4-A optimizes one threshold, then T4-B replaces it with unrelated low=.3/high=.7 defaults; the final policy does not use the optimized thr-vN.
findings.fix: Optimize/version low/high as the same decision-policy artifact and explain their relation to cost/capacity.

findings.title: decide accepts NaN and inverted bands; NaN becomes abstain and low>high is not rejected.
findings.fix: Validate finite score and 0<=low<high<=1 before routing.

findings.title: The opening says the gray band exists so a human decides, but decide() returns abstain while review is reserved for >high; abstain routing and capacity consumption are undefined.
findings.fix: Define operational destinations for skip/review/abstain and count all human-routed cases toward capacity.

findings.title: The heading promises slices and sensitivity but code only counts binary-threshold flips; no slice table exists and force_label=False is hard-coded.
findings.fix: Compute support/P/R/cost/abstain-rate by slice and sensitivity of the full policy.

findings.title: Theory intentionally uses different tiny fixtures but never closes with one versioned prediction table flowing through metrics, calibration, threshold and abstention.
findings.fix: Keep hand-calculation mini-demos, then add one integrated out-of-sample evidence table before the section gate.
findings.attack: Los helpers pueden ser localmente correctos pero inconsistentes entre sí; no existe un canonical end-to-end evidence table antes del gate.
findings.defense: Los mini-sets facilitan cálculo a mano y son defendibles.

findings.title: AP is described as an approximation to PR-AUC and ROC as inflated by many TN; both are oversimplifications that create a false metric model.
findings.fix: Define AP separately from trapezoidal PR-AUC and explain why PR metrics are often more informative under rare positives.

findings.title: No-positive denominators collapse to metric=0 without support/undefined state.
findings.fix: Report support and zero_division/undefined status.

findings.title: The prose says stratification keeps the same class proportion in every fold; in practice it is approximate subject to discrete counts.
findings.fix: Say approximately the same proportion and retain absolute-support checks.

findings.title: Brier is framed too close to a calibration-only signal; it combines reliability/calibration, resolution/discriminative power and uncertainty.
findings.fix: State this limitation and use reliability curves for calibration shape.

findings.title: Equal-cost thresholds silently keep the first/lower threshold, often creating more review load without a documented preference.
findings.fix: Version an explicit tie-break such as lower load, higher recall or higher threshold.

findings.title: Abstention is first-class but coverage/abstain-rate/performance-on-decided cases are absent.
findings.fix: Report n_skip/n_review/n_abstain, coverage and consumed review capacity.
findings.attack: Dos policies pueden tener la misma precisión en decisiones automáticas con coberturas radicalmente distintas.
findings.defense: S34 puede reservar teoría formal de selective classification para después.

findings.title: Specificity, headcount, slice, reliability, Platt, isotonic, resampling, holdout and PR-AUC are introduced unevenly; specificity is used causally without definition.
findings.fix: Introduce Spanish-first meanings and the causal relationship each term serves.
findings.attack: El lector avanzado puede inferir varios; «especificidad» aparece causalmente en T2-B sin haberse definido.
findings.defense: No todo anglicismo es defecto y varios términos sí tienen glosa.

findings.title: T3-B calls calibration-fit/evaluation separation a way to avoid training-serving skew; this is evaluation leakage/in-sample optimism, not train-serving parity.
findings.fix: Use the correct leakage term and reserve train-serving skew for transformation/distribution parity.
findings.attack: Separar calibration-fit de evaluation evita evaluación in-sample/data leakage; train-serving skew es una diferencia entre transformaciones/distribuciones de train y serving.
findings.defense: La preocupación operacional es válida.

findings.title: REJECT_UNCALIBRATED is absolute although S34 itself notes an uncalibrated score can still rank usefully; calibration is mandatory only when the product interprets scores probabilistically or makes it an explicit gate.
findings.fix: State that ranking-only use need not imply probability, while CP-N3-B explicitly requires calibrated probabilities for its decision policy.
findings.attack: La necesidad de calibración depende de si el score se interpreta como probabilidad o si la policy exige probabilidades calibradas.
findings.defense: El producto de S34 sí declara una cola calibrada, por lo que puede imponerla como requisito interno.

findings.title: S35 consumes S34 scores/metrics/policies as if validated although S34 remains REPAIR_REQUIRED.
findings.fix: Require a machine-valid frozen S34 prediction/policy artifact before S35 analysis.

findings.title: jobRelevance calls the work queue a 'cola de fraude', reframing the inherited needs_review target as fraud.
findings.fix: Call it cola de revisión/triage and keep fraud outside target semantics.
