findings.title: No explanation/fairness/uncertainty artifact is bound to sample_id, model/run, feature-set, split, target, horizon, policy or evidence provenance.
findings.fix: Introduce a versioned CaseExplanation/PredictionRow lineage contract.

findings.title: means_fraud=False, causal=False and auto_fraud=False are hard-coded booleans, not validators of prose/actions/labels.
findings.fix: Validate structured claims/actions and reject forbidden semantics.

findings.title: The opening states that an unfamiliar case's correct answer is abstention as a universal truth.
findings.fix: Frame abstention/escalation as the lab's fail-closed policy when a validated knowledge-limit condition fires.

findings.title: Outcome says calculate permutation importance, but canonical code only sorts externally supplied drops.
findings.fix: Compute baseline and permuted scores from a fitted frozen model and evaluation rows.

findings.title: Permutation importance lacks an evaluated fitted model, held-out dataset, repeated shuffles, variability and row/run provenance.
findings.fix: Use frozen candidate, held-out/CV data, n_repeats and mean/std evidence.

findings.title: rank_by_drop crashes on empty drops, accepts NaN as top feature and has undocumented insertion-order tie break.
findings.fix: Validate non-empty finite drops and define deterministic ties.

findings.title: value×weight is not bound to a fitted model, transformed row or actual prediction and never verifies additivity/explanation accuracy.
findings.fix: Bind to one frozen model/input and verify baseline+sum(contrib) against actual output in declared space.

findings.title: T1-B promises a four-layer case card, but canonical theory code returns only contributions, a score and causal=False.
findings.fix: Build and validate all four layers in canonical T1-B evidence.

findings.title: Theory playground labels derived features ['shared_phone','amount_z_high'] as observed evidence.
findings.fix: Use source-record/evidence IDs in evidence layer and keep derived features in model layer.

findings.title: Slice metrics are hand-written aggregates and compared=True, not derived from frozen prediction rows.
findings.fix: Compute per-slice metrics from keyed out-of-sample rows.

findings.title: Total n is treated as minimum fairness evidence while metric-specific denominators, prevalence/support and uncertainty are absent.
findings.fix: Report confusion/support/prevalence and CI/equivalent uncertainty per slice.

findings.title: slice_flag accepts negative/fractional counts and classifies NaN as ok_n.
findings.fix: Require finite non-negative integer support and fail closed on invalid n.

findings.title: tag_from_evidence receives n_by_group but ignores it; tiny groups can be tagged high.
findings.fix: Validate group support/uncertainty before risk tags.

findings.title: association_gap and fp_rate_gap are undefined quantities placed on one arbitrary 0.15 threshold.
findings.fix: Define each statistic/denominator/uncertainty and separate policies.

findings.title: Case says district_code is removed and proxies mitigated without retraining/re-evaluating utility and group metrics.
findings.fix: Treat removal as candidate mitigation and rerun full evaluation.

findings.title: Toy p±q has no empirical uncertainty/conformal basis yet a band is required as uncertainty evidence.
findings.fix: Keep toy band as visualization scaffolding; require empirical uncertainty for a real gate.

findings.title: score_interval accepts out-of-range/nonfinite p, negative q, reversed/out-of-range bounds and rounds internally.
findings.fix: Validate finite p∈[0,1], q>0 and bounds; keep full precision internally.

findings.title: Outcome/headline says detect OOD, but max(|z|)>thr cannot detect stated unseen categorical channel or multivariate novelty.
findings.fix: Rename as univariate range check or implement detectors for declared novelty types.

findings.title: reference_split='train' plus assert does not prove z scores came from a train-fitted scaler; asserts can be disabled.
findings.fix: Carry scaler/reference manifest IDs and validate runtime provenance.

findings.title: is_ood crashes on empty input, treats NaN as in-domain and accepts negative thresholds.
findings.fix: Validate non-empty finite vectors and positive finite thresholds.

findings.title: OOD abstain is not bound to S34 frozen abstention/threshold policy, destination or capacity accounting.
findings.fix: Route OOD through the immutable decision-policy manifest/workload model.

findings.title: Four-field 'minimum' attributed to Mitchell et al. omits major Model Cards elements such as model/version, evaluation procedures/data, factors, analyses and caveats.
findings.fix: Call four fields the lab subset and show broader framework.

findings.title: card_ok returns True for use='fraud_label', contestability=False and empty owner if keys exist and fraud_label is out_of_scope.
findings.fix: Validate values, forbidden uses, non-empty owner and contestability semantics.

findings.title: contestability=True is only a boolean; no appeal channel/event/status/history exists.
findings.fix: Represent contestability as a traceable process/state contract.

findings.title: Card is not bound to actual model/version/data/evaluation metrics/threshold/calibrator/policy.
findings.fix: Persist immutable governed-model and evaluation references.

findings.title: Outcome says case/human/by are reconstructible while T4-B admits those fields are insufficient.
findings.fix: Require the full reconstructible event fields in outcome/gate.

findings.title: audit_event accepts empty case/human, arbitrary actions and malformed timestamps.
findings.fix: Validate identifiers, action enum, timestamp/timezone, reason and model/policy refs.

findings.title: Lifecycle is only a printed list; no transition function prevents invalid state changes.
findings.fix: Implement allowed transition graph and persist transition events.

findings.title: Prose says drift_flag retires preserving history, but code has no drift handling, retirement operation or history store.
findings.fix: Implement/verify retirement transition and append-only history.

findings.title: Portfolio fields still omit event_id, prior/new state, evidence/explanation/policy refs and append-only persistence.
findings.fix: Define immutable append-only AuditEvent lineage.

findings.title: Theory playground can print portfolio_ready=True without validating evidence, uncertainty, OOD provenance, slices, model-card completeness or audit lineage.
findings.fix: Make portfolio_ready consume validators for every required layer.

findings.title: Coefficient interpretation omits the model/output scale; logistic coefficients operate on log-odds, not probability.
findings.fix: State exact link/output scale and feature scaling before magnitude interpretation.

findings.title: Prose moves from group metric gaps to unequal harm without first defining harm, affected groups and fairness question.
findings.fix: Start with harm/group/context, then choose disaggregated metrics and uncertainty.

findings.title: 'Un score puntual engaña' plus q>0 can imply any nonzero band is more honest than a point estimate.
findings.fix: Say a point is incomplete when uncertainty matters; unjustified intervals are not improvements.

findings.title: Always-0.5 calibrated predictor is called 'bad Brier' without a prevalence/reference benchmark.
findings.fix: Compare Brier to appropriate references and avoid absolute bad/good labels.

findings.title: Extreme z is declared same-domain tail while unseen channel is domain shift; extreme values may also be shift/corruption.
findings.fix: Present these as hypotheses/signals requiring provenance checks.

findings.title: score, feature, slice, proxy, high-risk, mitigate, OOD, conformal, model card, contestability and override arrive rapidly with inconsistent Spanish-first definitions.
findings.fix: Introduce each term in Spanish first with role, input/output and consequence.

findings.title: S35-F01/F03 explanation and fairness artifacts inherit invalid S34 metrics/policies without frozen sample/run lineage
S35-F06/F07 permutation importance is never computed from an evaluated fitted model and lacks repeat variability
S35-F10/F12 local explanation is not bound to the real model and Theory playground mislabels derived features as observed evidence
S35-F13/F14/F16 slice analysis uses handwritten aggregates; invalid NaN support can become ok_n and uncertainty/denominators are absent
S35-F17/F18/F19 proxy risk ignores support, conflates unrelated gaps and claims mitigation without retraining/evaluation
S35-F20/F21 toy p±q can create invalid/reversed probability bands while serving as required uncertainty artifact
S35-F25/F26/F27 OOD detector cannot detect stated novelty types and treats NaN as in-domain
S35-F29/F30/F31/F32 model-card validation can pass forbidden use and no contestability, with no binding to governed model
S35-F33-F38 audit/lifecycle/playground gates are not reconstructible/enforceable and can still print green
S36 assumes S35 outputs are valid although S35 remains REPAIR_REQUIRED.
findings.fix: Require machine-valid inherited prediction/policy/explanation/audit artifacts.

findings.title: Cluster/anomaly/P@k artifacts lack sample, data, feature, scaler, detector, threshold-policy and as-of lineage.
findings.fix: Introduce immutable UnsupervisedSignalManifest and keyed rows.

findings.title: misconduct_auto=False, verdict=False, human_review=True and similar fields are hard-coded, not validators.
findings.fix: Validate structured claims/actions and routing.

findings.title: Legacy ai-apis-advanced ID renders an LLM function-calling playground in S36 Theory.
findings.fix: Map the stable ID to an S36 clustering/anomaly playground.

findings.title: zscore_list crashes empty and certifies NaN/nonfinite values as scaled=True.
findings.fix: Validate non-empty finite inputs before producing fitted state.

findings.title: Scaling is recomputed from the current batch and not frozen/versioned.
findings.fix: Fit on reference/train and transform later rows with stored state.

findings.title: update_centroids zip-truncates mismatched rows and accepts invalid/negative labels.
findings.fix: Enforce exact lengths, k and label domains.

findings.title: density helper accepts invalid eps/min_samples.
findings.fix: Require finite eps>=0 and integer min_samples>=1.

findings.title: Rolling-origin temporal figure is attached to k-selection T1-B rather than temporal T4-A.
findings.fix: Move figure to T4-A.

findings.title: Multi-seed k selection uses handwritten score maps rather than seeded clusterings.
findings.fix: Run actual repeated seeded clusterings.

findings.title: Same selected k is not partition stability.
findings.fix: Measure partition agreement with ARI and/or centroid/assignment sensitivity.

findings.title: choose_k crashes empty, accepts NaN and has implicit ties.
findings.fix: Validate finite maps and deterministic ties.

findings.title: Prose says capacity/business sense affects k but code never consumes capacity.
findings.fix: Separate geometric candidate selection from downstream queue constraints.

findings.title: scale_xy crashes empty, propagates nonfinite state and lacks reusable fitted scaler.
findings.fix: Separate fit/transform and validate inputs.

findings.title: far_from_mean sees only positive-side extremes and NaN can false-green.
findings.fix: Use validated absolute deviation or declared distance.

findings.title: Two-token blacklist permits moralized names such as riesgo_moral/sospechoso.
findings.fix: Use structured allowed naming rather than blacklist.

findings.title: Exploratory PCA distance directly enqueues review outside frozen policy/capacity/evidence controls.
findings.fix: Route through governed decision policy.

findings.title: IF/LOF contamination is conflated with review capacity.
findings.fix: Separate estimator contamination/threshold semantics from queue budget policy.

findings.title: sigma rule misses lower-tail anomalies.
findings.fix: Declare upper-tail business rule or implement two-sided deviation.

findings.title: ref defaults to xs despite requiring clean/past reference.
findings.fix: Require frozen explicit reference.

findings.title: sd=0→1 makes 3-sigma threshold arbitrary for constant reference.
findings.fix: Handle constant reference explicitly with tolerance/data-quality policy.

findings.title: NaN/nonfinite values and invalid thresholds/references are not rejected.
findings.fix: Validate finite inputs and positive finite z.

findings.title: expected_flags accepts invalid contamination and population values.
findings.fix: Validate domain and distinguish detector from queue policy.

findings.title: int(n*contamination) is treated as exact detector flags and conflates estimator setting with policy.
findings.fix: Use it only as explicit queue-budget arithmetic, not estimator output.

findings.title: has_leakage only checks duplicate month and misses future training periods.
findings.fix: Parse timestamps and require train times strictly before test, with gap/availability rules.

findings.title: Backtest lacks keyed event/availability times and reference snapshot.
findings.fix: Use time-aware keyed rows and frozen reference manifest.

findings.title: backtest=True is literal and window flag rates are handwritten.
findings.fix: Derive and validate backtest from scored rows.

findings.title: mean_flag_rate crashes empty and accepts invalid rates without support.
findings.fix: Validate 0<=rate<=1 and retain counts per window.

findings.title: P@k consumes a pre-ranked utility-label list, so ranking/ties cannot be audited.
findings.fix: Rank keyed scores under stable tie policy.

findings.title: k>n and nonbinary labels produce distorted/impossible precision.
findings.fix: Require 1<=k<=n and validated binary utility labels.

findings.title: human_in_loop=True is literal and scarcity/coverage is not derived.
findings.fix: Require reviewer routing/capacity and actual count evidence.

findings.title: Labels concentrated among reviewed top-ranked cases can reinforce the ranking policy.
findings.fix: Track sampling/coverage and include random/blinded audit samples where needed.

findings.title: S36 gates remain prints/literals despite systematic pytest requirement since S27.
findings.fix: Add collected regression tests for all critical contracts.

findings.title: Scaling is framed as universally non-optional instead of a geometry/units choice.
findings.fix: Explain when standardization is appropriate and when deliberate units/weights matter.

findings.title: K-means is described as repeating until nothing moves, omitting tolerance/max_iter stopping.
findings.fix: State convergence within tolerance or iteration limit.

findings.title: One-dimensional single-feature toy cannot demonstrate cross-feature magnitude domination.
findings.fix: Use at least two features with different units.

findings.title: Numeric cluster labels are not explicitly taught as arbitrary/permutable.
findings.fix: Show label-swap example and prohibit semantics from cluster numbers.

findings.title: silhouette/ARI are underexplained.
findings.fix: Define them intuitively before use and state limitations.

findings.title: weight_share_pc1 is coefficient absolute mass, not explained variance/importance; zero vector returns meaningful-looking 0.
findings.fix: Rename metric and reject zero-mass vector.

findings.title: LOF novelty=True unseen-only prediction rule is omitted.
findings.fix: Teach sklearn novelty/outlier API distinction.

findings.title: Review-click utility is said to suffice without acknowledging selective feedback.
findings.fix: Track coverage/sampling and distinguish operational feedback from unbiased evaluation.

findings.title: P@k + human feedback is framed as categorically superior to ROC evaluation.
findings.fix: Make P@k the lab queue metric while explaining metric choice depends on objective/coverage.

findings.title: AML, LOF, ARI, silhouette, path length and English process terms lack consistent Spanish-first definitions.
findings.fix: Expand on first use and reuse compact terms thereafter.

findings.title: S36-F04 current Theory playground is function-calling/LLM content due legacy ai-apis-advanced ID
S36-F08/F10/F11 preprocessing/clustering helpers accept invalid data/parameters and can certify broken state
S36-F13/F14 k stability is handwritten and does not measure partition stability
S36-F21/F22 PCA interpretation misses negative-side outliers and moralized labels
S36-F24/F30/F31 contamination is conflated with review capacity and invalid fractions create impossible workloads
S36-F25/F26/F27/F28 sigma anomaly rule is one-sided, self-contaminating and unsafe under zero variance/NaN
S36-F32/F33/F34 temporal backtest cannot prove no future leakage and prints backtest=True
S36-F37/F38/F39/F40 P@k/HITL evaluation repeats ranking/input defects and adds selective-label bias
S36-F42 gates remain print-only
S37 benchmarks S36-era signals although S36 remains REPAIR_REQUIRED.
findings.evidence: Roadmap prerequisite S36; continuation explicitly says only repaired machine-valid S36 artifacts may be optimized.
findings.fix: Require machine-valid inherited fixture/results and carry S36 regression suite before any performance comparison.
findings.attack: A fast benchmark of an invalid detector/ranking can institutionalize upstream defects.
findings.defense: Referencing prior work is pedagogically appropriate if its contracts are green.

findings.title: The central before/after report has no executable manifest binding dataset hash, code commit, benchmark stage, hardware/runtime/library versions, repetitions and policy state.
findings.evidence: Prose demands dataset/hardware but snippets store none of these as artifacts.
findings.fix: Create versioned BenchmarkManifest and BeforeAfterResult with hashes/environment/stage boundaries.
findings.attack: Numbers cannot be reproduced or compared if either code, data, stage boundary or environment drifted.
findings.defense: The prose correctly names dataset and hardware as required context.

findings.title: same_result is a string/static promise rather than an executed equivalence gate.
findings.evidence: section_contract lists same_result; profile helper checks only s>=0 and s2>=0; T4-B never compares outputs.
findings.fix: Run baseline/candidate on identical keyed fixture and assert an explicit domain comparator.
findings.attack: Different nonnegative outputs pass CE01.
findings.defense: The prose repeatedly states equivalence as the core rule.

findings.title: Legacy id dbt-bigquery renders a simulated dbt model/tests/lineage playground inside S37 Theory.
findings.evidence: SectionView mapping for dbt-bigquery is dbt_model_daily_metrics and dbt tests, while S37 roadmap/source are profiling/performance.
findings.fix: Keep id stable; replace only the playground mapping with S37 profiling/equivalence content.
findings.attack: A learner receives a complete practice activity from a different topic.
findings.defense: The stable id itself should remain for progress compatibility.

findings.title: S37-percentiles is declared in theory but absent from both bespoke FIGURES and all FIGURE_DATA registries, so FigureFrame returns null.
findings.evidence: FigureFrame returns null for unknown IDs; bespoke registry lacks S37-percentiles; data registries contain S37-where-time-goes but no S37-percentiles.
findings.fix: Add a registered figure with validated data or remove the dead declaration.
findings.attack: The intended tail-latency visual silently disappears from learner-facing theory.
findings.defense: Alt/caption metadata exists in the section source.

findings.title: Theory categorically says C-extension buffers such as NumPy/pandas are outside tracemalloc.
findings.evidence: Current NumPy explicitly hooks PyDataMem allocations into tracemalloc and exposes np.lib.tracemalloc_domain; Python C API permits extensions to register other domains.
findings.fix: Say tracemalloc measures tracked allocations, not RSS; extension visibility depends on allocator/tracing integration, with NumPy as a positive example.
findings.attack: Learners are told a current profiling capability does not exist.
findings.defense: tracemalloc is not RSS and can miss allocations that extensions do not track; that distinction is valid.

findings.title: Wall, CPU and memory are measured on three separate path executions while result equivalence between them is not checked.
findings.evidence: profile_wall_cpu_mem calls path(n) once for wall, once for CPU, once under tracemalloc; only first and third outputs enter a nonnegative predicate.
findings.fix: Declare purity or snapshot/reset state; compare keyed outputs across runs and bind each measurement to the same fixture/version.
findings.attack: Stateful/nondeterministic work can produce different outputs and states while reporting result=True.
findings.defense: Separate runs can reduce interference among measurement tools for a pure deterministic function.

findings.title: hot_function claims to name the hottest function but hardcodes only expensive-vs-cheap and uses internal tottime without explaining cumulative time.
findings.evidence: Return expression can only produce 'expensive' or 'cheap'; Python docs distinguish tottime from cumtime.
findings.fix: Use pstats/argmax over the intended metric and teach internal vs cumulative timing.
findings.attack: Any third/nested dominant function cannot be returned; high-level bottleneck may appear in cumulative rather than internal time.
findings.defense: For the current toy of two leaf helpers, expensive is predictably hotter.

findings.title: bench.py times five single executions of a tiny sum loop without calibration or process isolation.
findings.evidence: Current timeit autorange targets >=0.2 s; pyperf calibrates loops, warmups and multiple workers/values.
findings.fix: Use timeit.autorange or pyperf-style calibrated loops and record raw values/environment.
findings.attack: Timer/jitter overhead can be material relative to a very short workload and a 5-sample median can move with noise.
findings.defense: Five runs plus a warmup is better than a single timing and is simple for learners.

findings.title: The benchmark reports median_ms_ok>=0, spread_ms_ok>=0 and warmup=True rather than benchmark evidence.
findings.evidence: Nonnegative timing/range are nearly tautological and warmup is a literal.
findings.fix: Persist actual measurements, variability, loop count and result checksum; assert only semantic invariants/budgets appropriate to a controlled runner.
findings.attack: A noisy, meaningless or unexpectedly slow run remains green.
findings.defense: Exact times cannot be hard-coded across machines.

findings.title: blocking_cost assumes every block has floor(n/B) rows and drops n%B rows from its pair count.
findings.evidence: CE02: n=10,B=3 returns 9 blocked pairs; balanced complete partition 4,3,3 has 12.
findings.fix: Compute cost from actual block membership/sizes, not a divisibility-only approximation.
findings.attack: The primary cost metric understates work and silently loses remainder population.
findings.defense: The nominal n=100,B=10 fixture divides evenly.

findings.title: blocking_cost has no domain validation.
findings.evidence: CE03/CE04 crash; CE05 reports 100% reduction for 10 blocks over 3 rows.
findings.fix: Validate n>=2 and 1<=blocks<=n or explicitly define singleton/empty semantics.
findings.attack: Invalid configurations look optimal or fail with incidental arithmetic exceptions.
findings.defense: Nominal fixture uses n=100,B=10.

findings.title: Theory says recall remains the matching gate but S37 computes only pair count/reduction and inherits unvalidated S30 debt.
findings.evidence: No labeled pair fixture or recall assertion appears in theory code.
findings.fix: Run baseline/blocking over the same labeled fixture and assert candidate recall plus downstream-equivalence contract.
findings.attack: A blocking change can remove all true pairs and still appear as a 100% cost win.
findings.defense: The prose explicitly warns against sacrificing recall.

findings.title: inverted_index builds city→IDs internally but returns only city→count, destroying the IDs needed to generate candidate pairs.
findings.evidence: return {k: len(v)}; no candidate pair generation or scorer input exists.
findings.fix: Return immutable IDs per key and generate canonical candidate pairs, then verify candidate reduction/recall.
findings.attack: The code cannot perform the mechanism its paragraphs describe.
findings.defense: It accurately demonstrates block cardinality for the tiny fixture.

findings.title: array.array('i') is labeled int32 and expected output itemsize_i32=4 although Python defines it as native C signed int with architecture-dependent representation.
findings.evidence: Python array docs state actual representation depends on C implementation/machine and 'i' minimum size is 2 bytes.
findings.fix: Use an explicitly fixed-width stack dtype (e.g. NumPy int32/int64) or label the stdlib demo native-int/native-long-long and avoid hard-coded 4.
findings.attack: The lesson's portable memory claim and expected output can fail on a supported architecture.
findings.defense: Most current student platforms use 4-byte C int and array('q') is commonly 8.

findings.title: bound_bytes is computed as len(Python-list)*array('i').itemsize even though data remains a Python list and no compact array is created/measured.
findings.evidence: data=list(range(10)); bound_bytes=len(data)*i32; bound_ok only compares i32<i64.
findings.fix: Actually construct/measure the target representation or name it payload_bytes_if_native_int, separate from peak/RSS.
findings.attack: The reported memory bound ignores list pointers, Python integers, allocator overhead and chunk copies.
findings.defense: The comment says it is a bound 'si usamos int32', so it is intended as hypothetical payload arithmetic.

findings.title: chunks accepts invalid size values.
findings.evidence: CE06 size=0 raises incidental ValueError; CE07 negative size silently produces no chunks.
findings.fix: Require positive integer chunk_size and test empty/remainder cases.
findings.attack: An invalid tuning parameter can erase processing or crash outside an explicit contract.
findings.defense: Nominal size=3 behaves correctly including remainder chunk.

findings.title: The outcome promises minimal columnar reading but code merely prints ['id','amount']; it never reads/project columns from a dataset.
findings.evidence: No file/table/columnar reader appears in theory code.
findings.fix: Use a small introduced columnar-capable fixture/stack or narrow the outcome to projection planning and explicitly defer real columnar I/O.
findings.attack: Learner cannot observe memory/I/O impact or verify unused blobs were not loaded.
findings.defense: The section intentionally stays stdlib-oriented and frames formats as a later-stack application.

findings.title: cache_put writes a value then returns key in store, and the example prints this as hit=True.
findings.evidence: CE08: store is empty before call yet function returns True after insertion.
findings.fix: Implement cache_get returning hit/miss before recomputation; keep put/write-success as a separate operation.
findings.attack: A cache miss followed by a write is taught as a cache hit.
findings.defense: The function does verify the write is present afterward.

findings.title: Invalidation is a literal string and key=(feature_set, cutoff) is insufficient for data revisions/backfills, code/scaler/detector/policy versions and source snapshot.
findings.evidence: invalidate_policy returns 'version_or_cutoff'; no invalidation operation or stale-entry test exists.
findings.fix: Use content/versioned dependency key and test miss after each relevant upstream change/backfill.
findings.attack: Same cutoff can contain revised data; same feature-set name can be produced by changed code/reference state.
findings.defense: Version+cutoff is a useful first mental model.

findings.title: Out-of-core is promised but executable evidence is only the string 'chunk_if_needed'.
findings.evidence: No threshold, iterator/spill path, bounded peak or disk-backed operation exists.
findings.fix: Implement bounded streaming/chunk processing with measured peak and explicit spill/temporary-file policy if taught.
findings.attack: The learner sees policy text rather than an out-of-core mechanism or measurable bound.
findings.defense: Chunking in T3-A introduces one building block.

findings.title: T4-A talks about p95 latency, memory and candidate budgets but code compares one hand-entered measured_ms=12 to 50.
findings.evidence: No repetitions, percentile, memory, candidates, fixture hash or CI-failing assertion.
findings.fix: Feed measured metrics from the benchmark artifact; assert all declared budgets in pytest on controlled CI tiers.
findings.attack: The supposed regression test can be green without measuring the program at all.
findings.defense: The scalar inequality correctly illustrates the final budget comparison once a metric exists.

findings.title: budget_pass accepts impossible/nonfinite measurements.
findings.evidence: CE09 -1 ms and CE10 -inf both pass a 50 ms budget.
findings.fix: Validate finite nonnegative measured/budget values and unit/schema before comparison.
findings.attack: Corrupt measurements are treated as excellent performance.
findings.defense: Real timers normally produce nonnegative finite values.

findings.title: Final before/after numbers are literals, not outputs of baseline/candidate benchmarks, and no functional equivalence is checked.
findings.evidence: before={ms:100,pairs:1_000_000}; after={ms:20,pairs:50_000}; micro_only=False literal.
findings.fix: Construct report from two BenchmarkResult artifacts with same manifest and explicit equivalence assertion.
findings.attack: The capstone-like headline can be satisfied with invented numbers.
findings.defense: The arithmetic 5x/20x example is internally correct for those nominal inputs.

findings.title: pair_factor uses // and calls it 'cuántas veces menos pares', corrupting noninteger ratios.
findings.evidence: CE13: 100/60 should be 1.6667 but function returns 1.
findings.fix: Use true ratio before/after as float and separately report reduction=1-after/before.
findings.attack: A generic reporting helper systematically understates ratios except exact divisibility cases.
findings.defense: The nominal 1,000,000/50,000 happens to divide exactly to 20.

findings.title: speedup/pair_factor do not validate positive finite denominators/counts.
findings.evidence: CE11/CE14 divide by zero; CE12 accepts negative time.
findings.fix: Validate before>0, after>0 for ratios; define special policy for zero work and finite timings.
findings.attack: Invalid benchmark artifacts become exceptions or meaningless ratios.
findings.defense: Nominal fixtures use positive values.

findings.title: Reversible/justified optimization is central to tagline/gate but no artifact identifies the candidate change, baseline commit/config, rollback action or justification.
findings.evidence: Theory outputs contain no commit/diff/config/version/rollback reference.
findings.fix: Benchmark report must reference baseline/candidate commits/configs and documented rollback/revert path.
findings.attack: A benchmark cannot be tied to the exact optimization or reversed reproducibly.
findings.defense: Git/PR mechanics were taught earlier and need not be retaught in depth.

findings.title: Since S27 the roadmap requires systematic pytest, yet S37's theory gates are print-only scripts with no assertions/regression tests.
findings.evidence: All nine theory snippets print outputs; none is a collected test despite T4-A explicitly promising tests that fail PRs.
findings.fix: Keep explanatory prints if desired but add collected pytest regressions for correctness and controlled performance gates.
findings.attack: Broken equivalence/performance contracts do not make CI fail.
findings.defense: Printouts are useful for explanatory labs.

findings.title: The renderable where-time-goes figure states the job spends 8/64/21/7 percent in stages and says where time 'really' goes, but no benchmark/run/dataset/hardware produces those percentages.
findings.evidence: FIGURE_DATA hardcodes values; T1-B benchmark only runs sum-of-squares and never parses JSON/features/output stages.
findings.fix: Label as a hypothetical profile or derive the bars from a reproducible synthetic staged benchmark and show its manifest.
findings.attack: The section's main epistemic rule is violated by its own visual: invented profiling numbers look measured.
findings.defense: The percentages sum to 100 and clearly illustrate why optimizing the largest stage matters.

findings.title: 'El mismo resultado' is never operationally defined for ordered rows, floating reductions, candidate sets/rankings or S36 scores.
findings.evidence: No comparator/tolerance/order/tie policy appears in theory, despite vectorization/chunking/blocking being able to alter order or floating accumulation.
findings.fix: Define per-artifact equivalence: keyed records, canonical order only where nonsemantic, numeric tolerances with rationale, exact ranking/tie/policy invariants where semantic.
findings.attack: Byte equality may reject valid numeric equivalents while permissive checks can hide changed rankings/decisions.
findings.defense: The phrase 'resultado funcional idéntico' conveys the correct high-level intent.

findings.title: The missing figure's caption says p95=5 s with mean=200 ms, numerically incoherent under the usual empirical p95 interpretation for nonnegative latency.
findings.evidence: At least roughly 5% at or above 5000 ms already contributes about 250 ms to the mean before all other observations.
findings.fix: Use a coherent sample/distribution and derive mean/median/p95 from it.
findings.attack: If the missing figure is repaired as written, it teaches impossible/incoherent summary statistics.
findings.defense: The intended lesson that tail latency can matter despite a low average is correct.

findings.title: T1-B/callout says 'La primera corrida miente' and publishing cold start deceives, contradicting the opening's correct caveat that cold start may be the target.
findings.evidence: Opening says if startup latency matters the first run is exactly the measurement; later callout uses an absolute prohibition.
findings.fix: Name benchmark mode: cold-start and steady-state are separate experiments; never discard a target metric.
findings.attack: Learners may erase a legitimate user-facing startup SLO.
findings.defense: Discarding warmup is appropriate when measuring steady-state algorithm throughput.

findings.title: Roadmap/heading promise vectorization but theory gives only a sentence and no executable contrast or decision rule.
findings.evidence: T2-B code is only defaultdict indexing; no array/vectorized operation is shown.
findings.fix: Add a small post-block vectorized-vs-loop example only after candidate reduction, preserving identical results.
findings.attack: A required subtopic becomes a widow term rather than an operational skill.
findings.defense: Vectorization was introduced in S14 and S37 correctly prioritizes reducing candidate count first.

findings.title: Tagline requires same hardware while CI-light budget discussion provides no runner fingerprint/pinning or variance strategy.
findings.evidence: No CPU model, affinity, Python version, runner class or baseline metadata is captured; pyperf explicitly records such metadata.
findings.fix: Pin/fingerprint performance runners or use environment-aware regression thresholds; persist metadata.
findings.attack: A shared-runner change can fail/pass a wall-clock PR budget independent of code.
findings.defense: Absolute budgets can be valid on controlled/pinned runners, and prose asks for a hardware note.

findings.title: Dense prose introduces wall/CPU, warmup, cold start, IQR, blocking, recall, scorer, dtypes, OOM, cutoff, out-of-core, spill, p95, CI light and microbenchmark with uneven first-use explanation.
findings.evidence: Some are glossed but several remain compressed or only expanded much later.
findings.fix: Spanish-first first occurrence plus concise operational definition; keep API identifiers in code formatting.
findings.attack: Advanced content becomes vocabulary decoding rather than performance reasoning, particularly for a prerequisite-aware but self-contained learner.
findings.defense: S37 is advanced and many terms were introduced earlier; current redaction has already glossed several English terms.

findings.title: Job relevance claims 'con n grande, el wall time se duplica' without defining what doubled or the algorithm/input scaling relation.
findings.evidence: Large n alone does not imply exactly 2x wall time; complexity and change in n determine scaling.
findings.fix: Replace with a bounded statement that small per-unit regressions can compound with n and must be measured on representative sizes.
findings.attack: It teaches a quantitative causal claim with no model or denominator.
findings.defense: The intended message is that regressions matter more at scale.

findings.title: The practical demonstration reverses the section's correct definition of idempotency identity.
findings.evidence: I Do T4-A preamble: «c1:features:v1 identifica el intento»; theory T4-A: «identifica la operación, no el intento».
findings.impact: A learner can generate a new key for each retry attempt, which makes deduplication impossible.
findings.fix: Replace «identifica el intento» with «identifica la operación lógica y se reutiliza en todos sus reintentos».

findings.title: The defining promotion gate (restart from durable state without duplicate effects) is downgraded to optional enrichment.
findings.evidence: You Do requirements require a reusable durable checkpoint; starter uses CKPT/APPLIED in RAM; portfolioNote says «si puedes, reinicia el proceso leyendo CKPT desde disco».
findings.impact: A learner can finish the project with in-memory state, see the same-process retry pass, and believe they demonstrated crash recovery.
findings.fix: Make persistence + fresh-process reopen mandatory, provide a SQLite/atomic-file scaffold, and fail the project gate if restart/resume evidence is absent.

findings.title: S38-U01 grading hard-gate semantics
S38-U02 live/main deployment drift

The text does not distinguish the version of the original operation/intent from the version of the currently deployed code. Regenerating an idempotency key from the new deploy version can make a delayed retry look like a new operation.
findings.evidence: I Do T4-A why: «La key case:step:ver es estable entre deploys de lógica»; We Do T4-A-E2 says v3 is needed after a deploy to avoid collision with v2.
findings.impact: A learner may break deduplication during deployment by changing the key for an old request.
findings.fix: State that the intent/version stored with the original logical operation is reused on retries. A new key is created only for a genuinely new logical operation, not merely because code was redeployed.

findings.title: The assessment converts known conditional/incorrect simplifications into authoritative 'correct' answers.
findings.evidence: Self-check Q1 scores «Procesos» as the generic CPU-bound answer; Q2 scores «Colas infinitas y OOM» and explains «maxsize acota memoria».
findings.impact: Even a learner who noticed the caveats is rewarded for reproducing the oversimplified rule, reinforcing the misconception.
findings.fix: Rewrite Q1 around the default GIL-enabled pure-Python case and runtime measurement; rewrite Q2 to say maxsize bounds item count/backlog and requires separate memory measurement.

findings.title: Does the grading runtime enforce «Idempotencia verificable + runbook (obligatorio)» as a hard gate independent of the 70% badge threshold?
findings.evidence: S38 rubric assigns that criterion 15%; the public course copy says badges use a 70% rubric threshold.
findings.impact: If there is no separate hard gate, a learner could score up to 85% while failing the criterion labelled obligatory.

findings.title: S38 treats S37 measurement discipline as usable although S37 remains REPAIR_REQUIRED and its benchmark harness is not machine-valid.
findings.fix: Require repaired BenchmarkManifest/BenchmarkResult and S37 regression gates before using performance evidence.
findings.attack: Concurrency choices and SLO numbers can be justified by invalid or handwritten timings.
findings.defense: Conceptually building concurrency after profiling is correct.

findings.title: No S38 artifact binds concurrency comparisons to fixture hash, code/config, stage boundary, environment fingerprint and equivalence oracle.
findings.impact: What is actually proven here, and under which runtime/operational assumptions?
findings.fix: Reuse a versioned manifest and compare baseline/candidate behavior plus latency/throughput/error/queue/resource metrics.
findings.attack: Changing executor can change ordering/state/result while looking faster.
findings.defense: The prose repeatedly says measure first.

findings.title: The lesson states CPU-bound CPython threads will not help because one thread executes bytecode, without bounding the claim to the default GIL-enabled build or pure Python.
findings.impact: What is actually proven here, and under which runtime/operational assumptions?
findings.fix: Teach interpreter/build/library boundary and measure rather than infer from CPU label alone.
findings.attack: CPython 3.13+ has optional free-threaded builds; current Python docs explicitly qualify the GIL rule.
findings.defense: The default CPython build remains GIL-enabled and pure-Python CPU work is usually process-bound.

findings.title: Dense/vector scoring is routed mechanically to processes even though many NumPy operations release the GIL and can run in parallel threads.
findings.impact: What is actually proven here, and under which runtime/operational assumptions?
findings.fix: Benchmark the actual kernel and library threading behavior; do not map vectorized=processes.
findings.attack: Processes may add serialization/copy cost and oversubscription while threads may be faster for native numeric kernels.
findings.defense: Some CPU work remains pure Python and benefits from processes.

findings.title: measure_bound uses arbitrary ratios and accepts zero, negative, NaN and infinity as operational evidence.
findings.impact: What is actually proven here, and under which runtime/operational assumptions?
findings.fix: Validate finite nonnegative measurements and present ratio thresholds as an explicit local heuristic, not diagnosis.
findings.attack: CE01-CE03 show invalid metrics produce io/cpu/mixed decisions.
findings.defense: The helper is intended as a toy decision heuristic.

findings.title: Outcome promises threads/processes/async and pools, but theory only returns plan strings and never runs ThreadPoolExecutor, ProcessPoolExecutor or asyncio.
findings.impact: What is actually proven here, and under which runtime/operational assumptions?
findings.fix: Use local-python artifact/tests for at least one real executor and async timeout path; browser can remain conceptual.
findings.attack: No concurrency, cancellation, ordering or worker failure is observed.
findings.defense: Avoiding heavy pools in browser is reasonable.

findings.title: ProcessPool serialization/IPC cost is represented by len(json.dumps(payload).encode()).
findings.impact: What is actually proven here, and under which runtime/operational assumptions?
findings.fix: Measure pickle serialization size/time and actual executor round-trip for the exact payload, or label JSON only as an approximate independent payload-size exercise.
findings.attack: ProcessPoolExecutor requires picklable objects and uses multiprocessing serialization/transport; JSON length neither measures that serialization nor IPC latency/copy cost.
findings.defense: Comparing compact vs bloated payload size is still a useful intuition.

findings.title: The lesson reintroduces ana@example.pe.
findings.impact: What is actually proven here, and under which runtime/operational assumptions?
findings.fix: Use ana@example.com or ana@example.test consistently.
findings.attack: example.pe is not an IANA reserved documentation domain and can represent a real external domain.
findings.defense: It visually looks synthetic.

findings.title: Theory and figure call Queue(maxsize) a memory cap.
findings.impact: What is actually proven here, and under which runtime/operational assumptions?
findings.fix: Call it an item-count/backpressure bound and add payload-size/RSS budget if claiming memory protection.
findings.attack: Python defines maxsize as an upper bound on number of items, not bytes/RSS; one huge item or worker-held payloads can still exhaust memory.
findings.defense: Bounding item count often bounds queue growth if item sizes are separately constrained.

findings.title: The lab TokenBucket never refills, yet the contract claims no more than R tokens per window.
findings.impact: What is actually proven here, and under which runtime/operational assumptions?
findings.fix: Either rename to fixed quota and narrow the criterion or implement monotonic-time refill/window behavior.
findings.attack: It enforces a lifetime quota, not a time rate/window; after two calls it denies forever.
findings.defense: The paragraph explicitly acknowledges that limitation.

findings.title: The mutable token counter has no synchronization and no 429/Retry-After behavior despite a concurrency/rate-limit contract.
findings.impact: What is actually proven here, and under which runtime/operational assumptions?
findings.fix: Use a concurrency-safe limiter/ownership model and test 429/Retry-After or explicitly exclude provider feedback from the lab.
findings.attack: Concurrent check/decrement can violate shared rate state on interpreters/runtimes without global serialization; provider feedback is never consumed.
findings.defense: Single-thread toy calls are deterministic.

findings.title: The Theory playground uses if q.full(): else q.put(), directly contradicting T2-A's own safe guidance.
findings.fix: Use put_nowait/Full or timed put in the playground too.
findings.attack: Python docs and S38 itself say full() is advisory; another producer can fill between check and put.
findings.defense: The playground runs sequentially so the demo happens to be deterministic.

findings.title: fetch_with_timeout only compares a supplied latency number to a threshold; it never waits, times out or cancels work.
findings.impact: What is actually proven here, and under which runtime/operational assumptions?
findings.fix: Add an actual asyncio.wait_for/timeout local coroutine and assert cancellation/elapsed behavior; keep pure classifier only as policy helper.
findings.attack: A declared 200 ms provider returns immediately, so cancellation semantics cannot be observed.
findings.defense: The comment clearly calls it a simulation.

findings.title: Resource cleanup is proved by assigning closed=True to a local boolean in finally.
findings.impact: What is actually proven here, and under which runtime/operational assumptions?
findings.fix: Use a tiny closable fake that records close(), or a real local context-managed resource, and assert post-condition outside the function.
findings.attack: No socket/file/context-managed resource exists; close_in_finally=True is also a literal returned before cleanup.
findings.defense: It demonstrates that finally executes.

findings.title: Timeout classifier accepts negative and non-finite latency/timeout values.
findings.impact: What is actually proven here, and under which runtime/operational assumptions?
findings.fix: Reject non-finite, negative latency and non-positive timeout before routing.
findings.attack: CE04-CE05 show negative timeout and NaN/negative latency produce plausible timeout/ok states.
findings.defense: Nominal fixture uses valid values.

findings.title: The roadmap/tagline requires tested handling of a slow provider, but no theory artifact actually blocks a worker, times out a call or demonstrates pool recovery.
findings.impact: What is actually proven here, and under which runtime/operational assumptions?
findings.fix: Induce a local slow coroutine/fake service, measure queue/worker effects, cancel it and prove subsequent work progresses.
findings.attack: Changing latency_ms changes a branch only, not elapsed time/resource occupancy.
findings.defense: The conceptual policy is present.

findings.title: scored_event returns one dict containing a nested metric and calls that logs+metrics+traces.
findings.impact: What is actually proven here, and under which runtime/operational assumptions?
findings.fix: Separate structured log record, metric recorder and trace/span stub with executable correlation tests.
findings.attack: No logger emits, no metric aggregates/exports, no span/trace exists.
findings.defense: A local dict can teach desired fields before introducing infrastructure.

findings.title: A custom corr string is treated as sufficient trace evidence.
findings.impact: What is actually proven here, and under which runtime/operational assumptions?
findings.fix: Teach corr as optional business correlation in addition to trace_id/span_id, not as a substitute for tracing.
findings.attack: OpenTelemetry correlates logs/traces using TraceId/SpanId/execution trace context; no span is created here.
findings.defense: A domain correlation_id is still useful across systems.

findings.title: pii_raw=False is a literal rather than an enforced log schema/redaction test.
findings.impact: What is actually proven here, and under which runtime/operational assumptions?
findings.fix: Allowlist log fields and test forbidden keys/patterns; do not use a boolean declaration as proof.
findings.attack: A payload could contain email/phone while the flag remains False.
findings.defense: The nominal event dict currently contains no raw email/phone.

findings.title: redact() preserves the first two characters of any string without field policy or minimization.
findings.impact: What is actually proven here, and under which runtime/operational assumptions?
findings.fix: Prefer no direct identifier; otherwise use field-aware approved masking/pseudonymization and tests.
findings.attack: Masking semantics differ for email/phone/IDs and may still leak identity; OWASP recommends omission/de-identification when identity is unnecessary.
findings.defense: The example only aims to show that raw values should not be logged.

findings.title: p95 and error_rate are handwritten scalar literals; no sample set, denominator or compliance window produces them.
findings.impact: What is actually proven here, and under which runtime/operational assumptions?
findings.fix: Compute SLIs from a synthetic request window and record count/errors/latency samples and SLO window.
findings.attack: The lesson cannot demonstrate p95, error rate or an SLO from operational data.
findings.defense: Simple numbers isolate threshold comparison.

findings.title: Any current SLI threshold violation immediately maps to freeze_nonurgent_deploys and is described as consuming/exhausting error budget.
findings.impact: What is actually proven here, and under which runtime/operational assumptions?
findings.fix: Track allowed bad events/time and consumed budget over the window; enact freeze only according to explicit policy after exhaustion/burn-rate condition.
findings.attack: Error budget is allowance over a defined SLO compliance window; one point miss is not identical to budget exhaustion, and a current pass does not restore spent budget.
findings.defense: Freeze-on-breach is conservative as a toy policy.

findings.title: Negative/non-finite SLI values are not rejected.
findings.impact: What is actually proven here, and under which runtime/operational assumptions?
findings.fix: Validate finite p95>=0 and 0<=error_rate<=1 plus non-empty denominators.
findings.attack: CE06: p95=-1 and error_rate=-0.1 yields slo_ok=True and ship_features.
findings.defense: Nominal example is valid.

findings.title: CKPT and APPLIED are module-global dict/set despite prose claiming restart-surviving durable stores.
findings.impact: What is actually proven here, and under which runtime/operational assumptions?
findings.fix: Use an on-disk temp SQLite/file fixture, reopen from a new process/test instance and assert resume state.
findings.attack: A process crash erases both, violating the central gate.
findings.defense: Comments label production alternatives such as SQLite/os.replace.

findings.title: make_checkpoint writes status=done before the side effect executes.
findings.impact: What is actually proven here, and under which runtime/operational assumptions?
findings.fix: Define transactional state transitions; do not persist done until the operation/effect contract is durably resolved.
findings.attack: CE08: crash after checkpoint before effect makes restart skip an effect that never happened.
findings.defense: The current side effect is only a list append and the happy-path test does not crash.

findings.title: APPLIED.add(key) executes before side_effects.append(step).
findings.impact: What is actually proven here, and under which runtime/operational assumptions?
findings.fix: Use atomic DB/outbox/inbox transaction or an external idempotent API keyed by the same operation identity.
findings.attack: If APPLIED were durable, crash between them suppresses all future retries while effect never occurred; AWS calls for atomic token+mutation semantics.
findings.defense: With an in-memory list/set the statements are adjacent.

findings.title: Because key/checkpoint stores are in memory, a successful external effect followed by process death loses dedup state.
findings.impact: What is actually proven here, and under which runtime/operational assumptions?
findings.fix: Persist dedup/outcome atomically or reconcile against idempotent provider response before replay.
findings.attack: CE09 shows new process sees empty stores and may repeat the effect.
findings.defense: A real durable store is named in prose but not implemented.

findings.title: if key not in APPLIED followed by APPLIED.add is not a cross-worker atomic claim.
findings.impact: What is actually proven here, and under which runtime/operational assumptions?
findings.fix: Use UNIQUE key/INSERT-if-absent transaction or compare-and-set in durable store and race-test two workers.
findings.attack: Two workers can both observe absent and execute the side effect; free-threaded/multiprocess execution makes reliance on interpreter serialization invalid.
findings.defense: Single-thread demo cannot race.

findings.title: The only side effect is append to an in-memory list.
findings.impact: What is actually proven here, and under which runtime/operational assumptions?
findings.fix: Use a safe local durable sink (SQLite/outbox/file) with unique constraint and induced crash points.
findings.attack: It cannot prove behavior against the real irreversible boundary the prose names: send/write/spend/review ticket.
findings.defense: Synthetic side effects avoid unsafe external actions.

findings.title: Unknown step names are persisted as done and resume to themselves.
findings.impact: What is actually proven here, and under which runtime/operational assumptions?
findings.fix: Validate state/transition enums and fail closed on unknown state/version.
findings.attack: CE07 shows silent acceptance rather than controlled failure/quarantine.
findings.defense: Only known steps occur in nominal fixture.

findings.title: case:step:ver is taught as stable but the contract does not state whether ver is workflow intent version pinned to the item or current deployment version.
findings.impact: What is actually proven here, and under which runtime/operational assumptions?
findings.fix: Persist operation/workflow version with the original work item and reuse it for retries; create new identity only for new intent.
findings.attack: A late retry after deploy could receive a new key and repeat an old logical operation.
findings.defense: Including version can correctly distinguish genuinely different intended operations.

findings.title: route() retries every kind except literal poison until attempts expire.
findings.impact: What is actually proven here, and under which runtime/operational assumptions?
findings.fix: Use explicit retriable error classes/statuses and fail closed/DLQ/handoff for unknown or permanent failures.
findings.attack: CE10: permanent/validation/auth/business errors become retry, contradicting transient-only prose and potentially amplifying failures.
findings.defense: The toy only names poison/retriable in prose.

findings.title: DLQ and replay are route strings only.
findings.impact: What is actually proven here, and under which runtime/operational assumptions?
findings.fix: Implement a local durable dead-letter table/list artifact with metadata and one-at-a-time replay after explicit fix/version selection.
findings.attack: No message body hash, failure reason, attempt count, first/last timestamps, idempotency key, code/version or controlled replay exists.
findings.defense: The lesson avoids deploying a broker.

findings.title: runbook evidence is print('runbook', True).
findings.impact: What is actually proven here, and under which runtime/operational assumptions?
findings.fix: Provide/version a small Markdown/JSON runbook and execute at least one synthetic drill linked to observed evidence.
findings.attack: No symptoms/checks/actions artifact exists or can be drilled/versioned.
findings.defense: The surrounding prose describes what a runbook should contain.

findings.title: Executable backoff has no cap/deadline/jitter and accepts negative attempt/base.
findings.impact: What is actually proven here, and under which runtime/operational assumptions?
findings.fix: Validate domain, add capped/truncated backoff plus jitter/deadline policy, while keeping deterministic RNG in tests.
findings.attack: CE11 produces a positive wait for negative attempt and a negative wait for negative base; unbounded 2**attempt can explode.
findings.defense: Prose explicitly says jitter in prod and max attempts is handled separately.

findings.title: Prose shows delays for attempts 0..3 while route with max_attempts=3 sends attempt 3 directly to DLQ.
findings.impact: What is actually proven here, and under which runtime/operational assumptions?
findings.fix: Define attempt/retry numbering once and derive waits/routes from that contract.
findings.attack: It is unclear whether max_attempts counts initial attempt or retries and whether the fourth delay is ever used.
findings.defense: Either convention can be valid if defined.

findings.title: Despite systematic pytest being required from S27, theory has no collected tests for queue overflow, timeout cancellation, retry classification, process reopen or idempotency races.
findings.impact: What is actually proven here, and under which runtime/operational assumptions?
findings.fix: Add pytest with induced crash/reopen and concurrent duplicate race tests plus invalid-input cases.
findings.attack: Happy-path prints/asserts cannot stop regressions in the operational gate.
findings.defense: Some snippets contain Python assert statements.

findings.title: Tagline/gate promises trace per case, queue metrics and tested slow-provider/process-crash/reexecution handling, but the artifacts are mostly literals/classifiers/in-memory state.
findings.impact: What is actually proven here, and under which runtime/operational assumptions?
findings.fix: Create one integrated local harness that queues cases, induces slow call and process crash, reopens store, resumes once, emits trace/metrics and validates no duplicate effect.
findings.attack: Each named failure mode lacks an end-to-end executable demonstration.
findings.defense: All concepts appear in prose.

findings.title: Theory playground only constructs an idempotency-key string and prints pii_raw=False; it has no dedup store, atomic claim or restart.
findings.fix: Use a safe durable local store and actual duplicate/restart test, or label key construction as syntax only.
findings.attack: A learner can infer that naming a key is equivalent to idempotence.
findings.defense: The playground is explicitly a compact practice surface.

findings.title: No experiment jointly reports throughput, latency distribution, timeout/error rate, queue depth/backpressure and resource saturation as concurrency changes.
findings.fix: Add controlled load matrix N-workers×queue/rate settings and report all operational metrics under same manifest.
findings.attack: Higher concurrency can increase throughput while destroying p95, error rate or memory/CPU; current lesson cannot detect that tradeoff.
findings.defense: Individual concepts are taught separately.

findings.title: Parallelism/retries do not test preservation of candidate/ranking order, tie policy, duplicate handling or review destination inherited from triage.
findings.fix: Carry an artifact-specific oracle from S37/S39 boundary and assert keyed outputs/routes independent of completion order.
findings.attack: Concurrency can reorder completion and retries can duplicate/miss work while all local snippets remain green.
findings.defense: S38 focuses on operational mechanics rather than model semantics.

findings.title: Is the GitHub Pages deployment currently behind main or is the web crawler snapshot stale?
findings.evidence: Crawler snapshot (last month) shows S38 as 19h and course total 1040h; main currently encodes S38 estimatedHours=9 and COURSE_META.totalHours=491.
findings.impact: Live learners may see outdated workload estimates and potentially older content.

findings.title: The section introduces threads/processes but never defines ownership/synchronization for mutable model/reference/cache state.
findings.fix: Add explicit rule: immutable/read-only shared reference or per-worker copy; synchronize intentional mutation and test deterministic semantics.
findings.attack: Shared mutable NumPy/cache state can race; process workers can instead silently fork stale copies.
findings.defense: Current toy examples barely share meaningful state.

findings.title: Theory says idempotency key identifies the operation, not the attempt; I Do says the opposite.
findings.impact: Direct concept-definition contradiction at the point where learners shift from reading to modeled practice.

findings.title: The section asks learners to reason about ProcessPool IPC but practice measures JSON text length and calls it the actual IPC blob.
findings.impact: Learners can optimize the wrong serializer and miss picklability/start-method/round-trip costs.

findings.title: Theory admits the token bucket is static/no-refill, yet practical titles and feedback continue to call it a rate limit and claim ban protection.
findings.impact: A quota is memorized as a rate algorithm; time never enters the learner's model.

findings.title: The learning outcome promises cancellation/timeouts/resource cleanup, but all practical evidence is numeric classification or boolean flags.
findings.impact: Recognition of timeout semantics is mistaken for operational cancellation behavior.

findings.title: The section names observability, trace and privacy gates but repeatedly validates them with a single dict and self-declared flags.
findings.impact: Learners can pass by naming signals instead of emitting/correlating/validating them.

findings.title: Durable crash/restart is simultaneously mandatory, absent from the scaffold, and explicitly optional ('si puedes').
findings.impact: The capstone can teach that same-process dictionaries constitute resumability.

findings.title: The scored self-check promotes known conditional/incorrect simplifications to authoritative answers.
findings.impact: Assessment reinforces misconceptions that the audit already identified.

findings.title: A criterion called obligatory is worth 15%, while the public badge copy states a 70% threshold; a hard-gate implementation was not located in this pass.
findings.impact: Potentially allows certification-within-course despite failing the named mandatory reliability gate.

findings.title: Crawler snapshot shows 19h/1040h while main encodes 9h/491h.
findings.impact: Possible deployment/content drift; not confirmed because the available crawler snapshot is a month old.

findings.title: The practice layer repeats many theory defects instead of repairing them: false CPU=>processes simplification, JSON-as-ProcessPool-IPC, queue maxsize as a memory cap, static quota as rate limiting, fake timeout/cancellation, fake observability, point-in-time SLO/error-budget logic, and in-memory recovery presented as resilient operation.

The strongest conceptual paragraph in T4-A says an idempotency key identifies the logical operation, but the I Do preamble later says it 'identifica el intento'. This directly reverses the mental model the section had correctly established.

The You Do says durable restart and reusable state are required, while its starter remains RAM-only and its portfolio note says reopening from disk is optional ('si puedes'). The capstone gate can therefore be completed without proving its defining property.
Which CPython runtime/build is being assumed when making GIL-based concurrency choices
What serialization ProcessPoolExecutor actually uses and what must be picklable
What maxsize bounds (number of queue items) versus what actually bounds memory
What evidence distinguishes a modeled timeout policy from real waiting/cancellation
What makes a checkpoint durable across a new process and what atomicity protects an external side effect
What SLO window/error-budget calculation justifies a release freeze
The theory correctly says the idempotency key identifies an operation, while I Do T4-A says it identifies an attempt.
The source alternates between Spanish prose terms (métricas, trazas) and English labels (metrics, traces) without always distinguishing conceptual term from code identifier.
The practice calls a no-refill counter a 'rate'/'rate limit' even after the theory admits it is only a static quota.
trace/span/trace context are used as if correlation_id were sufficient
rate limit/token bucket is used where the implementation is only a fixed quota
error budget is used without an explicit compliance window and denominator
durable/checkpoint/replay/runbook are often nouns whose evidence is not actually produced
Mechanism/evidence substitution: labels and booleans stand in for operational behavior.
Conditional systems rules are assessed as universal rules.
The capstone's defining durability/restart proof is simultaneously mandatory and optional.
You Do se presenta como cierre CP-N3-C pero no implementa el contrato canónico del capstone
findings.evidence: assess/decide return REJECT_STAGE_ORDER not only for an actual stage-order error but also when label_space != needs_review or auto_fraud violates policy.
findings.impact: A reasonable learner can learn that auto_fraud=True is a pipeline-order defect instead of a prohibited decision-policy defect, producing the wrong remediation and audit trail.
findings.fix: Return separate tokens such as REJECT_LABEL_SPACE and REJECT_AUTO_FRAUD_POLICY; reserve REJECT_STAGE_ORDER for stages != CANON.
findings.attack: Un cierre de capstone solo es defendible si el scaffold obliga a producir las evidencias que el rubric y el brief declaran críticas.
findings.defense: S35-S38 enseñan varias piezas y el texto de S39 las menciona.
findings.justification: Blocking is not enough when the lesson claims diagnostic specificity. The token tells the learner to debug stage order when the stage list may be correct.

findings.title: El scaffold escribe métricas y conclusiones a mano, creando pseudo-evidencia
findings.evidence: decide(packet) checks score-only, uncertainty, evidence and graph_path, then returns CONTINUE, 4; it never requires case_id or score in the accepted path.
findings.impact: A learner can pass an anonymous/unscored packet as ready for review and conclude that adding uncertainty compensates for missing identity/score.
findings.fix: Compose E3 with one canonical packet_ok validator that requires non-empty case_id, finite score in domain, non-empty source-backed evidence, graph path and uncertainty before counting explanation layers.
findings.attack: Una card debe resumir resultados derivados de artefactos verificables; hardcodear números permite que una entrega falsa parezca evaluada.
findings.defense: Los números están marcados como sintéticos/didácticos.
findings.justification: A transfer exercise must preserve prerequisites; otherwise it teaches that previously mandatory fields disappear when moving to the richer path.

findings.title: El proyecto promete override y apelación auditables, pero el audit no contiene los campos necesarios y la apelación no existe
findings.evidence: The title/feedback require an appeal to reopen with another reviewer, but assess merely checks that second_reviewer is truthy; there is no original reviewer field or inequality test.
findings.impact: A learner can set second_reviewer=ana when the original reviewer was also Ana and receive reopen, falsely believing an independent appeal occurred.
findings.fix: Include original_reviewer and require a distinct authorized second_reviewer; append an appeal audit event with actor, timestamp and reason.
findings.attack: Un booleano `override` sin actor, razón, tiempo y versión no demuestra quién cambió qué ni bajo qué política; una frase de card no implementa contestabilidad.
findings.defense: El run_id y case_id permiten cierta correlación didáctica.
findings.justification: The control being taught is independence/second pair of eyes, not string presence. The implementation cannot prove the advertised control.

findings.title: Registry, SemVer y ownership desaparecen del proyecto independiente
findings.evidence: The lesson calls the project cierre CP-N3-C, but the canonical CP-N3-C rubric requires baseline, reported calibration, cost-based threshold/human review, abstention, subgroup performance and model card. The starter uses a hand-built score, fixed thr=0.70, no baseline/calibration calculation and hard-coded subgroup/value metrics in Markdown cards.
findings.impact: A learner can believe they completed CP-N3-C by packaging a toy score and static cards while never showing calibration, baseline or cost-threshold evidence.
findings.fix: Require versioned upstream baseline/calibration/threshold/subgroup artifacts with hashes/run IDs or compute them from a canonical fixture; gate ready_for_human_acceptance on those artifacts and their tests.
findings.attack: Un objetivo que no deja artefacto ni prueba en You Do no es evaluable.
findings.defense: El tema fue practicado en I Do/We Do.
findings.location: YouDo title/context; YouDo objectives; YouDo starterCode; CP-N3-C RUBRIC.json; CP-N3-C BRIEF.md
findings.justification: If evidence is inherited, the bundle must reference and verify those artifacts. It currently substitutes a constant threshold and prose claims, so neither local proof nor verified provenance exists.

findings.title: El checklist de privacidad/fairness/seguridad se reduce a declaraciones en cards
findings.evidence: S39 displays six percentage criteria totaling 100% plus rows whose weight values are literal bonus checklist, gate process, and gate privacy. The canonical CP-N3-C rubric instead uses four 0–3 criteria with weights .35/.20/.25/.20 and a gate rule >=2.4/3, no critical criterion <2, zero P0. SectionView renders every string under a column labeled Peso without reconciling the two contracts.
findings.impact: A learner can optimize for the 25/20/20/15/10/10 table and still fail canonical calibration/abstention gates, or assume gate privacy is merely another weight row.
findings.fix: Use the canonical rubric as the S39 project rubric or explicitly label the local table checklist de preparación and link the canonical 0–3 rubric/hard gates. Render gate rows separately from numeric weights.
findings.attack: Los controles de release deben derivarse de tests o evidencia; texto libre no distingue un sistema protegido de uno no probado.
findings.defense: Los fixtures son locales y sintéticos, reduciendo riesgo real.
findings.location: YouDo rubric; SectionView YouDo rubric renderer; course-state/capstones/CP-N3-C/RUBRIC.json; course-state/capstones/CP-N3-C/gate.json
findings.justification: The lesson labels it `Rúbrica de evaluación` and says it closes CP-N3-C. Without an explicit distinction/link, a reasonable learner cannot know which evaluation governs acceptance.

findings.title: `force_failure` no demuestra drift, human_only ni rollback verificable
findings.evidence: The starter writes precision_at_k≈0.55, false_queue=0.08/0.11, override rates and median review time as literal text; says apelación con segundo revisor although no appeal workflow exists in the starter; and says rollback targets a versioned previous model although no model registry/rollback operation is implemented.
findings.impact: A learner can learn to satisfy governance by writing plausible metrics/control statements into Markdown rather than attaching evidence that those controls ran.
findings.fix: Generate cards from validated run artifacts; include provenance for each metric/control, mark unavailable claims not_evaluated, and remove appeal/rollback claims until corresponding tests/events exist.
findings.attack: Imprimir 'rollback' no revierte estado; activar un booleano no prueba que las acciones prohibidas sean imposibles.
findings.defense: Como laboratorio local, el ejemplo pretende ilustrar el flujo, no desplegar infraestructura real.
findings.location: YouDo starterCode: model-card.md; YouDo starterCode: system-card.md
findings.justification: Synthetic does not mean self-attested. A card used in an acceptance bundle must distinguish measured values, inherited verified values and illustrative placeholders.

findings.title: La rúbrica visible de S39 contradice la rúbrica canónica del capstone
findings.evidence: Theory states that an override audit event needs actor, reason and timestamp. The I Do reduces evidence to audit: True; the You Do JSONL records run_id/case/path/action/score/override/human_only but no actor, reason, timestamp, model/threshold/policy version or appeal linkage.
findings.impact: A learner can produce audit.jsonl that cannot answer who overrode what policy, why, or under which model/threshold version.
findings.fix: Add stable pseudonymous actor/reviewer ID, reason code, timestamp, original auto action, final action, model_id, threshold/policy version, appeal linkage and append-only integrity checks.
findings.attack: Dos rúbricas distintas para el mismo CP-N3-C hacen imposible saber qué evidencia decide el gate. Además, 'gate process/privacy' se renderiza bajo una columna titulada Peso aunque no es un peso.
findings.defense: La visible puede funcionar como guía formativa y la canónica como evaluación formal.
findings.location: I Do S39-T2-B-DEMO; WeDo S39-T2-B-E1/E3; YouDo append_audit
findings.justification: A pseudonymous reviewer ID and timestamp are not real PII and are necessary to demonstrate the section's own stated audit contract. The omission directly contradicts the lesson, not merely production hardening.

findings.title: I Do modela nombres, flags y listas en vez de modelar la ejecución que el alumno deberá defender
findings.evidence: BRIEF says the dataset contains case_id, features, label, subgrupo, timestamp, cost_fp and cost_fn. data/generate.py instead emits generic records with id, name, email, amount and status and no ML labels/cost/subgroup/timestamp fields.
findings.impact: A learner following the canonical dataset path cannot implement cost-based thresholds, temporal/subgroup checks or labeled calibration because the required fields do not exist.
findings.fix: Replace the generic generator with deterministic CP-N3-C cases matching BRIEF fields, including train/dev/test or evaluation partition metadata and reserved synthetic identifiers.
findings.attack: En Gradual Release, I Do debería mostrar el trabajo cognitivo y técnico de calidad que luego se pide en You Do. Aquí muestra versiones reducidas de los mismos anti-patrones que la teoría declara insuficientes.
findings.defense: Las demos son pequeñas para no sobrecargar y se complementan con We Do.
findings.justification: The catalog names `data/generate.py` as the canonical dataset path. A second hidden generator in demo.py does not repair the documented artifact contract.

findings.title: We Do sobreentrena reparación de predicados y tokens exactos, no integración de Responsible ML
findings.evidence: RUBRIC lists Sin calibración as a critical failure and requires calibración reportada. demo.py emits status=pass, but its model card explicitly states Toy linear score; not production calibrated; it reports accuracy/abstention, not a calibration curve/error/proxy tied to probability reliability.
findings.impact: A learner can infer that an abstention band or accuracy metric substitutes for calibration, contradicting the course's own S34/S39 distinction.
findings.fix: Align RUBRIC, gate.json and demo: either compute/report an explicit calibration assessment on held-out synthetic data or rename/document a separate confidence-proxy requirement without calling the result calibrated.
findings.attack: La práctica guiada debe retirar apoyo de forma progresiva y acercarse a la tarea final; aquí la complejidad de dominio queda reemplazada por una gramática de tokens.
findings.defense: El patrón repetido hace visibles los estados de error y refuerza fail-closed.
findings.location: CP-N3-C RUBRIC.json; CP-N3-C gate.json; CP-N3-C demo.py
findings.justification: The stricter canonical RUBRIC/BRIEF explicitly require calibration and define it as score-probability correspondence. Abstention is separately required. Conflating the two makes the gate internally inconsistent.

findings.title: All 52 inherited theory findings remain unpatched.
S39-F57 through F62 block trustworthy CP-N3-C closure evidence.
S39-U01 live hydrated-body parity remains unresolved.
El evidence packet final pierde incertidumbre, lineage y proveniencia que la teoría dice necesitar
findings.evidence: s.get('fp_rate', 0) > thr treats a missing per-slice fp_rate as zero, so a slice with no metric silently passes. It also does not validate rate/threshold domains or support counts.
findings.impact: A learner can omit fp_rate for the most problematic subgroup and accidentally make the release look safer.
findings.fix: Require name, fp_rate and sample/support count for every slice; validate finite rates in [0,1] and a finite threshold in [0,1]; return REQUEST_SLICE_METRICS for any missing metric.
findings.attack: El proyecto independiente debería ser más estricto que los ejemplos, no menos. Sin lineage el revisor no puede reconstruir el score o el path.
findings.defense: El packet es deliberadamente pequeño y sintético.
findings.justification: The stated lesson is fail-closed fairness monitoring. A missing metric is an explicit edge case and currently becomes the safest possible value.

findings.title: Varias soluciones de We Do producen falsos PASS frente a los edge cases que el propio ejercicio afirma cubrir
findings.evidence: CF-3 is repeatedly presented as an expediente/review gate, but S39 never gives a plain-language expansion or tells the learner what CF-3 is, what artifact defines it, who performs the review, or where its acceptance contract lives.
