findings.impact: A learner can know they must leave CF-3 ready but not know what to submit, how it differs from CP-N3-C, or what an external reviewer checks.
findings.fix: At first use, define CF-3 in one sentence and link/reference its canonical checklist or evaluation artifact; distinguish it explicitly from CP-N3-C.
findings.attack: Un ejercicio de validación que acepta el adverso enseña exactamente el contrato incorrecto.
findings.defense: Los fixtures felices/invalid/incomplete usados en la salida prevista sí pasan los asserts visibles.
findings.location: tagline; theory opening callout/reference; I Do T4-A; YouDo; SelfCheck Q2
findings.justification: The Solarized self-sufficiency rule rejects distant-memory dependency for a central gate. S39 itself needs a minimal practical introduction even if CF-3 was mentioned earlier.

findings.title: Where is the canonical CF-3 artifact/checklist and what formal mechanism records its external review?
findings.evidence: S39 repeatedly refers to CF-3 but does not identify a canonical file/contract; capstone catalog names CP-N3-C but not CF-3.

findings.title: S39 closes N3/CF-3 while S27-S38 remain REPAIR_REQUIRED; upstream evidence cannot be treated as green.
findings.evidence: S39 says it receives CP-N3-A/B/C plus regression S27-S39 and CF-3, while the continuation ledger records unresolved material debt through S38.
findings.impact: A capstone can launder known defects into a false level promotion.
findings.fix: Make every upstream gate a machine-readable dependency and block CF-3 on any open critical regression.
findings.attack: A capstone can launder known defects into a false level promotion.
findings.defense: An integrator should aggregate prior work rather than reteach every dependency.

findings.title: section_contract() prints policy booleans and gate names rather than evaluating any gate.
findings.evidence: It returns gates=['CP-N3-C','regression_S27_S39','CF-3_external_review'], auto_fraud=False and self_declared_promotion=False.
findings.impact: Learners can mistake declared strings/booleans for evidence that promotion controls exist.
findings.fix: Rename it manifest_template or connect it to actual test results, artifact hashes and external-review status.
findings.attack: Learners can mistake declared strings/booleans for evidence that promotion controls exist.
findings.defense: The function is clearly a map/reference artifact.

findings.title: The canonical pipeline is represented as an ordered list of stage names, not an executed end-to-end flow.
findings.evidence: build_pipeline_payload() returns six stage strings and metadata only.
findings.impact: The gate promises integrated triage, but stage ordering alone cannot detect broken interfaces, data loss or routing changes.
findings.fix: Execute a synthetic case through real stage interfaces and assert each contract plus final identity/routing.
findings.attack: The gate promises integrated triage, but stage ordering alone cannot detect broken interfaces, data loss or routing changes.
findings.defense: A declarative stage map is useful orientation.

findings.title: build_pipeline_payload() accepts empty case IDs and invalid/non-finite scores.
findings.evidence: No validation is performed on case_id or score.
findings.impact: Corrupt score telemetry can enter the level-closing queue artifact.
findings.fix: Require stable nonempty case_id and finite score in the declared score domain.
findings.attack: Corrupt score telemetry can enter the level-closing queue artifact.
findings.defense: The happy fixture is valid.

findings.title: label_space='needs_review' and auto_fraud=False are hard-coded metadata, not controls over downstream behavior.
findings.evidence: The payload always prints auto_fraud False regardless of consumer behavior.
findings.impact: The curriculum can claim no-auto-fraud while no executable guard prevents unsafe mapping.
findings.fix: Add a policy validator/test that rejects forbidden label/action mappings across downstream queue outputs.
findings.attack: The curriculum can claim no-auto-fraud while no executable guard prevents unsafe mapping.
findings.defense: The prose repeatedly states the intended safety boundary.

findings.title: The S39-triage-stages figure alt text describes five stages and omits the model stage from the six-stage canonical pipeline.
findings.evidence: Alt says 'Cinco etapas —intake, ER, grafo, features, cola—'; code includes model_score.
findings.impact: The visual model erases a boundary the text says must be versioned and governed.
findings.fix: Show all six stages or explicitly state what is collapsed.
findings.attack: The visual model erases a boundary the text says must be versioned and governed.
findings.defense: The caption focuses on leakage rather than stage count.

findings.title: The registry labels versions 'semver' merely when every string contains a dot.
findings.evidence: compat='semver' if all('.' in meta['ver'] ...); 'not.a.version' passes.
findings.impact: Invalid version metadata can satisfy a compatibility concept.
findings.fix: Parse SemVer 2.0.0 and define the public contract/API whose compatibility the version communicates.
findings.attack: Invalid version metadata can satisfy a compatibility concept.
findings.defense: The lesson is emphasizing intent rather than parser implementation.

findings.title: The registry omits artifacts the prose says must be owned/versioned: threshold and packet template.
findings.evidence: Prose lists ER engine, graph_schema, feature_set, ranker, threshold and packet template; code registers only four.
findings.impact: Critical decision/explanation artifacts can remain unowned while registry appears complete.
findings.fix: Test registry completeness against an explicit required-artifact list.
findings.attack: Critical decision/explanation artifacts can remain unowned while registry appears complete.
findings.defense: Four examples illustrate the pattern.

findings.title: Owner strings are counted but not validated as contactable owners or signers.
findings.evidence: owner_count() counts arbitrary strings and does not resolve contactability/review authority.
findings.impact: Governance ownership becomes decorative metadata rather than escalation.
findings.fix: Use a synthetic owner directory with stable IDs/contact route plus release signer fields.
findings.attack: Governance ownership becomes decorative metadata rather than escalation.
findings.defense: A full identity system is outside the small lab.

findings.title: packet_ok() omits uncertainty and model contribution although T2-A says the packet contains those explanation layers.
findings.evidence: need=('case_id','score','evidence','graph_path').
findings.impact: A packet can pass while missing layers that supposedly make it defensible.
findings.fix: Declare required vs conditional layers explicitly and make the validator match.
findings.attack: A packet can pass while missing layers that supposedly make it defensible.
findings.defense: The prose makes model_contrib optional in one sentence.

findings.title: packet_ok() rejects score 0.0 but accepts NaN and score 2.0.
findings.evidence: Runtime: 0.0→False; NaN→True; 2.0→True.
findings.impact: Malformed evidence can pass while a legitimate low score fails.
findings.fix: Separate key presence from value-domain validation; require finite score in domain.
findings.attack: Malformed evidence can pass while a legitimate low score fails.
findings.defense: Truthiness is compact for the happy path.

findings.title: The packet's evidence list contains derived feature-like labels instead of source evidence records.
findings.evidence: evidence=['shared_phone_synth','tx_path_len_2'].
findings.impact: S35's feature-vs-observed-evidence misconception is carried into CF-3.
findings.fix: Use immutable evidence IDs/source facts; keep derived features in a separate section.
findings.attack: S35's feature-vs-observed-evidence misconception is carried into CF-3.
findings.defense: Synthetic labels are easy to read.

findings.title: graph_path is only node labels, with no edge IDs, source records, timestamps or graph snapshot/version.
findings.evidence: ['E1','ph:900','E2'] is treated as path evidence.
findings.impact: The reviewer cannot reconstruct whether the path existed in the model's graph version.
findings.fix: Add edge/evidence refs, graph snapshot/version and as-of time.
findings.attack: The reviewer cannot reconstruct whether the path existed in the model's graph version.
findings.defense: A node sequence is a useful visual shorthand.

findings.title: uncertainty='in_distribution' is hand-entered rather than produced by a validated uncertainty/OOD artifact.
findings.evidence: The packet hard-codes in_distribution.
findings.impact: Known S35/S36 uncertainty defects can be laundered into the capstone.
findings.fix: Require uncertainty method/version/reference snapshot/value/status and validation provenance.
findings.attack: Known S35/S36 uncertainty defects can be laundered into the capstone.
findings.defense: S39 is intended to integrate prior lessons.

findings.title: model_contrib={'shared_phone':0.4} is not linked to the actual model run, prediction or transformed row.
findings.evidence: No model_run_id, explanation_id or fidelity check appears.
findings.impact: The packet can show an explanation unrelated to its score.
findings.fix: Bind explanation to model run, transformed feature lineage and prediction/fidelity.
findings.attack: The packet can show an explanation unrelated to its score.
findings.defense: S35 is supposed to provide the semantics.

findings.title: priority_bucket() accepts NaN/out-of-range scores and invalid threshold ordering.
findings.evidence: Runtime: NaN→skip; thr_hi=.4/thr_lo=.75 with score=.5→queue_now.
findings.impact: Invalid inputs silently become operational decisions.
findings.fix: Validate finite score and ordered thresholds in the declared domain; fail closed.
findings.attack: Invalid inputs silently become operational decisions.
findings.defense: The supplied thresholds are valid.

findings.title: The prose says thresholds are selected in validation by capacity/cost, but code uses hand-entered 0.75/0.40.
findings.evidence: No validation dataset, cost function, search or threshold artifact is referenced.
findings.impact: An arbitrary cut can be narrated as validated.
findings.fix: Load threshold/version from a validation artifact with objective and capacity assumptions.
findings.attack: An arbitrary cut can be narrated as validated.
findings.defense: Fixed values keep the example readable.

findings.title: decisions.py contradicts its own prose by omitting actor, reason and timestamp.
findings.evidence: Entries contain case_id, auto, final, override only.
findings.impact: Human override cannot be reconstructed or defended.
findings.fix: Persist actor_id, reason, occurred_at, policy/model versions and immutable event_id.
findings.attack: Human override cannot be reconstructed or defended.
findings.defense: The code keeps the example short.

findings.title: Any truthy human string becomes final, including 'fraud'; empty string yields auto while override=True.
findings.evidence: Runtime human='fraud'→fraud; human=''→queue with override True.
findings.impact: Human control can create forbidden labels and inconsistent audit state.
findings.fix: Validate an allowlisted action enum and explicit override semantics.
findings.attack: Human control can create forbidden labels and inconsistent audit state.
findings.defense: Human override should beat auto within an allowed action space.

findings.title: The audit log is a process-local list.
findings.evidence: log=[] at module scope.
findings.impact: Restart loses evidence needed for appeal and external review.
findings.fix: Use append-only persistent storage with event IDs and reopen tests.
findings.attack: Restart loses evidence needed for appeal and external review.
findings.defense: A list demonstrates accumulation.

findings.title: The section promises appeal with another reviewer, but no appeal object/state/reviewer-separation check exists.

findings.defense: Conceptual explanation is useful.

findings.title: The outcome promises feedback operation, yet there is no feedback capture or training-handoff artifact.

findings.attack: Leakage and verification bias remain untested at the integrator gate.
findings.defense: The warning itself is correct.

findings.title: release_ok() checks truthiness rather than evidence from real controls.

findings.attack: A release can pass while controls are absent.
findings.defense: Checklists can prevent omissions.

findings.title: slice_metrics=True substitutes for a fairness assessment.

findings.attack: 'We have slice metrics' can be mistaken for measured fairness evidence.
findings.defense: S35 introduced fairness concepts.

findings.title: SSRF prevention is a release requirement in prose but no URL validation/allowlist/network boundary exists.

findings.attack: Security is reduced to a checkbox.
findings.defense: The prose correctly identifies SSRF risk.

findings.title: The prose says the risk owner signs the checklist, but no owner/reviewer ID, timestamp or reviewed hash is stored.

findings.impact: External review cannot know who approved which version.

findings.attack: External review cannot know who approved which version.
findings.defense: Crypto signing is unnecessary for this lesson.

findings.title: mode() receives drift_high as an external boolean with no reference, metric, threshold or window.

findings.title: human_only is a returned mode string, not a policy that blocks automatic scoring/routing/actions.

findings.title: The outcome promises rollback of model/threshold, but code handles only a previous model ID.

findings.title: happy/override/ood_abstain are strings, not scenario runs.

findings.title: The dossier omits roadmap-required version/revision, date, responsible owner, reviewer, paths/hashes, commands, results and issues.

findings.title: CP-N3-A/B/C are named but not linked to concrete versions/hashes/results.

findings.title: value_metrics() checks only key presence and accepts impossible values.

findings.defense: A tiny validator cannot ensure writing quality.

findings.title: S39 has no collected pytest evidence for its critical integrator claims.

findings.attack: None of the false greens blocks CI.

findings.title: The current Theory playground for integrator-phase2 is still CI/CD and monitoring.

findings.defense: CI/CD/monitoring are adjacent concepts.

findings.title: risk_checklist contains auto_fraud=False, but release_ok() ignores it.

findings.impact: The central no-autofraud safeguard can be violated while release_ok=True.
findings.fix: Make forbidden automatic decision mappings a hard release blocker and integration test.
findings.attack: The central no-autofraud safeguard can be violated while release_ok=True.
findings.defense: Other prose repeats the safety boundary.

findings.title: The six acceptance criteria omit explicit privacy, fairness, no-leakage, durable-resilience and upstream capstone gate evidence.
findings.evidence: Criteria are e2e, baseline, abstention, audit log, no_auto_fraud_label, regression smoke.
findings.impact: A nominal acceptance bundle can omit controls required by CF-3/N3 regression.
findings.fix: Expand the manifest or require regression results to enumerate these controls explicitly.
findings.attack: A nominal acceptance bundle can omit controls required by CF-3/N3 regression.
findings.defense: Some could be intended inside regression_smoke.

findings.title: La apelación no comprueba que el segundo revisor sea distinto del primero
findings.evidence: El texto exige 'otro revisor' y 'segundo par de ojos', pero `assess` solo verifica `record.get('second_reviewer')`; ni siquiera existe `first_reviewer`/`reviewer_id` en el fixture.
findings.fix: Incluir original_reviewer y second_reviewer, exigir identidad diferente y referenciar decision_event_id.
findings.attack: Un mismo revisor puede llenar `second_reviewer` con su propio id y obtener reopen.
findings.defense: El ejercicio busca introducir primero la presencia del campo.

findings.title: El ejercicio de fairness trata `fp_rate` ausente como 0 y puede aprobar una métrica que nunca se midió
findings.evidence: La solución usa `s.get('fp_rate', 0) > thr`. Si el slice existe pero no trae `fp_rate`, el valor por defecto 0 permite CONTINUE.
findings.fix: Validar schema de cada slice, soporte/denominador y uncertainty antes de comparar threshold.
findings.attack: Missing de una métrica de fairness no es evidencia de ausencia de daño; debe fallar cerrado.
findings.defense: Los fixtures incluidos siempre traen `fp_rate`.

findings.title: El autocheck de cinco preguntas de reconocimiento no mide los outcomes ni el gate de una sección integradora
findings.evidence: Los cinco ítems preguntan label_space, CF-3, packet, incident y SemVer. No evalúan baseline, calibración vs threshold, costo/utility, fairness con soporte, audit fields/appeal, drift vs performance degradation, provenance, cards derivadas ni lectura de evidencia ejecutada.
findings.fix: Convertir autocheck en diagnóstico de 8-10 ítems con microcasos y separar claramente 'quiz de recuerdo' de 'gate CP-N3-C'.
findings.attack: Un alumno puede aprobar 70% reconociendo vocabulario y seguir sin poder defender el capstone que la sección dice cerrar.
findings.defense: El proyecto You Do debería ser la evaluación auténtica principal.

findings.title: Does the current hydrated GitHub Pages S39 body exactly match main?
findings.evidence: The web crawler (last month) exposes the S39 card/tagline, but cannot expose the hydrated section body and also shows workload totals inconsistent with current source.

findings.title: Is canonical CP-N3-C RUBRIC.json gate_rule consumed by an evaluator elsewhere, or is it currently documentary only?
findings.evidence: CapstonesPage presents evidence as required/not registered and links rubric/brief; S39 YouDo only renders its own rubric strings and can be manually marked done.

findings.title: S39 declares nine learning outcomes although the roadmap contract specifies exactly eight outcomes per section.

findings.attack: Blueprint drift weakens assessment mapping and equivalence at the level-closing section.
findings.defense: The ninth outcome is substantively relevant to CF-3.

findings.title: queue_load() counts only new queue_now cases and ignores backlog, queue_batch, service rate and horizon.

findings.fix: Rename it accordingly or model backlog/service capacity over a stated shift.
findings.attack: One batch count can be mistaken for operational queue feasibility.

findings.title: The prose uses 'false-queue rate' without numerator, denominator or ground truth.

findings.attack: Different teams can compute incompatible quantities under the same name.
findings.defense: The phrase is intuitively suggestive.

findings.title: The example labels 'calib_drift' as root_cause although drift is usually a detected condition, not necessarily the causal process failure.
findings.evidence: postmortem['root_cause']='calib_drift'.

findings.title: Responsible-AI controls collapse into one boolean checklist.
findings.evidence: release_ok() returns all([...]).
findings.impact: This promotes checkbox compliance at the integrator section.
findings.fix: Keep checklist as index but link each item to continuous GOVERN/MAP/MEASURE/MANAGE evidence.
findings.attack: This promotes checkbox compliance at the integrator section.
findings.defense: Checklists can prevent omissions.

findings.title: The opening implies degradation from world change is detected by comparing today's inputs with validation inputs.
findings.evidence: It says drift se detecta comparando lo que entra hoy con lo que entraba cuando se validó.
findings.impact: Input drift may not imply performance drift, and concept/performance drift can occur without obvious input shift.
findings.fix: Name it input/data drift and distinguish outcome-dependent drift/performance checks.
findings.attack: Input drift may not imply performance drift, and concept/performance drift can occur without obvious input shift.
findings.defense: Input comparison is one important signal.

findings.title: The opening says fairness 'es una métrica'.
findings.evidence: Fairness assessment is harm/context-specific and commonly uses multiple disaggregated metrics/supports.
findings.impact: Learners may look for one universal fairness number.
findings.fix: Say fairness is a recurring assessment using selected harm-relevant metrics, support and uncertainty.
findings.attack: Learners may look for one universal fairness number.
findings.defense: By-group monitoring is directionally good.

findings.title: La pregunta de incidente fusiona `human_only` y rollback como si fueran una sola respuesta obligatoria
findings.evidence: La opción correcta es 'human_only / rollback a artefacto previo'.
findings.fix: Preguntar primero por el modo seguro inmediato y tratar rollback en otro ítem condicionado a bundle verificado.
findings.attack: Human-only es un modo de seguridad inmediato; rollback es un tratamiento separado que requiere un target compatible y puede no ser la primera o única acción.
findings.defense: En muchos incidentes ambos ocurren juntos y la explicación intenta enfatizar fail-closed.

findings.title: Parte de los recursos no enseña lo que la nota afirma o es demasiado genérica para S39
findings.evidence: El enlace 'Google Model Cards' ahora redirige al catálogo de model cards de Google DeepMind, no a una guía sobre cómo construir una card.; Python logging documenta una librería de logging general; no cubre por sí sola integridad/tamper resistance, actor attribution y separación de audit trail.; Twelve-Factor App es una guía de aplicaciones SaaS y no una referencia específica de control plane de Responsible ML.; CS50P y Py4E son recursos generales de Python; en una sección N3 avanzada añaden ruido y no remedian los conceptos críticos de triage responsable.
findings.fix: Priorizar referencias directas: Model Cards paper/framework, NIST AI RMF Core/Playbook, scikit-learn calibration + threshold tuning, OWASP Logging Cheat Sheet; mover CS50P/Py4E a recursos generales del curso.
findings.attack: Los recursos deberían permitir al alumno cerrar exactamente las brechas del proyecto, no solo navegar a material prestigioso o general.
findings.defense: Algunos sirven como contexto amplio o pedagogía adicional.

findings.title: Generic label has no author/title/URL, so learner cannot identify the intended reference.
findings.impact: Which incident-management handbook should I use?
findings.fix: Name a specific referenced handbook or remove the entry.

findings.title: We Do promises precise fail-closed diagnostics but relabels decision-policy violations as stage-order failures.
T2-A E1/E2 teach case_id+score as mandatory; T2-A E3 silently accepts packets without them.
Theory requires a different reviewer and attributable audit; We Do/You Do cannot demonstrate either.
Fairness exercise says missing metrics fail closed but per-slice missing fp_rate is converted to zero.
S39 calls You Do the CP-N3-C closure while the canonical CP-N3-C gate requires evidence the scaffold never computes or verifies.
Two incompatible rubrics are presented for the same CP-N3-C and the lesson UI renders gate labels as if they were weights.
Cards claim appeal, rollback and metrics that the starter did not execute/measure.
Canonical CP-N3-C supporting artifacts disagree with their own brief/rubric: dataset fields do not match, and demo can self-report pass without required calibration.
CF-3 is central to closure but remains unexplained internal shorthand in S39.
Live crawler shows current card/tagline but a cached workload total (1040h) inconsistent with current source meta; full hydrated S39 body parity could not be independently observed from crawler text.
The lesson repeatedly substitutes declared metadata/booleans/strings for executable evidence of the control it names.
Practice sometimes weakens contracts that the preceding theory/earlier exercise established.
The S39 You Do and the canonical CP-N3-C package disagree on required evidence and grading semantics.
Generated governance artifacts contain unsupported hard-coded metrics/control claims.
Central closure identifier CF-3 is not self-sufficiently introduced.
What exact artifact proves calibration/baseline/threshold provenance
What formal rubric governs CP-N3-C acceptance
How reviewer identity/independence is proven
What CF-3 is and where its checklist lives
REJECT_STAGE_ORDER used for non-order policy failures
audit=True treated as audit evidence
layers=4 treated as explanation-layer evidence
local S39 rubric vs canonical CP-N3-C 0-3 rubric
CF-3
evidence packet source/provenance semantics when represented only by labels
external review contract
El proyecto independiente puede declarar READY mediante cuatro flags manuales sin validar los artefactos
findings.evidence: `readiness()` solo comprueba que cada key de REQUIRED sea exactamente True. El starter instruye al alumno a activar `evidence[...] = True`; no recibe qa_scenarios/context_map/c4/adrs para verificarlos. El counterexample con cuatro True devuelve READY aunque los ADR sigan draft y observed_ms siga None.
findings.impact: READY es derivable de cuatro booleans editables, no de evidencia.
findings.fix: Eliminar flags editables. `readiness()` debe recibir los artefactos y derivar resultados de validators ejecutables con evidence IDs; cada gate debe informar por qué pasa/falla.
findings.attack: El principal gate del You Do se puede saltar escribiendo cuatro booleanos. Es el anti-patrón que la propia sección denuncia: declaración presentada como evidencia.
findings.defense: Los comentarios dicen explícitamente que el alumno solo debe activar la bandera después de completar el artefacto.

findings.title: S40 presenta su dossier como gate/evidencia de CP-N4-A aunque el capstone canónico cierra en S43 y exige un servicio gobernado
findings.evidence: El catálogo/BRIEF/RUBRIC de CP-N4-A fija `gate_section: S43` y acceptance sobre API, auth, rate limit, health, non-root, redacted logs y migrations. S40 es contributing section. S40 usa frases como 'Evidencia de CP-N4-A', 'gate CP-N4-A (mapa de arquitectura gobernado)' y 'CP-N4-A exige fronteras explícitas'.
findings.impact: El alumno recibe una definición incorrecta del momento y alcance del gate CP-N4-A.
findings.fix: Nombrar el artefacto `evidence contribution to CP-N4-A` o `S40 architecture gate`; decir explícitamente que CP-N4-A se evalúa en S43 y acumula evidencia de S40-S43.
findings.attack: La sección convierte un artefacto incremental de arquitectura en una definición distinta del gate canónico del capstone.
findings.defense: S40 sí contribuye al CP-N4-A y sus fronteras son prerrequisito para el servicio que S43 cierra.
findings.location: callouts + I Do intro + You Do portfolioNote + self-check Q3

findings.title: El helper de ADR es mucho más débil que la rúbrica ADR que el mismo You Do declara obligatoria
findings.evidence: PortfolioNote exige contexto de negocio, >=2 alternatives, consequences con residual, rollback operable y status accepted firmado por dueño. `adrs_accepted()` solo exige dos ADRs y que decision/alternatives/consequences/rollback sean truthy + status accepted. No lee context, no exige dos alternatives por ADR, no modela residual, owner/firma ni verifica rollback.
findings.impact: ADRs pueden pasar un helper más débil que la rúbrica declarada.
findings.fix: Modelar local ADR rubric en el schema y checker: business_context no vacío; >=2 alternatives con tradeoff evidence; benefit + residual_cost/risk; rollback command/test; decision_owner; accepted_by/accepted_at.
findings.attack: El checker oficial false-greenea exactamente los ADR que el texto dice que no deben pasar.
findings.defense: El alumno puede ampliar el esquema y la función antes de activar evidence.

findings.title: La solución oficial aprueba un grafo de dependencias vacío aunque el texto dice que un grafo vacío no demuestra nada
findings.evidence: `all(tuple(edge) not in forbidden for edge in record['dependencies'])` es True para `dependencies=[]`; el retrospective de E2 dice literalmente que un grafo vacío no demuestra capas limpias.
findings.impact: La solución de referencia aprueba ausencia de grafo como arquitectura limpia.
findings.fix: Exigir `dependencies` no vacío y una cobertura mínima de relaciones esperadas antes de evaluar forbidden/cycles; el caso vacío debe ir a `REVIEW_LAYER_OWNER`.
findings.attack: La solución de referencia contradice la explicación pedagógica y recompensa ausencia de evidencia.
findings.defense: El fixture feliz contiene tres aristas y la intención era enseñar dos aristas prohibidas.

findings.title: S40 llama completo a un quality-attribute scenario que omite el artefacto afectado
findings.evidence: La forma enseñada es source + stimulus + environment + response + measure/target + owner. La estructura canónica de SEI usa seis partes: source, stimulus, environment, artifact, response y response measure. Owner es una extensión de gobernanza útil, pero no sustituye artifact.
findings.impact: El scenario QA incompleto se enseña, practica, proyecta y evalúa de forma consistente pero incorrecta.
findings.fix: Añadir `artifact` de forma explícita a la definición, fixtures, validators, You Do y Q1. Mantener `owner_id` como campo adicional de gobernanza, no como reemplazo.
findings.attack: La omisión se repite en demostración, práctica, proyecto y evaluación, por lo que el alumno no aprende a declarar qué parte del sistema recibe el estímulo.
findings.defense: El ejemplo siempre habla de intake y puede parecer que el artefacto está implícito.
findings.location: I Do T1-A + We Do T1-A + You Do + self-check

findings.title: Opening says S39 closed triage with controls/evidence and the system works, while the current audit continuation says S39 REPAIR_REQUIRED and CF-3 blocked.
findings.fix: State that S39 produced provisional artifacts with open defects; architecture must not promote them until repaired gates are linked.
findings.attack: Phase-3 architecture begins by laundering unresolved N3 evidence into a working-system premise.
findings.defense: S40 needs a narrative bridge from S39.

findings.title: Architecture dossier names stages but does not bind boundaries/interfaces to immutable artifact IDs, hashes, versions or contract-test evidence from S39.
findings.fix: Require an architecture manifest mapping every context/interface to artifact/version/hash/as-of and contract-test IDs.
findings.attack: A diagram can be internally tidy while referring to stale model, graph, feature, policy or decision artifacts.
findings.defense: S40 is intentionally stdlib/conceptual.

findings.title: S39 governance interfaces—human decision/override, appeal, feedback eligibility, drift events, rollback bundle and no-autofraud policy—are absent from S40's boundary model.
findings.fix: Represent governance as explicit interfaces/policies crossing contexts, with IDs and ownership, rather than omitting them.
findings.attack: Context separation can erase the cross-cutting traceability CF-3 requires.
findings.defense: S40 focuses on architecture concepts rather than reproducing every S39 detail.

findings.title: s40_map_contract.py returns gate names and literal booleans instead of evaluating architecture evidence.
findings.fix: Compute gate results from actual manifest/graph/contract artifacts; keep labels separate from evidence.
findings.attack: agent_orchestration_topic=False and pii_allowed=False prove nothing about rendered content or data flow.
findings.defense: Reference block says names explain criteria rather than asking learners to memorize them.

findings.title: Theory playground is a Researcher/Analyst/Writer multi-agent simulation even though S40 explicitly excludes agent orchestration.
findings.fix: Preserve id but replace mapping with architecture/DDD decision playground.
findings.attack: Learner practices the exact topic the section says is out of scope.
findings.defense: The stable id is historical and the playground likely predates the rewrite.

findings.title: The p95/100 req/s scenario is handwritten and qa_complete never computes p95 or binds it to benchmark samples/environment.
findings.fix: Reference a BenchmarkResult/manifest and distinguish target from measured evidence.
findings.attack: S37 measurement debt is silently converted into valid architecture evidence.
findings.defense: S40 is about scenario structure rather than load-testing mechanics.

findings.title: qa_complete validates key presence but empty source/stimulus/environment/response/owner still passes.
findings.fix: Validate non-empty normalized text and owner identity against an ownership registry.
findings.attack: CE01 produces complete=True without an owner or meaningful scenario.
findings.defense: The happy-path fixture uses populated fields.

findings.title: qa_complete accepts booleans, negative times and infinite targets.
findings.fix: Reject bool/non-numeric/non-finite/negative values and require observed measure semantics.
findings.attack: CE02–CE04 turn impossible telemetry into valid evidence.
findings.defense: Typed educational fixtures are intended.

findings.title: Owner is a free-form string such as platform/arquitectura despite outcomes requiring a contactable owner and residual acceptance.
findings.fix: Use synthetic owner_id plus approval metadata and contact/escalation reference; no external directory required.
findings.attack: No actor ID, role, approval event, timestamp or escalation path exists.
findings.defense: Human directory integration is outside stdlib scope.

findings.title: T1-A declares S40-layer-imports, but it is absent from bespoke FIGURES and all FIGURE_DATA registries; FigureFrame therefore returns null.
findings.fix: Register the figure or replace with an existing valid ID and test rendering.
findings.attack: Declared instructional figure is invisible.
findings.defense: Caption text remains in source but FigureFrame intentionally returns null for unknown IDs.

findings.title: Registered S40-ports-adapters is attached to T1-B trade-offs instead of T2-B ports/adapters.
findings.fix: Move the figure to T2-B; keep T1-B focused on criteria/risk.
findings.attack: The only ports/adapters visual appears before and away from its matching explanation.
findings.defense: It can serve as an example decision alternative.

findings.title: Theory calls 3.8/2.2 weighted-cost scores but defines no criteria, weights, raw values or calculation.
findings.fix: Expose criterion, weight, normalized value and contribution or stop calling the values weighted scores.
findings.attack: Decision table becomes an unexplained magic number ranking.
findings.defense: The lab emphasizes min-cost direction rather than MCDA mechanics.

findings.title: Prose defines residual risk as probability×impact with mitigation, but choose_option receives one scalar residual_ok only.
findings.fix: Represent risk record with likelihood, impact, mitigation, residual value, threshold and evidence.
findings.attack: Probability, impact, mitigation and residual rationale can all be absent while gate passes.
findings.defense: Scalar simplifies the lab.

findings.title: Outcome/callout require an owner to accept residual risk, but choose_option has no owner or acceptance event.
findings.fix: Require owner_id and signed/recorded acceptance in the decision artifact.
findings.attack: A critical governance requirement exists only in prose.
findings.defense: Fixture paragraph names arquitectura.

findings.title: choose_option crashes on empty options, accepts negative residual, can select NaN by ordering and collapses duplicate names in the scores dict.
findings.fix: Validate non-empty unique alternatives, finite scores, residual domain and deterministic tie policy.
findings.attack: CE05–CE08 make invalid decision evidence look valid or non-deterministic.
findings.defense: Happy-path options are clean.

findings.title: deps_ok([]), unknown layer names and dependency cycles all pass.
findings.fix: Validate node vocabulary, required layers, non-empty evidence, cycles and permitted dependency rules.
findings.attack: CE09–CE11 show absence/corruption of architecture evidence is green.
findings.defense: The helper only illustrates two prohibited edges.

findings.title: Two exact forbidden edges cannot prove dependency inversion, transitive boundaries or port ownership.
findings.fix: Use an explicit architecture policy/allowlist with graph semantics and contract edges.
findings.attack: The validator can approve arbitrary edges it has never defined.
findings.defense: A compact blacklist makes the core examples memorable.

findings.title: Theory promises implements_port, empty domain imports and ≥3 contract tests, but code runs one happy MemoryCaseRepo call and prints port_ok=True.
findings.fix: Run a shared contract suite against at least memory and one alternate fake/adapter; inspect/import-boundary evidence separately.
findings.attack: No contract tests or import evidence exist.
findings.defense: Protocol type hint demonstrates dependency direction.

findings.title: Text says SQL adapter can replace memory without rewriting business rule, but no second adapter or failure behavior is tested.
findings.fix: Add a second stdlib fake adapter with the same contract, including not-found/error semantics.
findings.attack: Structural shape alone does not prove semantic substitutability.
findings.defense: The section intentionally avoids SQL dependency.

findings.title: Lab makes token-set disjointness a bounded-context promotion rule even though DDD contexts may share the same term with different local models.
findings.fix: Validate local definition/ownership and explicit translation; never require vocabulary tokens themselves to be disjoint.
findings.attack: Fowler explicitly notes products/customers can be common concepts across contexts; mapping handles polysemy. CE12 rejects a legitimate mapped overlap.
findings.defense: Source labels disjointness as a didactic simplification.

findings.title: contexts_ok hard-codes only intake/ER and case→record; it does not model relation type, direction, ownership, version or other promised contexts.
findings.fix: Represent context nodes and typed directional relationships/translations across the promised contexts.
findings.attack: A one-pair dict is not the context map described by the outcome/tagline.
findings.defense: It is a minimal first example.

findings.title: Boundaries carry words but not S39 node/edge/source evidence IDs, artifact versions, graph snapshot or as-of.
findings.fix: Define interface envelopes that retain evidence/provenance fields through translations.
findings.attack: Translation can preserve terminology while losing investigative provenance.
findings.defense: DDD lesson focuses on language boundaries.

findings.title: merge_scores accepts non-finite/out-of-range scores and weights outside [0,1].
findings.fix: Validate finite score/weight domains or use a non-risk example that cannot contaminate triage semantics.
findings.attack: CE14–CE15 can emit values outside the triage score contract inherited from S39.
findings.defense: It illustrates a stateless service, not model validation.

findings.title: adr_ready treats {'context','container'} as sufficient C4 evidence without people, systems, containers, responsibilities or relationships.
findings.fix: Validate actual C4 model records and relationships; level presence is only schema, not evidence.
findings.attack: A set of level names can green the gate while no architecture map exists.
findings.defense: The source separately narrates example elements.

findings.title: adr_ready validates field-name membership and accepted string, not content quality.
findings.fix: Make the code enforce non-empty context, ≥2 alternatives, balanced consequences/residual, executable rollback and decision content.
findings.attack: CE16 passes an empty semantic ADR containing only labels.
findings.defense: T4-A paragraph later gives a richer five-part rubric.

findings.title: status='accepted' is not tied to the contactable owner/signature the prose requires.
findings.fix: Require decision_owner, accepted_by, accepted_at and review/reference IDs in the ADR record.
findings.attack: Any caller can type accepted and pass.
findings.defense: Owner verification is organizational metadata outside the minimal function.

findings.title: feature_flag_off is presented as rollback without compatibility, data-state or release-bundle evidence.
findings.fix: Define rollback preconditions, version bundle, verification test and irreversible side effects.
findings.attack: Turning off async flow may not reverse messages already emitted or schema/policy changes.
findings.defense: It is an illustrative rollback signal.

findings.title: Theory says compatible changes are additive and adding fields/events preserves old consumers.
findings.fix: Teach compatibility relative to a declared public contract and tolerant-reader/extensibility policy.
findings.attack: Compatibility depends on explicit contract/extensibility rules; strict clients can reject unknown fields and behavioral changes can break without field deletion.
findings.defense: The example consumer intentionally ignores priority.

findings.title: No API policy says whether clients must ignore unknown response fields, enums are evolvable, ordering is contractual, or new fields may be required.
findings.fix: S40 should define the compatibility policy S41 will implement before calling changes safe.
findings.attack: Microsoft guidelines explicitly require services to define breaking-change rules because different services make different choices.
findings.defense: S41 will implement the API.

findings.title: additive_ok compares one concrete v1 dict to one v_next dict and length.
findings.fix: Define schema/behavior contract fixtures and run old consumer contract tests against candidate versions.
findings.attack: CE17 cannot detect schema optionality/types/enums/behavior or other consumers.
findings.defense: consumer_view demonstrates one old reader survives the example.

findings.title: Versioning language is used without declaring the public API and compatibility surface first.
findings.fix: Define public contract/schemas/events and compatibility rules before version increments or compatibility claims.
findings.attack: SemVer explicitly requires a precise public API before version numbers can encode compatibility.
findings.defense: S40 does not explicitly claim full SemVer compliance.

findings.title: Outcome/callout require debt owner and retire_on, but Theory executable never consumes either field.
findings.fix: Include debt record in the executable contract with owner identity, retirement condition/date and review status.
findings.attack: The printed compatibility result can be green with no technical-debt governance at all.
findings.defense: The paragraph's example names platform and 2026-12-01.

findings.title: No Theory code is a collected pytest suite despite the roadmap's systematic pytest requirement from S27.
findings.fix: Convert architecture validators and compatibility contracts into collected tests, including adversarial cases.
findings.attack: All runtime false greens discovered here can regress without blocking CI.
findings.defense: S40 examples are short stdlib snippets.

findings.title: Theory repeats that ER does not imply fraud/relationship and review remains human, but architecture provides no explicit policy/interface preventing score or graph evidence from becoming a verdict across contexts.
findings.fix: Represent no-autofraud/abstention/human-decision policy as a named versioned boundary contract inherited from S39.
findings.attack: The critical N3 safety invariant can disappear at the architecture boundary while prose stays correct.
findings.defense: S40 is not a triage-policy lesson.

findings.title: El riesgo residual puede aprobarse con `risk_owner=''`
findings.evidence: Las soluciones incluyen `risk_owner` en `required`, pero el PASS/CONTINUE solo comprueba alternativa mínima y `residual_risk <= 2`.
findings.impact: Debido a este problema, un alumno razonable puede aprender que escribir una clave `risk_owner` vacía satisface accountability y que la aceptación humana del riesgo no necesita existir.
findings.fix: Validar owner no vacío y una aceptación sintética (`accepted_by`, `accepted_at`, `decision_id`) separada del cálculo de score.
findings.attack: El outcome y el propio texto exigen dueño que acepta el residual; la solución solo exige que exista una clave vacía.
findings.defense: El fixture feliz usa `arquitectura` y el objetivo principal del ejercicio es min frente a max.

findings.title: El ejercicio usa monto negativo como adverso pero la solución no valida el monto
findings.evidence: El fixture inválido contiene `amount:-1`; la solución solo valida prefijo CASE-, currency PEN, vo_frozen y service_stateless. Un `amount:-999` con el resto válido obtiene PASS.
findings.impact: Debido a este problema, un alumno razonable puede creer que el gate comprobó la invariante monetaria cuando nunca la leyó, o dedicar tiempo a arreglar un campo que no influye en la solución.
findings.fix: O eliminar el monto negativo del adverso y declarar que el dominio de amount queda fuera, o definir y validar la invariante de amount. No insinuar una regla que el checker ignora.
findings.attack: El dato adverso señala al alumno que amount forma parte del modelo sano, pero el checker ignora precisamente esa dimensión.
findings.defense: El subtema pretende distinguir entity/VO/service, no enseñar reglas monetarias completas.

findings.title: La práctica califica la disyunción léxica como regla de bounded contexts pese a que el propio texto admite que DDD no exige eso
findings.evidence: Los tres reference solutions exigen `intake.isdisjoint(er)`; hints y feedback reconocen que en DDD real un término puede repetirse con significado local si el mapa lo declara.
findings.impact: Debido a este problema, un alumno razonable puede memorizar que los bounded contexts deben usar vocabularios disjuntos y rechazar contextos legítimos que usan la misma palabra con modelos locales diferentes.
findings.fix: Practicar local_definition + owner + typed relationship + translation cuando corresponda; un token compartido solo es problema si el significado o integración quedan ambiguos, no por intersección de sets.
findings.attack: La caveat correcta queda subordinada a tres ejercicios en los que compartir un token significa SPLIT_CONTEXTS.
findings.defense: El archivo lo denomina explícitamente una simplificación didáctica para hacer visible la traducción case→record.

findings.title: I Do modela proxies declarativos precisamente donde You Do exige evidencia defendible
findings.evidence: Los demos modelan `qa_complete` por keys, scores escritos a mano, blacklist de dos aristas, `implements_port=True`, `vo_frozen=True`, `service_stateless=True`, sets de nombres de C4/ADR y set inclusion de campos.
findings.impact: Debido a este problema, un alumno razonable puede imitar el patrón superficial —poner un flag, un nombre o un número— y llegar a You Do sin un modelo de cómo demostrar arquitectura, compatibilidad, aprobación o rollback.
findings.fix: Mantener demos pequeñas, pero hacer que cada una ejecute una evidencia mínima real: dos adapters contra el mismo contract test, un C4 record con relaciones, un ADR con approval record, un benchmark result referenciado.
findings.attack: La demostración del experto enseña cómo producir una representación nominal del control, no cómo producir o verificar la evidencia que justificaría el control.
findings.defense: Las demos son deliberadamente pequeñas y stdlib-first para controlar carga cognitiva.

findings.title: El requisito exige seis contextos pero el starter entrega cuatro y aun así permite marcar context_map=True
findings.evidence: Requirements: intake/ER/relación/triage/reporting/IA. Starter rows: intake, er, triage, reporting. No existe relación ni IA. Retrospective vuelve a preguntar por filas de relación e IA. `evidence['context_map']=True` queda manual.
findings.impact: Debido a este problema, un alumno razonable puede creer que el context map starter ya representa el alcance pedido, entregar cuatro contextos y no saber que dos faltantes son criterio de gate, o simplemente activar el flag sin añadirlos.
findings.fix: O incluir los seis contextos mínimos con TODOs de relaciones/traducciones, o convertir el requirement en una tarea explícita y hacer que el validator compare el conjunto contra REQUIRED_CONTEXTS.
findings.attack: El scaffold que debe reducir carga omite dos objetos explícitamente requeridos y luego deja al alumno autodeclarar que el mapa está completo.
findings.defense: El comentario `amplía para tu diseño` puede interpretarse como invitación deliberada a completar el mapa.

findings.title: El proyecto exige normal/BLOCK_ARCHITECTURE/REVIEW_ADR pero el scaffold no implementa ni prueba esas rutas
findings.evidence: Requirement: automatiza un caso normal, breach (`BLOCK_ARCHITECTURE`) e incierto (`REVIEW_ADR`). Starter define qa/context_map/c4/adrs/readiness y no contiene router, fixtures ni asserts para ninguno de esos tres resultados.
findings.impact: Debido a este problema, un alumno razonable puede completar los cuatro artefactos y no saber qué función debe producir BLOCK_ARCHITECTURE o REVIEW_ADR, ni qué diferencia operacional hay entre breach e incertidumbre.
findings.fix: Proporcionar contrato de función y tres fixtures, no la implementación: `review_dossier(dossier)->status` con expected outputs NORMAL/ARCH_BREACH/UNCERTAIN_REVIEW.
findings.attack: La propiedad fail-closed más transferible del proyecto queda como prosa sin un punto de entrada común para demostrarla.
findings.defense: You Do es independiente y no necesita resolver todos los pasos al alumno.

findings.title: La rúbrica visible evalúa criterios no modelados en S40 y no coincide con la rúbrica canónica del capstone al que se vincula
findings.evidence: Visible S40 rubric: Correctitud 25, pruebas 20, comunicación 15, reproducibilidad 15, 'Operación: SLO, observabilidad y rollback' 15, 'Seguridad, privacidad y least privilege' 10. S40 no enseña/scaffoldea observabilidad ni least privilege de forma suficiente. CP-N4-A canonical rubric usa correctness 35, robustness 20, maintainability 25, responsible_use 20 y gate en S43.
findings.impact: Debido a este problema, un alumno razonable puede perder puntos por SLO/observabilidad/least privilege sin haber recibido modelado/práctica equivalente en S40 o asumir que esos pesos son los de CP-N4-A.
findings.fix: Etiquetar explícitamente `Rúbrica de S40 (artefacto incremental)` y restringirla a outcomes enseñados; enlazar por separado la rúbrica CP-N4-A que se aplicará en S43.
findings.attack: El alumno no sabe si está siendo evaluado por el dossier incremental, por conceptos no enseñados aquí o por una rúbrica de capstone diferente.
findings.defense: Una sección puede tener su propia rúbrica distinta de la rúbrica global del capstone.

findings.title: La explicación del quiz usa 'invertir la dependencia' para el anti-patrón justo después de enseñar Dependency Inversion como el diseño correcto
findings.evidence: T2-B define DIP/Inversión de dependencias como dependencias hacia el dominio. Q5 explica: 'Invertir la dependencia (dominio → framework) acopla el núcleo a la infra'.
findings.impact: Debido a este problema, un alumno razonable puede recordar 'inversión de dependencias = dominio→framework' o creer que aplicar DIP es el breach que el quiz penaliza.
findings.fix: Reservar `inversión de dependencias (DIP)` para el principio; llamar al breach `dependencia del dominio hacia infraestructura/framework`.
findings.attack: La misma locución designa en un lugar el principio correcto y en otro el breach, sin anclar dirección.
findings.defense: El paréntesis dominio→framework permite inferir qué dirección se considera mala.

findings.title: El autocheck enseña como ADR aceptable un mínimo que contradice la propia rúbrica ADR de S40
findings.evidence: Q7 da por correcto `decision + alternatives + consequences + rollback con status accepted`. T4-A/portfolioNote exige además business context, >=2 alternatives, residual y dueño contactable que firma.
findings.impact: Debido a este problema, un alumno razonable puede memorizar el conjunto de cuatro campos como definición completa del gate y omitir contexto, aceptación y calidad de alternativas en el proyecto.
findings.fix: Preguntar por el contrato local completo o cambiar la pregunta a 'qué campos forman parte del núcleo que luego se valida con la rúbrica local'.
findings.attack: La evaluación de recuperación reduce los requisitos justo donde debería consolidarlos.
findings.defense: La pregunta dice 'campos mínimos' y algunos requisitos pueden interpretarse como calidad interna de esos campos.

findings.title: El autocheck convierte `v1_fields ⊆ v11_fields` en regla suficiente de compatibilidad
findings.evidence: La opción correcta dice que el consumer contract permanece verde cuando los campos de v1 se conservan y la deuda tiene owner/retire_on. No menciona extensibility policy, tipos, requiredness, enums, behavior ni ejecutar el consumer contract.
findings.impact: Debido a este problema, un alumno razonable puede declarar seguro cualquier cambio aditivo de campos y confundir deuda técnica con prueba de compatibilidad del consumidor.
findings.fix: Condicionar la respuesta al contrato/policy declarados y a tests del consumidor v1; debt governance debe ser una condición separada.
findings.attack: La pregunta recompensa precisamente la generalización que el audit técnico ya demostró falsa.
findings.defense: El ejemplo concreto usa un consumidor antiguo que solo lee case_id/status y tolera priority.

findings.title: Tagline promises separation of intake, ER, relationship, triage, reporting and AI, while Theory's executable context-map contract only models intake and ER.
findings.fix: Teach at least the full boundary/interface skeleton in Theory or narrow the tagline to what Theory demonstrates.
findings.attack: Learner-facing headline overstates demonstrated breadth.
findings.defense: The You Do later expands the map, but it is outside this lesson-only theory evidence.

findings.title: Job relevance says this documentation is what a technical committee accepts before approving a serious project, phrased as a universal fact.
findings.fix: Use scoped language: 'puede formar parte de la evidencia que un comité técnico revisa'.
findings.attack: Architecture governance varies by organization; C4/ADR dossiers are useful practices, not universal approval prerequisites.
findings.defense: It is motivational shorthand for professional relevance.

findings.title: S40-layer-imports describes layers/framework imports but is attached to T1-A quality attributes rather than T2-A layers.
findings.fix: Move it to T2-A and use a QA-scenario figure in T1-A if needed.
findings.attack: Even after renderer repair, the diagram is separated from the concept it explains, increasing split attention.
findings.defense: It previews a later architectural concern.

findings.title: vo_frozen=True remains a literal checklist rather than an executable immutable value object, despite the outcome promising testable invariants.
findings.fix: Use a frozen dataclass/NamedTuple in Theory so the stated invariant is actually executable.
findings.attack: The code cannot detect mutation and therefore cannot substantiate the invariant.
findings.defense: The prose explicitly warns the flag does not freeze a dict and points to frozen dataclass/NamedTuple in production.

findings.title: Opening/T4-A describe alternatives and rollback as if every ADR definition requires them.
findings.fix: Say 'en la rúbrica de S40 añadimos alternatives y rollback' and distinguish it from the ADR concept.
findings.attack: Nygard core ADR fields are status/context/decision/consequences; MADR and local governance templates add considered options. Rollback is valuable but local.
findings.defense: S40 deliberately uses a stricter governance rubric.

findings.title: 'Versiona eventos (case.created) al cambiar semántica' gives no event schema/version field, migration strategy or consumer compatibility rule.
findings.fix: Show explicit event schema version/evolution rule and consumer contract.
findings.attack: A stable event name does not itself version changed semantics.
findings.defense: It is a forward-looking reminder before S41+.

findings.title: A single retire_on date substitutes for consumer inventory, support status, deprecation notice and removal criteria.
findings.fix: At minimum define affected consumers, support status, migration path and earliest removal condition.
findings.attack: API evolution needs an upgrade/deprecation path, not only a future date.
findings.defense: S40 only introduces debt governance, not full lifecycle operations.

findings.title: Veinticuatro ejercicios repiten casi la misma gramática de reparar predicates PASS/REJECT/MISSING
findings.evidence: Cada subtema usa E1 corregir una condición, E2 valid/invalid/missing y E3 CONTINUE/breach/REQUEST con cambios principalmente de tokens y nombres.
findings.impact: Debido a este problema, un alumno razonable puede completar gran parte del We Do por pattern matching sin poder transferir el criterio a un dossier de arquitectura que no venga premodelado como dict y token de error.
findings.fix: Conservar E1 predicate repair donde aporte, pero convertir parte de E2/E3 en generación, clasificación, crítica y reconstrucción de artefactos con variación estructural.
findings.attack: La repetición produce fluidez en reconocer `if missing` y cambiar comparadores, pero ofrece poca práctica en dibujar fronteras, formular escenarios, comparar alternativas, revisar un ADR o diseñar un context map desde evidencia nueva.
findings.defense: El patrón común reduce carga de interfaz y refuerza fail-closed de forma consistente.

findings.title: El context map mezcla nombres de patrones DDD con etiquetas genéricas sin explicar su semántica
findings.evidence: Rows usan relation=`customer`, `supplier`, `downstream`, `consumer`; T3-A nombra customer/supplier, ACL y shared kernel como relaciones/patrones, pero downstream/consumer no se introducen como patrones equivalentes ni se define dirección/ownership.
findings.impact: Debido a este problema, un alumno razonable puede usar `downstream` o `consumer` como si fueran patrones de Context Mapping equivalentes a Customer/Supplier o ACL y no saber qué obligaciones de traducción o poder implica cada relación.
findings.fix: Definir una enum local documentada o usar patrones DDD explícitos con dirección y explicación; separar `data_flow_role` de `context_mapping_pattern`.
findings.attack: El alumno recibe un campo `relation` cuyos valores parecen pertenecer a una taxonomía estable, aunque mezclan términos formales y etiquetas informales.
findings.defense: Los strings pueden ser etiquetas locales del lab, no una enumeración oficial DDD.

findings.title: artifact falta en toda la cadena de quality-attribute scenarios.
la explicación exige evidencia; el checker consume autoatestiguación.
se exigen 6 contextos, starter trae 4 y retrospective revela los 2 faltantes.
artefacto incremental se presenta como gate final con rúbrica distinta.
texto dice que grafo vacío no demuestra nada; solución le da PASS/CONTINUE.
owner que acepta residual se reduce a key presence y puede estar vacío.
se reconoce que vocabulario disjunto no es DDD general, pero se califica como regla en tres ejercicios.
'inversión de dependencias' se usa para principio correcto y para breach.
autocheck consolida versiones más débiles de ADR y API compatibility.
FastAPI + TestClient are optional; project is stdlib
findings.evidence: FastAPI + TestClient are optional; project is stdlib
findings.impact: The learner can pass a FastAPI section without using FastAPI.
findings.fix: Make FastAPI(), Pydantic, Depends, TestClient and app.openapi() mandatory after the pure pre-lab.
findings.attack: La sección se titula APIs con FastAPI y varios outcomes prometen FastAPI/Pydantic/Depends/OpenAPI, pero el alumno puede completar la evaluación final sin importar FastAPI ni ejecutar una petición HTTP.
findings.defense: La semántica HTTP puede aislarse con stdlib antes de añadir framework.

findings.title: same-process dict + sequential retry can satisfy readiness
findings.evidence: same-process dict + sequential retry can satisfy readiness
findings.impact: The learner can pass idempotency with a sequential in-memory dict despite explicit theory warning that this is insufficient.
findings.fix: SQLite/atomic unique claim + scoped fingerprint/response + concurrent requests + reopen/replay test.
findings.attack: La propia teoría declara que ese patrón no demuestra idempotencia bajo concurrencia ni reinicio y que hace falta claim atómico/durable. Sin embargo, exactamente esa evidencia insuficiente puede cerrar el proyecto.
findings.defense: El lab está acotado y puede enseñar primero la semántica de replay/conflict.

findings.title: missing `version` -> REPLAY_STORED_RESPONSE
findings.evidence: missing `version` -> REPLAY_STORED_RESPONSE
findings.impact: Missing version metadata is routed to replay rather than inspection, teaching an unsafe fail-closed rule.
findings.fix: Cambiar missing a INSPECT_IDEMPOTENCY_RECORD; replay solo con record durable completo.
findings.attack: El curso enseña fail-closed, pero convierte metadata incompleta en una acción que presupone que existe una respuesta almacenada y que es compatible con el contrato esperado.
findings.defense: El feedback dice 'reutiliza la respuesta almacenada o escala' para evitar inventar v1.

findings.title: created label but no POST HTTP 201/Location
findings.evidence: created label but no POST HTTP 201/Location
findings.impact: Final readiness never checks the core 201 create contract.
findings.fix: Test POST /v1/jobs=201 + public body + Location when URI exists; 404/405+Allow too.
findings.attack: LO1 y T1-A enseñan que el status forma parte del contrato, pero el proyecto final puede READY con un create que, trasladado a HTTP, devolvería cualquier status.
findings.defense: El label created modela la semántica antes de montar el endpoint.

findings.title: least privilege/lineage/trace/rollback scored though unscaffolded; wording blurs CP-N4-A
findings.evidence: least privilege/lineage/trace/rollback scored though unscaffolded; wording blurs CP-N4-A
findings.impact: The visible rubric scores future/unimplemented controls and blurs local S41 evidence with CP-N4-A.
findings.fix: Label local S41 rubric; tie every criterion to observable test/artifact; CP-N4-A gate remains S43.
findings.attack: Casi la mitad del puntaje visible se apoya en criterios no operativizados en el proyecto; 'least privilege' pertenece principalmente al security/authz que S42 añade.
findings.defense: Una rúbrica puede valorar README, límites y reflexión además del código.

findings.title: S41 starts Phase 3 while S39/CF-3 and S40 remain REPAIR_REQUIRED.
findings.evidence: Authoritative continuation explicitly keeps S39/CF-3 and S40 debt active.
findings.fix: Make upstream artifact/version/hash and gate status explicit preconditions of every S41 service example.
findings.attack: A clean HTTP facade can launder stale ER/graph/model/policy evidence into an apparently governed service.
findings.defense: Building an API after architecture is the correct curricular order.

findings.title: S41 repeatedly calls its local gate CP-N4-A even though the authoritative roadmap places CP-N4-A at S43.
findings.evidence: Roadmap capstone table: CP-N4-A gate S43; S41 callout says 'CP-N4-A se demuestra con evidencia local'.
findings.fix: Call S41 an increment/pre-gate toward CP-N4-A and reserve PASS/promotion language for S43.
findings.attack: Learner can believe the capstone is promoted two sections early, before S42 security/privacy and S43 deployment/contract work.
findings.defense: S41 legitimately contributes an increment toward CP-N4-A.

findings.title: A section titled FastAPI never constructs a FastAPI app, Pydantic model, Depends dependency, TestClient or generated OpenAPI contract in Theory.
findings.evidence: All nine theory executables are stdlib functions/dicts/lists.
findings.fix: Keep pure models as pre-step, then add a minimal real FastAPI/Pydantic/TestClient artifact for each boundary contract.
findings.attack: Learner can finish Theory without encountering the actual framework semantics named in title and outcomes.
findings.defense: Stdlib models can isolate concepts before framework syntax.

findings.title: Theory playground for legacy id llm-finetuning still teaches simulated QLoRA/fine-tuning.
findings.evidence: SectionView mapping title is 'Practica QLoRA concepts (simulado)'.
findings.fix: Preserve id; replace only its playground mapping with an on-topic HTTP/idempotency/422/compatibility activity.
findings.attack: The learner leaves HTTP contracts and is dropped into quantization/LoRA mathematics with zero transfer relation.
findings.defense: The stable legacy id itself is valid for progress compatibility.

findings.title: status_for returns 405 for unknown paths and emits no Allow contract for method-not-allowed responses.
findings.evidence: CE01: GET /v1/nope -> 405 while prose itself distinguishes unknown path 404 from known-path 405.
findings.fix: Resolve path existence first, then method; return 404 for unknown resource and 405 plus allowed methods for known resource.
findings.attack: The executable contradicts both HTTP semantics and its own prose.
findings.defense: The toy only enumerates a few known routes.

findings.title: T1-B prose requires durable scoped atomic idempotency, but canonical code is a process-local dict with check-then-set.
findings.evidence: replay_label(store,key,body) performs if key in store then store[key]=body.
findings.fix: Use SQLite/transactional unique claim or equivalent durable store and test two concurrent requests plus process reopen.
findings.attack: Concurrent requests and restarts can duplicate effects; this repeats unresolved S38 failure windows.
findings.defense: The paragraph explicitly warns that the sequential lab does not prove concurrency.

findings.title: The store retains a mutable body object rather than an immutable canonical fingerprint and stored response.
findings.evidence: CE06 mutating the caller's dict changes the stored comparison and turns a changed request into replay.
findings.fix: Canonicalize/fingerprint an immutable request representation and store original response/status with the claim.
findings.attack: The idempotency record does not preserve original intent.
findings.defense: Simple dict equality demonstrates the conceptual same/different branch.

findings.title: Prose says identity is tenant/client + operation + key, but code indexes only key and stores no side-effect/result identity.
findings.evidence: store[key] = body.
findings.fix: Represent scope explicitly and regression-test cross-tenant/cross-operation key reuse.
findings.attack: Same key across tenants/endpoints can collide or replay another operation.
findings.defense: Single synthetic client/end-point keeps nominal example small.

findings.title: page_keyset accepts invalid sizes and silently treats unknown cursors as end-of-data.
findings.evidence: CE02-CE04: size 0 crashes, negative size produces a page, unknown cursor yields empty terminal page.
findings.fix: Validate positive bounded page size; make cursor parse/lookup failure explicit 400/422 with stable error type.
findings.attack: Malformed/stale cursor can hide data instead of returning a typed client error.
findings.defense: Nominal fixture uses valid size and known cursor.

findings.title: Keyset cursor uses a raw ID without asserting uniqueness, immutable ordering, tie-break, filter/as-of snapshot or opaque integrity.
findings.evidence: CE05 duplicate IDs make continuation ambiguous; code relies on list.index(first occurrence).
findings.fix: Declare ordered unique cursor tuple, immutable sort semantics and filter/as-of binding; encode/sign opaque cursor in the production bridge.
findings.attack: Concurrent inserts/duplicates/filter changes can skip or repeat rows.
findings.defense: The fixture job IDs happen to be unique and sorted.

findings.title: '/v1 congela campos públicos' reduces compatibility to preserving field names and has no explicit evolution policy.
findings.evidence: T1-B and T4-B focus on job_id/status rename/removal.
findings.fix: Define compatibility matrix for additions, requiredness, types, enum evolution, errors, ordering/pagination and behavioral limits; run old-consumer tests.
findings.attack: Consumers can break through type/requiredness/enum/error/ordering/pagination/semantic/rate-limit changes without any field rename.
findings.defense: Stable fields are a useful beginner anchor.

findings.title: domain_imports_http=False is printed as a mental flag rather than proven by dependency direction/contract tests.
findings.evidence: routing_deps_models.py prints the literal False after two list-backed calls.
findings.fix: Separate modules/interfaces and enforce import/port rules plus fake/adapter contract tests.
findings.attack: A real domain module could import FastAPI and the gate would still print False.
findings.defense: Injecting get_store does demonstrate substitutability at a toy scale.

findings.title: create_job derives job identity from len(store)+1.
findings.evidence: job id is f'job-{len(store)+1}'.
findings.fix: Use a supplied stable synthetic ID/UUID-like generator and test uniqueness independently of collection length.
findings.attack: Deletion, concurrent writers or multiple stores can generate duplicate IDs; the API identity contract is not stable.
findings.defense: It is a tiny deterministic fixture.

findings.title: T2-B promises field types and ranges but executable validates only key presence.
findings.evidence: CE07 wrong types return 200.
findings.fix: Use a real Pydantic model with types/ranges/extra policy and assert 422 through TestClient.
findings.attack: A core FastAPI/Pydantic learning outcome false-greens malformed data.
findings.defense: Required-field presence is one legitimate validation layer.

findings.title: OpenAPI alignment is narrated but no OpenAPI schema is generated or compared to runtime responses.
findings.evidence: public_view/reject_if_invalid are hand-written dict functions only.
findings.fix: Use response_model/status declarations and assert paths/status/schema in app.openapi() plus TestClient responses.
findings.attack: Code and docs can drift while all S41 Theory examples stay green.
findings.defense: Allow-list serialization communicates the public/private distinction.

findings.title: Prose requires invalid input not call create_job, but the validator executable is not wired to the domain and cannot demonstrate zero side effects.
findings.evidence: reject_if_invalid returns tuples and never invokes create_job on either path.
findings.fix: Integrate validator + domain fake and assert store unchanged on 422.
findings.attack: A real handler could validate after mutating and still satisfy this disconnected demo.
findings.defense: Separation keeps validation concept simple.

findings.title: Canonical work_boundary('durable') returns sync although the paragraph says durable work must leave request and be durably queued.
findings.evidence: CE08.
findings.fix: Represent CPU isolation and durability as independent dimensions; durable always requires durable enqueue before response.
findings.attack: The code teaches the opposite routing for the explicit durable case.
findings.defense: Demo later has a slightly different mapping, showing author intent.

findings.title: The only queue is a process-local Python list.
findings.evidence: q=[]; queue.append({'id':..., 'status':'queued'}).
findings.fix: Use local SQLite/outbox/queue fixture that survives reopen; keep list only as explicitly non-durable counterexample.
findings.attack: Restart loses work, directly violating the paragraph's durability requirement and inherited S38 recovery contract.
findings.defense: List makes the state transition visible without infrastructure.

findings.title: trace_id is presented inside the RFC 9457 standard member list rather than as an extension.
findings.evidence: Paragraph says 'RFC 9457 Problem Details: type, title, status, trace_id'.
findings.fix: Teach standard members type/title/status/detail/instance and label trace_id as a service extension.
findings.attack: Learner mislearns the standardized Problem Details schema.
findings.defense: RFC 9457 permits extension members such as trace identifiers.

findings.title: within_budget compares two numbers; it does not enforce a timeout or cancel work.
findings.evidence: No async wait, socket/future, deadline or cancellation appears in Theory.
findings.fix: Use a local async slow coroutine/TestClient upstream fake and assert elapsed timeout/cancellation.
findings.attack: 'timeout' can be printed without any operation having waited or been interrupted.
findings.defense: Numeric policy helper is useful for teaching budget order.

findings.title: Resource lifecycle is represented by printing ['startup','shutdown']; no pool/resource is opened or closed.
findings.evidence: errors_timeouts_lifecycle.py contains no resource object/lifespan context.
findings.fix: Use FastAPI lifespan or a closable fake and assert exactly-once open/close around TestClient lifecycle.
findings.attack: The outcome can green without proving cleanup on normal or timeout paths.
findings.defense: The paragraph explains intended lifecycle correctly.

findings.title: Timeout/cascade helpers accept impossible negative/non-finite budgets as valid evidence.
findings.evidence: CE09-CE10.
findings.fix: Require finite positive durations and explicit headroom/deadline semantics before evaluating order.
findings.attack: Corrupt monitoring/configuration can produce 'ok' or cascade=True.
findings.defense: Nominal examples use positive values.

findings.title: level_detects is a hard-coded mapping of bug names to test layers, not a seeded bug caught by tests.
findings.evidence: Function returns booleans from two string comparisons.
findings.fix: Seed actual domain/status/adapter faults and run unit/TestClient/integration tests that fail for the expected reason.
findings.attack: No code defect is ever introduced or detected.
findings.defense: The mapping communicates conceptual ownership of test layers.

findings.title: T4-A promises unit/contract/integration but canonical detector only handles domain->unit and http->contract.
findings.evidence: level_detects has no adapter/integration branch in Theory code.
findings.fix: Add a controlled adapter/SQLite integration fault and an actual integration assertion.
findings.attack: The third layer exists only in a count set, not in executable behavior.
findings.defense: The paragraph names a temp/in-memory adapter conceptually.

findings.title: S41 still has no collected pytest/FastAPI TestClient gate despite systematic pytest being mandatory since S27.
findings.evidence: Theory snippets print values; no tests collect endpoint behavior/OpenAPI/idempotency/restart/privacy regressions.
findings.fix: Promote nominal/edge/error cases into pytest + TestClient contract tests and preserve pure unit tests underneath.
findings.attack: Critical API-contract regressions cannot block CI.
findings.defense: Print-based examples can remain useful for first exposure.

findings.title: Compatibility evidence is only a printed X-API-Version string and prose; no old consumer is run against a candidate response.
findings.evidence: T4-B prints compat_header only.
findings.fix: Freeze a v1 consumer/schema fixture and run it against candidate API responses/OpenAPI.
findings.attack: A breaking v1 response can still print the header and pass.
findings.defense: Stable job_id/status names are a reasonable anchor.

findings.title: Read compatibility is framed mainly as preserving job_id/status fields.
findings.evidence: T4-B wording focuses on rename/remove.
findings.fix: Teach additive-change rules and explicit compatibility policy across schema, semantics and operational contracts.
findings.attack: Required fields, types, enum values, errors, semantics, ordering/pagination and rate-limit behavior can all break consumers.
findings.defense: Field preservation is the simplest visible example.

findings.title: rate_decision compares supplied used/limit values but has no clock/window, client scope, mutable claim, refill or concurrency safety.
findings.evidence: Function is a pure if used>limit.
findings.fix: Use a deterministic fake clock/window and client key, atomic counter/token bucket, and test rollover/concurrency.
findings.attack: It cannot prove requests per time window or protect a service under concurrent clients, repeating S38's static-quota defect.
findings.defense: It illustrates allow vs 429 decision shape.

findings.title: Negative/NaN usage and invalid limits can allow traffic or manufacture impossible remaining quota.
findings.evidence: CE12-CE13.
findings.fix: Validate finite nonnegative integer counts and positive policy limits before decision.
findings.attack: Corrupt quota telemetry fails open.
findings.defense: Nominal fixture uses integers 73/100 and 110/100.

findings.title: trace_safe checks only exact top-level field names against a small ban list.
findings.evidence: CE14-CE15 pass PII embedded in values or differently cased keys.
findings.fix: Use an allowlisted structured telemetry schema with nested validation/redaction and tests containing adversarial PII values/aliases.
findings.attack: Logs/traces can leak email/DNI/secret while trace_ok=True.
findings.defense: Allow/deny field-name examples can introduce minimization.

findings.title: The lesson treats a trace_id string as observability evidence without spans/span_id/propagation across request->job->result.
findings.evidence: T4-B only passes {'trace_id','job_id'} to trace_safe.
findings.fix: Model at least trace_id + span_id + propagation into durable job context and one child span/result.
findings.attack: A random identifier cannot show parent/child timing or cross-boundary trace continuity.
findings.defense: Correlation identifiers are useful first observability primitives.

findings.title: Tagline/gate promise no PII or internal keys across API evidence, but only one hand-picked response allow-list and top-level trace ban list are checked.
findings.evidence: Errors, OpenAPI examples, headers, nested payloads and trace attributes are not machine-validated.
findings.fix: Define shared public/error/log/trace schemas and run leakage regression tests over all response and telemetry surfaces.
findings.attack: The service can leak secrets outside the single public_view example while still passing all printed flags.
findings.defense: The section consistently advocates minimization in prose.

findings.title: imprime PASS y luego `meets_contract=False` por usar key nueva k1 esperando replay
findings.evidence: imprime PASS y luego `meets_contract=False` por usar key nueva k1 esperando replay
findings.impact: La referencia se contradice internamente.
findings.fix: Eliminar esa línea o reutilizar `idem-are-1` para el replay.
findings.attack: `k1` es nueva; la propia función correcta devuelve `created`. La referencia finaliza con una variable de contrato falsa inmediatamente después de anunciar PASS.
