findings.defense: `meets_contract` parece metadata auxiliar y no forma parte de los asserts anteriores.

findings.title: key presence + `openapi_matches` boolean
findings.evidence: key presence + `openapi_matches` boolean
findings.impact: La práctica no ejecuta tipos/rangos Pydantic ni OpenAPI que la teoría promete.
findings.fix: Requests reales con Pydantic/TestClient y `app.openapi()`.
findings.attack: La práctica contradice la teoría que promete tipos, rangos, Pydantic y OpenAPI. Un entero como name y un dict como priority obtienen 200.
findings.defense: Presence-first puede ser una primera etapa didáctica.

findings.title: cpu_heavy y durable -> `background`; lista RAM/flags
findings.evidence: cpu_heavy y durable -> `background`; lista RAM/flags
findings.impact: Colapsa aislamiento CPU y durabilidad después de que la teoría los separa correctamente.
findings.fix: Dos ejes: execution_boundary y durability; proceso/worker para CPU, store durable + reopen para durabilidad.
findings.attack: El párrafo teórico más fuerte de T3-A dice que aislamiento CPU y durabilidad son garantías distintas, pero la práctica vuelve a colapsarlas.
findings.defense: Una sola etiqueta reduce complejidad del laboratorio.

findings.title: números + `resource_closed`/clear()
findings.evidence: números + `resource_closed`/clear()
findings.impact: No ejecuta timeout/cancel/lifecycle; budgets negativos pueden pasar.
findings.fix: Timeout local real, budgets positivos, observar cancelación y cierre.
findings.attack: No existe espera cancelable, tarea cancelada ni recurso con estado lifecycle real; además valores negativos satisfacen la desigualdad.
findings.defense: Los fixtures permiten razonar primero sobre el presupuesto.

findings.title: conteos + `seeded_failure_detected=True`
findings.evidence: conteos + `seeded_failure_detected=True`
findings.impact: No se ejecuta el seed; conteos negativos pueden cumplir la pirámide.
findings.fix: pytest real con seeds domain/http/adapter y test que falle en el nivel esperado.
findings.attack: No se siembra ni ejecuta el bug que supuestamente demuestra la red de seguridad. Incluso conteos negativos cumplen la forma.
findings.defense: El objetivo puede ser aprender qué nivel debería detectar qué bug.

findings.title: used>limit + exact-key redaction + booleans compat/privacy
findings.evidence: used>limit + exact-key redaction + booleans compat/privacy
findings.impact: No hay ventana temporal, old consumer ejecutado ni inspección robusta de telemetría.
findings.fix: Reloj/window fake, consumer v1 real, Retry-After y schema allow-list adversarial.
findings.attack: No hay ventana temporal del rate limit, consumidor congelado ejecutado ni inspección robusta de logs/traces. Un mensaje que contiene email pasa el filtro.
findings.defense: Los valores 73/100 y 110/100 son una tabla de decisión fácil de inspeccionar.

findings.title: required-key presence only
findings.evidence: required-key presence only
findings.impact: Wrong types/ranges can pass final project.
findings.fix: Pydantic types/ranges/extra policy; 422 before domain/store for multiple invalid classes.
findings.attack: No se prueban tipos, rangos, campos extra ni side-effect cero ante request inválida.
findings.defense: Missing required field es un caso mínimo visible.

findings.title: GET 200 + job_id treated as stable v1 reading
findings.evidence: GET 200 + job_id treated as stable v1 reading
findings.impact: No frozen consumer/schema/error/pagination compatibility is executed.
findings.fix: Run old v1 consumer/fixture against candidate.
findings.attack: No existe consumidor v1 congelado, snapshot/schema anterior ni matriz de compatibilidad; tipos, requiredness, errores, pagination y semántica pueden romperse y READY seguir verde.
findings.defense: job_id/status son los campos estables más importantes del ejemplo.

findings.title: claims timeout/rate/trace/rollback, readiness tests none
findings.evidence: claims timeout/rate/trace/rollback, readiness tests none
findings.impact: READY overclaims operational evidence.
findings.fix: Either add those tests or narrow project/rubric scope.
findings.attack: El proyecto anuncia un gate más amplio que su función de aceptación.
findings.defense: T3/T4 ya practicaron esos temas y el You Do puede concentrarse en create/get.

findings.title: requires uncertain RETRY_OR_ESCALATE/MISSING; starter has no uncertain route
findings.evidence: requires uncertain RETRY_OR_ESCALATE/MISSING; starter has no uncertain route
findings.impact: Fail-closed uncertainty is not transferred independently.
findings.fix: Add explicit incomplete record/cursor/upstream fixture and separate INSPECT/RETRY_OR_ESCALATE decision.
findings.attack: El gate fail-closed que la sección repite no tiene una ruta de incertidumbre en el proyecto independiente.
findings.defense: El rechazo de body inválido y conflicto cubren error/breach.

findings.title: CPU-bound OR durable collapsed into one background/worker answer
findings.evidence: CPU-bound OR durable collapsed into one background/worker answer
findings.impact: Undoes T3-A's correct distinction.
findings.fix: Separate CPU isolation and durability into different questions/guarantees.
findings.attack: El propio T3-A correcto dice que aislamiento CPU y durabilidad son garantías distintas y un trabajo puede necesitar una, la otra o ambas.
findings.defense: La opción ganadora menciona worker y persistencia y busca alejar ambos del request.

findings.title: 201 creation is taught while Location is treated as merely optional rather than teaching the standard recommendation/representation relationship.
findings.evidence: T1-A says 'opcionalmente header Location'.
findings.fix: State that 201 is the create status and Location is recommended when the new resource has a URI; test it in the real FastAPI response.
findings.attack: Learner misses an important part of discoverable create semantics.
findings.defense: A 201 response body can identify the created resource and Location is not universally mandatory.

findings.title: Idempotency-Key is presented as an industry header without clarifying that the IETF specification is still a draft rather than a finalized RFC.
findings.evidence: T1-B references Stripe/industry practice.
findings.fix: Label it an industry convention with an IETF draft and document the service-specific scope/fingerprint/retention policy.
findings.attack: Learner may mistake widespread vendor convention for finalized core HTTP semantics.
findings.defense: Calling it an industry header is broadly fair and the behavior taught is common.

findings.title: One string 'background' stands for both CPU isolation and durable job execution even though the prose correctly distinguishes the guarantees.
findings.evidence: work_boundary returns background for cpu_heavy and demo maps durable/background together.
findings.fix: Return separate fields such as execution={inline_async, process_pool} and durability={request_scoped,durable_queue}.
findings.attack: Learner can conflate FastAPI BackgroundTasks, process pools and external durable workers.
findings.defense: The paragraph explicitly distinguishes them.

findings.title: The lesson never teaches/asserts application/problem+json and omits detail/instance from the practical contract.
findings.evidence: problem_details returns only type/title/status/trace_id.
findings.fix: Declare media type and distinguish optional standard members from extensions; add one real FastAPI exception response.
findings.attack: Learner may think any JSON dict with those fields is the wire-level RFC contract.
findings.defense: detail and instance are optional; minimal examples need not include every member.

findings.title: unit>=contract>=integration is taught as shape_ok, turning a heuristic into a numeric quality gate.
findings.evidence: pyramid_counts and callout explicitly use the inequality; CE11 negative counts still pass.
findings.fix: Present pyramid as cost/feedback heuristic, validate nonnegative counts, and gate on required behaviors rather than count inequality.
findings.attack: Teams can game counts while missing critical contracts; architecture/risk should drive test mix.
findings.defense: A broad base of cheaper tests is a useful heuristic.

findings.title: 429 returns a JSON retry_after_s member but no Retry-After response header or explicit time-window semantics.
findings.evidence: rate_decision output contains retry_after_s:1 only.
findings.fix: Teach/use Retry-After when the service knows the retry time and bind it to the limiter window.
findings.attack: Client interoperability is taught as body convention rather than HTTP response contract.
findings.defense: RFC 6585 makes Retry-After optional, not mandatory.

findings.title: Dense English/API jargon appears faster than self-contained Spanish explanations in an already advanced transition section.
findings.evidence: path operation, body, keyset, boundary, background, shape, allow-list, rate limit, trace, lifecycle, replay, handler appear densely.
findings.fix: Define each once Spanish-first, retain the API term in parentheses/code, then reuse consistently.
findings.attack: Learners can memorize tokens without a causal model of trigger/input/action/result.
findings.defense: Many are actual framework/industry terms and should remain recognizable.

findings.title: T1-A states resources should use nouns and not verbs with protocol-like certainty.
findings.evidence: 'Modela recursos con sustantivos versionados ... no verbos en la URL.'
findings.fix: Label noun-oriented paths as this service's resource-style convention and distinguish protocol semantics from house style.
findings.attack: This is a useful REST-style design convention, not an HTTP correctness requirement; RPC/action endpoints can be legitimate.
findings.defense: Resource-oriented noun paths are a strong default for the course's API design.

findings.title: E1 repair/E2 valid-invalid-missing/E3 continue-breach-review casi uniforme
findings.evidence: E1 repair/E2 valid-invalid-missing/E3 continue-breach-review casi uniforme
findings.impact: Pattern matching puede sustituir transferencia a FastAPI.
findings.fix: Intercalar construcción de endpoint, dependency override, OpenAPI, restart/concurrency y seeds.
findings.attack: La repetición favorece reconocimiento del molde y tokens `RETURN_*` más que transferencia a requests, routers, dependencies, stores y tests reales.
findings.defense: Una interfaz estable reduce carga extrínseca y hace visible el patrón fail-closed.

findings.title: `retry_after_s` presented as retry signal
findings.evidence: `retry_after_s` presented as retry signal
findings.impact: Local body field can be mistaken for interoperable HTTP mechanism.
findings.fix: Teach 429 and Retry-After header when known; body field is local convention.
findings.attack: `retry_after_s` es un campo de body inventado por el lab; HTTP define `Retry-After` como header utilizable cuando el servidor conoce cuándo reintentar.
findings.defense: RFC 6585 no obliga a emitir Retry-After y un body estructurado adicional es válido.

findings.title: FastAPI remains a named concept/resource link, not a mandatory executable skill.
The lesson correctly says sequential dict is insufficient, then uses it as final acceptance evidence.
Pydantic types/ranges are promised; presence-only validation is taught and graded.
The correct distinction CPU isolation vs durability is lost in both practice and retrieval assessment.
Incremental API evidence is repeatedly described as the capstone gate even though the canonical gate is S43.
Old-consumer compatibility is never executed in You Do.
Privacy/trace claims are checked by one key or boolean rather than across response/error/log/trace surfaces.
201 is central in theory/self-check but absent from final acceptance.
Types/ranges/Pydantic promised; key-presence validator graded.
read compatibility promised; no old consumer executes.
timeout/rate/trace/rollback/least privilege are named/scored but not accepted by tests.
recovery assessment collapses CPU isolation and durability again.
El proyecto final puede quedar READY sin Pydantic, tipos ni JSON Schema reales; además acepta valores mal tipados.
findings.evidence: You Do `policy_engine` solo comprueba presencia/extras; contraejemplo: `{case_id:123,status:{bad:1}}` puede llegar a CONTINUE.
findings.impact: El outcome principal “schema estricto (tipos + rechazo de campos extra)” queda sin evaluar; una API insegura puede aprobar.
findings.fix: Hacer obligatorio un modelo Pydantic `extra="forbid"`, restricciones de tipo/enum y `model_json_schema()`, con tests válidos/inválidos.
findings.attack: The executable contradicts the outcome 'schema ... estricto (tipos + rechazo de campos extra)' and can certify a payload that violates its own exported schema.
findings.defense: The helper intentionally isolates extra-field and business-status concepts.

findings.title: La teoría explica correctamente que hostname allowlist sola no basta, pero We Do, You Do y self-check vuelven a host-only y pueden aprobar SSRF por DNS rebinding/resolución interna.
findings.evidence: T3-A p1 exige IP resuelta y revalidación de redirects; You Do solo `if host not in allow_hosts`; Q5 dice host allowlist como control suficiente.
findings.impact: El assessment enseña exactamente el bypass que la teoría advierte no usar; el gate de seguridad puede quedar READY con una defensa insuficiente.
findings.fix: Unificar toda práctica con parser URL seguro, resolución A/AAAA, política de IP, redirect disabled/revalidated y tests de hostname permitido→IP privada.
findings.attack: The code claims to reject private/loopback/link-local addresses while demonstrably allowing several of them.
findings.defense: The synthetic fixture covers the classic metadata IP and one DNS rebind example.

findings.title: `url_allowed` parsea URLs con split, resuelve una sola vez y no ejecuta redirects ni múltiples A/AAAA.
findings.evidence: T3-A code: `url.split("://",1)...`; `resolve(host)` una vez.
findings.impact: Contradice la propia explicación de redirects/DNS y no modela el punto de conexión real.
findings.fix: Usar `urllib.parse`, validar scheme/host/port, todas las IP resueltas, desactivar redirects o revalidar cada salto y fijar el destino verificado.
findings.attack: The learner is explicitly warned that host allowlisting alone is insufficient, then rewarded for implementing exactly that insufficient defense. This is a security assessment false-green.
findings.defense: The literal 169.254.169.254 adversarial fixture is still blocked because that host is not allowlisted.

findings.title: Teoría/We Do representan borrado y separación de key como booleans, sin stores ni prueba de no-reaparición.
findings.evidence: `purge_ok(... deleted, derived_deleted, key_separate)` acepta flags.
findings.impact: No demuestra borrado primario/derivado, backups o reapertura; la propiedad crítica se autoatestigua.
findings.fix: Usar stores locales reales/fixtures de primary+derived+index, ejecutar delete, reopen y búsqueda de no-reaparición.
findings.attack: The final project can claim purga limpia without proving that data ever existed or that primary/derived copies were removed; it is a vacuous test of deletion.
findings.defense: I Do T4-B separately demonstrates a primary deletion while a derived copy survives.

findings.title: El You Do declara privacy_ok usando stores vacíos y un case_id que nunca existió.
findings.evidence: `purge_ok({}, {}, "C1", ...)` devuelve True por vacuidad; no borra nada y ni siquiera usa CASE_ID.
findings.impact: El gate final de privacidad puede READY sin ejecutar una purga; “no reaparece” se prueba sobre un dato que jamás estuvo.
findings.fix: Insertar CASE_ID + dato sensible en primary/derived, ejecutar purga, reabrir/leer y demostrar ausencia en todas las superficies declaradas.
findings.attack: The central privacy promise can pass while a log or restored snapshot reintroduces the data.
findings.defense: Theory/We Do discuss audit and derivatives conceptually.

findings.title: `readiness` solo exige cuatro booleans y no valida el threat model ni varios requisitos críticos.
findings.evidence: `readiness(bundle: dict[str,bool])`; rubric/requirements incluyen deps, threat model, rollback, riesgo residual, pero no afectan READY.
findings.impact: Un checklist manual o evidencia incompleta puede producir READY; la propia retrospectiva admite que READY no basta.
findings.fix: Calcular readiness desde resultados/artifacts tipados y hacer hard gates de threat model, SSRF robusto, authz, deletion y critical security tests.
findings.attack: This violates the course's own Gradual Release promise: 'You Do' is supposed to transfer responsibility, but the final project contains the solution and success state.
findings.defense: A complete runnable scaffold can reduce setup friction and let the learner extend it.

findings.title: S42 depende de S41, pero S41 permanece REPAIR_REQUIRED en la auditoría vigente.
findings.evidence: El opening dice “La sección anterior te enseñó a versionar y responder” y el roadmap exige no iniciar S(n+1) hasta cerrar la retrospectiva de S(n).
findings.impact: Una capa de seguridad puede legitimar una API S41 que todavía false-greenea FastAPI/idempotencia.
findings.fix: Mantener la secuencia, pero hacer explícito que S42 parte del artefacto S41 solo después de pasar sus gates locales.
findings.attack: A security/privacy layer can appear green while wrapping an API contract whose implementation/evidence is still false-green; that launders upstream uncertainty into a stronger downstream claim.
findings.defense: The S42 concepts can legitimately be taught on a synthetic request even if S41 is not production-ready.

findings.title: S42 llama “Gate de promoción CP-N4-A” a un incremento cuyo gate autoritativo está en S43.
findings.evidence: Callout: “Gate de promoción CP-N4-A”; referencia: “Gate global. CP-N4-A solo se aprueba…”; roadmap: CP-N4-A | S43 y S43 “cierre CP-N4-A”.
findings.impact: El alumno puede creer que el capstone se promociona antes de contenedores/reproducibilidad operativa de S43.
findings.fix: Renombrar a gate local/incremento S42 hacia CP-N4-A; reservar promoción CP-N4-A para S43.
findings.attack: Learners can believe security/privacy checks at S42 complete the capstone before S43 container/health/migration/recovery evidence exists.
findings.defense: S42 is legitimately a contributing section and its controls are prerequisites for CP-N4-A.

findings.title: El “schema exportado” stdlib no representa fielmente el contrato que afirma enseñar.
findings.evidence: `export_schema` declara todas las propiedades como string y deja `status ∈ {open,closed}` fuera del JSON Schema.
findings.impact: El alumno puede confundir un dict que “se parece” a JSON Schema con un schema que realmente expresa restricciones.
findings.fix: Usar Pydantic/JSON Schema real o etiquetar el dict como mapa conceptual no interoperable; incluir enum/tipos/restricciones en el schema generado.
findings.attack: Learners can finish the schema/evolution sequence without learning the framework behavior explicitly named in headings/outcomes.
findings.defense: Stdlib-first modeling reduces incidental framework syntax and can be good progressive disclosure.

findings.title: La lección presenta todo campo extra silencioso como una grieta de seguridad universal.
findings.evidence: Opening: “Un campo extra aceptado en silencio es la grieta por donde entra un valor que nadie validó.”
findings.impact: Mezcla una política defensiva válida con una afirmación absoluta; la amenaza real depende de binding, uso y mass assignment.
findings.fix: Explicar que `extra=forbid` es la política elegida en el borde no confiable y que extras son especialmente peligrosos si se enlazan/usan sin autorización.
findings.attack: A breaking reader can be labeled compatible by setting a field True; the lesson teaches the name of consumer compatibility rather than producing its evidence.
findings.defense: The I Do business_amount example does execute one tiny v1 reader on an additive currency field.

findings.title: El outcome de discriminated unions se reduce a `if type == ...` y sets de tags.
findings.evidence: T1-B `event_kind` es un if/raise; We Do usa `union_tags == handled_tags`.
findings.impact: El alumno nunca construye ni valida la unión discriminada prometida, ni observa errores reales del modelo.
findings.fix: Añadir unión Pydantic discriminada con variantes y tests de tag desconocido, evolución y lector v1.
findings.attack: The model creates a false breaking change when handlers are a safe superset, conflating exhaustiveness with set identity.
findings.defense: Exact equality is a simple classroom invariant and may intentionally reject stale/unreachable handlers.

findings.title: T2-A afirma authn≠authz, pero el ejecutable confía en strings de actor/role sin prueba de autenticación.
findings.evidence: `can_read(actor, owner, role, scopes)` carece de un principal autenticado/verified claim; We Do introduce un booleano `authenticated`.
findings.impact: Se sustituye autenticación por autoatestación de identidad y se desdibuja la frontera entre claims verificados y datos del request.
findings.fix: Representar un `Principal` producido por authn y separar claims confiables de `owner/resource_id` controlados por el cliente.
findings.attack: The same lesson simultaneously defines cross-tenant access as a promotion failure and as an allowed privileged path; the learner cannot know which invariant the gate actually means.
findings.defense: An explicit administrator capability can be valid if privileged access is part of the threat model and separately audited.

findings.title: `actor == owner` se presenta como resource binding suficiente para autorización de objeto.
findings.evidence: T2-A: allow analista si actor==owner + case:read. OWASP BOLA exige comprobar política/jerarquía sobre cada objeto y advierte que comparar user ID con object ID no es una solución general.
findings.impact: El modelo mental no escala a casos asignados, equipos, delegación, tenancy o acciones distintas.
findings.fix: Etiquetar owner-equality como política mínima del caso sintético y añadir policy function `(principal, action, resource)` con matriz de relaciones/permisos.
findings.attack: A learner can pass the authn/authz outcome while never seeing where trustworthy identity comes from or why actor/tenant/role claims cannot be accepted from the request body.
findings.defense: S42 can focus on authorization policy and assume upstream authentication for a bounded lab.

findings.title: El prefijo `svc-` se usa como evidencia de identidad de servicio.
findings.evidence: T2-B `allow(... service_id.startswith("svc-") ...)`.
findings.impact: Cualquier string inventado `svc-attacker` satisface la puerta; nombre convencional ≠ autenticación M2M.
findings.fix: Usar un principal autenticado de servicio con issuer/subject/audience o fixture equivalente; el nombre puede ser metadata, no prueba.
findings.attack: A naming convention is not authentication or registration; arbitrary attacker-controlled text can satisfy the predicate.
findings.defense: The prefix is an intentionally lightweight namespace convention in a synthetic lab.

findings.title: Incluso el mejor código teórico usa una denylist de prefijos IP incompleta y textual.
findings.evidence: `BLOCKED_PREFIXES=(127.,10.,192.168.,169.254.,::1)` acepta 172.16/12, 100.64/10, ULA IPv6 y link-local IPv6.
findings.impact: Un alumno que copie el patrón puede permitir destinos no públicos.
findings.fix: Usar `ipaddress.ip_address()` y una política explícita de destinos globales/permitidos, con IPv4/IPv6 y casos especiales.
findings.attack: The helper is neither a robust URL parser nor fail-closed under DNS failure and teaches protocol handling that OWASP explicitly warns against.
findings.defense: The example is deliberately small and not a production URL client.

findings.title: El confinamiento de path es comparación de strings/literal `..`, no canonicalización del filesystem.
findings.evidence: `safe_path` concatena y `startswith(root + "/")`; You Do repite el patrón.
findings.impact: Symlinks, normalizaciones y rutas equivalentes pueden escapar aunque el string parezca estar bajo root.
findings.fix: Resolver/canonicalizar con `pathlib.Path.resolve()` y comprobar relación con root resuelto; incluir symlink fixture donde el entorno lo permita.
findings.attack: The code claims filesystem confinement while operating only lexically; Python's own pathlib docs warn to resolve symlinks/.. when filesystem containment matters.
findings.defense: The Linux-style '../etc/passwd' fixture is correctly rejected in the nominal lab.

findings.title: El outcome y T3-A incluyen límite de bytes, pero You Do no recibe ni valida tamaño.
findings.evidence: `policy_engine` no tiene `size/max_bytes`.
findings.impact: El proyecto final puede READY sin demostrar uno de los controles explícitos del outcome 5.
findings.fix: Añadir tamaño al boundary y pruebas below/at/above limit antes de parse/fetch.
findings.attack: The final project can READY while omitting one of the three anti-abuse gates taught as conjunctive.
findings.defense: We Do T3-A does include bytes <= max_bytes.

findings.title: La sección nombra “injection” en roadmap/heading, pero no enseña una familia de injection ni su control específico.
findings.evidence: T3-A cubre tamaño, SSRF y path traversal; no hay query parameterization, command/template injection ni fixture de injection.
findings.impact: El alumno cree haber cubierto “injection” por haber validado URL/path, una generalización incorrecta.
findings.fix: O retirar “injection” del alcance S42 o añadir un caso delimitado (p.ej. command/SQL injection) con API segura y tests.
findings.attack: Learners can complete S42 without demonstrating two thirds of a stated security outcome.
findings.defense: A fully realistic vault/KMS/SCA stack would overload a local course lab.

findings.title: Cifrado en reposo, gestión de claves, provenance y scans reales son outcomes/prosa, pero la evidencia son booleans y un contador CVE.
findings.evidence: T3-B code solo sha256 + `promote_ok(secret_in_repo,pinned,critical_cves)`; You Do no evalúa T3-B.
findings.impact: Se puede aprobar sin implementar la mitad del outcome 6 ni demostrar supply-chain/secret hygiene.
findings.fix: Ejecutar scan local controlado/fixture, lock/hash/provenance, ensayo de rotación y ejemplo de envelope/key management; delimitar cifrado si no se implementa.
findings.attack: Setting rotation_tested=True or critical_cves=0 is not evidence that rotation occurred or a scan ran.
findings.defense: The lesson explicitly distinguishes missing critical_cves from zero and routes missing to ASSESS_DEPENDENCY_RISK.

findings.title: La regla de retención acepta días negativos y techos inválidos.
findings.evidence: `days <= max_days` hace PASS con -365 y 30, e incluso con valores negativos ordenados.
findings.impact: Datos imposibles false-greenean la política y ocultan falta de validación de dominio.
findings.fix: Validar enteros finitos/no negativos y `max_days > 0` antes de comparar.
findings.attack: Impossible retention durations can be certified as privacy-compliant.
findings.defense: Nominal fixtures use 30 and 3650 days, so the bug is outside demonstrated examples.

findings.title: “bloqueo al vencer” se reduce a comparar dos números declarados.
findings.evidence: Outcome 7 promete bloqueo al vencer; T4-A solo `retention_days <= max_retention_days`.
findings.impact: No demuestra enforcement temporal, expiración ni purga después del deadline.
findings.fix: Introducir reloj inyectable `now`, `expires_at` y tests antes/en/después del vencimiento con bloqueo/purga.
findings.attack: A policy value can be compliant while the actual record remains readable forever.
findings.defense: The section may intend to teach policy design before operational expiry.

findings.title: La pseudonimización usa SHA-256 determinista con prefijo fijo y no usa la “llave separada” que la prosa dice necesaria.
findings.evidence: `pseudonym(subject)=sha256("synth:"+subject)[:16]`.
findings.impact: IDs de baja entropía son enumerables/linkables y el código contradice el modelo de reidentificación controlada.
findings.fix: Usar token aleatorio persistido en un mapping protegido o HMAC con clave separada; explicar que pseudonimización no es anonimización.
findings.attack: The executable contradicts the privacy property it describes and teaches that hashing predictable identifiers equals key-separated pseudonymization.
findings.defense: The function is labeled synthetic/didactic and the purge predicate has a separate key_separate flag.

findings.title: `audit.isdisjoint(pii)` inspecciona nombres de campos, no valores, nested payloads ni aliases.
findings.evidence: Un audit `{actor_id,message}` con `message="email=..."` pasa aunque contenga PII.
findings.impact: La promesa “audit sin PII” puede aprobar una fuga real.
findings.fix: Definir schema allowlisted de audit, validar valores/nesting y fixtures adversariales con PII embebida/aliases.
findings.attack: A log can leak PII while the privacy gate returns PASS.
findings.defense: An allowlisted field-name schema is a useful first minimization primitive.

findings.title: La redacción final solo filtra keys top-level y puede conservar PII dentro de valores permitidos.
findings.evidence: `redact_view` allowlista `region`; un `region={note:"email=..."}` sale intacto.
findings.impact: No demuestra “campo redactado no reaparece” de forma transversal.
findings.fix: Usar modelos públicos tipados y leakage tests sobre valores/nesting en response/error/log/audit.
findings.attack: READY functions as a certificate for unexecuted controls.
findings.defense: The portfolio note asks learners to expand the starter and warns against hand-flipped booleans.

findings.title: El proyecto final exige matriz RBAC/scopes/service identities, pero implementa solo actor==owner + `cases:read`; service identity no aparece.
findings.evidence: Requirements vs `policy_engine`.
findings.impact: El alumno puede obtener READY sin demostrar T2-B ni RBAC real.
findings.fix: Añadir principal humano/servicio, roles, scopes y resource policy; tests same/cross tenant, missing grant y service principal no autenticado.
findings.attack: Outcome 2 can be completed without transfer.
findings.defense: T1-B is practiced in I Do/We Do.

findings.title: El threat model es el producto central del roadmap/S42, pero solo aparece como requisito textual del You Do.
findings.evidence: No hay estructura STRIDE/actores-activos-entry points/amenazas-mitigaciones ni criterio ejecutable/documental en readiness.
findings.impact: El artefacto principal puede omitirse y aun así status==READY.
findings.fix: Proveer template mínimo versionado y hard gate que exija actores, activos, trust boundaries, amenazas, mitigaciones, residual risk, owner y revisión.
findings.attack: The artifact name asserts more least-privilege evidence than exists.
findings.defense: Resource binding is the highest-value authorization check in the final path.

findings.title: La rúbrica puntúa SLO, observabilidad, rollback, lineage y evidencia que el starter no produce.
findings.evidence: Rubric 15% “Operación: SLO, observabilidad y rollback”; starter carece de SLO/trace/rollback/lineage.
findings.impact: La evaluación no es transparente: se puntúan capacidades no enseñadas/scaffolded en el entregable.
findings.fix: Alinear rúbrica con observables S42 o añadir explícitamente artefactos/tests para esos criterios; no usar futura S43 como puntos ocultos.
findings.attack: A stated learning outcome becomes optional post-completion work.
findings.defense: Security supply-chain details may continue in S44.

findings.title: El roadmap exige ≥70% y 100% de ítems críticos, pero el scorer global solo aplica score>=70 y QuestionKey no modela `critical`.
findings.evidence: `PASS_THRESHOLD=70`; `passed: clamped >= PASS_THRESHOLD`.
findings.impact: Una respuesta incorrecta de SSRF/authz/privacy puede compensarse con preguntas fáciles y aprobar una sección de seguridad.
findings.fix: Añadir `critical` al banco/grade y exigir todos los críticos correctos además del 70%; marcar los security gates S42 como críticos.
findings.attack: Outcome 7 is absent from independent transfer.
findings.defense: One response allowlist demonstrates minimization at a small scale.

findings.title: Los 24 We Do repiten casi siempre E1 reparar predicado, E2 PASS/breach/MISSING, E3 CONTINUE/breach/review.
findings.evidence: La estructura se repite en los 8 subtemas.
findings.impact: El alumno puede aprender la gramática del ejercicio en vez de transferir a schemas/authz/filesystem/network/security artifacts reales.
findings.fix: Intercalar construcción, debugging, test adversarial, threat modeling, policy review y pruebas integradas; conservar fail-closed sin usar la misma plantilla 24 veces.
findings.attack: A learner can get READY without producing the named primary product 'threat model'.
findings.defense: The requirement text can be evaluated manually outside readiness.

findings.title: Términos avanzados aparecen densamente con explicación desigual: discriminated union, resource binding, provenance, purpose, pseudonymization, key separation, threat model.
findings.evidence: Aunque algunos acrónimos se expanden, varios términos dependen de jerga adyacente.
findings.impact: Carga lingüística extra puede convertirse en memorización de etiquetas, especialmente en transición a seguridad.
findings.fix: Definir una vez en español con actor→input→decisión→resultado y conservar el término inglés entre paréntesis.
findings.attack: Learners cannot infer what evidence earns the points; grading rewards future/unimplemented work.
findings.defense: Rollback/residual operational thinking is relevant to production-governed systems.

findings.title: El recurso enlaza SP 800-63-3, retirado/superseded.
findings.evidence: URL actual en S42: `https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-3/`; NIST indica superseded por SP 800-63-4 desde 2025.
findings.impact: Un curso de producción gobernada manda al alumno a una guía de identidad retirada.
findings.fix: Actualizar a SP 800-63-4 y, si aplica, partes A/B/C-4.
findings.attack: The lesson gives two incompatible definitions of completion in adjacent learner-facing surfaces.
findings.defense: The sentence may intend to distinguish automated checks from manual portfolio quality.

findings.title: El recurso enlaza SP 800-88 Rev.1, superseded por Rev.2 en 2025.
findings.evidence: URL Rev1 en resources.
findings.impact: La referencia de sanitización/borrado está desactualizada justo en el subtema de deletion.
findings.fix: Actualizar a SP 800-88 Rev.2 y contextualizar que media sanitization no equivale por sí sola a deletion lógica de una app.
findings.attack: The quiz's 70% unlock can be earned without recalling several material outcomes.
findings.defense: A self-check need not mirror every outcome one-to-one.

findings.title: Los ejemplos usan `a@example.pe`/`x@example.pe`; `.pe` es un ccTLD real y `example.pe` no es el dominio IANA reservado estándar.
findings.evidence: T1-B code y You Do view.
findings.impact: Aunque sea sintético, enseña un patrón que puede apuntar a dominios reales/registrables.
findings.fix: Usar `example.com`, `example.net` o `example.org` para correos/hosts ficticios cuando no se requiera `.pe`.
findings.attack: Retrieval practice strengthens the weaker misconception precisely after theory corrected it.
findings.defense: For the literal URL http://169.254.169.254/, hostname rejection is indeed one valid blocking layer.

findings.title: The resources link to superseded NIST SP 800-63-3.
findings.evidence: Resource URL is pages.nist.gov/800-63-3/. NIST states SP 800-63-4 final (July/August 2025) supersedes SP 800-63-3.
findings.fix: Replace with NIST SP 800-63-4 and, where relevant, its A/B/C companion volumes.
findings.attack: A security lesson in 2026 points learners at withdrawn identity guidance as its named NIST identity reference.
findings.defense: The old page itself now warns that it is superseded and links forward.

findings.title: The resources link to NIST SP 800-88 Rev.1, withdrawn in September 2025 and superseded by Rev.2.
findings.evidence: Resource URL targets rev-1/final. NIST says Rev.1 withdrawn 2025-09-26 and Rev.2 final supersedes it.
findings.fix: Link SP 800-88 Rev.2 final and describe its current program/validation focus; keep Rev.1 only as historical context if needed.
findings.attack: The deletion/sanitization subtopic sends learners to a superseded authoritative reference.
findings.defense: Rev.1 remains useful historical background and many core sanitization concepts persist.

findings.title: La práctica usa `roles` como contenedor de scopes como `case:read`.
findings.evidence: T2-A E2/E3: campo `roles` contiene `{case:read}`.
findings.impact: Cambia el significado de RBAC/roles y scopes en la misma sección, elevando carga y errores conceptuales.
findings.fix: Separar `roles` de `scopes/permissions` y mantener nombres consistentes en prosa, fixtures y código.
findings.attack: The action name nudges the learner toward requesting privilege when the correct next step may simply be to inspect/register the route policy.
findings.defense: A human narrow-grant workflow could include checking the route catalog.

findings.title: `sha256(secret)[:12]` enseña un identificador determinista derivado directamente de un secreto.
findings.evidence: `secret_fingerprint(raw)` devuelve digest truncado.
findings.impact: Para secretos de baja entropía facilita correlación/guessing y sugiere que loguear derivados del secreto es una práctica general segura.
findings.fix: No loguear fingerprints de secretos por defecto; si se necesita correlación, usar identificador del secret manager o HMAC con clave separada y explicar límites.
findings.attack: Learners can confuse package age with CVE/provenance risk.
findings.defense: Age can be a maintenance signal and the demo separately checks CVE count.

findings.title: Hay una ruptura visible de capitalización/redacción en T1-B.
findings.evidence: “...para que añadir uno sea aditivo. si aparece `type=push`...”
findings.impact: Interrumpe el flujo en un párrafo ya cognitivamente denso y reduce acabado editorial.
findings.fix: Cambiar “si aparece” por “Si aparece” y dividir el párrafo en dos unidades causales.
findings.attack: Learners can memorize tokens and lab action codes without a stable actor→asset→request→control→result model.
findings.defense: Many are authentic industry/API terms and S42 is an advanced production section.

findings.title: There is at least one visible sentence-boundary grammar error and several avoidable code-switching fragments.
findings.evidence: T1-B p3: after a period, 'si aparece `type=push`...' begins lowercase. Phrases such as 'silent cast', 'promote limpio', 'scope granted' and 'missing ≠ breach' are used in prose without consistent Spanish framing.
findings.fix: Correct capitalization and use Spanish-first phrasing while preserving literal identifiers in code formatting.
findings.attack: The style looks like internal engineering notes rather than polished Peruvian Spanish teaching prose.
findings.defense: Code-adjacent English can be useful when it names literal API fields/actions.

findings.title: Resources include RFC 6749 but omit the current OAuth 2.0 Security Best Current Practice RFC 9700.
findings.evidence: RFC 9700 (BCP 240, Jan 2025) updates/extends RFC 6749/6750/6819 security advice and deprecates insecure modes; S42's resource note is specifically 'Scopes y autorización'.
findings.fix: Keep RFC 6749 for protocol semantics and add RFC 9700 as the mandatory security companion.
findings.attack: The base protocol alone is incomplete as a 2026 security reading list.
findings.defense: RFC 6749 remains the foundational OAuth 2.0 framework and is not obsolete.

findings.title: The optional reference block hardcodes redaction_holds=True before any evidence is computed.
findings.evidence: section_contract returns 'redaction_holds': True while only schema/authz handle() is computed.
findings.fix: Rename target fields as requirements (e.g. `require_redaction_holds`) or compute observed evidence from tests; never mix desired policy with measured result in the same shape.
findings.attack: The reference teaches the same evidence-substitution habit the course elsewhere warns against: a boolean name masquerades as a gate result.
findings.defense: The reference object can be read as a target specification, not observed evidence.

findings.title: All eight subtopics repeat the same E1 repair-predicate / E2 valid-adversarial-missing / E3 continue-breach-review template.
findings.evidence: 24 We Do exercises follow the same three-step grammar even when the skills differ materially (Pydantic schema, authz, SSRF, secrets, retention, deletion).
findings.fix: Keep some tri-state drills but interleave authentic tasks: construct Pydantic model/schema, run frozen consumer, inspect principal catalog, parse/resolve URLs, use Path.resolve, parse SCA output, drive a clock expiry, and execute purge/restore.
findings.attack: Learners can pattern-match the exercise shell instead of transferring security reasoning to actual libraries/artifacts.
findings.defense: A stable fail-closed routine reinforces missing≠breach and reduces extraneous UI load.

findings.title: Types/Pydantic are promised; key sets are executed.
Contract evolution is taught but omitted from final readiness.
Authenticated principal becomes names/prefixes and service identity disappears from final project.
Strong SSRF/path explanation degrades to hostname/string checks everywhere assessment occurs.
Security supply-chain evidence becomes flags and then disappears from final project.
Retention expiry is not executed and disappears from final project.
No-reappearance/key separation becomes field-name/empty-store assertions.
S42 repeatedly claims capstone promotion two steps before canonical gate.
The final S43 project does not close the canonical CP-N4-A contract.
findings.evidence: Canonical rubric requires 200/429/401, token-redacted logs and migrations; You Do focuses Docker/Compose and never calls service.serve or verifies those API/auth/rate-limit tests.
findings.impact: A learner can complete S43 while failing required CP-N4-A behavior from S40-S42.
findings.fix: Make You Do an integrated S40-S43 gate: run the canonical seven acceptance tests plus container/recovery evidence.

findings.title: The visible S43 rubric contradicts the canonical CP-N4-A rubric and gate rule.
findings.evidence: Visible: 25/20/15/15/15/10 percentages; canonical: correctness .35, robustness .20, maintainability .25, responsible_use .20, scale 0-3, weighted>=2.4, no critical<2, zero P0.
findings.impact: Two different evaluators can reach incompatible pass/fail decisions for the same capstone.
findings.fix: Render/use the canonical rubric in S43; remove the competing percentage rubric or explicitly derive it from the canonical source.

findings.title: You Do readiness accepts manually flipped booleans and gate_case hardcodes outputs from a label.
findings.evidence: `readiness(bundle)` checks only `bundle.get(name) is True`; `gate_case('normal'|'breach'|...)` returns tokens without inspecting artifacts.
findings.impact: READY and breach evidence can be manufactured without Dockerfile, Compose, runbook, service or tests.
findings.fix: Read/execute artifacts and derive a signed result record from commands, exit codes and checks; booleans may summarize evidence but cannot be the evidence.

findings.title: Roadmap says local con contenedores, but I Do/We Do are almost entirely local-Python simulations of strings/booleans and never build/run containers.
findings.evidence: Eight I Do demos and 24 We Do tasks inspect dicts/text; no docker build, compose up, inspect, exec, health request, SIGTERM, restore or scanner command is performed.
findings.impact: The learner reaches the independent container capstone without guided practice on the actual environment; outcomes are not demonstrated.
findings.fix: Use real Docker/Compose in I Do, then faded guided commands/tests in We Do, then independent one-command rebuild in You Do. Keep stdlib parsers only as preflight exercises.

findings.title: T4-A theory explicitly rejects short fake digests, but I Do and We Do approve `sha256:abc` using `startswith('sha256:')`.
findings.evidence: Theory uses exact `^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$`; I Do calls `stages(...,'sha256:abc')` and prints pinned; We Do solutions repeat prefix test.
findings.impact: The reference practice trains the learner to pass the exact invalid value the theory warned against; supply-chain/reproducibility gate false-greens.
findings.fix: Reuse the exact digest validator everywhere and couple the digest to a real lock/artifact; add short/malformed digest regression tests.

findings.title: Ejecución como root
Sin health checks
Secretos embebidos
Sin migraciones
root
no health checks
embedded secrets
no migrations
S43 closes a capstone on top of S42 although the current S42 audit remains REPAIR_REQUIRED with P0 security evidence failures.
findings.evidence: Roadmap prereq S42; S43 opening says the S42 service can now be containerized.
findings.impact: Container packaging can legitimize an upstream service whose schema/SSRF/deletion gates are not trustworthy.
findings.fix: Require S42 critical evidence to be green before CP-N4-A closure; do not let container checks compensate for upstream security failures.

findings.title: The public CP-N4-A brief leaks pre-V3 section identities: S41 LLM finetuning, S42 graph RAG and S43 LLMOps.
findings.evidence: `public/capstones/CP-N4-A_BRIEF.md` is loaded by learner-facing CapstonesPage and contains those old names.
findings.impact: Learners see a capstone prerequisite map that contradicts the current curriculum they just completed.
findings.fix: Update public/canonical brief labels to current S40 architecture, S41 API FastAPI, S42 schemas/security, S43 containers; preserve stable IDs separately.

findings.title: The public/canonical brief says the container is specified by Dockerfile and is not built, while S43/roadmap require a repeatable build in a new environment and one-command operation.
findings.evidence: Brief limitation: 'no se construye en el demo'; S43 callout/outcomes require build repeatible/entorno nuevo.
findings.impact: The authoritative capstone contract itself disagrees about whether the core artifact must execute.
findings.fix: Choose one contract. For current S43, require an actual local build/run/health test and revise the brief limitation accordingly.

findings.title: T1-A calls a fabricated string comparison a stable build/dependency digest.
findings.evidence: `digest_a=f'deps:{lock_hash}'`; `digest_b` is constructed identically; equality is guaranteed by code, not measured from builds.
findings.impact: Learner can confuse a label derived from input with evidence produced by a build system.
findings.fix: Measure cache/build outputs from Docker/BuildKit or clearly call the string a conceptual cache key and never use it as gate evidence.

findings.title: The lesson treats same lock + dependency cache reuse as evidence that a repeatable build exists.
findings.evidence: T1-A criterion and self-check use 'same logical deps digest'; Docker docs distinguish cache reuse from reproducible build controls.
findings.impact: A fast cached rebuild can pass while fresh builds differ because of base images, package indexes, timestamps or other inputs.
findings.fix: Separate objectives: cache efficiency vs reproducible fresh build. Add clean/no-cache build comparison and pin all declared inputs; optionally teach SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH as an advanced reproducibility control.

findings.title: Multiple learner-facing Dockerfile fixtures use `@sha256:demo`, which is not a valid image digest.
findings.evidence: T1-A and T1-B We Do GOOD_DF use the placeholder; exact-digest theory later says short/fake digests must fail.
findings.impact: The supposedly transferable Dockerfile cannot be built and directly conflicts with the section's own digest validation mental model.
findings.fix: Use a deterministic fixture image reference valid for the test environment or an explicit `<64-hex-demo-digest>` token that is never presented as runnable; preferably build from a local fixture image/digest.

findings.title: You Do explicitly accepts 'digest o tag no latest' although Docker documents tags as mutable and S43 theory requires digest for exact bytes.
findings.evidence: You Do requirement versus T1-B exact DIGEST regex/T4-A discussion and Docker build best practices.
findings.impact: A mutable base can pass the final reproducibility gate.
findings.fix: Require digest pin for the graded reproducibility path; teach controlled update automation separately.

findings.title: T1-B E3 rejects valid named non-root users and accepts malformed digest references.
findings.evidence: `_user_uid` only understands digits/root; `pinned='@sha256:' in dockerfile` accepts `sha256:abc`.
findings.impact: Reference solution produces both false negatives and false positives on a security gate.
findings.fix: Inspect built image/container user (`docker inspect`/id) and parse exact digest; do not infer runtime identity from a two-case text parser.

findings.title: Runtime size predicates allow nonsensical negative values and nonpositive budgets.
findings.evidence: `slim_ok = runtime_mb <= max_mb` without domain checks.
findings.impact: Invalid measurements can create PASS and teach incomplete validation.
findings.fix: Require finite positive runtime_mb and positive max_mb before budget comparison; get actual image size from Docker rather than a supplied integer in final evidence.

findings.title: The outcome promises no extra capabilities, but the final project never verifies container capabilities.
findings.evidence: T1-B theory uses a supplied `caps` set; You Do requirements/readiness have no capability artifact or command.
findings.impact: A privileged/cap-add container can satisfy the final four booleans.
findings.fix: Add runtime inspection/test for granted capabilities and define the course policy as 'no additional capabilities unless justified', rather than `not caps` as an abstract set.

findings.title: Secret leakage detection searches only the substrings SECRET= and PASSWORD=.
findings.evidence: T2-A theory/I Do/We Do scanners ignore TOKEN, API_KEY, ARG/RUN secrets, copied .env, command history and arbitrary secret names.
findings.impact: Images with embedded credentials can pass the lesson's security gate.
findings.fix: Teach build-context exclusion and real secret scanning/history inspection with synthetic seeded tokens; pattern lists are demonstration aids, not proof.

findings.title: `runtime_only` is inferred solely from not detecting a baked secret.
findings.evidence: `runtime_only: not baked`.
findings.impact: No secret at all and a correctly injected runtime secret are treated as the same evidence.
findings.fix: Verify the service receives the secret at runtime from the declared secret mechanism while image/history remains clean; test rotation without rebuild.

findings.title: The lesson lists orchestrator environment variables as a normal secret-injection mechanism without explaining the leakage risk or preferring Compose secrets.
findings.evidence: T2-A prose; current Docker docs explicitly recommend secrets rather than sensitive container environment variables.
findings.impact: A security section can normalize a weaker pattern exactly where a safer Compose mechanism is in scope.
findings.fix: Prefer Compose/runtime secret mounts; mention host env only as a source for a Compose secret or a constrained platform-specific fallback with explicit risk.

findings.title: S43 warns against copying .env/secrets but never teaches `.dockerignore` or build-context minimization.
findings.evidence: No `.dockerignore` artifact appears in outcomes/You Do; Docker's current lab and best-practices guide use it to keep `.env`/irrelevant files out of build context.
findings.impact: Learner can follow the lesson and still send secrets into build context or accidentally COPY them later.
findings.fix: Require `.dockerignore` with synthetic secret/context regression test.

findings.title: T2-B claims readiness and SIGTERM are tested, but code accepts booleans like `drains=True` and never sends a signal or calls a health endpoint.
findings.evidence: `health_status(ready,live)` and `on_sigterm(drains,grace)` are pure proxies.
findings.impact: A process that ignores SIGTERM or always returns 200 can pass if the fixture says otherwise.
findings.fix: Run container; curl readiness with dependency healthy/unhealthy, create in-flight work, send docker stop/SIGTERM and assert drain/exit within configured grace.

findings.title: T3-A says Compose declares healthchecks per service, but MINI_COMPOSE has no `healthcheck:` and health is a supplied set.
findings.evidence: MINI_COMPOSE services only contain networks/depends_on/retry env; `healthy` set drives PASS.
findings.impact: The exemplar teaches that writing `healthy={'api',...}` is equivalent to a service healthcheck.
findings.fix: Use actual healthcheck definitions and `docker compose up --wait`/inspect; include `depends_on.condition: service_healthy` where startup readiness matters.

findings.title: A `DB_MAX_ATTEMPTS` environment token/boolean is treated as proof of application retry/backoff.
findings.evidence: T3-A contract requires token of retries; stack_ok receives `retries=True`.
findings.impact: Configuration can exist while application ignores it or retries incorrectly.
findings.fix: Exercise dependency restart/failure and assert bounded retry/backoff from real service logs/behavior.

findings.title: Theory teaches expand then later contract, but code/We Do allow only `migration == 'expand'` and classify contract as rollback.
findings.evidence: migration_gate and T3-B exercises.
findings.impact: Learner cannot model the second half of the migration strategy and may infer contract is always unsafe.
findings.fix: Represent phases: expand while old code exists; deploy compatible code; only then contract when no reader needs old schema; test both valid and invalid contract transitions.

findings.title: `migrate_before_api=True`, `old_ok`, `ephemeral_reset` and `backup_restored` are declared flags rather than executed migration/recovery evidence.
findings.evidence: T3-B code and reference exercises.
findings.impact: A critical CP-N4-A failure 'Sin migraciones' can be masked by booleans.
findings.fix: Run a small real DB migration and restore fixture, record command/exit/schema state before/after, and gate API startup on migration success.

findings.title: A string that looks like a digest is allowed to stand in for a dependency lock without proving what file it hashes or whether installation enforces it.
findings.evidence: T4-A I Do/We Do records `lock_hash` separately; final requirements do not verify lock content/`--require-hashes` execution.
findings.impact: Learner can hash arbitrary text and claim reproducible dependencies.
findings.fix: Hash the actual lock file, verify the hash in the evidence manifest, and execute package installation with that lock/hash policy.

findings.title: Theory permits signed CVE exceptions, but every executable gate requires critical==0 and has no exception record/expiry/owner.
findings.evidence: T4-B p1 vs scan_gate and We Do.
findings.impact: The written policy and automated policy disagree; learners cannot implement governed exceptions.
findings.fix: Either remove the exception claim from S43 or model a versioned exception with vulnerability ID, rationale, owner, expiry and compensating control.

findings.title: The scan gate trusts a critical-CVE count detached from image digest, scanner version and vulnerability database timestamp.
findings.evidence: T4-B inputs are `critical: int` and text `CRITICAL: 0`.
findings.impact: A stale or unrelated scan can approve a different image.
findings.fix: Persist image digest + scanner/tool version + DB timestamp + report hash; gate the exact built artifact.

findings.title: Tagline/roadmap demand one-command operation and a repeatable build in a new environment, but You Do starter only names file paths and prints status tokens.
findings.evidence: ARTIFACTS contains names; no subprocess/command/test opens those files or starts the stack.
findings.impact: The central learner-facing promise is not assessed.
findings.fix: Provide a real acceptance command such as `make verify`/script that builds, starts, waits for health, runs canonical tests, stops, cleans, and emits an evidence manifest.

findings.title: Visible rubric grades SLO, observability and lineage even though S43's final starter neither produces nor teaches those artifacts as assessed constructs.
findings.evidence: 15% 'Operación: SLO, observabilidad y rollback'; roadmap places CI/CD/supply-chain in S44 and later production observability elsewhere.
findings.impact: Learner is graded on hidden/future requirements while canonical rubric already defines a different contract.
findings.fix: Use canonical CP-N4-A rubric; keep S43-specific operational evidence inside its defined acceptance tests.

findings.title: The learner-facing Theory playground for legacy id `llmops` still teaches LLMOps tracing, RAG, RAGAS metrics and token cost instead of S43 containers.
findings.evidence: SectionView maps `'llmops'` to `Practica tracing y eval (simulado)` with retriever/generator/RAGAS/cost tracking.
findings.impact: A complete unrelated conceptual graph appears inside the container lesson, increasing interference and reviving the obsolete pre-V3 topic.
findings.fix: Keep stable id `llmops` but replace the playground mapping with an on-topic Docker/Compose/reproducibility simulation or disable it for S43.

findings.title: Self-check Q1 calls the fabricated logical deps digest sufficient evidence; Q3 defines CP-N4-A only as container build/non-root/limits/shutdown.
findings.evidence: Current five self-check questions.
findings.impact: Retrieval practice strengthens two curriculum defects instead of detecting them.
findings.fix: Replace Q1 with actual fresh-build/cache evidence distinction; make CP-N4-A question include canonical API/auth/rate/log/migration acceptance plus container criticals.

findings.title: Five recognition questions cannot sample the eight outcomes or integrated capstone gate; migration, lock validation, scan provenance and real restore are largely absent.
findings.evidence: Self-check covers cache, health/root response, gate summary, secrets, cache ordering.
findings.impact: Learner can pass recall while missing the riskiest operational contracts.
findings.fix: Use at least one scenario per critical gate and integrated troubleshooting decisions; keep recognition only as retrieval warm-up.

findings.title: The seeded S43 bank has broad concept coverage but mostly asks declarative multiple-choice facts rather than interpreting concrete Docker/Compose/scan/migration artifacts.
findings.evidence: Examples: COPY requirements cache benefit, multi-stage definition, lockfiles, CVE scan, non-root purpose.
findings.impact: The authenticated exam does not independently verify the portfolio skills it gates.
findings.fix: Keep concept variants but make them artifact-based: Dockerfile diff, Compose health condition, migration runbook, scan report and resource config.

findings.title: Roadmap requires >=70% plus 100% critical items, but platform scoring has no `critical` field and passes solely on total >=70.
findings.evidence: `QuestionKey` lacks critical; `passed: clamped >= PASS_THRESHOLD`.
findings.impact: A learner can miss root/secrets/migration/health security questions and compensate with easy cache questions.
findings.fix: Add critical metadata and require all critical answers correct in addition to total threshold.

findings.title: The two T1 figures are effectively attached to the wrong conceptual moment: T1-A shows builder→runtime/toolchain (the T4-A multi-stage concept), while T1-B shows cache invalidation/source-before-deps (the T1-A concept).
findings.evidence: T1-A figure id `S43-multistage`, caption 'Un gcc en la imagen final...' and alt builder→runtime; T1-B figure id `S43-image-layers`, caption 'Copiar el código antes que las dependencias...' and alt image layers/cache.
findings.impact: The visual channel introduces a future concept before it is explained and then repeats the previous concept when the learner needs a privilege/base mental model; dual coding reinforces the wrong node-to-concept edge.
findings.fix: Move the cache/layer figure to T1-A. Move the multi-stage builder/runtime figure to T4-A, or replace T1-B with a base/non-root/capabilities/runtime-size visual. Do not renumber section IDs.
findings.attack: Checked whether captions were intentionally anticipatory. They are not referenced as previews, and each caption describes the neighboring subtopic more naturally than the one where it is rendered.
findings.defense: Both figures are relevant somewhere in S43, so the assets themselves are not wrong.

findings.title: The lesson equates non-root with UID >=1000.
findings.evidence: Outcome/T1-B repeatedly define application UID >=1000 as non-root.
findings.impact: Learner can infer that UID 1-999 is root or that 1000 itself proves least privilege; neither is generally true.
findings.fix: State: UID 0 is root; this lab adopts >=1000 as a course policy to avoid system/service UIDs. Verify the actual runtime user and privileges.

findings.title: The prose groups slim and distroless as if both necessarily remove the shell.
findings.evidence: 'Distroless/slim recortan shell y paquetes'.
findings.impact: Learner may expect Python slim to behave like distroless during debugging/security review.
findings.fix: Separate the cases: slim reduces packages but may retain shell/tools; distroless intentionally omits many conventional userland tools.

findings.title: `grace >=20` is presented as the definition of graceful shutdown.
findings.evidence: T2-B code and exercises hardcode >=20 seconds.
findings.impact: Learner may optimize to a magic number rather than a workload-specific termination budget; Docker's stop timeout is configurable.
findings.fix: Define a lab `termination_grace_seconds` configuration and require observed drain <= configured budget; explain 20/30 seconds as examples, not universal thresholds.

findings.title: front/back networks are made a universal PASS condition without tying the requirement to actual exposed ports/trust boundaries.
findings.evidence: T3-A `NETS <= networks` hard gate.
findings.impact: Learner memorizes topology names instead of least-exposure reasoning; equivalent secure compositions can false-fail.
findings.fix: Grade the security property: DB/cache not publicly exposed and service communication matches the threat model. front/back is one implementation pattern.

findings.title: Runtime toolchain detection is a substring search for gcc/g++.
findings.evidence: T4-A multistage parser.
findings.impact: clang, make, rustc, build-essential or comments can evade/trigger the rule; the construct is 'minimal runtime', not two words.
findings.fix: Inspect installed packages/files or assert explicit runtime allowlist/base; use substring parsing only as a toy preflight.

findings.title: 512 MiB and 1 CPU are treated as the valid upper range without consistently labeling them as CASO-TRU-043 lab budgets.
findings.evidence: T4-B predicate `0 < mem <=512` and `0 < cpu <=1.0`.
findings.impact: Learner may infer these numbers are container best practices rather than a workload budget.
findings.fix: Declare `LAB_MEMORY_BUDGET_MB=512`/`LAB_CPU_BUDGET=1.0` and explain that production budgets come from workload/SLO/capacity evidence.

findings.title: The 24 We Do tasks repeat E1 inverted-predicate repair, E2 valid/adversarial/missing, E3 text parser/token routing.
findings.evidence: Pattern repeated across all 8 subtopics.
findings.impact: The learner can master task grammar without learning Docker commands, runtime inspection or recovery procedure; guidance is not faded toward authentic performance.
findings.fix: Alternate worked real commands, completion tasks, debugging, prediction, failure injection and independent container verification; return to a worked example only when a genuinely new operation is introduced.

findings.title: Advanced terms accumulate faster than their operational relationships are demonstrated: digest, capabilities, distroless, build context, restore drill, OOM, CVE, expand/contract, builder/runtime.
findings.evidence: Several are named/briefly glossed but never tied to a real command/artifact before repeated exercise tokens.
findings.impact: Learners may memorize labels without a trigger→artifact→command→observable-result model.
findings.fix: Introduce each term with Spanish-first mechanism and one real observable command before abbreviating it later.

findings.title: The resource list mixes strong primary Docker/NIST/OWASP references with generic or beginner Python course links and omits direct links for controls the section currently gets wrong.
findings.evidence: Coursera generic Docker search, MIT 6.100L, CS50P, Py4E; no direct Compose secrets/startup-order/resource constraints/reproducible-build/.dockerignore resources.
findings.impact: Learners are sent to broad beginner material instead of the exact authoritative docs needed to repair the section's hardest misconceptions.
findings.fix: Prioritize Docker secrets, startup order/service_healthy, resource constraints, build cache/reproducible builds, `.dockerignore`, USER/capability hardening and scan provenance; demote generic Python courses.

findings.title: portfolio_ready trusts four learner-editable booleans and gate_case hard-codes normal/breach/uncertain outcomes without reading ARTIFACTS.
findings.impact: A learner can manufacture READY and apparently correct gate routes without a workflow, SBOM, provenance, canary or rollback evidence.
findings.fix: Parse and verify the actual workflow/SBOM/provenance/canary files; derive every gate result from those artifacts.

findings.title: You Do readiness and gate_case are self-attested/hard-coded; READY can be manufactured without artifacts.
T2-A theory and T2-A We Do encode incompatible least-privilege rules.
findings.fix: Use scope-aware workflow/job permission fixtures across all three surfaces.

findings.title: The E3 exercise family confuses pure uncertainty with mixed uncertainty+breach.
findings.fix: Adopt one explicit precedence rule and retain multiple reasons instead of single mutually exclusive labels.

findings.title: Theory correctly allows narrowly scoped job-level write permission when a release operation needs it, while E2/E3 rejects any `write` regardless of scope or capability.
findings.evidence: `packages: write` / any `write` value
findings.impact: Is every write permission insecure, or is a narrowly scoped release-job permission valid?
findings.fix: Represent workflow permissions and job permissions separately, and validate the minimum capability required by each job.

findings.title: Missing evidence is allowed to mask a known breach in another field. The classifier collapses two simultaneous facts into a weaker uncertainty state.
findings.evidence: if missing: return REVIEW_* before breach evaluation
findings.impact: If a record is both incomplete and already demonstrably unsafe, should the pipeline merely request review or block for the known failure?
findings.fix: Evaluate independently observable breaches first (or collect both breach and missing reasons), then route pure uncertainty only when no known breach exists.

findings.title: Existing P0 F02: You Do can manufacture READY from learner-editable booleans.
Existing authentic-evidence cluster remains unresolved.
New F49 and F52 remain unresolved until Fixer applies and validates repairs.
S44 requires S43, but the preceding S43 audit remains REPAIR_REQUIRED with unresolved P0 blockers.
findings.impact: The release-engineering lesson assumes a trustworthy container/service artifact that the prerequisite has not demonstrated.
findings.fix: Keep S44 locked until S43 critical blockers are closed or explicitly teach the prerequisite evidence as provisional.

findings.title: Roadmap environment is controlled CI/cloud, but all eight I Do demonstrations declare local-python and the 24 We Do tasks are Python predicates/parsers.
findings.impact: The learner never observes a real workflow run, artifact upload/download, environment gate, attestation verification or rollback evidence before the independent project.
findings.fix: Retain local models as first scaffold, then fade into an actual CI workflow fixture and downloaded evidence before You Do.

findings.title: Multiple validators accept any string beginning sha256:, including sha256:def, sha256:abc and sha256:x, as a digest.
findings.impact: Malformed identifiers are taught as cryptographic evidence and can pass promotion.
findings.fix: Require ^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$ and bind it to a measured artifact.

findings.title: Artifact evidence is represented by a supplied digest string rather than hashing or verifying the artifact.
findings.impact: The evidence can describe a file that never existed or whose content differs.
findings.fix: Hash a produced fixture artifact and verify the stored digest after re-download.

findings.title: Cache key uses only the first eight characters of a supplied lock hash and never demonstrates that the value is the actual lockfile hash.
findings.impact: The cache can collide or drift from dependency state while still appearing contract-compliant.
findings.fix: Compute a full digest of the lockfile plus relevant runtime dimensions; keep cache non-authoritative.

findings.title: Release-path condition coverage is reduced to booleans/string labels rather than inspecting workflow triggers and job if expressions.
findings.impact: A bypass path on tags, forks or manual dispatch can remain invisible.
findings.fix: Parse a real workflow and test main/tag/PR/fork/manual cases explicitly.

findings.title: Any secret_scan hit is mapped to REVOKE_AND_ROTATE, ignoring false positives, synthetic/test credentials, validation status and audited bypass workflows.
findings.impact: Learners conflate detection with confirmed credential compromise and learn the wrong incident response routing.
findings.fix: Block first; classify/validate the finding; revoke/rotate confirmed active exposed credentials; record approved false-positive/test-secret disposition.

findings.title: Permission validation is substring-based and does not model effective workflow/job permissions required by attestation jobs.
findings.impact: A workflow can be declared least-privilege without demonstrating the authority actually used by each job.
findings.fix: Parse YAML structure and check effective permissions per job, including explicit id-token/attestations permissions where provenance is generated.

findings.title: pin_ok is overwritten for every uses line; a final pinned action makes an earlier unpinned third-party action disappear from the verdict.
findings.evidence: evil/action@v1 followed by a full-SHA actions/checkout returns pinned=True.
findings.impact: A vulnerable workflow can pass the lesson's hardening validator.
findings.fix: Collect every uses reference and require every non-local action to satisfy the pin policy.

findings.title: A 40-hex ref is accepted without verifying that the commit belongs to the intended action repository rather than a fork or unrelated object.
findings.impact: Format validation is mistaken for provenance validation.
findings.fix: Teach repository+commit verification and retain the resolved action identity as evidence.

findings.title: dependency_review is a supplied boolean rather than evidence from a dependency review check/report.
findings.impact: A critical supply-chain gate is self-attested.
findings.fix: Use a stored dependency-review result/fixture and verify its conclusion and policy threshold.

findings.title: The lesson requires artifact digest == SBOM digest == provenance subject. An SBOM document has its own content digest; what must bind is the SBOM/provenance subject identity to the artifact, not equality of the SBOM file hash with the artifact hash.
findings.impact: Teaches a materially incorrect evidence model and can reject valid SBOMs while accepting fabricated equal strings.
findings.fix: Represent artifact_digest, sbom_document_digest, sbom_subject_digest and provenance_subject_digest separately; compare subject digests to the artifact.

findings.title: Attestation validity is supplied as a boolean.
findings.impact: Cryptographic verification is replaced by self-assertion.
findings.fix: Verify an attestation fixture with expected subject digest, issuer/builder identity and source workflow.

findings.title: The provenance gate does not inspect builder identity, workflow/repository, source revision or attestation authenticity despite teaching those concepts.
findings.impact: Matching strings can pass even when provenance came from the wrong builder/source.
findings.fix: Verify subject + trusted builder/issuer + repo + workflow + commit/revision.

findings.title: bool(approved_by) is treated as independent approval.
findings.impact: The author can type their own name or any arbitrary string and pass promotion.
findings.fix: Model initiator, approved_by and allowed reviewer set; require approved_by != initiator and a verified environment approval record.

findings.title: Environment protection is represented as a list of names/approvers rather than enforcement such as required reviewers/prevent-self-review/branch policy.
findings.impact: The learner can confuse configuration documentation with an enforced deployment gate.
findings.fix: Inspect an environment policy fixture or CI evidence showing the job waited for and received an authorized review.

findings.title: Promotion accepts malformed prefix-only sha256 values.
findings.impact: Same-string equality is insufficient if neither string is a valid measured digest.
findings.fix: Validate full digest and verify it against the staged artifact before promotion.

findings.title: No lower-bound validation exists for error rate, rollback seconds or RTO; negative values pass.
findings.evidence: canary_ok(-1,0.01,-999,120) returns True.
findings.impact: Nonsensical telemetry can authorize release.
findings.fix: Validate 0<=error<=1, 0<=max<=1, rollback_s>=0 and rto>0 before evaluating policy.

findings.title: The final canary helper omits migration_compatible and rollback_tested even though T3-B teaches both as required.
findings.impact: You Do is weaker than its own guided practice and can pass an untested rollback.
findings.fix: Carry the full T3-B contract into the final verifier.

findings.title: Rollback is timed but not bound to a previous known-good digest/config/data state.
findings.impact: A fast action can be called rollback without proving restoration of the intended version.
findings.fix: Record before_digest, failed_digest, restored_digest and assert restored_digest==last_known_good, plus migration/data recovery evidence.

findings.title: migration_compatible and rollback_tested are learner-supplied booleans rather than test outputs.
findings.impact: The highest-risk release properties remain self-attested.
findings.fix: Run compatibility/rollback fixture checks and retain their logs/results.

findings.title: Branch protection, required checks and reviews are modeled by values/sets, not by an enforceable repository policy or evidence snapshot.
findings.impact: Governance becomes descriptive rather than verified.
findings.fix: Audit a branch/ruleset fixture or exported policy and assert required checks/review count/bypass policy.

findings.title: PASS requires critical_failure=True; a healthy pipeline with no critical failure is classified STOP_SILENT_FAILURE.
findings.evidence: critical_failure=False, evidence otherwise complete -> STOP_SILENT_FAILURE.
findings.impact: The state machine defines successful evidence handling only for an incident, not normal operation.
findings.fix: Separate normal success from critical-failure handling; only require blocked=True when critical_failure is true.

findings.title: Missing evidence_retained routes to ASSIGN_INCIDENT_OWNER even when an owner is already present.
findings.impact: The remediation code points to the wrong missing control.
findings.fix: Use RETAIN_INCIDENT_EVIDENCE (or equivalent) for evidence absence and ASSIGN_INCIDENT_OWNER only when owner is absent.

findings.title: logs_redacted, owner and evidence_retained are self-attested fields rather than inspection of retained evidence.
findings.impact: Auditability is represented by claims about auditability.
findings.fix: Inspect a redacted log fixture, evidence manifest and ownership record.

findings.title: All eight triads repeat nearly the same E1 inverted predicate -> E2 valid/adversarial/missing dict -> E3 fail-closed classifier grammar.
findings.impact: Learners can master the exercise template without mastering CI/CD or supply-chain operations.
findings.fix: Diversify tasks: edit YAML, inspect logs, compare artifacts, verify attestation, diagnose environment protection, execute rollback evidence.

findings.title: Most E3 tasks reuse the same fixture/schema and do not meaningfully change context, contrary to the roadmap's transfer requirement.
findings.impact: The apparent gradual release does not test structural transfer.
findings.fix: Change repository/workflow/evidence representation and require the learner to select the relevant control without being told the gate name.

findings.title: All eight demos are local-python simulations although the roadmap specifies controlled CI/cloud for S44.
findings.impact: Worked examples never model the target procedure that You Do asks the learner to produce.
findings.fix: Introduce at least one complete real CI run worked example, then fade pieces across subsequent exercises.

findings.title: Legacy id multimodal still renders 'Practica CLIP y Whisper (simulado)' with obsolete multimodal content inside S44 Theory.
findings.impact: Direct learner-facing topic contamination and meta/order leak.
findings.fix: Keep the stable id but replace only its playground mapping with an S44 CI/supply-chain exercise.

findings.title: Learner-facing prerequisite labels still say S44 multimodal, S45 IaC, S46 GPU computing, S47 opensource.
findings.impact: The capstone path contradicts the current roadmap and teaches the wrong section identities.
findings.fix: Update display labels while preserving stable IDs/paths.

findings.title: Self-check asks what demonstrates 'the gate CP-N4-B' inside S44 even though canonical CP-N4-B gate is S47.
findings.impact: Learners can infer that S44 closes the capstone rather than starts it.
findings.fix: Ask what demonstrates the S44 increment toward CP-N4-B and state that S47 is the final gate.

findings.title: Roadmap requires four authentic topic assessments; S44 source exposes selfCheck but no four topic-assessment artifacts in the CourseSection content.
findings.impact: The section does not satisfy the quantified assessment architecture of its own authoritative roadmap.
findings.fix: Add one integrated authentic assessment after each T1-T4 pair, jointly scoring both subtopics.

findings.title: Prerequisite S43 remains REPAIR_REQUIRED with 5 P0; S44 cannot treat upstream artifact as trusted evidence.
Roadmap targets controlled CI/cloud but practice is overwhelmingly local Python predicates/parsers.
