Prefix-only sha256 validation accepts malformed digests.
Artifact digest is supplied rather than measured and reverified from an artifact.
Cache key truncates a supplied lock hash and never proves it came from the lockfile.
Workflow condition coverage is self-reported, not inspected across triggers/branches/tags/forks/manual paths.
Any secret-scan hit is routed directly to revoke/rotate without classification or false-positive/test-secret handling.
Permission validation does not compute effective workflow/job permissions.
pin_ok is overwritten per action, so a later pinned action can hide an earlier unpinned action.
40-hex format is accepted without verifying commit identity belongs to intended action repository.
Dependency review is a learner-supplied boolean instead of check/report evidence.
Lesson incorrectly requires artifact digest == SBOM document digest == provenance subject.
Attestation validity is a boolean rather than cryptographic/policy verification.
Provenance gate omits builder/issuer, repo/workflow and source revision identity.
Truthy approved_by is treated as independent deployment approval.
Environment protection is represented by names/approvers, not enforceable protection rules.
Promotion again accepts malformed prefix-only sha256 values.
Canary validator accepts negative error rates and negative rollback/RTO values.
You Do canary drops migration_compatible and rollback_tested from the guided contract.
Rollback is timed but not bound to last-known-good digest/config/data.
Migration compatibility and rollback testing are self-attested booleans.
Branch protection/check/review requirements are values/sets, not repository ruleset evidence.
T4-B PASS requires critical_failure=True; a healthy run is misclassified STOP_SILENT_FAILURE.
Missing retained evidence routes to ASSIGN_INCIDENT_OWNER even when owner already exists.
Log redaction, owner and evidence retention remain self-attested fields.
All 24 We Do exercises repeat a predicate-repair/classify/fail-closed grammar.
E3 transfer is weak because representation/context barely changes.
All eight I Do demos are local Python simulations instead of target CI procedures.
Theory playground leaks obsolete `Practica CLIP y Whisper (simulado)` through legacy id mapping.
Canonical/public CP-N4-B brief exposes stale pre-V3 section labels for S44-S47.
Self-check calls an S44 result the CP-N4-B gate although canonical gate is S47.
Four roadmap-required authentic topic assessments are absent.
Intro conflates GitHub Action SHA pinning with Python/package dependency locking/hashing.
Attestation teaching omits the explicit least-privilege permissions required to generate GitHub attestations.
Secret scanning is represented by `run: echo gitleaks-stub-ok`, and `workflow_security` accepts any raw occurrence of `secret-scan` or `gitleaks` as proof that scanning exists.
findings.evidence: A comment `# secret-scan` plus `echo nothing`, with no scanner invocation, returns `secret_scan=True`.
findings.impact: A workflow that never runs any scanner can pass the taught supply-chain security gate, turning decorative text into security evidence.
findings.fix: Use an actual controlled scan or deterministic scan fixture and verify structured execution evidence/exit status; require the real scanner step structurally, not token presence.
findings.attack: Remove all scanner execution but preserve only a label/comment/token and rerun the canonical verifier.
findings.defense: A stub can reduce tool/setup burden in an early explanation.
findings.verdict: The defense fails because the stub is not clearly quarantined as non-evidence and the same substring detector is presented as the gate. This is a verifier defect, not merely simplified prose.
findings.justification: Supply-chain security instruction must distinguish 'the workflow says it scans' from 'the scan executed and produced evidence'.

findings.title: Least-privilege exercise rejects legitimate scoped job-level write permissions.
Missing-first E3 routing masks independently observable breaches.
The prose broadly says dependencies are fixed by immutable SHA rather than version ranges, conflating GitHub Action pinning with normal package locking/hash verification.
findings.impact: Learners may apply Git commit-SHA policy indiscriminately to package dependencies.
findings.fix: Separate action refs (full commit SHA) from Python/package dependencies (lockfile + exact versions/hashes as supported by the package tool).

findings.title: The least-privilege model never teaches the explicit permissions needed to generate GitHub artifact attestations, so the T2-A permissions story does not connect to the T2-B provenance operation.
findings.impact: A learner following the model cannot reason about why the attestation job needs narrowly elevated identity/attestation permissions.
findings.fix: Add a dedicated attestation job example with the exact minimal permissions and explain why elevation is scoped there.

findings.title: The term/status is undefined, not derived from any input and not part of the stated release contract.
findings.evidence: conventional
findings.impact: What is conventional here—Conventional Commits, a release-note format, or something else—and why is it automatically true?
findings.fix: Remove the signal; or, if Conventional Commits is intended, define it and compute the result from a real commit-message fixture.

findings.title: The food-label analogy is useful, but 'everything' overstates SBOM scope. An SBOM inventories software components/dependencies and related information; broader build inputs and builder/workflow evidence belong to provenance or other evidence.
findings.evidence: todo lo que entró en tu artefacto
findings.impact: Should the SBOM contain every build script, compiler setting, workflow input and runner detail?
findings.fix: Keep the ingredients analogy but say 'componentes y dependencias de software' and state that provenance records how/by whom the artifact was built.

findings.title: retention_days >= 7 is presented as a general promotion criterion without deriving the period from policy, investigation window or capstone needs.
findings.impact: Creates false precision and confuses a lab parameter with an industry rule.
findings.fix: Label seven days as CASO-PIU-044 policy and require an explicit retention policy input.

findings.title: The permission/action-pin figure is attached to T1-A lint/types/tests rather than the T2-A hardening concept it depicts.
findings.impact: Visual guidance arrives before its concept and weakens figure-text coherence.
findings.fix: Move S44-permission-scope to T2-A; keep the supply-chain pipeline figure with T1.

findings.title: Provenance is described as recording 'en qué máquina' in a way that overstates what generic provenance guarantees.
findings.impact: Learners may expect physical runner identity rather than attested builder/workflow/environment metadata.
findings.fix: Say builder/runtime/workflow identity and recorded build environment information according to the attestation format.

findings.title: The section alternates prod and production in environment contracts and examples.
findings.impact: Adds needless schema/terminology friction in an otherwise strict string-based exercise family.
findings.fix: Choose one canonical environment identifier and distinguish display label from machine value.

findings.title: A single error-rate threshold is treated as sufficient canary evidence without minimum sample/window or other health signals.
findings.impact: At Level 4, learners may infer that a tiny sample below threshold is enough to expand traffic.
findings.fix: Make the lab contract require a measurement window/sample count and at least one additional SLO signal, while labeling the simplification.

findings.title: signed_commits appears in branch_policy code but is not consistently part of the stated contract or subsequent assessment.
findings.impact: Creates a decorative security signal that learners cannot tell is required, optional or unrelated.
findings.fix: Either teach and assess commit/tag signing explicitly or remove it from the gate example.

findings.title: Notes are reduced to presence of four labels, not actionable content, owner/effective migration command, verification or rollback target.
findings.impact: A release note containing empty headings can pass.
findings.fix: Require minimally structured nonempty values and link rollback to the tested prior digest/runbook.

findings.title: Local S44 rubric uses 25/20/15/15/15/10 while canonical CP-N4-B rubric uses 35/20/25/20 and a 2.4/3 critical gate.
findings.impact: Because S44 only starts CP-N4-B, a section-specific rubric can be valid, but its current presentation does not clearly distinguish itself from the capstone rubric.
findings.fix: Label it 'Rúbrica del incremento S44' and explicitly link the canonical S47 capstone rubric.

findings.title: The S44 bank is current CI/CD content but is dominated by short conceptual multiple-choice recall such as matrix compatibility, caching and artifact purpose rather than evidence interpretation.
findings.impact: Assessment under-samples Level-4 artifact diagnosis/transfer.
findings.fix: Keep conceptual items but replace several variants with workflow/log/SBOM/provenance snippets requiring a decision and rationale.

findings.title: Resource list is generally strong but omits direct first-party artifact-attestation, dependency-review and secret-scanning/push-protection pages while including broad generic course links.
findings.impact: Learners must infer key implementation details from less targeted resources.
findings.fix: Prioritize current GitHub first-party implementation references and SLSA verification guidance; demote generic links.

findings.title: Seven-day retention is presented as a general rule instead of lab policy.
Permission/pinning figure is placed under T1-A rather than T2-A.
Provenance prose overstates generic guarantee as exact machine identity.
prod/production identifier terminology is inconsistent.
Canary relies on one error-rate threshold without minimum sample/window or second health signal.
signed_commits appears decoratively/inconsistently in the taught contract.
Release notes can pass with required labels but empty/non-actionable values.
Visible S44 rubric differs from canonical CP-N4-B rubric without labeling/mapping itself as interim.
Authenticated S44 exam is topically current but mostly short conceptual recognition, weak for Level-4 artifact inspection.
Resource list omits direct first-party docs for key attestation/dependency-review/secret-protection operations.
Dense unexplained English/ops vocabulary raises avoidable language load in Peruvian Spanish.
Declared `S44-permission-scope` figure is absent from FIGURES/FIGURE_DATA; FigureFrame returns null so it never renders.
findings.fix: Register and test the figure and move it to T2-A if retained, or remove/replace the dead reference with a valid aligned visual.
findings.location: S44-T1-A figure reference + shared FigureFrame registries
findings.justification: Referenced learner-facing figures must resolve; otherwise intended dual-coded support silently disappears.

findings.title: Spanish prose carries dense unexplained or inconsistently translated ops vocabulary (artifact, provenance, attestation, owner, hold, breach, lead, ops).
findings.impact: Raises extraneous linguistic load for learners using Peruvian Spanish as the instructional language.
findings.fix: Define each unavoidable term once in Spanish-first form and keep machine identifiers/code words visually distinct.

findings.title: `conventional True` is an unexplained, hard-coded green signal.
Opening SBOM mental model overstates scope as everything that entered the artifact.
Current canonical source has estimatedHours=9 while the public rendered snapshot observed during the audit reports 20h.
findings.fix: Resolve the deployed SHA/build source before changing either value; do not guess which number is authoritative.

findings.title: The section repeatedly collapses policy scope into boolean/string predicates, causing the learner model to diverge from the real CI/CD control.
Uncertainty is routed before already observable breaches in multiple E3 classifiers, so a missing field can downgrade a known failure into a review state.
The section still contains learner-visible decorative or unexplained green signals that are not derived from evidence.
The opening SBOM explanation overstates scope and blurs SBOM component inventory with broader build inputs/provenance.
permission scope: workflow-level default vs job-level exception
precedence when a record contains both missing evidence and an independently observable breach
SBOM scope vs provenance/build metadata
`write` is correctly presented in theory as sometimes necessary at job scope, but exercises treat every write value as a breach.
`conventional` appears as a boolean/status without a defined concept or relationship to the release gate.
conventional
Theory's central restart/durability question is not represented in You Do acceptance; volatile collections can pass before restart.
findings.fix: Make process restart/reopen/redelivery a final acceptance test.

findings.title: The final project claims `estado durable`, object store, durable idempotency and DLQ but implements all four as process-local `dict`, `set` and `list`; the final assert can pass before a restart while every claimed durable effect disappears after restart.
findings.evidence: Executed RED: after completing the commented TODOs, the final assert is True; reinitializing the process makes artifact/status/idempotency/DLQ survival all False.
findings.impact: A learner can pass the capstone increment while failing the section's central question: `si el proceso muere justo aquí, ¿qué queda?`
findings.fix: Use durable local evidence (SQLite/files or an emulator) and make the acceptance test kill/recreate the worker process, reopen stores, redeliver the same message and verify one effect + surviving DLQ/status.
findings.justification: This is the core construct of S45, not an optional production enhancement.

findings.title: Roadmap S45 environment is cloud-lab/emulator while all I Do/We Do are local Python predicates.
findings.fix: Introduce controlled emulated artifacts progressively.

findings.title: CP-N4-B is repeatedly presented as S45's gate although S47 is authoritative closure.
findings.fix: Rename all S45 references to incremento hacia CP-N4-B.

findings.title: Shared renderer uses historical id iac as semantic playground key, leaking obsolete Terraform content.
findings.fix: Decouple stable key from current semantic mapping.

findings.title: Missing-first E3 pattern repeats across domains and masks known adverse facts.
findings.fix: Return/retain multiple reasons and prioritize proven breach for blocking.

findings.title: S45 requires S44, but the effective S44 Explorer state is still REPAIR_REQUIRED with a P0 and many unresolved P1s.
findings.evidence: The authoritative roadmap declares `Prerrequisito: S44` and its sequential ledger says S45 cannot begin until S44 is closed.
findings.impact: S45 assumes a trustworthy S44 artifact/supply-chain input that the prerequisite has not yet demonstrated.
findings.fix: Keep the learner gate locked until S44 critical findings are fixed, or mark S45 practice explicitly provisional and bind its input artifact to a verified S44 fixture.
findings.justification: A prerequisite is an evidence dependency, not just a navigation label.

findings.title: The same canonical source declares 9 estimated hours and ~20 hours (6 theory/demos + 8 We Do + 6 You Do).
findings.evidence: `estimatedHours: 9`; opening callout: `~20 h`; optional contract: `Alrededor de veinte horas`.
findings.impact: Learners and platform planners receive materially incompatible workload expectations; the 20-hour decomposition is more than double the UI metadata.
findings.fix: Choose one provisional estimate backed by the roadmap/pilot policy. If 20h is the working estimate, set metadata consistently and label it provisional until pilot data exists.
findings.location: metadata + opening callout + optional section contract
findings.justification: Workload is part of the instructional contract and should not contradict itself.

findings.title: S45 repeatedly calls its increment `Gate CP-N4-B` even though the authoritative roadmap closes CP-N4-B at S47; S44 starts it and S45 is an intermediate increment.
findings.evidence: Roadmap: `S47 — ... cierre CP-N4-B`; S45 roadmap gate is only `job asíncrono...`.
findings.impact: Learners can infer that S45 completes a capstone that the roadmap says remains open through S46 and S47.
findings.fix: Use `Incremento S45 hacia CP-N4-B` everywhere in S45 and reserve `cierre/gate CP-N4-B` for S47.
findings.location: opening callout, I Do copy, You Do objective/portfolio/self-check
findings.justification: Capstone gates must have one unambiguous closure point.

findings.title: The roadmap requires `cloud-lab o emulador`, but all eight I Do demos are `local-python` predicates and the 24 We Do tasks are dictionary/boolean exercises.
findings.evidence: S45 roadmap environment is `cloud-lab o emulador`; every I Do `environment` is `local-python`.
findings.impact: The learner never observes persistence across process death, real/emulated delivery semantics, an IAM policy artifact, an IaC plan, or a restore/export operation before the independent project.
findings.fix: Keep local predicates as first scaffolds, then fade into deterministic emulated evidence: SQLite/file-backed stores, a queue emulator/fixture, structured IAM policy, saved Terraform plan fixture, and an executed restore/export drill.
findings.location: roadmap environment → all eight I Do demos / We Do
findings.justification: Authenticity can be achieved locally without paid cloud, but the target procedure must eventually be practiced.

findings.title: The authoritative roadmap requires four authentic topic evaluations (one after each T1–T4 pair), but S45 source exposes no four topic-evaluation artifacts.
findings.evidence: Roadmap quantifies `Evaluaciones de tema: 4 por sección` and says each topic ends with an authentic integrated evaluation.
findings.impact: The section lacks the required checkpoints that jointly assess both subtopics before the final section exam/project.
findings.fix: Add four authentic topic evaluations with two tasks each, one per subtopic, scored jointly on the roadmap's 0–3 rubric.
findings.justification: Twenty-four exercises are practice, not a substitute for the roadmap's distinct topic assessments.

findings.title: All eight families repeat nearly the same grammar: E1 invert a predicate, E2 classify valid/adversarial/missing dicts, E3 map the same schema to continue/breach/review.
findings.evidence: The We Do intro explicitly standardizes this pattern across eight fixture families.
findings.impact: Learners can learn the exercise template and boolean direction rather than storage, queue, network, IaC, cost, and recovery reasoning.
findings.fix: Diversify tasks: inspect a persisted store after restart, diagnose queue traces, review IAM resources, inspect a Terraform plan JSON, test restore evidence, and reconcile budget/quota telemetry.
findings.justification: Interleaving representations prevents template memorization from masquerading as domain mastery.

findings.title: E3 is labeled transfer but usually reuses the same case, fields, representation, named gate and almost the same predicate from E1/E2.
findings.evidence: Each E3 keeps the same `CASO-IQU-045-x`, same required keys and same domain fixture.
findings.impact: Scaffold removal occurs syntactically, but structural transfer to a new representation/context is weak.
findings.fix: For E3, change representation and context: YAML/policy/log/plan/manifest inputs, different case details, and require learners to select the control without being given the gate name.
findings.justification: The roadmap explicitly says E3 changes context and demands independent transfer.

findings.title: Missing-first routing can hide an independently observable breach.
findings.evidence: Executed mutations: T1-B eventual consistency + RPO breach + missing RTO → `RUN_RESTORE_DRILL`; T3-A overload/public network + missing backpressure → `REQUEST_CAPACITY`; T4-A unsafe plan + missing destructive count → `REVIEW_DRIFT`; T4-B over-budget/over-quota + missing export → `COST_OWNER_REVIEW`.
findings.impact: Deleting one field can downgrade a known failure from block/containment to review/uncertainty.
findings.fix: Compute known breaches from fields that are present, retain missing fields separately, block on any proven breach, and use review states only for pure uncertainty.
findings.justification: Fail-closed does not mean erasing known adverse evidence when some other evidence is missing.

findings.title: The prose says another reader seeing the same state may require a guarantee `monotónica o lineal`, conflating different guarantees.
findings.evidence: Monotonic reads prevent a session from going backward; they do not by themselves guarantee that another client sees another client's latest write.
findings.impact: Learners can select session/monotonic consistency for a cross-client freshness requirement it does not satisfy.
findings.fix: Separate guarantees: read-your-writes/session guarantees for a writer/session; monotonic reads prevent a session from observing older versions after newer ones; cross-client latest-write visibility may require stronger consistency depending on the store and requirement.
findings.justification: Consistency vocabulary is a core distributed-systems construct and must not be interchangeable.

findings.title: The demo calls a process-local `dict` an idempotent effect store; it is neither durable across restart nor atomic across concurrent consumers.
findings.evidence: `effects: dict[str, str] = {}` is checked and updated in-process.
findings.impact: Two workers can race on the same key, and a worker restart erases all deduplication state—the exact failure mode the lesson is about.
findings.fix: Use a deterministic persistent idempotency fixture (e.g. SQLite with a unique key and INPROGRESS/COMPLETE states) and show duplicate/concurrent attempts.
findings.justification: At-least-once delivery requires idempotency state that survives retries and coordinates concurrency.

findings.title: The demo writes the effect after the visibility timeout has already expired and then returns `ACK_AFTER_REDELIVERY_WINDOW`, without representing a concurrent redelivery.
findings.evidence: `effects[key] = 'done'` occurs before checking `processing_s >= VISIBILITY_TIMEOUT_S`.
findings.impact: The code creates a false sense that noticing the expired timeout after the effect is sufficient; a second worker may already be processing the same message.
findings.fix: Model visibility extension or a persistent idempotency claim before the side effect, then demonstrate the race/redelivery explicitly.
findings.justification: Visibility timeout is a lease, not a post-hoc label.

findings.title: Theory explicitly requires a durable dedup store, but the worked demo uses a process-local `set` and list.
findings.evidence: `seen: set = set()` and `dlq: list = []`.
findings.impact: Restart erases both dedup and DLQ evidence, contradicting the taught contract.
findings.fix: Persist dedup and DLQ fixtures to SQLite/files and re-open them after a simulated restart.
findings.justification: A worked example must model the property it names as essential.

findings.title: Capacity predicates do not validate worker/count domains; the I Do helper accepts zero or negative workers, while We Do divides directly by workers.
findings.evidence: Executed: `capacity_ok(0,6,1,25) -> True`; `capacity_ok(-1,6,0,25) -> True`. E1/E2 solutions use `backlog / record['workers']` and can divide by zero.
findings.impact: Nonsensical capacity values can pass or crash the assessor.
findings.fix: Validate `workers >= 1`, `quota_workers >= 1`, `backlog >= 0`, `target_per_worker > 0` before capacity math; invalid domain → explicit schema/domain error.
findings.justification: Production gates must reject impossible telemetry rather than normalize it with `max(workers,1)`.

findings.title: The prose says an image packages interpreter, libraries and `variables de entorno`, without distinguishing runtime configuration from Dockerfile ENV/ARG and secrets.
findings.evidence: Docker warns that sensitive values in Dockerfile `ENV`/`ARG` persist in images/metadata.
findings.impact: Learners may bake environment-specific configuration or credentials into images, conflicting with S43/S45 secret-handling goals.
findings.fix: Say the image packages code/runtime/dependencies; inject environment-specific config at runtime. Never bake secrets with Dockerfile ARG/ENV; use runtime secret/config mechanisms.
findings.justification: The image/runtime configuration boundary is a security and reproducibility boundary.

findings.title: Four long paragraphs re-teach container/orchestration basics immediately after S43, rather than using S43 as prerequisite and connecting the artifact to S45's worker/queue/capacity problem.
findings.evidence: Roadmap makes S43 container reproducibility the prerequisite path before S44/S45.
findings.impact: High extraneous cognitive load interrupts the S45 narrative exactly when the learner should be reasoning about queue lag, quotas, private networking and backpressure.
findings.fix: Compress to a short bridge: `S43 ya te dio una imagen reproducible; aquí decides cuántas instancias del worker ejecutar, cuándo escalar y cómo aislar su red.` Move Docker/K8s refresher to an optional recall box.
findings.justification: Prerequisites should reduce repetition and preserve narrative momentum.

findings.title: Theory defines least privilege as action **and resource**, but all code validates only action membership, private path and egress host; it never checks bucket/prefix/queue resource scope.
findings.evidence: `allow(action, allowed, host, egress_allow, private)` has no resource parameter.
findings.impact: A role with `object:get` over every bucket could pass despite violating the exact resource-scope rule the prose teaches.
findings.fix: Represent allowed `(action, resource)` pairs or policy statements and add negative tests for a different bucket/prefix/queue.
findings.justification: Least privilege is not only verb-level authorization.

findings.title: The lesson says to reject **unexpected** destructive changes but its canonical predicate rejects every `destroys > 0`.
findings.evidence: `plan_acceptable(... destroys) -> ... and destroys == 0`.
findings.impact: Learners can conclude that legitimate reviewed replacements/deletions are categorically invalid rather than risk-managed plan changes.
findings.fix: Model destructive changes as expected/approved vs unexpected, with explicit resource identity and review evidence; reject unapproved destruction.
findings.justification: IaC review is about intended change semantics, not a universal zero-destroy rule.

findings.title: `declared == planned` set equality reduces a Terraform plan to resource names and cannot represent update, replace, delete, unknown values, drift reasons or resource attributes.
findings.evidence: The code compares `{'queue','bucket'}` sets and a destroy count.
findings.impact: A materially unsafe plan can look identical at the resource-name level.
findings.fix: Use a small checked-in Terraform plan JSON fixture and inspect resource change actions/addresses plus an allowlist of expected changes.
findings.justification: The target skill is plan review; a set-of-names predicate is not a faithful plan model.

findings.title: `secret_values_in_plan` is a learner-supplied boolean, and the prose implies a plan can simply be `sin secretos`; Terraform plan/state artifacts may contain sensitive values even when terminal output is redacted.
findings.evidence: HashiCorp warns saved plan files can contain sensitive data in cleartext and must be treated as sensitive artifacts.
findings.impact: Learners may store/commit plan artifacts unsafely or treat a boolean assertion as evidence that no sensitive data exists.
findings.fix: Teach secure handling of plan/state as sensitive by default; inspect a redacted/synthetic plan fixture and verify no course secret is committed, rather than trusting a boolean.
findings.justification: Security should be demonstrated at the artifact boundary.

findings.title: Recovery and portability are represented by `restore_tested` and `portable_export` booleans rather than outputs/artifacts from a restore/export.
findings.evidence: `recovery_portable(True, True)` and exercise fixtures use supplied flags.
findings.impact: A learner can assert the most important operational evidence instead of demonstrating it.
findings.fix: Create a synthetic backup, restore it, verify checksum/state, export a portable manifest/data artifact, and derive status from those outputs.
findings.justification: The paragraph itself says recovery/portability are rehearsed, not asserted.

findings.title: IAM and egress constants are declared but never consumed by `process_once`, `gate_budget_ok` or the final assert.
findings.evidence: Executed mutation to broad `*:*` IAM and `0.0.0.0/0`-style egress leaves the final gate green because neither value participates.
findings.impact: The project can pass while violating one of its explicit objectives and requirements.
findings.fix: Add an authorization function that validates action+resource+private path+egress host; include positive and negative policy tests in the final gate.
findings.justification: Unused constants are documentation, not enforced security evidence.

findings.title: The final gate omits several explicit section requirements: quota, RPO/RTO, IaC plan evidence, visibility/backoff behavior, resource-scoped IAM and actual restore/export outputs.
findings.evidence: `gate_budget_ok()` checks only forecast<=budget plus two booleans; final assert checks store/status/DLQ/budget/cache.
findings.impact: The independent project is weaker than the guided content and rubric; major subtopics can be skipped without failing.
findings.fix: Make a structured portfolio verifier read evidence artifacts for T1–T4 and fail with precise reasons for any absent/failed requirement.
findings.location: You Do starter and final assertion
findings.justification: You Do should integrate, not discard, the contracts established by I Do/We Do.

findings.title: The portfolio note says the skeleton is not a checklist of booleans, yet `RESTORE_TESTED=True` and `PORTABLE_EXPORT=True` directly decide readiness.
findings.evidence: Those booleans feed `gate_budget_ok()` with no linked files/results.
findings.impact: The prose warns against the exact anti-pattern implemented by the starter.
findings.fix: Replace flags with paths/results from restore/export fixtures and verify them.
findings.justification: A warning cannot compensate for a verifier that rewards the forbidden shortcut.

findings.title: The final handler trusts any caller-provided `idempotency_key` and does not bind it to case/artifact/operation even though earlier S45 explains a stable composite identity.
findings.evidence: `key = msg['idempotency_key']`; fixtures use arbitrary strings.
findings.impact: Two different operations can collide or the same logical operation can be retried with different keys and duplicate side effects.
findings.fix: Define and validate a canonical key from stable business inputs (e.g. case_id + artifact digest + operation/version) or verify a producer-generated key against those fields.
findings.justification: Idempotency depends on the semantic identity of the operation, not merely on a nonempty string.

findings.title: The project requires risk residual, owner, rollback criterion, SLO/observability and recovery, but the starter has no evidence structure or test for them.
findings.evidence: Rubric allocates 15% to `SLO, costo/cuota, observabilidad y rollback`; starter only prints a skeleton/budget status.
findings.impact: Operational readiness can receive credit without an executable recovery/observability path.
findings.fix: Add an evidence manifest with owner, SLO measurements, rollback/recovery command/result, residual risk and artifact paths; make the gate parse it.
findings.justification: Rubric criteria need observable evidence.

findings.title: S45's legacy id still selects an obsolete `Practica Terraform concepts` playground with ML cluster/Redis/Prometheus/terraform-destroy simulation.
findings.evidence: Canonical S45 comment explicitly says the old id no longer describes its topic and must not be used semantically; shared renderer still uses it as the semantic key.
findings.impact: Learners encounter stale old-topic material inside the current S45, fragmenting the mental model and leaking historical ordering.
findings.fix: Preserve id `iac` for URL/progress compatibility but map the playground by current section index/content key to an S45 async-job/storage/queue exercise.
findings.location: shared `SectionView.tsx` playground mapping for stable id `iac`
findings.justification: Stable identifiers are compatibility contracts, not content taxonomies.

findings.title: RPO is repeatedly reduced to `edad máxima del backup` and `backup_age_h <= rpo_h`.
findings.evidence: RPO is a business recovery objective describing the maximum acceptable interval since the recovery point / acceptable data loss; backup age is only one lab proxy under explicit assumptions.
findings.impact: Learners can equate a fresh backup with a satisfied RPO without verifying that it is complete, usable, replicated/retained as required, or the actual recovery point.
findings.fix: Define Recovery Point Objective (RPO) first, then state that `backup_age_h` is a deliberately simplified lab proxy when backups are complete and cadence is the only recovery-point mechanism.
findings.justification: A simplified metric must be labeled as a proxy rather than redefined as the concept.

findings.title: The solution hard-codes `len(processed_ids) == 2`, a fixture-specific magic number.
findings.evidence: The valid fixture happens to contain unique IDs `{m1,m2}`.
findings.impact: A correct generalized dedup solution can fail if the fixture grows, while a learner can memorize the expected cardinality.
findings.fix: Derive the expected count from `len(set(message_ids))` and assert set equality/terminal policy, not a literal 2.
findings.justification: Acceptance tests should encode invariants, not the current fixture size.

findings.title: The history says a small startup called Docker published Docker in 2013; Docker began as a project inside dotCloud, which later renamed itself Docker, Inc.
findings.evidence: Docker's own history describes Docker as a project in dotCloud and the later company rename.
findings.impact: A factual error appears in a section that otherwise emphasizes provenance and evidence.
findings.fix: Say Docker debuted publicly in 2013 as a project created inside dotCloud; dotCloud later renamed itself Docker, Inc.
findings.justification: Historical color is optional; if retained, it should be accurate.

findings.title: `La regla de oro es un proceso por contenedor` is presented as an absolute.
findings.evidence: Containers/Pods legitimately use multiple cooperating processes/containers in some designs; the useful principle is one primary responsibility, not a universal process count.
findings.impact: Learners can overfit a heuristic and misdiagnose legitimate sidecar/supervision designs.
findings.fix: Frame it as a beginner-friendly default: one primary responsibility/process per application container unless a design justifies otherwise.
findings.justification: Heuristics should not be promoted to invariants.

findings.title: `Si un Pod muere, K8s lo reemplaza en segundos` overpromises timing and mechanism.
findings.evidence: Kubernetes may restart a failed container or controllers may create replacement Pods; recovery can include exponential backoff, scheduling delay, image pull, readiness and node-failure delay.
findings.impact: Learners can mistake eventual controller reconciliation for a fixed recovery-time guarantee.
findings.fix: Say Kubernetes/controllers attempt to restore desired state; replacement/restart time is measured and depends on failure type, backoff, scheduling and readiness.
findings.justification: Recovery time is an SLO to measure, not a fixed property of Kubernetes.

findings.title: The claim that Docker+Kubernetes lets a small team operate with `la misma madurez operacional que una gran empresa` is unsupported promotional language.
findings.evidence: Operational maturity also depends on observability, incident response, security, staffing, governance, testing and runbooks.
findings.impact: The statement replaces a causal explanation with prestige/hype.
findings.fix: Say containers and orchestration can reduce some deployment/operations toil, while maturity still depends on controls, practices and evidence.
findings.justification: Technical teaching should not convert tool adoption into an organizational maturity claim.

findings.title: Cost/quota predicates do not reject negative usage/forecast/limits or zero/negative budgets before ratio calculations.
findings.evidence: `cost_ok` only uses `<=`; `cost_ratio` divides by `budget_pen`.
findings.impact: Impossible telemetry can pass and a zero budget can raise division by zero.
findings.fix: Validate `forecast>=0`, `budget>0`, `used>=0`, `limit>=0` before budget/quota decisions; invalid measurements route to data-quality review.
findings.justification: Operational gates need domain validation before comparisons.

findings.title: The theory says DLQ evidence should retain a safe payload, but the final starter appends the entire message object to `dlq` without redaction/minimization.
findings.evidence: `dlq.append(msg)`.
findings.impact: The pattern encourages copying full payloads—including future sensitive fields—into failure storage/logging.
findings.fix: Persist a minimized DLQ record: case/key, reason, attempts, timestamps/hash and only fields explicitly safe for replay; keep sensitive payload separately under the store's access policy.
findings.justification: Failure paths need the same minimization discipline as normal paths.

findings.title: The source has seven fallback self-check questions, duplicates DLQ/poison coverage, and under-samples consistency/RPO-RTO, ack/visibility/idempotency concurrency and IaC plan review.
findings.evidence: Q2 and Q5 both test poison→DLQ; no fallback item directly tests T1-B or T4-A.
findings.impact: Conceptual recall is uneven and does not mirror the eight-subtopic architecture.
findings.fix: Use eight balanced items (one/subtopic) for fallback self-check; reserve richer authentic evidence interpretation for the four topic evaluations and section exam.
findings.justification: Balanced sampling is especially important when the section has exactly eight declared subtopics.

findings.title: Several acronyms/ops terms arrive before a full Spanish-first introduction: RPO, RTO, IAM, IaC, ADR, SLO, stdlib, hot-path, drill, lineage; the container detour also contains grammar/orthography issues such as `un pequeño startup` and `cambiaria`.
findings.evidence: The source often gives a practical hint but not the acronym's expanded name at first meaningful use.
findings.impact: The section adds avoidable linguistic load precisely while introducing distributed-systems concepts.
findings.fix: At first use, give full name + practical meaning, then keep the short form: `Objetivo de Punto de Recuperación (RPO)`, `Objetivo de Tiempo de Recuperación (RTO)`, `Identity and Access Management (IAM)...`, `Infraestructura como Código (IaC)...`, `Registro de Decisión de Arquitectura (ADR)...`. Prefer Spanish causal prose around machine identifiers.
findings.justification: Terminology should be learned, not guessed; this follows the project's no-widow-term rule.

findings.title: The resource list mixes strong primary references with a `Python queue module` whose queue is intra-process/thread-oriented and a broad generic Coursera search, without explaining that neither is evidence for a distributed managed queue.
findings.evidence: Resource note calls Python queue `Semántica de colas didáctica` but does not explicitly state its durability/distribution limitations.
findings.impact: A beginner can incorrectly transfer `queue.Queue` guarantees to SQS-like delivery semantics.
findings.fix: Keep Python `queue` only as a clearly labeled local mechanics analogy; prioritize primary docs for managed-queue redelivery, persistent idempotency, Terraform plan sensitivity, IAM resource scoping and restore drills.
findings.justification: Resources should reinforce the actual evidence model of the section.

findings.title: The final project can appear successful while losing every supposedly durable state on process restart.
The lesson's evidence model repeatedly substitutes booleans/process-local collections for persistence, recovery, policy and IaC evidence.

findings.title: allowed lateness is incorrectly modeled as watermark-minus-event grace and propagates across theory/figure/I Do/We Do/self-check/You Do
findings.evidence: Canonical example uses window_end=120, watermark=110 and labels event_time=105 ALLOWED_LATE even though the watermark has not yet passed that window's end. Current Flink docs define allowed lateness from window end until window end + allowed lateness.
findings.impact: The core concept is wrong across explanation, diagram, worked example, exercises, fallback assessment and final project. Learners can be graded correct for a model incompatible with the reference systems the section cites.
findings.fix: Model a concrete window `[window_start, window_end)`. `ON_TIME` while watermark <= window_end; after the watermark crosses window_end, events assigned to that window are late-but-accepted until watermark > window_end + allowed_lateness; later arrivals go to side output/drop according to policy.
findings.attack: Apply the canonical numbers to event-time window lifecycle semantics in Flink/Beam-style systems.
findings.defense: The paragraph explicitly calls the model a simplification for a stdlib lab.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED P0 because the simplification changes the construct being named, not merely the implementation detail.
findings.location: T1-A theory + S46-event-time figure + I Do + We Do + selfCheck + You Do
findings.justification: A simplification may omit engine machinery, but it cannot redefine the central timing relation and then assess it as the standard concept.

findings.title: Incorrect allowed-lateness model propagates theory→figure→I Do→We Do→selfCheck→You Do.
S46 prerequisite S45 remains REPAIR_REQUIRED with P0 durability failure
findings.evidence: The authoritative roadmap declares `Prerrequisito: S45`; the completed S45 audit is 2.0/10 with P0 restart-loss of supposedly durable state.
findings.impact: S46's promise to consume S45 idempotency/state inherits a prerequisite that has not yet demonstrated durable retry semantics.
findings.fix: Keep S46 learner release blocked until S45 P0/P1 are fixed, or bind S46 labs to an independently verified synthetic S45 fixture.
findings.attack: Treat S45 as a hard evidence dependency and ask whether S46 can rely on its idempotency key/state after restart.
findings.defense: An Explorer audit may inspect downstream content provisionally even while a prerequisite is blocked.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED for learner release sequencing; it does not prevent this provisional audit.
findings.justification: A prerequisite in this roadmap is a gate, not merely a recommended reading order.

findings.title: estimatedHours 9 conflicts with roadmap provisional 16–24h without pilot evidence
findings.evidence: Canonical S46 metadata declares 9 hours; roadmap states each section initially uses 16–24 hours according to difficulty.
findings.impact: The UI/planning layer underestimates a section with 8 demos, 24 exercises, assessments and a project by roughly 44–63% versus the authoritative planning range.
findings.fix: Use a workload value consistent with current pilot evidence; absent pilot evidence, keep S46 within the roadmap's provisional 16–24h range and label it provisional.
findings.attack: Compare canonical section hours to the roadmap's explicit provisional workload policy.
findings.defense: Nine hours could be a later pilot-adjusted value.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED because no pilot evidence or superseding workload note accompanies the 9-hour value.
findings.justification: Workload metadata is part of the learner contract and should have one authority.

findings.title: `La cuarentena de S45` is a false cross-section reference and conflates DLQ with side output
findings.evidence: The audited S45 source uses DLQ for terminal failed messages and contains no `quarantine` teaching surface in the canonical section.
findings.impact: The bridge tells learners to retrieve a prior concept from a section where it is not actually introduced, creating a widow reference and conflating queue DLQ with stream side output.
findings.fix: `La DLQ de S45 es una analogía útil — un camino separado para elementos que no siguen el flujo normal — pero una DLQ de mensajería y un side output de streaming no son la misma abstracción.`
findings.attack: Search canonical S45 for quarantine and compare its failure path with S46 side-output semantics.
findings.defense: DLQ and side-output are analogous alternate paths for records that leave the happy path.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED; analogy is useful but identity claim is false.
findings.justification: The bridge should transfer the pattern without erasing domain distinctions.

findings.title: stateless max(event_time)-lag watermark can regress across successive batches
findings.evidence: Executed RED: first batch `[100,108,115]` gives 110; later batch `[90,95]` gives 90.
findings.impact: A regressing watermark can reopen already-closed event-time progress and invalidate downstream window/late-data decisions.
findings.fix: Track `max_event_time_seen = max(previous_max, *new_event_times)` and emit `max_event_time_seen - lag`; alternatively rename the helper to a one-shot fixture calculation and explicitly forbid interpreting it as stateful watermark generation.
findings.attack: Call the helper on two successive batches where the second batch contains older timestamps.
findings.defense: If `event_times` means all timestamps ever observed, `max(...)` is monotonic.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED because the function and prose call it a streaming advance operation but do not preserve max-so-far state or state that the argument is complete history.
findings.justification: Watermarks are progress signals and must not regress under the stated streaming interpretation.

findings.title: exactly-once demo uses process-local set and claims checkpoint without persistent recovery evidence
findings.evidence: Executed RED: first `e1` applies, same-process retry is skipped, but after recreating `seen=set()` the same `e1` applies again.
findings.impact: The demo demonstrates only in-process duplicate suppression, not recovery-safe end-to-end behavior.
findings.fix: Use a persistent local store/checkpoint fixture (SQLite/file) and rerun after process restart; show a replayable source position plus idempotent/transactional sink behavior.
findings.attack: Restart the process between first delivery and retry.
findings.defense: The theory correctly says exactly-once is composite and the set is a minimal conceptual fixture.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED because the output names `checkpoint` and the section is specifically about production/recovery, while the example has no persistent/recoverable state.
findings.justification: Flink's end-to-end guarantees depend on replayable/snapshotted sources and participating transactional or idempotent sinks, not an ephemeral set.

findings.title: checkpoint==2 is magic-value self-attestation rather than recoverable state evidence
findings.evidence: Exercises accept an integer 2 supplied in the fixture without binding it to source position, sink state, run, partition, checksum or restart.
findings.impact: Learners can satisfy the exactly-once gate by copying a literal while never demonstrating consistent recovery.
findings.fix: Represent checkpoint `{source_offset, sink_version, run_id}` or a persisted state file and verify that replay resumes from it without reapplying committed events.
findings.attack: Set a fabricated checkpoint value that happens to equal 2 while the sink/source states are unrelated.
findings.defense: The integer is intended as a simple modeled offset.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED; a modeled offset still needs a stated source and consistency relation.
findings.justification: The checkpoint's value is meaningful only through the state it certifies.

findings.title: DAG/asset outcome promises typed IO, ownership and invalidation but executable contract only checks topology plus a boolean
findings.evidence: Kahn correctly tests topology, but no data structure represents I/O types, owners, asset versions or the affected downstream set.
findings.impact: A learner can pass T2-A while proving only graph topology, not the operational asset contract the outcome promises.
findings.fix: Use an asset manifest with `inputs`, `outputs/schema`, `owner`; compute topological order and affected descendants/ancestors from that manifest.
findings.attack: Supply `typed_io=True` for a graph whose asset interfaces/owners are undefined.
findings.defense: Topology is the hardest algorithmic part and boolean scaffolding reduces setup.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED because the boolean self-attests the omitted construct.
findings.justification: A boolean named after missing evidence is not equivalent to that evidence.

findings.title: backfill validator accepts empty, inverted, zero-length and negative intervals
findings.evidence: Executed RED: `[]`, `[[3,1]]`, `[[1,1]]`, and `[[-5,-1]]` all return True when checkpoint equals resume.
findings.impact: Impossible or meaningless plans can be certified as safe because only pairwise overlap is checked.
findings.fix: Validate nonempty intervals, two endpoints, `start < end`, permitted time domain/type, and optionally normalize real timestamps before overlap checks.
findings.attack: Mutate interval domain while preserving non-overlap and checkpoint equality.
findings.defense: The course fixtures use small abstract numeric intervals and may assume valid interval construction upstream.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED because no such upstream precondition is declared or tested.
findings.justification: A scheduling gate must validate the objects it reasons about.

findings.title: backfill code cannot verify the live-run overlap/concurrency the prose promises
findings.evidence: No active-run registry, lock, concurrency token or current scheduled interval participates in `backfill_ok`.
findings.impact: The very concurrency failure described in the Huancayo scenario cannot be detected by the lab gate.
findings.fix: Pass/derive active runs separately, compute interval intersections, and reject or serialize according to an explicit reprocessing/concurrency policy.
findings.attack: Run a clean non-overlapping backfill list while a separate live run writes the same interval.
findings.defense: The list could conceptually include all active intervals.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED because the source never states or enforces that invariant and separately describes a live job.
findings.justification: Concurrency evidence needs an independently represented concurrent actor.

findings.title: checkpoint/resume string equality does not prove checkpoint existence, ownership or consistent state
findings.evidence: Any two fabricated equal strings pass; the code never verifies that the checkpoint exists, belongs to this run/partition, or represents consistent source/sink state.
findings.impact: Recovery can pass with a nonexistent or stale checkpoint.
findings.fix: Persist a checkpoint record with run/partition/source offset/output version and reopen it after a simulated failure before resuming.
findings.attack: Set both fields to the same arbitrary string.
findings.defense: The fixture intentionally abstracts checkpoint identity.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED because the learning outcome is `reanudar desde checkpoint consistente`, not merely compare labels.
findings.justification: Consistency is a relationship among states, not equality of names.

findings.title: missing-first E3 routing masks already-known breaches in all eight practice families
findings.evidence: Executed mutations across T1A–T4B returned uncertainty actions (`WAIT`, `CHOOSE`, `DECLARE`, `RECOVER`, `PAGE`, `TRACE`, `REVIEW`, `ACTIVATE`) even while an independent late/sink/cycle/overlap/schema/lineage/merge/SLO breach was present.
findings.impact: Deleting one evidence field can downgrade a known failure from block/containment to an uncertainty workflow.
findings.fix: Collect `breaches` from observable fields and `missing` fields separately. If any known breach exists, block/contain while retaining missing metadata; route to pure review only when no breach is known.
findings.attack: Start with an adverse fixture, remove one unrelated required field, and observe the first missing branch win.
findings.defense: The author wants to avoid making claims when the record is incomplete.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED; uncertainty and known breach are independent dimensions.
findings.location: all eight We Do E3 decision functions
findings.justification: Fail-closed means absence cannot create success or suppress a demonstrated failure.

findings.title: lineage validity is incorrectly conflated with data-quality null-rate threshold
findings.evidence: OpenLineage models run/job/dataset lineage separately from data-quality metrics/assertion facets.
findings.impact: A perfectly traceable bad-quality run is taught as if it had invalid lineage, erasing the distinction needed to debug incidents.
findings.fix: Compute `lineage_complete` and `quality_ok` separately; a high null rate should open a quality incident while preserving complete lineage to diagnose it.
findings.attack: Give a fully identified run with valid inputs/outputs/owner and null_rate=0.30.
findings.defense: The local gate is testing `lineage + quality + owner` as one readiness bundle.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED because function/text name it lineage validity and later need to distinguish `what produced it` from `was it good`.
findings.justification: Observability dimensions should compose without deleting each other's evidence.

findings.title: lineage prose promises code/version but executable record omits transformation/code revision
findings.evidence: Current facet contains run, inputs, outputs, null_rate and owner only.
findings.impact: A postmortem cannot answer which code revision or transformation definition created the bad output.
findings.fix: Add job/transform identity and immutable code revision (e.g. git SHA or version) to the local lineage event.
findings.attack: Run two code revisions with the same run/output names and ask the fixture which one produced the row.
findings.defense: The run_id could be used to look up code elsewhere.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED because no such lookup or reference is included in the evidence contract.
findings.justification: The section explicitly promises reconstructibility.

findings.title: You Do first-wins duplicate event_id can silently discard a conflicting payload
findings.evidence: `seen_ids` drops every subsequent row with the same key before merge without comparing payload/content.
findings.impact: A conflicting duplicate is misclassified as a harmless retry; potentially newer/correct data disappears without quarantine or conflict evidence.
findings.fix: If the same key repeats with identical normalized payload/hash, treat as retry; if payload differs, emit `CONFLICTING_DUPLICATE`/quarantine and retain both evidence hashes.
findings.attack: Use `e1 payload=1` followed by `e1 payload=2`.
findings.defense: The supplied fixture contains an identical retry.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED because the code teaches the generalized dedup pattern, not a fixture-only special case.
findings.justification: Idempotency keys identify a logical operation; conflicting content under one key is a data-integrity event.

findings.title: SLI/SLO/RTO validator can PASS ratios outside [0,1] and negative time values
findings.evidence: Executed RED: `sli=-0.1,slo=-0.2,rto=-10,target=-5` returns PASS; `sli=1.2,slo=1.1` also returns PASS.
findings.impact: Operational gates can certify nonsense telemetry and recovery times.
findings.fix: Validate `0 <= SLI <= 1`, `0 <= SLO <= 1`, `rto >= 0`, `target_rto >= 0`, `actions >= 0` before readiness logic; invalid telemetry gets a distinct evidence-quality state.
findings.attack: Supply ratios outside [0,1] and negative time values that still satisfy inequalities.
findings.defense: The fixtures assume prevalidated metrics.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED because no precondition or validator is declared.
findings.justification: Range validation is part of an operational contract.

findings.title: all 24 We Do exercises repeat the same predicate/tri-state/router grammar
findings.evidence: Only field names and domain predicate change.
findings.impact: Learners can memorize the exercise template and branch order instead of interpreting event traces, DAG manifests, lineage events, backfill plans or partition evidence.
findings.fix: Keep one or two tri-state classifier families, then interleave event timelines, plan/manifest review, log diagnosis, filesystem/SQLite fixtures and artifact comparisons.
findings.attack: Solve later families mechanically from the pattern without reading domain explanation.
findings.defense: Repeated structure reduces extraneous load and makes fail-closed policy salient.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED because repetition dominates all 24 exercises rather than being one scaffold among varied representations.
findings.justification: Worked-example fading should support the end target, not train a reusable answer template.

findings.title: E3 is labeled transfer but reuses the same case, fields, representation and gate names
findings.evidence: Each E3 uses `CASO-HYO-046-*` and nearly identical record schema.
findings.impact: Support is removed syntactically, but learners do not transfer the concept to a novel representation/context as required by the roadmap.
findings.fix: Change E3 representation: parse a stream trace, DAG YAML/JSON, backfill run table, OpenLineage-like event, partition manifest or incident report without supplying the final gate name.
findings.attack: Compare E2 and E3 information structures rather than just hint count.
findings.defense: The learner independently writes/repairs the final decision function.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED under the roadmap's explicit `E3 cambia el contexto y exige transferencia independiente` contract.
findings.justification: Transfer requires recognizing structure across surface change.

findings.title: multiple solutions print hard-coded tautological `meets_contract True` markers unrelated to domain evidence
findings.evidence: The same pattern recurs with `1A-1`, `1B-2`, `1B-3`, `2A-4`, etc.
findings.impact: The lesson literally prints a green `meets_contract` token that proves nothing, contradicting the course's evidence-first philosophy.
findings.fix: Remove the tautologies. If the harness needs markers, keep them outside learner-visible code/output or derive them from actual assertions/results.
findings.attack: Break the domain logic while leaving the tautological equality untouched.
findings.defense: These may be harness markers for exercise plumbing.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED learner-facing evidence theater unless hidden from output; current solution outputs explicitly include them.
findings.location: multiple We Do E2/E3 solution outputs
findings.justification: A success label must be causally tied to the property it names.

findings.title: You Do filters LATE/OUT_OF_WINDOW from accepted but creates no required side-output/quarantine artifact
findings.evidence: `accepted` includes only ON_TIME/ALLOWED_LATE; LATE/OUT_OF_WINDOW are absent from downstream data and only remain in printed labels.
findings.impact: The final project can discard late business events rather than preserving the explicit handling evidence the theory requires.
findings.fix: Create `late_events`/`side_output` and assert every input is reconciled to exactly one destination: accepted, side-output/quarantine, or explicit drop-with-reason policy.
findings.attack: Trace `e2` through the starter after it is labeled late.
findings.defense: The printed labels show it was not silently accepted, and learners could add side-output in their implementation.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED because the provided acceptance surface does not require or inspect such an artifact; a comment is not evidence.
findings.justification: No silent loss means reconciling the entire input population.

findings.title: You Do proves incremental retry only in one process; no restart/checkpoint recovery is exercised
findings.evidence: No process kill/reopen, persistent sink, checkpoint read, or recovery from stored state is required.
findings.impact: A learner can prove `second_run_changes == 0` without proving behavior after the production failure modes S46 claims to handle.
findings.fix: Persist target/checkpoint locally (SQLite/files), terminate/recreate the worker, reopen state and rerun the same interval to verify zero duplicate changes.
findings.attack: Restart between c1 and c2.
findings.defense: S46 is allowed to be local and the project demonstrates deterministic merge semantics.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED as insufficient for the stated `production-grade`, checkpoint and recovery outcomes; it does not imply cloud is required.
findings.justification: Authenticity comes from failure/recovery behavior, not vendor infrastructure.

findings.title: You Do ops_status drops the RTO/postmortem contract taught and required by objectives
findings.evidence: T4-B I Do/We Do explicitly teach SLI/SLO + RTO + actions + owner; You Do drops RTO/actions from the function contract.
findings.impact: The independent project is less demanding than guided practice and can finish without demonstrating T4-B recovery.
findings.fix: Extend ops evidence with `freshness_sli`, `freshness_slo`, `rto_minutes`, `target_rto_minutes`, `postmortem_actions`, `owner`, and derive the final operational decision from them.
findings.attack: Implement every supplied You Do function exactly to its signature and ask where measured RTO is gated.
findings.defense: Learners could document RTO in comments or README.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED because the rubric/objective says measured recovery and the executable gate does not consume it.
findings.justification: Independent assessment should integrate rather than remove the prior contract.

findings.title: You Do ends in print-only evidence with no integrated executable acceptance for normal/breach/uncertainty/restart
findings.evidence: Starter ends with `print(...)` calls; no final asserts verify reconciliation, late side-output, second-run zero, DAG/backfill, lineage completeness or operational decisions.
findings.impact: A plausible-looking output can be submitted with partially stubbed or inconsistent functions unless manual review catches every gap.
findings.fix: Provide a transparent local test harness with positive, breach, missing, restart and conflicting-duplicate cases; manual rubric remains for design/trade-offs.
findings.attack: Return hard-coded expected strings/booleans from functions and observe that the starter has no integrated oracle.
findings.defense: The project has a rubric and can be manually reviewed.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED P1 because the roadmap requires technically verified code/tests and this final independent artifact is intended to be reproducible.
findings.justification: Executable acceptance complements, rather than replaces, human assessment.

findings.title: roadmap-mandated four authentic topic evaluations are absent from canonical section surface
findings.evidence: Canonical source has theory, I Do, We Do, You Do, selfCheck and resources; no `topicEvaluations` surface is present.
findings.impact: Twenty-four practice exercises substitute for a distinct required mastery checkpoint.
findings.fix: Add T1–T4 authentic two-task evaluations scored jointly on the roadmap rubric, using new representations rather than predicate repairs.
findings.attack: Inventory section assets against the quantified roadmap blueprint.
findings.defense: Self-check/exam/project may provide other assessment.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED because the roadmap explicitly distinguishes practice from four topic evaluations.
findings.justification: Practice volume does not satisfy an independently specified assessment asset.

findings.title: fallback self-check covers only five of eight subtopics; exam route does not enforce exactly eight concepts
findings.evidence: Fallback covers event time, schema drift, SLI/SLO, watermark and DAG; it lacks direct coverage for exactly-once, backfill/checkpoint, lineage, incremental merge/recovery. Exam route groups available bank concepts and uses dynamic `N`, so route-level logic does not guarantee eight.
findings.impact: If the authenticated bank is incomplete, S46 can be assessed on fewer than eight constructs without the platform rejecting the exam configuration.
findings.fix: Require eight expected subtopic concept IDs server-side before starting S46 exam; provide balanced fallback coverage or clearly label selfCheck as non-exam practice.
findings.attack: Compare fallback items and API invariant to the exact eight-subtopic roadmap requirement.
findings.defense: A complete authenticated question bank could still contain all eight concepts.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED as a coverage/invariant gap; **absence of a complete S46 bank is not claimed**, because it was not proven.
findings.justification: The platform should enforce the blueprint rather than trust seed completeness.

findings.title: S46 learner copy blurs increment toward CP-N4-B with closure gate, which roadmap assigns to S47
findings.evidence: Roadmap labels S46 as the production-grade pipeline increment and S47 as `cierre CP-N4-B`; S46 learner copy says `El gate CP-N4-B exige...` / `Evidencia de CP-N4-B`.
findings.impact: Learners can believe the capstone is closed one section early and misread S47's role.
findings.fix: Use `incremento/evidencia S46 hacia CP-N4-B`; reserve `cierre/gate CP-N4-B` for S47.
findings.attack: Compare section copy to the roadmap's capstone table/section sequence.
findings.defense: S46 contributes required evidence toward CP-N4-B, so referencing the gate is relevant.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED wording defect, not a reason to remove the connection.
findings.justification: Progressive capstone identity must have one closure point.

findings.title: Recovery/exactly-once claims repeatedly rely on volatile or self-attested state.
Practice grammar is over-regular and E3 lacks genuine representational transfer.
Independent project drops key T1/T4 evidence: side-output handling, restart, RTO/postmortem and integrated assertions.
Missing-first E3 state machines mask already-known breaches across all eight domains.
S46 copy blurs `increment toward CP-N4-B` with closure gate, which belongs to S47.
opening `Nada falló` wrongly implies a 44-minute delay cannot be an operational/SLO failure
findings.evidence: The text attributes the delay to temporary loss of phone signal and states that nothing failed.
findings.impact: A reader can infer that delayed delivery cannot itself be an SLO breach, outage symptom or operational failure.
findings.fix: `No hace falta que exista un bug en tu código: una red intermitente puede retrasar el evento. Operacionalmente, ese retraso sí puede violar un SLO, por eso el pipeline debe modelarlo.`
findings.attack: Ask whether a 44-minute delay can violate a freshness/latency objective even if software logic is correct.
findings.defense: The author is trying to explain that out-of-order arrival is normal in distributed systems.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED as an overstatement, not as a rejection of the underlying example.
findings.justification: The repair preserves the intended mental model while separating normal disorder from service health.

findings.title: processing-time aggregates are called meaningless instead of scoped to a different question
findings.evidence: Processing-time aggregates can be meaningful for system throughput, arrival rate, congestion and latency even when wrong for event-occurrence business totals.
findings.impact: Learners may treat processing time as useless instead of understanding that it answers a different question.
findings.fix: `Agrupar por processing time responde cuándo llegó o se procesó el dato; no cuándo ocurrió el hecho. Para el total de actividad de las 10:00, usarlo atribuiría un atasco de red a esa hora.`
findings.attack: Find valid metrics whose construct is explicitly arrival/processing time.
findings.defense: The paragraph is warning against using processing time for the business question `qué ocurrió a las diez`.
findings.justification: Precision teaches selection of the right clock rather than denigrating one clock.

findings.title: DAG `única regla dura` / `nada arranca nunca` wording overcompresses definition and orchestrator behavior
findings.evidence: A DAG is directed and acyclic; real orchestrators generally reject cyclic definitions during validation rather than deadlocking a running graph.
findings.impact: The learner receives an imprecise mental model of both the abstraction and failure mode.
findings.fix: `Un DAG es dirigido y acíclico. Si introduces un ciclo, deja de existir un orden topológico; un orquestador serio debería rechazar ese grafo antes de ejecutarlo.`
findings.attack: Compare definition and typical orchestrator validation behavior.
findings.defense: The sentence is an intuition-building shorthand.
findings.justification: This keeps the intuition and makes the operational consequence accurate.

findings.title: no-overlap is presented as universal backfill rule instead of conservative lab concurrency policy
findings.evidence: Airflow supports explicit reprocessing policies for past logical dates and separate concurrency controls; intentional reruns can cover the same logical interval.
findings.impact: Learners can confuse idempotent controlled reprocessing with inherently invalid overlap.
findings.fix: `En este lab adoptamos una política conservadora: no ejecutamos dos writers concurrentes sobre el mismo intervalo. Un orquestador real puede permitir reprocessing del mismo logical date bajo una política explícita y un sink idempotente.`
findings.attack: Compare with orchestrators that explicitly permit reprocessing completed/failed logical dates.
findings.defense: Avoiding concurrent writes to the same partition is a sound beginner-safe default.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED as an overgeneralization; keep the default but label it.
findings.justification: Policy should be named as policy, not mistaken for the definition of backfill.

findings.title: exact schema equality is presented without stating the lab's strict no-unversioned-change policy
findings.evidence: Additive/compatible changes can be valid under versioned data-contract policies, but current code quarantines every difference.
findings.impact: Learners may equate all schema evolution with breakage.
findings.fix: State: `Este lab usa un contrato estricto: cualquier cambio no versionado exige revisión. En producción, políticas de compatibilidad pueden permitir ciertos cambios aditivos.`
findings.attack: Add a documented optional field that does not break the consumer.
findings.defense: Exact equality is a legitimate strict contract for this lab.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED as missing policy context, not as a demand to allow additive drift.
findings.justification: The same predicate becomes pedagogically sound once its policy scope is explicit.

findings.title: arbitrary run- prefix rejects valid UUID run IDs and local dict is ambiguously called OpenLineage-like facet
findings.evidence: Current OpenLineage docs describe globally unique run IDs, usually UUIDs (recommended UUIDv7), and facets as metadata attached to Run/Job/Dataset entities.
findings.impact: A legitimate UUID can be falsely rejected and learners may misunderstand the external specification linked in resources.
findings.fix: Validate nonempty/unique run ID without `run-` dependency, or explicitly say `run-` is a course convention. Call the dict a local lineage record unless it conforms to the OpenLineage entity/facet model.
findings.attack: Use a valid UUID run ID with complete inputs/outputs and quality.
findings.defense: `run-...` is a simple local naming convention.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED if retained as an interoperability lesson; acceptable only if explicitly labeled course-local.
findings.justification: Local conventions should not masquerade as external protocol requirements.

findings.title: small-files evidence is learner-supplied counts rather than derived from output layout
findings.evidence: No actual partition directory/manifest is inspected.
findings.impact: The exercise can pass by changing a number rather than demonstrating layout quality.
findings.fix: For E3/You Do, create a synthetic partition directory or manifest and count files programmatically.
findings.attack: Report `small_files=2` while the actual fixture directory contains dozens of files.
findings.defense: The goal is the decision rule, not filesystem tooling.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED P2; acceptable as early scaffold but weak as independent evidence.
findings.justification: The scaffold should fade from stated measurements to derived measurements.

findings.title: dense SLA/SLI/SLO/RTO/sink/checkpoint/backfill/lineage terminology violates first-use no-widow-term rule
findings.evidence: Several terms are explained later, but jobRelevance/outcomes introduce acronyms/English nouns before the learner has a practical definition.
findings.impact: The reader must hold unexplained labels while learning event-time and orchestration semantics.
findings.fix: At first use provide Spanish role + standard term: `acuerdo de nivel de servicio (SLA)`, `indicador de nivel de servicio (SLI)`, `objetivo... (SLO)`, `objetivo de tiempo de recuperación (RTO)`, `destino de escritura (sink)`, etc.; then use the short term.
findings.attack: Read S46 linearly without prior cloud/data-engineering jargon and mark terms whose practical role is not available at first meaningful use.
findings.defense: This is Level 4 and many terms are industry vocabulary.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED P2; advanced level reduces but does not remove the no-widow-term requirement.
findings.justification: The goal is to learn industry vocabulary through meaning, not inference.

findings.title: resources are broad where direct primary pages are needed for the section's high-risk constructs
findings.evidence: Flink/Beam/Airflow/OpenLineage are linked broadly while allowed lateness, fault-tolerance guarantees, backfill reprocessing and RunEvent/facet semantics are the concepts most likely to be misunderstood.
findings.impact: A learner trying to validate a disputed contract must navigate large documentation trees and may miss the authoritative page.
findings.fix: Add direct links to Flink windows/allowed lateness, Flink fault-tolerance guarantees, Airflow backfill reprocessing, OpenLineage object model/run facets and Google SRE pipeline freshness.
findings.attack: Attempt to answer S46's disputed questions from the linked landing pages alone.
findings.defense: Broad docs are durable entry points and reduce link rot.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED P2; keep broad links but supplement precise primary references.
findings.justification: Resource design should target the section's conceptual fault lines.

findings.title: CP-N4-B/CF-4 path can go green without the deployable Production Data/ML Platform and immutable integrated evidence required by the roadmap.
findings.evidence: Executed RED: `path_ok` is True using only five local predicates while no CI/CD run, orchestration artifact, registry record, serving endpoint, staging E2E, immutable review link, supply-chain evidence, or executed rollback exists. Roadmap CP-N4-B explicitly requires CI/CD, orchestration, registry, serving and rollback; CF-4 requires staging/E2E/rollback plus artifacts linked to immutable revisions.
findings.impact: The terminal Level-4-B capstone can be 'passed' by booleans and strings. This is a false credential/evidence risk, not just a missing enrichment.
findings.fix: Make CF-4 consume versioned evidence from S43-S46 (commit/artifact digests, workflow run, orchestration/backfill evidence, staging endpoint, registry version/alias, E2E result, rollback drill) and compute the gate from those immutable artifacts.
findings.attack: Delete every real deployment artifact and run only the supplied You Do starter. `normal_ok` still becomes True.
findings.defense: S47 is designed to integrate previous sections rather than reimplement S43-S46.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING P0 because the project neither consumes immutable evidence from prior capstones nor verifies the missing integration; it simply self-attests the closure.
findings.justification: A capstone closure must verify the integrated system promised by the roadmap; flags are not execution evidence.

findings.title: CF-4/CP-N4-B closure is computed from toy predicates rather than integrated immutable platform evidence.
S47 requires S46, but S46 remains REPAIR_REQUIRED with a P0 known defect.
findings.evidence: Roadmap: `Prerrequisito: S46`. The immediately preceding Explorer audit recorded S46 as FAIL/REPAIR_REQUIRED with a P0 event-time/allowed-lateness defect.
findings.impact: A learner can reach the CP-N4-B closure while its production-data prerequisite has not passed its own release gate.
findings.fix: Keep S47 learner release/capstone closure blocked until S46's P0/P1 are repaired and revalidated, or explicitly mark S47 as provisional and bind it to independently verified synthetic prerequisite artifacts.
findings.attack: Apply the roadmap's explicit rule that S(n+1) does not release before S(n) retrospective and known P0/P1 are closed.
findings.defense: Explorer may audit downstream content provisionally to expose future defects.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING for release sequencing; provisional analysis may continue.
findings.justification: A roadmap prerequisite is an evidence dependency, not merely a reading suggestion.

findings.title: Canonical estimatedHours is 9 while live public card declares 20h.
findings.evidence: `s47-opensource.ts` metadata: 9. Live GitHub Pages card: `20h·Producción gobernada`.
findings.impact: Learners and planners receive two incompatible workload contracts for the same section; the 9-hour value also sits below the roadmap's provisional planning range.
findings.fix: Use one evidenced workload value. Until pilot data supersedes the roadmap, expose the same provisional estimate in source and public UI and label it provisional.
findings.attack: Compare canonical source metadata, public rendered card, and roadmap planning policy.
findings.defense: The 9-hour value might be a later local estimate.
