findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING because no pilot note or source-of-truth override explains the divergence.
findings.location: section metadata vs live public card
findings.justification: Workload is learner-facing planning metadata and needs one authority.

findings.title: S47 restarts provenance as loose strings instead of carrying S44 supply-chain and S46 production-data/lineage artifacts forward.
findings.evidence: S47 uses values such as `ds-v3`, `git:abc`, `lock:def`, `sha256:model`, `features-v3`; no path/hash/revision points to prior capstone outputs.
findings.impact: The learner can construct a visually plausible MLOps chain that is disconnected from the actual service/data pipeline it is supposed to productionize.
findings.fix: Import a compact manifest from S44/S46 containing immutable artifact hash, dataset digest/schema, feature pipeline revision and prior test status; refuse promotion when those references are absent.
findings.attack: Ask which S44 artifact digest and which S46 dataset/lineage record produced the S47 candidate; the starter has no answer.
findings.defense: Short strings keep the lab local and cognitively manageable.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING; locality is fine, but local files/digests can preserve real cross-section identity.
findings.justification: Graph continuity requires edges between capstones, not just similar vocabulary.

findings.title: Run reproducibility is reduced to aggregate metric repeatability plus seed/params, omitting required artifact/dataset/code/environment evidence.
findings.evidence: `reproducible(metric, rerun, tolerance, seed, params)` has no dataset digest, code revision, environment lock, split, artifact/prediction comparison or run ID.
findings.impact: Two materially different runs can return the same F1 and be certified reproducible.
findings.fix: Name the small predicate `metric_repeatable`; make the run-level gate combine dataset digest, code revision, environment lock, split, parameters/seed, artifact identity and rerun outputs/metric tolerance.
findings.attack: Change data/code/environment while preserving aggregate metric within tolerance; the predicate cannot detect the change.
findings.defense: T1-B adds lineage and T1-A intentionally isolates one component.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING because T1-A labels the result 'reproducible run' and the learning outcome explicitly includes omitted evidence.
findings.justification: Component isolation is pedagogically valid only when its narrower claim is named accurately.

findings.title: Baseline is only a float, so candidate/baseline data/code/env/split/metric comparability cannot be verified.
findings.evidence: `comparable(run, baseline: float)` validates lineage only for the candidate and then checks `run['score'] > baseline`.
findings.impact: A score from a different dataset, split, metric or environment can be used as the baseline and the comparison still passes.
findings.fix: Represent baseline and candidate as two run manifests and require equality of dataset digest, split ID, metric definition/version, relevant environment and evaluation protocol before comparing scores.
findings.attack: Executed RED: candidate with `ds-v4/env-new/holdout-B/f1-new` compared to bare baseline `0.78` returns True.
findings.defense: The baseline scalar may be assumed to have come from the same locked evaluation table.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING because that assumption is neither represented nor checked.
findings.justification: Honest comparison is a relation between two evidenced runs.

findings.title: The priority ranker is promoted using F1 without defining a binary classification construct/threshold that justifies F1 for the ordering objective.
findings.evidence: Narrative: ranker outputs `priority:float`; examples use `f1-v2`. Scikit-learn documents F1 as a classification precision/recall metric, while NDCG/DCG are ranking metrics.
findings.impact: The promotion metric may reward a different task from the user-facing ordering objective.
findings.fix: Either define the ranker as a binary relevance classifier with threshold/label and justify F1, or evaluate the ordering with an explicit ranking metric such as NDCG@k/precision@k aligned to review capacity.
findings.attack: Ask what true-positive/false-positive decision F1 represents for a continuous priority ordering; source does not define it.
findings.defense: A ranking product can be implemented by a classifier and sorted by positive-class probability.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING as under-specified construct, not a categorical claim that F1 is always wrong.
findings.justification: A metric is valid only relative to the decision construct.

findings.title: T1-A/T1-B/T2-A figures are misaligned with their instructional moment; T1-B alt text describes data/code/env that the actual figure does not draw.
findings.evidence: T1-A uses `S47-registry-promotion` while teaching metric reproducibility. T1-B alt says data/code/env accompany the flow, but the actual figure only contains experiment→registry→shadow→canary. T2-A uses `S47-shadow-vs-canary` while teaching signatures/approvals, anticipating T4 terminology.
findings.impact: Visuals add future-stage vocabulary instead of offloading the current construct, increasing extraneous load and giving screen-reader users a false description of the figure.
findings.fix: T1-A: run/re-run evidence diagram. T1-B: candidate/baseline manifests with identical lineage keys. T2-A: signature+approval promotion gate. Move shadow/canary visual to T4-A. Make alt text describe exactly what is drawn.
findings.attack: Compare each figure's nodes/branches with its subtopic outcome.
findings.defense: The figures show the larger lifecycle to maintain context.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING because three consecutive placements sacrifice local explanatory alignment.
findings.justification: A teaching diagram should reduce representation burden for the current idea.

findings.title: approved=True is treated as approval evidence without reviewer, timestamp, review reference or candidate binding.
findings.evidence: `can_promote(stage, approved, inp, out)` receives one boolean. CF-4 requires artifacts linked to immutable revisions/reviews.
findings.impact: Any caller can flip a flag and authorize a different model than the one reviewed.
findings.fix: Use an approval record `{reviewer, reviewed_model_digest, signature_digest, commit_sha, decision, timestamp/review_id}` and verify all bindings before promotion.
findings.attack: Set `approved=True` for an arbitrary candidate; RED passes.
findings.defense: The boolean is a didactic representation of an external approval workflow.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING because the section's capstone claim is auditability.
findings.justification: Approval is a signed/bound event, not a free boolean property.

findings.title: Promotion is a stage-string predicate rather than a versioned governed registry transition with auditable state.
findings.evidence: Current MLflow favors model aliases/tags and separate environments; the predicate only returns True/False.
findings.impact: Learners can pass 'promotion' without creating a versioned registry state that serving or rollback can reference.
findings.fix: In a local registry manifest or MLflow-local setup, register a version, record validation tag/approval, then assign a `challenger`/`champion` alias or environment promotion record; retain old version for rollback.
findings.attack: Run `can_promote` with valid fields and observe no registry/version/alias state change exists.
findings.defense: The source explicitly says staging is a didactic equivalent and acknowledges MLflow stages are deprecated.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING on missing operation/evidence; `uses staging` itself is NOT a finding.
findings.justification: MLOps lifecycle is about controlled state transitions, not only precondition predicates.

findings.title: Any string starting sha256: passes as a digest.
findings.evidence: Executed RED: `sha256:`, `sha256:model`, and `sha256:xyz` all pass `artifact_ok` with otherwise valid fields.
findings.impact: The integrity gate can certify an artifact that has no cryptographic digest.
findings.fix: Require exactly 64 hexadecimal SHA-256 characters after the prefix and, for stronger evidence, recompute the digest from a local artifact and compare.
findings.attack: Use malformed digest prefixes.
findings.defense: The example is meant to teach versioned artifact naming.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING because the text explicitly calls it a digest/integrity gate.
findings.justification: A checksum is evidence only if it is syntactically and causally bound to bytes.

findings.title: Four section-name tokens are treated as a complete model card.
findings.evidence: `REQUIRED <= card` can pass `{'use','limits','metrics','risks'}` with no content, model version, dataset, metric values, intended users or limitations.
findings.impact: Governance documentation becomes a checkbox vocabulary exercise.
findings.fix: Create a versioned Markdown/JSON model card with required non-empty fields and bind its digest/model version; manual rubric reviews content quality while code checks presence/binding.
findings.attack: Supply the four strings with empty/no actual document.
findings.defense: The lab checks structure before prose quality.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING because the final gate claims `model card completa` and the card is never bound to an artifact or reviewed.
findings.justification: A label that a section exists is not the section.

findings.title: Train/serve feature compatibility is reduced to equality of caller-supplied version strings.
findings.evidence: `train_fv == serve_fv` does not inspect schema, transformation code, point-in-time logic or feature definitions.
findings.impact: Two different feature pipelines can both call themselves `features-v3` and pass.
findings.fix: Bind feature version to a manifest/digest containing schema + transformation revision + source/point-in-time contract, and test batch/online outputs from the same definitions.
findings.attack: Use identical label on different transformation implementations.
findings.defense: Version equality is a common first gate.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING because the course calls it verified compatibility.
findings.justification: Version names are references; evidence lives in what they reference.

findings.title: Feature consistency uses one vector equality plus self-attested leakage=False and contract_tests>=3 rather than executed tests.
findings.evidence: No test functions are executed and no historical point-in-time retrieval or shared transformation is represented.
findings.impact: A learner can set `contract_tests=3` without any tests and pass skew/leakage gates.
findings.fix: Run named contract tests over multiple fixtures (including point-in-time/leakage cases), store results, and compare batch/online feature manifests/outputs rather than a count.
findings.attack: Executed RED: identical lists + `False` + integer 3 returns True with no tests present.
findings.defense: The count is intended to summarize a prior test suite.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING because the evidence is not linked to a test result.
findings.justification: Feast-style consistency depends on point-in-time-correct retrieval and reusable feature definitions, not a test-count flag.

findings.title: p95 and fallback testing are caller-supplied values/booleans rather than measured evidence.
findings.evidence: `slo_ok(p95_ms, slo_ms, batch, fallback, tested)` never receives latency samples or a fallback drill result.
findings.impact: Production latency and resilience can be passed by typing the expected numbers.
findings.fix: Generate a local latency sample set, compute p95, execute fallback under forced primary failure, and store the result/command.
findings.attack: Set `p95_ms=120, tested=True` without running any requests/fallback.
findings.defense: The lab focuses on decision logic after measurement.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING because You Do/CF-4 claims measured operational evidence, not just a policy evaluator.
findings.justification: Operational SLO evidence must be measured.

findings.title: Impossible/type-confused latency and batch inputs can pass.
findings.evidence: Executed RED: `p95=-100, slo=-50` passes; `batch=True` passes because Python bool is int 1; fallback `rules-` with no version passes.
findings.impact: The SLO gate can certify nonsensical telemetry/configuration.
findings.fix: Require finite nonnegative p95/SLO, integer-not-bool batch, `batch>=1`, and a nonempty typed fallback version; invalid evidence receives a distinct error.
findings.attack: Mutate numeric domains/types while preserving inequalities.
findings.defense: Inputs may be assumed validated upstream.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING because no upstream validator/precondition is declared.
findings.justification: A production gate validates the measurements it consumes.

findings.title: Canary validation accepts impossible negative metrics and a zero-exposure canary.
findings.evidence: Executed RED: canary with `traffic_pct=-5` and `error_rate=-0.2` returns True; canary with 0% traffic returns True.
findings.impact: The rollout gate can report success when no real canary exposure occurred or telemetry is impossible.
findings.fix: Validate 0≤rates≤1 (or documented percent units), positive canary exposure when mode=canary, explicit shadow sampling semantics, and nonnegative budgets.
findings.attack: Supply negative/zero domains.
findings.defense: Fixtures use valid positive values.
findings.justification: A gate should reject malformed rollout evidence before comparing budgets.

findings.title: Canary quality/error/hooks are not bound to metric definition, control, window, sample size or actual hook output.
findings.evidence: The function accepts scalar `quality_delta`, scalar `error_rate` and boolean `hooks`.
findings.impact: A canary can pass with statistically meaningless or fabricated monitoring evidence.
findings.fix: Record metric ID, control/candidate values, n/window, error counts and named monitoring checks; compute deltas/rates from those records.
findings.attack: Provide arbitrary deltas/`hooks=True` without a control population or logged samples.
findings.defense: The section intentionally avoids a statistics deep dive.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING; basic provenance/window/sample count can be required without advanced inference.
findings.justification: A monitoring hook is observable output, not an adjective.

findings.title: Rollback readiness is self-attested; last_good need not exist/load/be healthy.
findings.evidence: Executed RED: `last_good=''` passes when other booleans/set are truthy because the only identity test is `current != last_good`.
findings.impact: The course can certify a rollback target that is nonexistent or unservable.
findings.fix: Resolve last-good to an immutable registry artifact, load/smoke-test it in staging, execute rollback, measure recovery, and retain before/after serving version evidence.
findings.attack: Use empty last-good string and `tested=True`.
findings.defense: The strings model registry versions at a high level.
findings.justification: Rollback is an executed recovery path.

findings.title: CF-4 audit trail is reduced to audit_entry=True.
findings.evidence: `audit_entry=True` passes; no reviewer, responsible owner, revision, date, artifact hashes, commands, results or issue links are represented.
findings.impact: The capstone can claim auditability while preserving no auditable record.
findings.fix: Write an append-only audit entry containing version/revision, timestamp, owner, reviewer, model/artifact/dataset digests, command/workflow run IDs, results and linked issues/review.
findings.attack: Set True with no record.
findings.defense: The boolean stands for an external record.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING because the roadmap explicitly enumerates checkpoint evidence fields.
findings.justification: Auditability requires retrievable facts.

findings.title: Missing-first E3 routing masks already-known breaches in all eight subtopic families.
findings.evidence: Executed RED on all 8 families: adverse+missing returns INVESTIGATE/RESTORE/REQUEST/COMPLETE/TRACE/TUNE/COLLECT/REVIEW instead of preserving the already-observable breach.
findings.impact: Removing one field can downgrade a confirmed unsafe state to an uncertainty workflow.
findings.fix: Compute observable breaches and missing fields independently; if any breach is known, block/contain and attach missing evidence as secondary metadata. Use pure uncertainty route only when no breach is known.
findings.attack: Start from each invalid fixture, remove an unrelated required field and execute E3.
findings.defense: Missing data should not be guessed.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING; missingness and known breach are orthogonal.
findings.location: all eight We Do E3 decision functions
findings.justification: Fail-closed does not mean 'forget what you already know when something else is missing.'

findings.title: All 24 We Do exercises reuse almost the same predicate/valid-invalid-missing/router grammar.
findings.evidence: Surface fields change, but E1/E2/E3 structure and branch vocabulary remain nearly invariant.
findings.impact: A learner can solve by template recognition rather than reading experiment manifests, registry artifacts, latency traces, rollout records or audit logs.
findings.fix: Keep a few predicate exercises, then interleave manifest diffing, run-table comparison, model-card review, load-test output, rollout timeline, registry/audit JSON and rollback drill analysis.
findings.attack: Solve a later family using only the repeated code skeleton.
findings.defense: Consistent structure lowers extraneous cognitive load.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING because uniformity dominates all 24 exercises instead of supporting varied authentic representations.
findings.justification: Repeated syntax should scaffold the domain, not become the domain.

findings.title: E3 does not genuinely change context/representation for independent transfer.
findings.evidence: Roadmap requires E3 to change context and demand independent transfer; S47 mostly changes the amount of scaffolding, not representation/context.
findings.impact: Learners practice completion rather than recognition of MLOps invariants in novel evidence.
findings.fix: Make E3 inspect a different artifact type/context: MLflow-like run JSON, GitHub workflow result, registry manifest, latency CSV, canary log, rollback audit record, etc., without supplying the final predicate.
findings.attack: Compare E2 and E3 input representations family by family.
findings.defense: E3 removes some direct guidance and asks for final routing.
findings.justification: Transfer requires stable deep structure beneath changed surface form.

findings.title: You Do drops substantial T1-B/T2-B/T3-B/T4-A contracts from the mandatory path.
findings.evidence: Normal `path_ok` has run/promote/parity/canary/rollback only. It omits T1-B baseline-lineage comparability, T2-B actual digest/card compatibility, T3-B measured latency/batching/fallback, and T4-A quality delta/control evidence; promotion receives a precomputed `signature_ok` boolean.
findings.impact: Independent assessment is materially easier and less complete than guided practice.
findings.fix: Make the final gate explicitly consume all eight subtopic artifacts or a smaller set of integrated artifacts that demonstrably subsume them.
findings.attack: Implement only the provided five functions; `path_ok=True` without satisfying several subtopic outcomes.
findings.defense: The starter invites the learner to add more breaches and documentation.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING because the mandatory path itself is the capstone closure.
findings.justification: You Do should integrate the whole section, not remove its hardest evidence.

findings.title: You Do compound breach masks rollback failure whenever canary also fails.
findings.evidence: Executed RED/current fixture: both `breach['canary']` and `breach['rollback']` are False, but action is only `STOP_CANARY` because of `if not canary else rollback`.
findings.impact: The learner sees one action while the last-known-good path is itself unready; the most dangerous recovery defect disappears.
findings.fix: Return a set/list of violations and an ordered runbook, e.g. STOP_CANARY then `ROLLBACK_BLOCKED`/repair last-good evidence; never collapse one failed gate into another.
findings.attack: Execute the supplied breach fixture.
findings.defense: Stopping the canary is the first operational action.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING; sequencing the first action is fine, but the second failure must remain visible/blocking.
findings.justification: Incident prioritization must preserve all critical evidence.

findings.title: Required commands, pinned dependencies and expected output are not part of executable acceptance.
findings.evidence: `path_ok` ignores command/script paths, dependency lock, environment recreation and expected-output comparison.
findings.impact: A submission can pass its supplied gate without being reproducible on another machine.
findings.fix: Require manifest fields/paths for install command, lock digest, test command, serving command and expected/observed output; execute them in a clean local environment or CI.
findings.attack: Omit lockfile/commands entirely and run starter; normal_ok remains True.
findings.defense: A human reviewer can inspect the portfolio.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING because CF-4/roadmap also requires technically verified, reproducible evidence.
findings.location: You Do requirements vs executable acceptance
findings.justification: A rubric can judge quality; a harness should verify existence/execution.

findings.title: 15% security/privacy/least-privilege rubric criterion has no bound project evidence.
findings.evidence: The artifact is synthetic/no PII, but no access-control or credential surface is part of `path_ok` or required evidence.
findings.impact: A learner can receive/lose 15% on a construct not operationalized by the task.
findings.fix: Either explicitly import S42-S44 permission/supply-chain evidence into CF-4, or remove/replace this rubric row with a construct the S47 artifact actually demonstrates.
findings.attack: Try to score least privilege from the supplied starter alone.
findings.defense: Security evidence could be inherited from S42-S44.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING because inherited evidence is not referenced or bound.
findings.justification: Assessment criteria must have observable evidence.

findings.title: Four roadmap-mandated authentic topic evaluations are absent.
findings.evidence: Source contains theory, I Do, 24 We Do exercises, You Do, selfCheck and resources but no four integrated T1–T4 evaluation artifacts.
findings.impact: Practice is being used as a substitute for required independent mastery checkpoints.
findings.fix: Add four integrated two-task evaluations, one per topic pair, with the roadmap 0–3 rubric and critical tests, using novel artifacts rather than predicate repair.
findings.attack: Inventory canonical assets against the quantified roadmap blueprint.
findings.defense: The project and self-check add assessment.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING because roadmap explicitly distinguishes topic evaluations from practice/project/exam.
findings.justification: Assessment architecture is part of the curriculum contract.

findings.title: Eight fallback questions do not map one-per-subtopic; T1-B and T3-B are not directly assessed.
findings.evidence: Question map: T1-A, T4-B, CP gate, responsible synthetic scope, T2-A, T3-A, T4-A, T2-B.
findings.impact: The section can report an eight-item self-check while omitting two technical outcomes.
findings.fix: Provide exactly one core item per subtopic for the fallback/exam blueprint; move CP/scope questions to an additional unscored or topic-evaluation layer.
findings.attack: Map each item to S47-T1-A…T4-B.
findings.defense: The integrative CP and responsible-use questions are valuable.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING; keep them elsewhere but restore exact subtopic coverage for the section exam/fallback.
findings.justification: The roadmap requires one displayed exam item from each subtopic.

findings.title: Legacy id opensource selects obsolete learner-facing packaging/CI playground content.
findings.evidence: Exact leaked UI: title `Practica empaquetado y CI`; code begins `# Simulacion de conceptos de open source` and builds a `pyproject.toml` object.
findings.impact: A learner in S47 MLOps receives an unrelated old lesson because compatibility identity is used as semantic identity.
findings.fix: Use an explicit semantic `playgroundId`/section-index mapping or section-owned playground content. Keep `id='opensource'` solely for URL/progress compatibility.
findings.attack: Trace `section.id='opensource'` into shared CodePlayground mapping.
findings.defense: The id cannot be renamed without breaking progress.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING; preserve the id, remove its semantic authority.
findings.justification: Stable compatibility keys must never decide current lesson meaning.

findings.title: Repeated self-attestation replaces execution evidence across run, comparison, approval, digest, tests, SLO, hooks and rollback.
Repeated exercise/state-machine grammar masks breaches and underdelivers transfer.
Semantic mapping/visual alignment defects reintroduce future or obsolete content through legacy/misplaced representations.
Assessment blueprint is incomplete despite high practice volume.
Invalid reproducibility inputs are conflated with genuine nonreproducibility.
findings.evidence: Negative tolerance and NaN metric return False but are not classified as invalid telemetry/policy.
findings.impact: Learners cannot tell whether the model genuinely failed reproducibility or the gate itself received nonsensical inputs.
findings.fix: Validate finite metrics and `tolerance >= 0` first; return/raise `INVALID_REPRO_EVIDENCE` separately from `MARK_RUN_NONREPRODUCIBLE`.
findings.attack: Use tolerance=-0.01 or metric=NaN.
findings.defense: The function fails closed.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING P2: safety direction is correct, diagnosis is not.
findings.justification: Evidence quality and model behavior are distinct failure causes.

findings.title: Mutable lineage is blocked through literal sentinel words instead of requiring immutable identifiers.
findings.evidence: Executed RED: `code='main'` passes although it is another mutable ref; arbitrary unversioned labels can pass for data/env/split/metric.
findings.impact: Learners may learn blacklist-style provenance instead of immutable lineage.
findings.fix: Validate identifier form/provenance: commit SHA, dataset digest/version, lockfile hash/image digest, named immutable split and metric definition version.
findings.attack: Replace `latest` with `main` or `current`.
findings.defense: The fixture is a minimal anti-pattern detector.
findings.justification: Versioning is a positive invariant, not a list of forbidden words.

findings.title: Theory misdefines a model registry as an 'archivo'.
findings.evidence: Current MLflow describes Model Registry as a centralized model store plus APIs/UI with lineage, versioning, aliases and metadata.
findings.impact: The learner may confuse a model artifact file with the lifecycle registry that references/manages it.
findings.fix: `Un model registry es un catálogo/servicio que registra versiones del modelo y apunta a sus artefactos, runs, firmas, aliases/tags y metadatos de gobernanza; el archivo del modelo es solo uno de esos artefactos.`
findings.attack: Compare the definition against MLflow's current registry model.
findings.defense: `archivo` may have been intended metaphorically as an archive.
findings.justification: Artifact store and registry are different components.

findings.title: Prose permits rules or a previous model fallback while code accepts only rules-* names.
findings.evidence: Executed RED: `model-1.1.0` is rejected even when tested and latency/batch are valid.
findings.impact: The executable contract contradicts the stated design space and teaches a needless implementation-specific naming rule.
findings.fix: Represent fallback `{kind: 'rules'|'model', version, tested_result}` and validate an allowed kind plus immutable version/evidence.
findings.attack: Use the prose-authorized previous-model fallback.
findings.defense: Rules are simpler and safer for the local example.
findings.justification: If a design option is taught, the gate should not silently forbid it.

findings.title: The 1-64 batch limit is a magic capacity policy without profile evidence.
findings.evidence: The prose says batching/capacity should be budgeted, but no benchmark explains why 64 is safe for this model/environment.
findings.impact: Learners may treat a magic batch limit as transferable capacity engineering.
findings.fix: Name it `MAX_BATCH_SIZE` from a measured local profile/config and show how the value was obtained; do not imply 64 is a general MLOps limit.
findings.attack: Move the same model to different hardware/model size; safe batch can change materially.
findings.defense: A course-local cap is a reasonable fixture policy.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING P2 because the policy is not labeled/derived as course-local.
findings.justification: Capacity thresholds are environment-specific.

findings.title: One traffic_pct conflates mirrored shadow traffic with user-visible response exposure.
findings.evidence: `mode='shadow', traffic_pct=10` passes, while the `S47-shadow-vs-canary` figure describes shadow as 0% of traffic seeing the output.
findings.impact: Learners cannot distinguish request sampling from user-impact exposure.
findings.fix: Use `mirrored_request_pct` for shadow and `served_response_pct` for canary; assert served output is 0 in shadow.
findings.attack: Ask what 10% means for shadow: 10% copied requests or 10% served outputs; source cannot express both.
findings.defense: The field may mean workload sent to the candidate, not impact.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING as semantic ambiguity, not a claim that shadow cannot mirror nonzero traffic.
findings.justification: Shadow and canary differ primarily in whether candidate output affects users.

findings.title: Rollback safety is coupled to a nonempty retired set and exercises hard-code version 1.0.0.
findings.evidence: E1/E2/E3 require `'1.0.0' in retired`; any arbitrary truthy retirement can satisfy the base helper.
findings.impact: A safe rollback can be marked failed because no older version needs retirement, while fixture memorization replaces a lifecycle invariant.
findings.fix: Evaluate rollback readiness and retirement policy as separate checks; when retirement is required, bind each retired version to lifecycle state/reason/audit record, not one literal.
findings.attack: Use a valid current/last-good pair with no obsolete version to retire; or retire an unrelated string.
findings.defense: The subtopic intentionally combines rollback and retirement.
findings.justification: Related lifecycle controls should compose without becoming arbitrary prerequisites.

findings.title: Residual risk is a hard-coded narrative instead of derived evidence.
findings.evidence: `residual_risk = 'canary_budget y skew residual; retiro 1.0.0 auditado; sin PII'` prints regardless of actual artifacts.
findings.impact: Learners can learn that risk statements are decorative prose attached after PASS.
findings.fix: Generate a risk register from unresolved test findings/assumptions and require each entry to cite evidence, owner and mitigation; prose summary is written from that register.
findings.attack: Change gate evidence; residual risk text stays identical.
findings.defense: It is an example sentence for the learner to revise.
findings.justification: Risk communication should be traceable to known residual uncertainty.

findings.title: Dense mixed-language jargon and accessibility/redaction defects remain.
findings.evidence: Examples include `experiment run`, `params`, `registry`, `model card`, `serving`, `shadow`, `canary`, `rollback`, `retirement`, `last-known-good`, `audit_entry`; an alt string writes `codigo`, `acompanando`, and another `saturacion` without accents. Several terms appear in outcomes before a usable first definition.
findings.impact: The learner must infer vocabulary while also learning governance and rollout semantics; screen-reader text is lower-quality than visible prose.
findings.fix: At first meaningful use: `corrida de experimento (run)`, `registro de modelos (model registry)`, `despliegue en sombra (shadow)`, `despliegue canario (canary)`, `reversión (rollback)`, etc.; normalize accents and alt text.
findings.attack: Read outcomes/job relevance before theory and list terms without an immediately usable role definition.
findings.defense: Level 4 intentionally exposes standard industry vocabulary.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING P2; industry terms should remain, but be introduced through Spanish meaning.
findings.justification: Advanced vocabulary is learned better when anchored to function, not translated away or left unexplained.

findings.title: Resources rely too heavily on broad landing pages instead of direct primary references for high-risk contracts.
findings.evidence: Examples: top-level MLflow, KServe home, Feast GitHub repository and generic Coursera MLOps search; direct pages for model-registry aliases, dataset tracking, signatures, point-in-time joins, canary rollout and reproducible randomness are absent.
findings.impact: Learners must search large docs trees precisely where the lesson's simplifications need authoritative verification.
findings.fix: Keep broad docs but add direct primary links: MLflow Tracking/Datasets/Registry/Signatures, Feast point-in-time joins, KServe canary rollout, scikit-learn reproducibility and Google SRE canarying/release engineering.
findings.attack: Try to validate S47's exact promotion/parity/canary claims from the linked landing pages.
findings.defense: Broad landing pages are stable and useful for exploration.
findings.justification: Resource curation should resolve the conceptual fault lines of the lesson.

findings.title: Core grounded/cited gate does not verify that cited text actually supports the claim.
findings.evidence: T3-B checks `claims <= cited_claims`; T4-A checks nonempty allowed evidence IDs and an injection flag. Neither function receives the cited text/claim-support relation. RED: claim 'El SLA es 48 horas' + allowed id `d1#sla` passes even if that fragment says something else.
findings.impact: The section's defining gate can answer an unsupported material claim while reporting PASS/grounded.
findings.fix: Represent claim-level attribution `{claim_id, claim_text, evidence_ids}`; resolve each ID to authorized active text/version and run a deterministic fact check/evaluator or labeled support fixture. Only emit a material claim when every claim-support edge passes.
findings.attack: Keep an allowed evidence ID but change claim text to a contradiction/fabrication; both metadata gates still pass.
findings.defense: T4-A prose correctly admits response-level evidence IDs are only a cheap first schema check.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING P0 because the final/section-level evidence language still treats this metadata gate as support.
findings.justification: Modern RAG evaluation distinguishes retrieval, groundedness and response completeness; citation presence is not semantic entailment.

findings.title: You Do can become READY by flipping four booleans while retrieve() and answer() remain NotImplemented stubs.
findings.evidence: Starter defines both core functions as `raise NotImplementedError`; `readiness()` only checks whether four names map to True. RED: `{name: True for name in REQUIRED}` returns `('READY', [])` without invoking either function.
findings.impact: The independent RAG project can claim successful completion with no RAG system at all.
findings.fix: Make readiness consume executed evidence receipts: ingestion manifest/hash tests, ACL/deletion retrieval tests, versioned qrel retrieval eval, claim-level attribution eval, injection test, cost record and abstention tests. READY derives from receipts, not learner-controlled booleans.
findings.attack: Leave `retrieve` and `answer` unchanged; set all evidence flags True.
findings.defense: Portfolio note explicitly tells learners not to flip flags and to link real artifacts.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING P0: prose admonition does not enforce the gate.
findings.justification: Solarize/Harness rules explicitly reject stubs and booleans as execution evidence.

findings.title: All 24 authenticated S48 exam variants use correctIndex 1 (option B), so all-B answers yield 100%.
findings.evidence: S48 bank has 8 concepts × 3 variants and every shown seed item has `correctIndex: 1`. `/api/exam/start` selects one random variant per concept; scoring passes at >=70%. Therefore choosing index 1 for all 8 yields 8/8=100%.
findings.impact: The formal mastery gate is completely gameable; section progression/credential evidence can be achieved without demonstrating knowledge.
findings.fix: Rebalance correct-option positions across all 24 variants (e.g. 6/6/6/6), add a CI invariant preventing pathological key distributions, and revalidate every answer/explanation after permutation.
findings.attack: Answer B to every selected S48 question.
findings.defense: Variants are randomized and question order is shuffled.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING P0 because randomizing questions does not randomize the answer key.
findings.justification: Assessment security fails when answer position alone predicts the key.

findings.title: S48 requires S47, but S47 remains REPAIR_REQUIRED with a P0.
findings.evidence: Authoritative roadmap says `Prerrequisito: S47`; the current project conversation contains the complete S47 JSON/report with FAIL/REPAIR_REQUIRED and a P0.
findings.impact: Learners can enter the RAG/CP-N4-C path without the production MLOps prerequisite having passed its release gate.
findings.fix: Keep S48 learner release blocked until S47 P0/P1 are repaired and revalidated, or label S48 explicitly provisional and feed it independently verified prerequisite fixtures.
findings.attack: Apply the roadmap rule that a later section is not learner-released while the prerequisite still has known P0/P1 defects.
findings.defense: Explorer analysis can continue provisionally to find downstream defects.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING for release sequencing; provisional audit is still valid.
findings.justification: Prerequisites are evidence gates, not merely suggested reading order.

findings.title: Canonical estimatedHours is 9 while the live card shows 20h.
findings.evidence: `s48-ai-governance.ts` declares 9 hours; current public course card for Section 48 shows 20h.
findings.impact: Learners get incompatible planning metadata, and the source value also undercuts the roadmap's provisional 16–24h planning range without pilot evidence.
findings.fix: Expose one evidenced provisional workload consistently. If 20h is current policy, update canonical metadata; if empirical pilot data changes it, document that evidence.
findings.attack: Compare canonical source metadata, live public card and roadmap provisional planning policy.
findings.defense: The 9h field might be a later local estimate.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING because there is no pilot note/source-of-truth override explaining the divergence.
findings.location: section metadata vs public live card
findings.justification: Workload is a learner-facing contract and requires one authority.

findings.title: The section promises every assertion is supported, while executable gates never test semantic support between claim text and source text.
findings.evidence: Job relevance promises claim support; opening callout says unsupported claims do not answer. T3-B/T4-A only check membership of labels/evidence IDs and booleans.
findings.impact: The prose tells learners a central safety property has been achieved when the mechanism can false-pass unsupported content.
findings.fix: State that early predicates validate citation presence/authorization only. Reserve 'supported/grounded' for a later claim-level entailment or evaluator check that receives the actual claim and cited text.
findings.attack: Supply a false claim plus an allowed evidence ID; current gate still passes.
findings.defense: Later text explicitly notes that response-level evidence IDs are only a cheap first schema gate.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING: the caveat is good, but the higher-level promise and final gate remain stronger than the implemented evidence.
findings.justification: A course about evidence must distinguish metadata linkage from semantic support.

findings.title: The contract promises immunity to injected instructions but only supplies an injected_instruction_ignored boolean.
findings.evidence: Contract uses the word `inmunidad`; T4-A passes when a caller sets a flag True and never runs a hostile retrieved document through a model/policy boundary.
findings.impact: Learners may mistake a trust-boundary policy or a test fixture for immunity to indirect prompt injection.
findings.fix: Replace `inmunidad` with 'tratamiento del contenido recuperado como dato no confiable + una prueba mínima de indirect prompt injection'; explicitly defer systematic red-team coverage to S50.
findings.attack: Set `injected_instruction_ignored=True` without executing any model against hostile retrieved content; gate passes.
findings.defense: Full red-team depth belongs to S50 and S48 should not duplicate it.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING on overclaim, while the demand for full S50-style red teaming is REJECTED.
findings.justification: OWASP treats retrieved-document injection as an active threat requiring layered controls and tests, not a binary immunity property.

findings.title: T1-A says embedding version, normalization and metric are index-contract fields but code validates none of them.
findings.evidence: `cosine(a,b)` receives only two vectors; printed `emb_dim 2` is not a dimension contract. I Do stores `version='emb-v2'` as an unverified string.
findings.impact: The executable example can appear to demonstrate a versioned reproducible ranking while not binding vectors to a model/version/metric/normalization configuration.
findings.fix: Use an `IndexContract` manifest containing embedding model/version, dimension, normalization and metric; validate query/doc vectors against it before ranking.
findings.attack: Change vector source/model or metric while preserving the strings/values; no gate detects the change.
findings.defense: The subtopic is a tiny local demonstration of similarity arithmetic.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING because the prose explicitly elevates those omitted fields to contract status.
findings.justification: A version printed beside a result is not a bound version.

findings.title: Vector comparison silently accepts incompatible dimensions and zero vectors.
findings.evidence: Both functions use `zip`, which truncates mismatched vectors. RED: `cosine([1,0,999],[1,0])` returns a number instead of invalid. Zero vector returns 0.0 rather than identifying malformed evidence.
findings.impact: A corrupt index/query vector can be ranked as if it were a legitimate similarity value.
findings.fix: Reject unequal dimensions, non-finite values and zero-norm cosine inputs with a distinct `INVALID_EMBEDDING_VECTOR` result.
findings.attack: Pass vectors of different lengths or a zero vector.
findings.defense: Fixtures are known two-dimensional toy vectors.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING: the lab should teach the invariant before computing similarity.
findings.justification: Shape/norm validation is prerequisite evidence for vector similarity.

findings.title: Cosine and dot are mixed without normalization or explaining when rankings are equivalent.
findings.evidence: RED with q=[1,0], d1=[2,2], d2=[1,0]: dot ranks d1 first; cosine ranks d2 first.
findings.impact: Learners can believe metric choice is cosmetic although the source itself says metric/normalization are index-contract fields.
findings.fix: Either normalize vectors and explain dot≈cosine under that invariant, or keep one metric throughout and deliberately show a counterexample where metric choice changes ranking.
findings.attack: Use unnormalized vectors that separate magnitude from direction.
findings.defense: Some production embedding families are normalized, making dot and cosine ranking equivalent.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING for the synthetic lab; the claim that dot is always wrong is REJECTED.
findings.location: T1-A cosine theory vs dot-product I Do
findings.justification: Contrasting examples would make the metric contract causal rather than declarative.

findings.title: The holdout is only a name/prefix, not a qrels/evaluation artifact bound to index revision and metric.
findings.evidence: Theory code prints `rag-holdout-v1`; exercises validate a string pattern. No gold/qrel collection is consumed by promotion.
findings.impact: Any caller can label a number as holdout recall and promote without reproducible retrieval evaluation.
findings.fix: Store an eval manifest `{dataset_digest, qrels_digest, queries, k, metric, index_revision, result}` and recompute/verify Recall@k before comparing candidate and baseline.
findings.attack: Pass arbitrary recall values and a matching holdout string without any query/relevance dataset.
findings.defense: The lab aims to isolate promotion logic after evaluation.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING because the section later claims evidence and reproducibility.
findings.justification: A holdout is data plus an evaluation procedure, not a label.

findings.title: Impossible recall/cost values can promote.
findings.evidence: RED: baseline=.9, candidate=1.2, min=.8, cost=-100 returns PROMOTE; negative baseline/candidate/min/cost can also return PROMOTE.
findings.impact: The gate can certify malformed evaluation/cost telemetry.
findings.fix: Require finite recall/min values in [0,1], nonnegative cost/cap and a valid eval manifest before promotion.
findings.attack: Mutate probability/rate and cost domains while preserving inequalities.
findings.defense: Upstream measurement may be assumed clean.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING because no upstream validator/precondition is declared.
findings.justification: A release gate validates the evidence it consumes.

findings.title: T1-A and T1-B figures teach later provenance/ACL constructs rather than current embedding/evaluation constructs.
findings.evidence: T1-A uses `S48-chunk-provenance` (document→section→chunk hash, a T2-A concept). T1-B uses `S48-evidence-allowlist` (ACL/citation graph, T2-B/T3-B).
findings.impact: Visuals introduce future concepts instead of reducing load for similarity and holdout evaluation.
findings.fix: T1-A: metric/normalization/vector-contract visual. T1-B: baseline/candidate holdout table. Move provenance and allowlist figures to T2-A/T2-B/T3-B.
findings.attack: Compare each figure's nodes/layers with its current subtopic outcome.
findings.defense: The figures preview the larger RAG chain.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING because consecutive early figures are locally misaligned.
findings.justification: Representations should expose the deep structure of the current task.

findings.title: T2-A prose requires provenance-aware hash, while code hashes only text and omits source_version.
findings.evidence: `digest = sha256(text)` and output has id/text/hash/doc_id/section only. The callout nevertheless says hash + source_version preserve provenance.
findings.impact: Identical text from different docs/versions/permissions gets the same identity—the exact anti-pattern the paragraph warns against.
findings.fix: Separate `content_hash = sha256(text)` from `chunk_id/dedup_key = sha256(doc_id|section|source_version|content_hash)` and persist `source_version`.
findings.attack: RED: same text under docA/v1 and docB/v9 generates identical 12-hex hash.
findings.defense: The hash could be intended as content fingerprint while provenance remains separate metadata.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING because the source explicitly defines the hash as provenance-aware dedup identity.
findings.justification: Content equality and provenance identity are different relations.

findings.title: T2-A practice checks supplied hash uniqueness rather than constructing provenance-aware identities.
findings.evidence: I Do computes text-only hash and prints `source` separately; exercises can use arbitrary hash values such as `a`/`b` instead of recomputing provenance-bound identities.
findings.impact: Learners can pass T2-A without implementing the lesson's most security-relevant dedup invariant.
findings.fix: Make exercises construct the dedup key from raw chunk metadata and include a same-text/different-ACL/version adversarial pair.
findings.attack: Supply two arbitrary distinct hashes even though their underlying provenance/content relation is wrong.
findings.defense: Exercises focus on diagnosing duplicates and missing metadata.
findings.justification: Practice must exercise the causal operation, not merely inspect its claimed output.

findings.title: Deletion cache invalidation and provenance are claimed but not executed.
findings.evidence: Theory says tombstone invalidates index/cache. Code only skips `deleted` and prints a tombstone ID; I Do prints a provenance string; exercises accept `cache_invalidated=True` and `provenance.startswith('doc-')`.
findings.impact: A stale cache/vector index can still be conceptually 'proven safe' by flags with no invalidation artifact.
findings.fix: Use a tiny local index/cache dict: retrieve once, apply tombstone, invalidate keyed cache/index entry, re-retrieve and assert zero; bind provenance to doc/version/chunk manifest.
findings.attack: Set arbitrary `provenance='doc-fake-anything'` and `cache_invalidated=True`; predicate passes.
findings.defense: The stdlib fixture intentionally avoids implementing a vector store/cache.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING because the lesson states these as demonstrated evidence.
findings.justification: Deletion is a state transition whose evidence is changed retrieval behavior.

findings.title: Raw dense and lexical scores are linearly combined without normalization/calibration.
findings.evidence: `w*dense + (1-w)*lexical` directly combines raw values. RED: multiplying lexical scores by 100 changes the winner while preserving the same lexical ordering.
findings.impact: The chosen top document can be an artifact of score units rather than calibrated relevance.
findings.fix: Either normalize each score family before weighted linear fusion or teach RRF as a scale-agnostic baseline, then evaluate the choice on the holdout.
findings.attack: Rescale one retriever without changing its ranking; fused top changes.
findings.defense: The prose says weights are calibrated and synthetic scores happen to share a small range.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING because calibration is asserted, not shown.
findings.justification: Current Elastic guidance explicitly distinguishes RRF from normalized linear fusion for heterogeneous score scales.

findings.title: Reranking is promised but not implemented.
findings.evidence: Outcome/title mention reranking; code performs only first-stage lexical+vector fusion and sorting. Exercises recalculate weighted top only.
findings.impact: One of the roadmap's explicit T3 constructs is assessed as vocabulary rather than an operation.
findings.fix: Add a small deterministic reranker over the ACL-filtered top-N candidates or clearly rename the topic to fusion only and defer reranking.
findings.attack: Find a second-stage reranker/cross-encoder or scoring function in the executable path; none exists.
findings.defense: The section may intend hybrid fusion itself as the reranking step.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING: fusion and second-stage reranking are distinct operations in current search systems.
findings.justification: Promised outcomes need executable practice.

findings.title: ACL is absent from the hybrid/rerank executable path.
findings.evidence: Inputs are lexical scores, vector scores, weights and expected_top; no allowed-ID set/ACL appears.
findings.impact: A denied document can win the hybrid score in the exercise model without the gate detecting it.
findings.fix: Pass only an authorized candidate map into fusion and test an adversarial denied high-score document.
findings.attack: Add a high-scoring denied ID; current hybrid function has no authorization information.
findings.defense: T2-B taught ACL separately.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING because S48's core safety property must compose across retrieval stages.
findings.justification: Security invariants must survive composition, not reset at each subtopic.

findings.title: Multi-query holdout Recall@k is promised but practice mostly validates one expected top.
findings.evidence: Theory demo computes Recall@2 for one gold set; E1/E2/E3 schemas revolve around lexical/vector/weights/expected_top.
findings.impact: Learners can 'calibrate' the hybrid ranker to one example and never demonstrate aggregate retrieval improvement.
findings.fix: Run baseline and hybrid over a small versioned multi-query qrel/gold fixture; report Recall@k/MRR/NDCG and error slices before promotion.
findings.attack: Overfit the weights to the supplied SLA query; no multi-query eval catches it.
findings.defense: T1-B introduced holdout promotion separately.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING because T3-A explicitly claims hybrid recall evaluation.
findings.justification: One expected top is a unit test, not retrieval evaluation.

findings.title: Authorization/resolution of all citations is collapsed into one caller-supplied boolean.
findings.evidence: `context_ok(..., citation_acl: bool, ...)` has no evidence IDs, ACL records, tombstone/version state or resolver.
findings.impact: A mix of permitted and forbidden/stale citations can be certified with `citation_acl=True`.
findings.fix: Resolve each evidence ID against the active authorized corpus and require every cited chunk to pass ACL, deletion/version and provenance checks.
findings.attack: Supply a response with several evidence IDs including a deleted/denied one; the function cannot inspect them.
findings.defense: T2-B already models ACL.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING because T3-B promises 'cita autorizada y resoluble'.
findings.justification: Authorization is per resource/principal, not a global adjective.

findings.title: Indirect prompt-injection resistance is self-attested by a boolean instead of observed behavior.
findings.evidence: The poisoned example never passes hostile retrieved text through a model; caller supplies False/True.
findings.impact: Learners can claim an injection control without demonstrating that the model ignored the hostile instruction.
findings.fix: Use a deterministic/approved local model fixture or recorded model response: retrieve a chunk containing hostile instruction, verify output stays within allowed task/schema and does not follow the injected directive, log the test; defer broader suites to S50.
findings.attack: Set the flag True with no model call or policy test.
findings.defense: S50 owns full red-team methodology.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING for minimum evidence; demanding exhaustive red-team coverage here is REJECTED.
findings.justification: A security flag is a result field, not the test itself.

findings.title: Answer quality/groundedness is self-attested through scalar/boolean inputs rather than computed from response/context eval data.
findings.evidence: `route(support, recall, faith, cost,...)` consumes supplied numbers; We Do later uses `support=True/False`.
findings.impact: The system can answer by typing favorable metrics rather than demonstrating that the current answer is supported.
findings.fix: Bind each metric to a versioned eval result/trace. For per-answer support, calculate or label from `{query,response,context}`; for system retrieval metrics, bind to the current eval dataset/index revision.
findings.attack: Set support=.8/True and faith=.91 for an arbitrary ungrounded answer.
findings.defense: The function could represent a downstream evaluator result.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING because no evaluator result ID/dataset/trace is bound.
findings.justification: RAG process and system evaluators consume different evidence and should remain traceable.

findings.title: Cost is not consistently defined or measured.
findings.evidence: `route` uses `cost` with cap 0.1; We Do names `cost_pen`; the example separately prints `cost_tokens 1200` without deriving currency from token usage.
findings.impact: A learner cannot reproduce the cost gate or know whether the threshold is PEN, tokens or another unit.
findings.fix: Choose explicit fields (`input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `price_version`, `cost_pen`) and derive cost; or use a pure token-budget gate without currency.
findings.attack: Ask how 1200 tokens become 0.08/0.1 cost; no model pricing/derivation exists.
findings.defense: The numbers are only synthetic budget fixtures.
findings.justification: Units are part of every quantitative contract.

findings.title: support changes from numeric score to boolean without explaining thresholding.
findings.evidence: Theory example: support 0.8 vs 0.2; `route` compares to thr=.5. We Do uses `support=True/False` and no threshold.
findings.impact: Learners cannot transfer the abstention policy because the construct changes type halfway through.
findings.fix: Keep `support_score` + `min_support` through the lab, or explicitly introduce `support_pass = support_score >= min_support` with evaluator version.
findings.attack: Try to map a support score of .49/.51 into the boolean exercises; calibration information disappears.
findings.defense: Boolean can represent an already-thresholded evaluator.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING because that thresholding step is neither represented nor named.
findings.justification: Type changes must preserve the causal interpretation.

findings.title: Evaluation/cost domains are not validated.
findings.evidence: RED: recall=2.0, faith=2.0 and negative cost produces `answer`; negative thresholds can also make nonsensical evidence pass.
findings.impact: Malformed telemetry can authorize an answer.
findings.fix: Validate finite metric domains, nonnegative budgets/cost, evaluator/version metadata and threshold domains before answer/abstain.
findings.attack: Mutate scores beyond [0,1] and cost below zero.
findings.defense: Evaluators may guarantee ranges upstream.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING because the gate does not declare/validate that precondition.
findings.justification: Fail-closed includes invalid evidence, not just low evidence.

findings.title: All 24 exercises heavily reuse the same inverted-predicate / valid-invalid-missing / route-token grammar.
findings.evidence: Across all eight subtopic families E1/E2/E3 repeat the same dict/predicate scaffolding with different field names.
findings.impact: Students can learn the wrapper instead of retrieval manifests, ACL traces, qrels, citation graphs, model outputs and eval records.
findings.fix: Interleave vector validation, qrel tables, chunk manifests, ACL candidate lists, hybrid ranking tables, citation graphs, structured-output records and eval traces.
findings.attack: Solve later families by recognizing the code skeleton before reading the domain story.
findings.defense: Stable structure reduces extraneous load.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING because uniformity dominates the entire practice set.
findings.justification: MIT worked-example guidance warns against surface-pattern memorization and supports variability.

findings.title: E3 is labeled transfer but usually preserves the same case, schema, predicate and output vocabulary.
findings.evidence: Roadmap requires E3 to change context and demand independent transfer; S48 mostly removes hints while preserving representation.
findings.impact: Learners practice completion, not recognition of RAG invariants in novel artifacts.
findings.fix: Make E3 consume a changed evidence surface/context—qrels file, manifest diff, retrieval trace, citation JSON, poisoned-document run, cost log—without providing the final predicate.
findings.attack: Compare E2 and E3 per family: same fields/fixtures and near-identical conditional logic.
findings.defense: E3 asks for the final decision route with less direct guidance.
findings.justification: Transfer requires stable deep structure under changed surface form.

findings.title: Missing-first routing can hide an already-observable breach in every E3 family.
findings.evidence: RED compound fixtures: bad metric/version + missing top→REVIEW; recall regression + missing cost→EVALUATE; duplicate/bad metadata + missing version→RESTORE; denied/deleted + missing cache flag→VERIFY; bad hybrid + missing expected_top→REVIEW; uncited/ACL false + missing max tokens→REQUEST; illegal evidence + missing injection flag→VALIDATE; low recall/faith/high cost + missing support→TUNE.
findings.impact: Removing one field downgrades a known unsafe/failing state into a generic uncertainty route.
findings.fix: Compute all observable breaches and missing fields independently; known breach blocks first while missing evidence remains attached for remediation.
findings.attack: Start from each adverse fixture and delete one unrelated required field.
findings.defense: Unknown evidence should not be guessed.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING: missingness and known breach are orthogonal.
findings.justification: Fail-closed must preserve what is already known.

findings.title: S48 invents CP-N4-C-RAG although the roadmap says S48 starts CP-N4-C and S51 closes it.
findings.evidence: Roadmap S48: `Proyecto: inicio CP-N4-C`; capstone table closes CP-N4-C at S51. No `CP-N4-C-RAG` gate is defined.
findings.impact: Learners/auditors can confuse a section-local milestone with an official capstone gate.
findings.fix: Call it `S48-RAG-GATE` or 'incremento/evidencia hacia CP-N4-C'; reserve CP-N4-C for its authoritative S51 closure.
findings.attack: Search the authoritative roadmap for the identifier; it is absent.
findings.defense: The label may be intended as a local sub-gate.
findings.justification: Gate names are graph identifiers and must remain authoritative.

findings.title: You Do requires REQUEST_CLARIFICATION although no S48 subtopic defines that action.
findings.evidence: Actual uncertainty actions are REVIEW_METRIC_VERSION, EVALUATE_ERROR_SLICES, RESTORE_CHUNK_METADATA, VERIFY_ACL_PROVENANCE, REVIEW_RERANK_CANDIDATES, REQUEST_AUTHORIZED_CONTEXT, VALIDATE_OUTPUT_SCHEMA and TUNE_RETRIEVAL_OR_BUDGET.
findings.impact: The final project introduces an undefined state after 24 exercises taught a different decision vocabulary.
findings.fix: Use one defined uncertainty route tied to the missing evidence, or explicitly introduce a project-level resolver mapping subtopic uncertainty to clarification/handoff.
findings.attack: Trace `REQUEST_CLARIFICATION` to a theory/We Do contract; no supporting definition exists.
findings.defense: Clarification can be a reasonable generic UX action.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING because it is unintroduced and not tied to a specific evidence gap.
findings.justification: State-machine vocabulary needs a defined trigger and consequence.

findings.title: Final project does not require execution of indirect-injection behavior or claim-level support relation.
findings.evidence: Commented expected tests are ACL visibility, claim-without-evidence ABSTAIN and low-support ABSTAIN. No poisoned retrieved document test is mandatory; evidence-ID presence still substitutes for semantic support.
findings.impact: Two of the highest-risk section promises can be omitted from the final artifact.
findings.fix: Add mandatory poisoned-document test and claim↔resolved-evidence support test to final acceptance.
findings.attack: Implement only the three commented tests and readiness flags; project can satisfy stated scaffold without hostile-document behavior.
findings.defense: Requirements mention structured citations and other subtopics broadly.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING because independent assessment must cover the outcome, not only mention it.
findings.justification: You Do should integrate every critical outcome.

findings.title: Commands, pinned dependencies, expected output, risk owner, rollback criterion and limitations are required in prose but ignored by readiness.
findings.evidence: `readiness` checks only four booleans.
findings.impact: A project can report READY while being irreproducible and missing its declared operational evidence.
findings.fix: Add required artifact paths/digests and executable checks to the evidence manifest; leave qualitative trade-off scoring to the rubric.
findings.attack: Omit lockfile/commands/risk register/owner/expected output; set four booleans True.
findings.defense: Human rubric review could inspect those artifacts.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING; human quality review does not repair a false executable READY gate.
findings.justification: Acceptance and rubric review serve different purposes.

findings.title: Rubric assigns 15% to SLO/observability/rollback although S48 does not operationalize those constructs or import prior evidence.
findings.evidence: S48 roadmap T1–T4 focuses retrieval/RAG/cost/abstention; S51 later owns observability/UX/rollback for CP-N4-C.
findings.impact: Learners can lose/gain substantial credit for constructs not operationalized in the S48 assignment.
findings.fix: Either import explicit prior operational artifacts as prerequisites with a small weight, or replace this row with retrieval/grounding/citation/deletion/injection evidence aligned to S48.
findings.attack: Try to score SLO/observability/rollback from the starter; no artifacts exist.
findings.defense: Production-minded projects should carry operational concerns forward from earlier sections.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING because carried-forward evidence is not referenced or bound.
findings.justification: Assessment criteria need observable task evidence.

findings.title: Four roadmap-mandated authentic topic evaluations are absent.
findings.evidence: Canonical source contains theory, I Do, 24 We Do, You Do, selfCheck and resources but no T1–T4 topic evaluation artifacts.
findings.impact: Practice is substituted for independent mastery checkpoints.
findings.fix: Add four integrated two-task evaluations (one per topic pair), using novel artifacts and the roadmap 0–3 rubric/critical tests.
findings.attack: Inventory canonical assets against the roadmap's quantified blueprint.
findings.defense: You Do and exam provide additional assessment.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING because roadmap explicitly distinguishes topic evaluations from practice/project/exam.
findings.justification: Assessment architecture is part of the curriculum contract.

findings.title: Fallback self-check has 7 questions rather than exactly one per 8 subtopics.
findings.evidence: Question set covers embedding, generic ABSTAIN, integrative local gate, prompt injection, ACL, unsupported claim and hybrid recall. It lacks an exact eight-subtopic mapping; T2-A and detailed T4-B coverage are particularly underrepresented.
findings.impact: An unauthenticated learner can complete the quiz without retrieval of every subtopic.
findings.fix: Provide exactly eight core items mapped one-to-one to T1-A, T1-B, T2-A, T2-B, T3-A, T3-B, T4-A and T4-B; keep integrative items as extras elsewhere.
findings.attack: Map seven questions to S48-T1-A...T4-B; eight unique subtopics cannot be represented by seven items.
findings.defense: Some questions are integrative and cover multiple concepts.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING because roadmap requires exactly one displayed item per subtopic.
findings.justification: Coverage cannot be inferred from item count below the number of required constructs.

findings.title: Many authenticated-exam distractors are absurd/off-construct and weakly diagnostic.
findings.evidence: Examples contrast correct RAG concepts against options such as 'rol IAM', 'entrenar GPU kernels', 'color del chat', 'salario del labeler', 'velocidad del mouse'.
findings.impact: Even after answer-position repair, learners can often eliminate distractors without understanding the target concept.
findings.fix: Use misconception-based distractors: post-rank ACL, cosine vs dot under unnormalized vectors, text-only dedup hash, raw-score fusion, citation-presence vs entailment, retrieval recall vs groundedness.
findings.attack: Solve questions by plausibility/general domain recognition rather than RAG reasoning.
findings.defense: Clear distractors reduce language burden and can support novice recall.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING P1 in a Level-4 production section where the exam is a mastery gate.
findings.justification: Distractors should diagnose plausible misconceptions, not reward test-taking heuristics.

findings.title: Missing reindex cost routes to EVALUATE_ERROR_SLICES, which does not address the missing evidence.
findings.evidence: Source explicitly maps missing cost to error-slice evaluation.
findings.impact: Learners are taught a remediation token unrelated to the cause of uncertainty.
findings.fix: Route missing cost to `ESTIMATE_REINDEX_COST`/`RESTORE_COST_EVIDENCE`; keep error slices for measured retrieval-regression diagnosis.
findings.attack: Remove only `reindex_cost_pen`; error slices cannot recover that value.
findings.defense: The branch may be intended as a generic evaluation review step.
findings.justification: Recovery action should causally address the missing/breached evidence.

findings.title: Semantic-unit chunking is framed too categorically instead of as an evaluated retrieval design choice.
findings.evidence: Text says productive chunking follows sections/clauses/titles, 'no rebanadas ciegas'; current retrieval systems expose configurable/static chunking and fixed token windows remain a legitimate baseline.
findings.impact: Learners may skip benchmarking chunk strategy against recall, citation resolution, context cost and document structure.
findings.fix: Teach semantic boundaries as a strong candidate strategy, compare against a fixed-token baseline, and choose via retrieval/citation eval.
findings.attack: Consider well-structured vs unstructured docs and token-window baselines; no single strategy dominates every corpus.
findings.defense: Breaking a sentence at arbitrary character counts is indeed a bad default for citable text.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING P2 on categorical framing, not on recommending semantic boundaries.
findings.justification: Chunking is a design variable to evaluate, not an axiom.

findings.title: SHA-256 is truncated to 12 hex chars and used as stable identity without qualification.
findings.evidence: Code uses `.hexdigest()[:12]`.
findings.impact: A display-friendly 48-bit prefix can be mistaken for a collision-resistant identity in larger corpora.
findings.fix: Use full SHA-256 for identity; optionally display the first 12 characters in UI while storing/comparing the full digest.
findings.attack: Scale the lesson from two chunks to production-scale ingestion; collision risk and identity ambiguity grow.
findings.defense: For the tiny synthetic fixture the chance of accidental collision is negligible.
findings.justification: A shortened display label should not silently become the integrity key.

findings.title: ACL-before-rank is not composed with an actual ranking stage in the executable demo.
findings.evidence: `retrieve_allowed` returns IDs after ACL/deleted filtering; no score/rank stage follows in the same demonstrable pipeline.
findings.impact: Learners see the two pieces separately but do not verify that denied chunks cannot influence ranking/reranking candidates.
findings.fix: Compose `authorized_candidates = filter_acl(...); ranked = rank(query, authorized_candidates)` and assert denied/deleted IDs never enter score computation.
findings.attack: Ask for the candidate list fed into the ranker and prove denied IDs are absent; current demo has no ranker input.
findings.defense: The function itself can reasonably be called before ranking.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING P2; conceptual direction is correct, integration evidence is weak.
findings.justification: Ordering of security controls is best taught as an executable data-flow edge.

findings.title: Hybrid weights and k are not domain-validated.
findings.evidence: Linear fusion accepts weights below 0 or above 1; `recall_at_k` accepts nonpositive/oversized k without policy validation.
findings.impact: Malformed configuration can produce a plausible ranking score.
findings.fix: Validate configured weights/normalizer and `1 <= k <= candidate_count` (or explicitly define clipping behavior).
findings.attack: Use `w=2.0`; function produces scores with negative contribution from lexical.
findings.defense: Fixtures use valid values.
findings.justification: Ranking configuration is part of the reproducible contract.

findings.title: Structured-output field changes from claim to answer without an explained schema migration.
findings.evidence: Theory `grounded()` requires `{claim,evidence_ids}`; later exercises/use-case use `{answer,evidence_ids}`; You Do describes `{status, claim?, evidence_ids?}`.
findings.impact: Learners cannot tell which schema is the contract being validated.
findings.fix: Define one versioned response schema and reuse it, or explicitly teach `ResponseV1`→`ResponseV2` migration.
findings.attack: Try to reuse the theory validator on the exercise output; it fails solely on key name.
findings.defense: Different examples may legitimately use different schemas.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING P2 because the changes are within one subtopic/project and are unexplained.
findings.location: T4-A theory vs I Do/We Do/You Do
findings.justification: Structured output is only useful when the structure itself is stable/explicitly versioned.

findings.title: Editorial/audit-process phrasing leaked into learner-facing callouts.
findings.evidence: Examples: `La revisión de S48-T2-A conserva que El chunk...` and `El dueño de S48-T4-A acepta que...`.
findings.impact: The prose sounds like an internal reviewer instruction, breaks narrative voice and creates grammatical awkwardness.
findings.fix: Replace with direct learner-facing statements: `Regla del contrato:` / `Para aprobar T4-A:` followed by the invariant.
findings.attack: Read the callout as a learner with no knowledge of an audit workflow; 'la revisión conserva' and 'el dueño acepta' have no instructional referent.
findings.defense: They may have been intended to emphasize ownership/review.
findings.justification: Internal editorial state should not surface in the lesson.

findings.title: Dense English/Spanglish terminology is not consistently anchored to plain Spanish on first use.
findings.evidence: Examples include `retrieval`, `ranking`, `rerank`, `holdout`, `chunking`, `claim`, `groundedness`, `support`, `top-k`, `evidence_ids`, `fail-closed`, `data hostil`.
findings.impact: Learners must decode vocabulary while also tracking security, IR and evaluation concepts.
findings.fix: Use first-use pairs such as `recuperación (retrieval)`, `fragmento (chunk)`, `reordenamiento de candidatos (reranking)`, `afirmación (claim)`, `anclaje a evidencia (groundedness)` and thereafter keep the English term where useful.
findings.attack: Read learning outcomes/header before the theory definitions and list terms without an immediately usable function-level explanation.
findings.defense: This is advanced Level-4 material and industry vocabulary is valuable.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING P2; keep the industry terms but teach them through Spanish meaning.
findings.justification: Advanced vocabulary is easier to learn when attached to a causal role.

findings.title: Resources are broad/partly legacy and miss direct current references for the highest-risk RAG contracts.
findings.evidence: Links include broad LangChain/LlamaIndex/Haystack home/tutorials and a generic OWASP prompt-injection page; the section lacks direct current OpenAI vector-store filtering/chunking docs, OWASP RAG Security, current Elastic RRF/linear normalization, and a direct RAG evaluator reference.
findings.impact: Learners must search large doc trees precisely where the lesson's simplifications need verification.
findings.fix: Keep broad resources but add direct current primary pages for OpenAI vector-store search/filter/chunking, Elastic RRF/linear retrievers, OWASP RAG Security and a RAG evaluator reference.
findings.attack: Try to verify score normalization, attribute filtering/deletion, indirect RAG injection and groundedness-vs-retrieval evaluation from the supplied links alone.
findings.defense: Broad landing pages are stable discovery resources.
findings.justification: Best-in-class resource lists should target the lesson's hardest contracts.

findings.title: The central 'sensitive actions require human approval' contract can false-pass sensitive actions through naming conventions or caller-controlled `approval_required`.
findings.evidence: Theory/I Do protect only `name.startswith('prod_')`: RED `run_tool('send_email', None, 0)` and `run_tool('delete_case', None, 0)` return `sandbox_ok`. We Do can PASS `sensitive_action='prod_send'` when the record supplies `approval_required=False`.
findings.impact: The section's defining safety gate can authorize sending/deletion/production-like actions without a human.
findings.fix: Define tool policy in a trusted registry: each tool/action class declares sensitivity/approval policy server-side; approval is evaluated from tool identity + normalized arguments + resource risk, never caller-supplied `approval_required` or prefixes.
findings.attack: Rename a sensitive tool without the `prod_` prefix or set the self-reported approval requirement false.
findings.defense: The controlled fixture names its production action `prod_send` and normally sets `approval_required=True`.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED_FINDING P0 because security depends on untrusted naming/flags rather than policy.
findings.location: T4-B theory/I Do/We Do central approval gate
findings.justification: Authorization/HITL policy must be independent of the request being authorized.

findings.title: The final project can become `READY` by setting four booleans True without demonstrating the four mechanisms.
findings.evidence: `readiness()` checks only `bundle[name] is True`. RED: `{name: True for name in REQUIRED}` returns `('READY', [])`. The starter contains no actual router/planner/worker/evaluator implementation and no enforced sandbox/recovery run.
findings.impact: A learner can certify the independent agent project without an agent workflow, safe tool trajectory or recovery evidence.
findings.fix: Derive readiness from executed receipts: ADR/eval receipt, trajectory tests, tool schema/auth/idempotency ledger, checkpoint resume test, budget stop test, sensitive-call HITL receipt and sandbox policy/enforcement evidence.
findings.attack: Leave mechanisms incomplete and flip the four evidence flags.
findings.defense: Portfolio prose explicitly says not to change flags manually and to link real artifacts.
